\"수성 완료. 성벽에 탄흔만 늘었습니다.\" — 데시마: "Defense complete. Only the scars on the walls increased." — Decima
\"성채 수성 열 번이면 성벽이 우리 편이 됩니다.\" — 데시마: "Ten Citadel defenses and the walls take our side." — Decima
\"열. 도전하는 쪽이 먼저 망설이기 시작했습니다.\" — 데시마: "Ten. The challengers have begun to hesitate first." — Decima
\"성채 수성 서른 번. 그쯤이면 성채가 연합명을 기억합니다.\" — 데: "Thirty Citadel defenses. By then the Citadel remembers the Alliance name." — Decima
\"서른. 성벽 수리 기록이 공격 기록보다 깁니다.\" — 데시마: "Thirty. The wall repair records are longer than the attack records." — Decima

깨운 사람이 아니라 맞아들인 사람: Not the one who woke her, but the one who welcomed her

밤 도크에 켜진 두 번째 불: A second light on in the night dock
표류하는 배와 스스로 가는 배: A drifting ship and a ship that steers itself
두 항적이 한 번 겹친 날: The day two wakes crossed once
서보 소리로 전력 비율을 읽는 둘: Two who read the power ratio from servo sound
번호판 숫자를 크게 칠하는 소녀와 관제관: The girl who paints her number big on the board, and the controller

회수 기록 칸을 두고 벌이는 서류 전쟁: A paperwork war over the salvage log columns
두고 온 것을 가지러 가는 짝: A pair who go back for what was left behind
두고 온 것과 버린 것: What was left behind and what was thrown away
한 칸을 저녁과 한낮으로 나눈 사이: Who split one column into evening and noon
저녁 신청곡의 단골: A regular at the evening request hour
올가의 왕복 시간에 배당을 거는 상인: A merchant taking bets on Olga's round-trip time
출력을 더 올려 달라 조르는 소녀: The girl who begs for more output
귀환 순서를 예약표 끝에 붙이는 둘: Two who tack the return order onto the end of the reservation sheet
늘 마지막에 오는 바람: The wind that always arrives last
빈 시간을 꾸리는 쪽과 문을 열어 두는 쪽: One who runs the empty hours and one who leaves the doors open
기다리는 법을 가르치는 교관: The instructor who teaches how to wait
사과 대신 조명을 고쳐 주는 친구: A friend who fixes the lights instead of apologizing

위에서 길을 불러 주는 사수: The gunner who calls out the way from above

\"예순. 당직을 두 배로 세운 배가 늘었어.\" — 그리젤: "Sixty. More ships are doubling their watch." — Grizel
\"백 번이면 단골입죠. 저쪽은 그렇게 안 부르겠지만요.\" — 티케: "A hundred makes them regulars. Not that they'd call themselves that." — Tyche
\"백. 우리 깃발 보면 문부터 닫더라.\" — 그리젤: "A hundred. They see our flag and shut the doors first." — Grizel
\"이백 번. 배당표가 두꺼워서 저울에 달아 봤습니다요.\" — 티케: "Two hundred. The dividend sheets got so thick I weighed them, I did." — Tyche
\"이백. 우리가 지나가면 전장이 조용해져.\" — 그리젤: "Two hundred. The battlefield goes quiet when we pass." — Grizel
\"스물다섯 번… 금고 문이 한 번도 안 열렸어. 나는 더 심심해졌고…\: "Twenty-five times… The vault door never opened. And I got even more bored…" — Rocca
\"스물다섯. 약탈 편성이 지휘관 배 좌표를 보고 방향을 튼다.\" —: "Twenty-five. Plunder squads see the commander's coordinates and turn away." — Grizel
\"쉰 번이면… 이제 이 금고는 지도에 없는 거나 마찬가지야. 낮잠 자도: "Fifty times… This vault might as well not be on the map. Guess I can nap…" — Rocca
\"쉰. 돌려보낸 편성 이름으로 벽 한 면을 채웠어.\" — 그리젤: "Fifty. I filled one wall with the names of squads we sent back." — Grizel
\"백 번… 아무도 손을 못 댔어. 금고 열쇠 어디 뒀더라…\" — 로카: "A hundred times… No one laid a hand on it. Where did I put the vault key again…" — Rocca
\"백. 이 배는 아무도 못 열어. 우리가 서 있는 한.\" — 그리젤: "A hundred. Nobody opens this ship. Not while we stand." — Grizel
\"경유지 천 곳이요. 엔진이 그러는데요, 이제 계기판보다 그을음이 많대: "A thousand waypoints. The engine says there's more soot than gauge now." — Auria
\"천 곳입니다. 다음 경유지는 예측하지 않겠습니다. 돌아올 길만 적습니: "A thousand. I won't predict the next waypoint. I only record the way back." — Cassandra
\"이천 곳이요. 엔진이 그러는데요, 소리만 들어도 어느 구역인지 안대요: "Two thousand. The engine says it knows the sector just by sound." — Auria
\"이천. 항해 일지가 세 권째입니다. 예측이 맞은 장은 그중 한 권쯤입: "Two thousand. The logbook is on its third volume. About one of them is predictions that came true." — Cassandra
\"삼천 곳이요. 엔진이 그러는데요, 판이 좁게 느껴진대요.\" — 아우: "Three thousand. The engine says the board feels small now." — Auria
"Three thousand. I could not predict the course. Still, this ship always came back." — Cassandra
\"실례지만, 첫 요격입니다. 배에 닿기 전에 빛이 먼저 닿았습니다.\": "Pardon me, our first intercept. The light reached them before they reached the ship." — Mona
\"마중 나간 편성이 막았습니다. 문을 열 필요도 없었습니다.\" — 모: "The squad that went out to meet them stopped them. No need to even open the door." — Mona
\"요격 열 번입니다. 조준선이 길 위에 미리 그어져 있습니다.\" —: "Ten intercepts. The aiming line is already drawn across their path." — Mona
\"열 번. 실례지만, 이제 오는 길목을 먼저 압니다.\" — 모나: "Ten. Pardon me, but I now know their route before they take it." — Mona
\"서른 번입니다. 배 앞이 아니라 길 위에서 끝납니다.\" — 모나: "Thirty. It ends on the road now, not before the ship." — Mona
\"서른. 제 빛이 기다리는 길로는 아무도 오지 않습니다.\" — 모나: "Thirty. No one takes the road where my light is waiting." — Mona
\"요격을 뚫었습니다요. 깎인 몫은 저쪽 배당표에 달아 둡죠.\" — 티: "We broke through their intercept, we did. I'll charge what we lost to their dividend sheet." — Tyche
\"마중 나온 놈들을 지나쳤어. 남은 전력으로도 충분했지.\" — 그리젤: "We passed the ones who came to meet us. What we had left was plenty." — Grizel
\"습격 막기 삼백 번. 사격 기록은 이제 권으로 세.\" — 그리젤: "Three hundred raids stopped. We count the firing log in volumes now." — Grizel
\"삼백. 예고가 와도 포탑들이 고개도 안 들어.\" — 그리젤: "Three hundred. Warnings come and the turrets don't even look up." — Grizel
\"오백. 데시마가 같이 쏜 게 몇 번인지 이제 안 세.\" — 그리젤: "Five hundred. I've stopped counting how often Decima fired with us." — Grizel
\"오백 번. 이 배 치러 오는 습격은 이제 훈련 같아.\" — 그리젤: "Five hundred times. Raids on this ship feel like drills now." — Grizel
\"8세대! 처음 본 좌표가 몇 번째로 살아났는지 이론이 헷갈려!\" —: "Gen 8! My theory's losing track of how many times the first coordinates came back!" — Agata
\"여덟 번째! 같은 자리에 같은 이름이 또 떴어!\" — 아가타: "The eighth! The same name popped up at the same spot again!" — Agata
\"10세대! 화면에 겹쳐 그린 선이 열 겹이야!\" — 아가타: "Gen 10! The lines I traced on the screen are ten deep!" — Agata
\"열 번째 세대! 다 캐 낸 자리도 다시 차올라. 이론 하나 추가!\": "The tenth generation! Even emptied ground fills back up. One more theory!" — Agata
\"12세대! 같은 좌표인데 적은 처음 보는 얼굴이야!\" — 아가타: "Gen 12! Same coordinates, but the enemies are brand-new faces!" — Agata
\"열두 번째! 보이는 건 다 셌는데 끝은 안 보여!\" — 아가타: "The twelfth! I counted everything visible and still no end!" — Agata
\"15세대! 지도보다 내 이론 노트가 더 오래됐어!\" — 아가타: "Gen 15! My theory notebook is older than the map!" — Agata
\"열다섯 번째! 처음 별명 붙인 날을 기억하는 건 나뿐이야!\" — 아: "The fifteenth! I'm the only one who remembers the day we nicknamed it!" — Agata
\"격파 이천 번! 귀환 신호가 숨소리처럼 들려!\" — 아가타: "Two thousand clears! Return signals sound like breathing!" — Agata
\"이천 번! 셀 때마다 손가락이 먼저 움직여!\" — 아가타: "Two thousand! My fingers move before I even count!" — Agata
\"삼천 번! 범위 밖에서 오는 것도 이제 먼저 느껴져!\" — 아가타: "Three thousand! I can even feel the ones coming from out of range!" — Agata
\"삼천! 셀 수 있는 건 다 셌어. 다음 것도 셀 거야!\" — 아가타: "Three thousand! Counted everything I could. I'll count the next one too!" — Agata
\"오천 번! 화면을 꺼도 귀환 점이 보여!\" — 아가타: "Five thousand! I see the return blips even with the screen off!" — Agata
\"오천! 돌아온 날이 훨씬 많아. 그걸 다 봤어!\" — 아가타: "Five thousand! Way more days of return. I saw them all!" — Agata
\"완공 사백 번. 비계를 걷는 날보다 세우는 날이 많을 거라고 예측합니: "Four hundred completions. I predict more days of raising scaffolding than taking it down." — Cassandra
\"사백 번입니다. 도면 보관함 열쇠가 하나 더 늘었습니다.\" — 카산: "Four hundred. One more key for the blueprint cabinet." — Cassandra
\"완공 오백 번. 처음 용접한 자리는 이제 지도가 있어야 찾습니다.\": "Five hundred completions. Finding the first weld now takes a map." — Cassandra
\"오백 번입니다. 배는 다 자라지 않았습니다. 예측대로입니다.\" —: "Five hundred. The ship hasn't finished growing. As predicted." — Cassandra
\"레벨 합 삼백오십이면 맨 위 갑판에서 함교가 내려다보일 거라고 예측합: "At a level total of three hundred fifty, I predict the bridge will be visible below from the top deck." — Cassandra
\"삼백오십입니다. 갑판 하나를 올라가는 데 숨이 찹니다. 그건 예측 못: "Three hundred fifty. Climbing one deck leaves me winded. That I did not predict." — Cassandra
\"사백이면 관측창 너머로 손을 뻗어도 될 거라고 예측합니다.\" — 카: "At four hundred, I predict one could reach past the observation window." — Cassandra
\"레벨 합 사백입니다. 별은 아직 멉니다. 어제보다는 가깝습니다. 이건: "Four hundred levels in total. The stars are still far. Closer than yesterday. That one I got right." — Cassandra
첫 인형. 트릭시가 회전자 하나 더 달자고 한다. 더 달면 더 빨리 돈다: The first figure. Trixie wants one more rotor on it. More rotors, faster spin. Leave it as is?
Leave the first one as it is. We can make a second figure together.
A second. Then the first stays untouched. I will go pick the scraps.
My call, then. But I only half listen to that girl.
Not for sale. It is the first one that spun. No price on that.
브리기타가 오늘 내 정보다 먼저 쳤다. 벽은 열렸다. 그런데 속이 안 편: Birgitta struck before my chisel today. The wall opened. Still, my gut is not settled. Why.
You two had an order you'd worked out. That's what was missing.
Order. That is it. Tomorrow I set the chisel first and wait.
Not tired. Hands are fine. The inside is not carved down yet.
If I strike, it is not a gap. It is a hole. I do not want that.
What have you made with your hands. Not broken. Made.
Not much. That's why I end up watching your hands so long.
Watching does not train hands. Tomorrow I put a scrap in yours.
Then start one now. I give you an easy grain first.
Paper has grain too. Fold it, and it takes shape. Try.
This chisel. The grip groove is bigger than my hand. I still do not swap it.
Don't. Your hand growing into that groove is carving too.
그 정 좀 보여 줘. 무슨 표시 있어?: Show me that chisel. Any marks on it?
My hand is being carved. Then it stays. Done.
A chisel is a chisel. But every grip, my hand goes into someone else's place.
No marks. Worn off, or never there to begin with.
부름종 울리면 왜 나는 손부터 나가는지 알아? 처음 들은 날, 옆이 텅: Know why my hand shoots out first when the call bell rings? The first day I heard it, there was nobody beside me!
So now you reach for the nearest arm first. Count my arm in too.
I'll ask them to ring it softer.
넣었다! 멀리 있어도 뛰어가서 걸 거야!: Counted in! Even if you're far, I'll run over and hook on!
It is loud! So instead of covering my ears, I hook an arm.
I'd hear it even soft! Soft is actually scarier.
갈고리가 빠지면 나 울어. 다 큰 브리처가. 웃기지?: When my hook slips off, I cry. A grown-up Breacher. Funny, right?
Not funny. Anyone gets a fright when what they're holding slips.
누구라도? 그럼 너도 울어? 그땐 내가 걸어 줄게!: Anyone? So you'd cry too? Then I'll hook on for you!
그치? 근데 그날은 콧물까지 났어. 그건 비밀!: Right? But that day my nose ran too. That part's a secret!
If it's tight, there's no fun in picking it, she says. The girl who picks my hook.
아무 일 없을 땐 팔 걸 핑계가 없어. 그런 날엔 뭐라고 하고 너한테 가: When nothing's happening, I have no excuse to hook your arm. On days like that, what do I say when I come to you?
Come without one. Just say, "Let's be together."
종을 하루에 한 번씩 울려 줄까?: Want me to ring the bell once a day?
그냥 같이 있자? 그거 말하기 제일 어려운 거잖아!: Just "let's be together"? That's the hardest thing to say!
볼일? 그럼 볼일을 만들어 올게! 매일!: Need something? Then I'll come up with something! Every day!
가짜 종은 안 돼! 다들 뛰어나오잖아!: No fake bells! Everyone comes running out!
녹 냄새 맡으면 괜히 코끝이 시큰해. 왜 그런지 몰라! 너도 그런 냄새: When I smell rust, the tip of my nose stings for no reason. No idea why! You've got a smell like that too, right?
I do. Old engines. When your rust smell comes, I'll be beside you.
I'll pick up some rust remover.
그럼 같이 맡자! 둘이 맡으면 덜 시큰할 거야!: Then let's smell it together! With two of us, it'll sting less!
It's just rust, so why this? One of my hands clenches tight.
닦지 마! 냄새까지 지워지면 아깝단 말이야!: Don't scrub it! If the smell goes too, that'd be such a waste!
Quiz! Why do I always tidy up after I pick a lock? Hint: the first place I cracked was a mess.
If you open something, you leave it better. As a sign you were there.
Just lock it back and leave.
A sign, huh. Not many people notice. You did.
Neat? You'd be shocked by my room. I only tidy other people's stuff.
If I just lock it, nobody knows I dropped by. I don't like that.
힐데 갈고리, 장난으로 따 본 날이 있어. 걔가 울더라. 그 뒤로 몇 번: One day I picked Hilde's hook as a prank. She cried. How many times have I hooked it back since? Go on, try!
You didn't count. Every time you hooked it, you'd have done it like the first time.
If she cries, just leave her be.
Didn't count. Me, not counting? That's against the rules.
If it were once, she'd still be crying. Way more.
Can't do that. If I picked it, it's on me to hook it back.
맨날 내가 퀴즈 내잖아. 너도 하나 내 봐. 나 진짜 못 맞힐걸?: I'm always the one with the quizzes. Give me one. Bet I really can't get it, hmm?
What was I waiting for most today? You talking to me.
That's not a quiz, that's cheating. …Give me a few more.
Then I'll wait. Till you think of one, however many seconds.
That's my specialty. It'd be so easy I'd feel bad.
자물쇠를 따면 꼭 뒷면부터 뒤집어 봐. 뭘 찾는지 나도 몰라. 이건 퀴즈: When I pick a lock, I always flip it to the back first. I don't know what I'm looking for. This one's not a quiz. Really.
When you really don't know, we can not-know together. That's a round too.
Don't flip it. Just put it away.
같이 모르는 판은 처음이야. 둘 다 지는 건가?: First round where we both don't know. Do we both lose?
If it's a habit, when did I pick it up? I don't remember that either.
Then my hands itch. Only seeing the front feels like I only half picked it.
반장님이 나무못을 쥐여 주시던 날요, 저 사실 용접이 더 멋있어 보였어요: The day the Chief pressed a wooden peg into my hand — honestly, welding looked cooler to me. Would you kindly keep that a secret?
I'll keep it secret. Still, fitting things so they can come apart, not fusing them — that's you.
Hearing that, one peg looks prettier. The sparks stay a secret, though.
Both? If the Chief heard that, sparks would fly first thing.
I'm afraid I'd weld everything shut. My hands are pretty quick.
오늘 다툰 두 분이 둘 다 옳은 말만 하셔서요. 볼트 하나 못 건드렸어요: The two who quarreled today were both completely right. I couldn't touch a single bolt. What do I do at times like this?
Some days don't loosen. If both are right, today you can just listen.
Just listen? Then tomorrow, shall I loosen up my ears first and go?
Leave it, and it rusts. I'll wait just one day and see.
Scold them, and they'd team up. Oh my — that's a way too.
지휘관이 쉬실 때 제 손도 같이 쉬어요. 일 없을 땐 뭐 하고 지내세요?: When you rest, Commander, my hands rest too. What do you do when there's no work?
I sit by the window. Put your tools down then too.
Without tools? My hands will feel empty, but I'll come.
You keep your fists clenched even when you sleep. I saw it all.
Paperwork on your day off? Shall we lighten that pile a little first?
처음 손이 가는 볼트가 늘 제일 약한 자리예요. 제 손이 저보다 먼저 알: The first bolt my hand goes to is always the weakest spot. My hands know before I do.
Loosening the weak spots first hurts less. Your hands know that.
Reinforce the weak spots with a weld.
덜 아프게요… 그 말, 다음 다툼에 빌려 써도 돼요?: So it hurts less… Can I borrow that line for the next quarrel?
A hundred coincidences make a habit, right? I stopped counting, too.
Reinforce it and it can't be loosened next time. That's not my job.
리브 멀미하던 날부터 해치를 안 닫았대. 그 전엔 닫는 게 당연했는데,: They said I haven't closed the hatch since the day Liv got seasick. Before that, closing it was a given. Now it seems I've forgotten how.
A path for one became a path for two.
Two, you said. Lately there were times it was three. You, I mean.
Even just one — for a girl who went alone, it was a heavy lid.
Air does get in. They said it's less stuffy down below now.
위에선 길을 자주 잃어. 밑에선 한 번도 안 잃는데. 위에서 헤매면 너: Up top I lose my way a lot. Down below, never once. If I'm lost up there… can I come find you?
Come. I'll show you the upper paths. You show me the ones below.
A trade, then. I'll show you the paths below one at a time, saving them up.
Getting lost wasn't something I got to choose. Up top it all looked the same.
Signs are for people who look up, they said. I walk looking at the floor.
Where's quietest for you? I heard there are places like that up top too.
The passage behind the engine room. It's up top, but it's quiet.
Quiet places make me sleepy. Not a fan.
Behind the engine room, you said. I'll run a path down there, under it.
If you don't have one, I'll lend you mine. The third bend in the pipes. It was warm and quiet.
If you get sleepy, you can sleep. They said nobody wakes you down below.
내가 판 굴 끝은 다 같은 모양이더라. 둥글지도 네모나지도 않아. 무슨: The ends of the tunnels I dug were all the same shape. Not round, not square. What does it look like to you?
Now I'm curious. Next time, let's go to the end together and look.
둥글게 파면 덜 힘들지 않아?: Wouldn't digging it round be easier?
They said it'd look different seen together. Bring knee pads.
It's just a hole, but my hands kept shaping it that way.
Even when I dug round, at the end there was that shape again.
얼굴 없이 건네는 말이 편했습니다. 마주 보고 물으면 대답이 안 올 것만: Words offered without a face were easier for me. I had a feeling that if I asked face to face, no answer would come.
Ask me face to face and I'll still answer. Like now.
Just say it to my face.
놀래키는 게 재밌어서 아니었어?: Wasn't it because scaring people is fun?
Like now, you say. Then today I shall step out before the door to speak.
To your face… I shall practice. One step at a time.
That too, I confess. A scream is the fastest of all answers, you see.
농담이 안 나오는 날이 있습니다. 그런 날은 어디 숨어 있으면 좋겠습니까: There are days when no jokes come. On such days, where would you have me hide?
Don't hide. Stay beside me. You don't have to talk.
Then I shall stay beside you, quieter than a ghost.
A room is something one locks from inside. Today I shall leave it open a little.
I shall borrow someone else's laughter. Heh heh… If it is not funny, the video is to blame.
Do you, too, have a door locked from inside? Who holds the key?
I do. The key's still in my hand. Someday I'll show it to you.
On that day I shall stand outside the door. I will do the knocking.
You have none, then. If I said I envied you, it would sound like a joke, I suppose.
Her hands are quick, yes. This is a door that is not to be opened quickly.
이 표식 말입니다. 가끔 혼자 방향을 바꿉니다. 지금은 당신 쪽을 가리키: This mark, you see. Now and then it changes direction on its own. At present it points toward you.
Let's not decide what it means. I'll stand wherever it points.
If you will be standing there, I shall never lose my way.
If my mood shows on the back of my hand, it is a rather honest hand.
It turns even with the lights off. I have tried it more than once.
…브리콜라가 제 자리에 판을 덧대 주었습니다. …제가 옮기면… 그 판은: …Bricola patched a plate onto my place. …If I move… will that plate be left alone?

내일도! 그래서 하루 하나구나. 오늘 몫은 끝까지 지킬게!: Tomorrow too! So that's why it's one a day. I'll keep today's share to the end!
그 애는 귀찮아도 볼트는 끝까지 푸는 애야!: Even when she can't be bothered, she undoes every bolt to the end!
다 풀면 아침에 할 말이 없어져! 그건 정말 싫어!: If she undid it all, I'd have nothing to say in the morning! I'd really hate that!

내가 증인! 그날은 맨 앞줄에서 들을게. 박수는 끝나고!: I'm the witness! That day I'll listen from the front row. Applause after!
안 하는 사람도 있구나. 그럼 내가 두 사람 몫 할게!: So some people don't. Then I'll do enough for two!

다리야가 그러는데, 내가 맹세할 땐 목소리가 두 겹으로 들린대! 너도 그: Darya says when I swear, my voice sounds like it's in two layers! Do you hear it that way too?

잡음이면 고치면 되는데! 그럼 내 목이 고장인가? 맹세할 때만?: If it's static, it can just be fixed! Then is my throat broken? Only when I swear?

얘, 이리 와. 지금이야, 지금. …맡았어? 그치?: Dear, come here. Now, right now. …Smell it? You did, didn't you?

가깝긴 하지! 늘 여기 있으니. 안 움직이는 안내판이다!: Close, sure! I'm always here. A signpost that never moves!

다들 그렇게 깨어나지 않아?: Doesn't everyone wake up like that?

처음 손 내민 사람! 후배한테 그 말 크게 써 붙일래!: First to hold out a hand! I'm writing that big and sticking it up for Box Kid!

좁았는지는 몰라. 뚜껑 열리는 소리는 엄청 컸어!: Dunno if it was cramped. The lid opening was super loud, though!
문틀이 늦게 오는 날엔 나 판에 안 껴. 지는 게 싫어서야, 진짜로!: On days Doorframe comes back late, I stay out of the pool. 'Cause I hate losing, for real!

내가 처음? 진짜지? 그럼 내 손목도 너한테 제일 먼저 보여 줄게!: I'm first? For real? Then you get to see my wrist first, too!

Hold a pen, hand goes stiff. Not with cord.

내가 안 돌아오면. 너, 가지러 와?: If I don't come back. You come get me?

등 하나로 뭐가 달라져?: What difference does one lamp make?

드물대— 그럼 오늘 기록 옆에 그 말도 붙여 둘래!: Rare, huh— then I'm sticking that next to today's record!

Day to day. Just hearing it, my finger wants to draw a circle.
And what comes after coffee? I will ask as far as the second.
제 손가락 원은 늘 지름이 같습니다. 재 본 일은 없는데, 어디서 본 크: The circle my finger draws always has the same diameter. I have never measured it, yet it seems a size I have seen somewhere.
Keep drawing it that size. Your hand will know where it came from first.
A compass would be more accurate.
The hand first. Then today's first circle, I will draw with my eyes closed.
They are not alike. My circle closes at the same point every time.
I cannot bring a compass on sorties. My finger is always attached.
그대 없는 날 지휘를 대신 서는 아이 곁에서 차만 따르다 왔소. 한마디도: On a day without you, I stood beside the one who takes command in your stead and did naught but pour tea. Not a word did I say. Does that count as helping?
Having someone beside you while you grumble is the biggest help there is.
It's her job, so she'll be fine.
Next time, you take command for me.
Is that so? Next time I shall bring two teacups. And warm the grumbling, too.
Just so, it is her task. Still, I could not bear to watch the tea go cold.
Were I to command, every door would open, and she would only be busier.
작은 첫째가 내게 바람쟁이라는 별명을 붙였소. 그대도 그리 부르겠소?: The little firstborn has given me the nickname Windy. Will you call me that as well?
Windy's nice, but I'll call you the one who opens doors.
One who opens doors… I shall count that as received before the child's nickname.
A name is good too. Though that child coins the nickname before the name.
Do not stop her. When that child is quiet, the ship grows far too wide.
그대가 훗날 누군가에게 넘겨줄 것이 있다면, 무엇이겠소?: If there were something you would one day hand on to someone, what would it be?
What I learned on this ship. With a little more added than I got.
All I'd pass on is debt.
A little more added… there is the sound of wind in your words.
Nothing in particular. Then wait for the day I hand you something.
Debt, ha ha. Then when you hand that on, hand it on lightly.
Hold out your hand a moment. …There. It is nothing.
You can look longer. Even if it's not the hand you were looking for, I won't let go of this one.
A hand that does not let go… so there is one more hand to remember.
Nothing on it. Looking at hands is an old habit of mine.
Palms I cannot read. On yours I shall draw a path for the wind instead.
The ones who stand next to me use less fuel, they say. I didn't do anything.
Even if you did nothing, you're right there beside them. That's what you did.
Then go sit by the fuel bay.
If being beside them counts as work… I've done a lot of work.
Maintenance would like hearing that. Tell them.
It's kind of cold there. Still… maybe I'll sit.
음, 하는 거. 언제부터 했는지 몰라. 너 처음 들은 날 기억나?: Mm, that thing I say. Don't know when it started. Remember the first day you heard it?
Yeah. That one word, and the whole squad came together. It's stayed with me since.
Hard to say. I hear it every day.
Try saying something else for once.
It stayed with you. Then I'll use it sparingly.
Every day's good enough. Counting dates is a bother.
If I say anything long, everyone's startled. Not doing it.
너. 명령 안 하고 하루 보낼 수 있어?: You. Could you get through a day without giving orders?
I'll try. In return, show me, right beside me, how you hold out.
명령 안 하면 누가 움직여?: If I don't give orders, who moves?
Tough, huh. Then I'll do nothing for both of us.
Everyone moves. Look at me. I don't give any.
너무 조용하면 잠이 안 와. 이상하지. 너는 뭘 들으면서 자?: Too quiet and I can't sleep. Weird, huh. What do you listen to when you sleep?
The hum of the ship running. If it gets too quiet, I'll at least talk to you.
말 걸어 줘. 대답은… 안 해도 되지?: Talk to me, then. I don't have to answer… right?
"Just sleeping" is the hardest. I envy you.
(covers her ears) Mm. Even quieter. Backwards.
깃대를 세울 때 늘 조금 기울게 됩니다. 규정은 수직인데도 말입니다!: Whenever I raise the flagpole, it always leans a little. Even though regulations say vertical!
That lean is your flagpole. You've kept it longer than any regulation.
규정보다 오래라… 규정집 여백에 써 두겠습니다!: Longer than regulations… I shall write that in the margin of the regulation book!
똑바로 보이셨다니, 오늘 자세는 합격입니다!: It looked straight to the Commander? Then today's posture passes!
고쳐 세워도 손이 먼저 기웁니다. 다시 해 보겠습니다!: Even when I reset it, my hand leans first. I shall try again!
저는 앉아서도 등을 등받이에 대지 않습니다. 지휘관께선 편히 기대 앉으십: Even seated, I do not let my back touch the backrest. Commander, please lean back and sit at ease!
Lean back just once. I'll keep an eye on this ship's posture meanwhile.
의자를 바꿔 줄까?: Want me to swap your chair?
That posture is not in the manual. …Just once, as a trial.
편한 게 이 자세입니다! 정말입니다!: This posture is the comfortable one! Truly!
의자는 죄가 없습니다! 저는 원래 이렇습니다!: The chair is not at fault! I am simply built this way!
지휘관께서 깃발을 하나 고르신다면 어떤 무늬로 하시겠습니까? 보고해 주십: If the Commander were to choose a flag, what pattern would it bear? Please report!
A plain one. Once you salute it, it's complete.
A ship with no flag is easier.
경례로 완성되는 깃발이라니! 매일 아침 올리겠습니다!: A flag completed by a salute! I shall raise it every morning!
"Anything" is not in the regulations! I shall submit three drafts.
Then I shall leave only the flagpole standing. Guarding a flagpole is familiar duty.
꿈에서도 경례합니다. 받는 분 얼굴은 늘 비어 있습니다. 지휘관께선 꿈을: I salute even in my dreams. The face of the one receiving it is always blank. Does the Commander dream?
Sometimes. Today, try putting my face in that blank.
I accept that as an order! I shall expect a return salute in the dream as well.
I envy you! I am on duty even in my dreams.
그럼 꿈속 경례는 비번으로 처리하겠습니다. 경례!: Then I shall log the dream salute as off duty. Salute!
카산드라가 오늘 또 함교를 돌았어요. 저 그 바퀴 수를 세요. 하아, 왜: Cassandra circled the Bridge again today. I count her laps. Haah, I do not even know why I count them.
Maybe Cassandra can circle without worry because you're counting.
You could've gone around with her.
She circles without worry? Then today's relief matches today's lap count.
If I stop counting, who counts? Oh. Nobody has to.
If we both circle, the whole Bridge spins. One of us has to stand still.
오늘 하나만 지휘관이 대신 정해 주실래요? 아무거나요. 남이 정한 걸 받: Commander, would you decide just one thing for me today? Anything. I would like to try receiving something someone else decided.
Sure. I'll set tonight's order. You just listen.
You decide things better than I do.
Just listen? Haah… This is more comfortable than I thought. That is a problem.
I know. That is why I always do it. I will take the compliment.
Making the lots is my job too, you know. I will go cut the paper.
여기 안 계실 때요, 거기선 누가 지휘관을 기다려요?: When you are not here, Commander, who waits for you over there?
Someone waits there too. So I try not to be late to either side.
Both sides? That sounds busy. Then I will not rush you from my end.
So busy people wait for each other. Without the other knowing.
Then I will have to wait twice as much. More work again.
이 모래시계요, 예전 배에서 가져온 거예요. 거기선 장식이었어요. 지휘관: This hourglass — I brought it from my old ship. There it was only decoration. Commander, is there anything you have carried around a long time?
There is. Carry something long enough and it becomes yours. That hourglass is yours now too.
Mine. Haah, hearing that, it got a little heavier. In a good way.
You have none? Then hold mine for a moment. Just 30 seconds.
If someone left it, they will come back for it someday. Until then, I will flip it.
The day I first came aboard, the only thing to read was the Charter, you know? So I memorized it.
So you made that one book your own.
Memorizing it, the sentences became friends. Friends who never start a conversation.
I was bored, so I read it aloud from Article 1. The walls never answered.
If there had been, I'd be quoting novels at you by now.
마르가가 취소 수수료 조항을 빼 달래. 꼬리표 하나 떼는 데 무슨 수수료: Marga wants the cancellation fee article taken out. Says what fee could there be for peeling off one tag. Whose side are you on?
You two can fix it together. Put one of Marga's tags on your sentence.
An article with a tag on it… Kind of cute, actually? I'll draft it.
알아서 하면 수수료가 생기는데, 괜찮겠어?: If you leave it to us, there's a fee for that. You okay with it?
The amount's still blank. That's where the fight broke out, you know.
Do you have a rule you keep too? One nobody set for you.
On a day I said I'd be back, I always come in. I set that one myself.
자작 조항이네. 내 헌장 부록에 옮겨 써도 돼?: A self-made article. Can I copy it into my Charter's appendix?
If you don't have one, I'll write you one. The draft's free.
질색인 것도 규칙이야. 너 벌써 하나 있거든?: Hating them is a rule too. You've already got one, you know?
너는 계약서 끝까지 읽는 쪽이야, 서명부터 하는 쪽이야?: Are you the type who reads a contract to the end, or the type who signs first?
I read to the end. If you wrote it, down to the footnotes.
Down to the footnotes, huh. Then anything I give you gets plenty of footnotes.
There's always one. From now on, I'll read yours first for you.
Then make your first signature on my Charter. The signature line's always been empty.
좋은 소식부터 말하는 거요, 사실 떨려서이기도 해요. 첫마디가 밝으면 목: Starting with the good news — honestly, it is partly nerves. When the first words are bright, my voice shakes less.
So that's why your first words are always bright. Even if you shake, I'll listen to the end.
If you hear the shaking too, that is a broadcast accident! …A good accident.
Keeping you from noticing was the technique. Today it is all out.
My voice is warmed up! The shaking is lower than the throat.
요즘 라다가 가끔 저한테만 먼저 알려 줘요. 그럼 저는 발표를 일부러 천: Lately Lada sometimes tells only me first. Then I make the announcement slowly, on purpose.
Leaving Lada her share. You both treasure the news.
Then Lada could just announce it.
Treasuring the news — that is headline material! Not a word to her, though.
Go fast and the whisper gets buried. Half a beat late is good manners.
그 애가 마이크 잡으면 다 귓속말이에요. 아무도 못 들어요!: When she takes the mic, it is all whispers. No one can hear a thing!
지휘관이 제일 듣고 싶은 소식은 뭐예요? 오면 제가 제일 먼저 전해 드릴: What news would you most like to hear, Commander? When it comes, I will bring it to you first.
News you deliver without running out of breath. Anything like that is fine.
Without running out of breath… I will practice. I am a little out of breath even now.
없으면 제가 하나 찾아 올게요! 취재 들어갑니다!: If there is none, I will go find one! Heading out on assignment!
The menu is the mess hall notice board's department! I only handle breaking news.
제 목소리, 녹음해서 들으면 낯설어요. 방송할 땐 모르는데요. 어느 쪽이: My voice sounds strange when I hear it recorded. I never notice while broadcasting. Which one is my real voice?
Both are yours. Even the way it speeds up before good news.
You even heard it speed up? Then it really is mine.
Everyone? What a relief! That will be today's good news.
I will have the recorder apologize. As a correction notice.
함교에 들면 짐은 맨 윗자리가 아니라 여섯 번째 자리부터 손으로 쓸어 보: On entering the Bridge, We run Our hand not over the top seat, but from the sixth seat onward. What does the guest make of it?
Maybe to keep the top seat empty. For whoever's coming.
Top first is the proper order.
For whoever is coming… Then We shall be brushing for a long while yet.
If it were dust, one would sweep from the top. We, too, find that strange.
A guest who knows proper order. Yet Our hand will not obey.
마리나가 짐에게 묻더구나. 기다리다 지치면 어찌하느냐고. 손님이라면 무엇: Marina asked Us: what does one do when weary of waiting? What would the guest answer?
That she can wait sitting down. Because you're doing the standing in her place.
You answer by way of Us. We shall pass those words on as they are.
She is not a child who rests when told to. That is why We asked.
That child, not waiting… We cannot picture her.
If the guest were to give Us one command, what would it be?
Next squadron, watch beside me. That's the command.
A command to watch at your side… We accept it gladly.
A guest sparing with commands. That, too, is a kind of majesty.
Cleaning! We, with Our own hands… Yet the top seat We shall leave empty.
거함 편대에서 그 큰 그림자를 마주하면, 짐은 어째서인지 고개가 숙여지노: Facing that great shadow in the Dreadnought squadron, Our head bows, for some reason. What does the guest feel?
I go quiet. So when you bow your head, I'll watch ahead for you.
If the guest watches ahead, We shall simply pay that shadow its due courtesy.
Fear… perhaps. Yet Our head did not tremble.
Breaking it is the guests' part. We shall record that We saw it.
오늘 힐데가 딴 데 갔어! 짐은 사십 가벼운데 손이 자꾸 기다려. 이상하: Hilde went off somewhere else today! The load's forty lighter, but my hands keep waiting. Weird, right?
Hilde was part of your load too. Your hands are still counting that forty.
If it feels empty, load more.
사십! 손이 그거 빼먹을까 봐 계속 세고 있어. 오면 크게 더한다!: Forty! I keep counting so my hands don't drop it. When she's back, I'm adding it big!
Some days light is good! But not today.
더 실으면 무게는 같은데 소리가 안 나. 매달린 애는 시끄럽거든!: Load more and the weight's the same, but there's no noise. The one hanging on is loud!
When Liv says lift here, I just lift! I can't feel the tilt one bit, though. That's okay, right?
You know weight, and Liv knows lean. You two lift it together.
Then try measuring the tilt yourself too.
둘이 같이! 그럼 하나, 둘에 나는 들고 걔는 본다!: Together! Then on one, two—I lift and she watches!
Should be! If not, she'll tell me again in that little voice.
나는 손으로 재! 기울기는 발로 재는 거래. 내 발은 둔해!: I measure with my hands! They say you measure tilt with your feet. My feet are numb to it!
넌 뭐가 제일 무거웠어? 숫자 말고! 손이 기억하는 거로!: What's the heaviest thing you ever lifted? Not a number! The one your hands remember!
The weight of someone leaning on me. That one doesn't count in numbers.
That weight—what do you call it, if not a number? I've got one I want to name too.
기억 안 나면 지금 하나 만들자! 나 들어 볼래? 몇인지는 비밀!: If you don't remember, let's make one now! Wanna lift me? How much—that's a secret!
백 개! 크다! 근데 그건 내 손도 아는 무게라 재미없어!: A hundred! Big! But my hands know that weight too, so it's no fun!
만약에 말이야! 내 팔이 안 올라가는 날이 오면 어떡해? 하나도 못 드는: Say, what if! What if a day comes when my arms won't go up? A day I can't lift a single thing!
That day, you call out the weight and I'll lift. If we're wrong, we laugh.
네가 들고 내가 외친다! 그것도 꽤 대결 같다. 숫자는 크게!: You lift and I shout! That's pretty much a contest too. Numbers nice and big!
Resting's the thing I'm worst at… but next to you, I'll try keeping still.
은퇴하면 맞히기만 할래! 들지 않고 외치기만! 그것도 재밌겠다!: If I retire, I'll just do the guessing! No lifting, only shouting! That'd be fun too!
멀미 나는 날엔 배 밑 해치가 미리 열려 있어요. 에델 씨한테 말한 일도: On days I feel seasick, the hatch under the ship is already open. I have never told Edel. How does she know?
Maybe your footsteps change. You're not the only one who can tell a tilt.
Leaving a hatch open is dangerous.
My footsteps… Then today I will try walking straight. To see if she still finds out.
That is the tenth coincidence already. At that point, it feels like kindness.
She is always the one who closes it, too. Just a hand pops up from below.
기울었다고 말할 때요, 목소리가 자꾸 작아져요. 크게 말하면 정말 기울어: When I say we are tilting, my voice keeps getting smaller. Because if I say it loudly, I feel we really will tip over.
Quiet is fine. I'll be the one listening for your voice first.
It only carries if you say it loud.
방송으로 알려 볼래?: Want to try announcing it on the PA?
Then I say it softly, and you find it, Commander. Two of us make one person's share.
Yes… Today I will count to three and then say it. A little louder.
On the PA, the whole ship would look at me… Then I think it would tilt the other way.
여긴 수평선이 없어서요… 지휘관님은 어지러울 때 어디를 보세요?: There is no horizon out here… Where do you look when you are dizzy, Commander?
One far-off star. Next time, let's look at it together.
One star. Then I will look at the space between that star and you, Commander.
Closing them makes it sway more… But I will try once. If you hold my hand.
I envy you… On my dizzy days, please stay beside me. I will lean toward you.
지휘관님 배는요, 어디로 기울어 있어요? 거긴 제가 한 번도 못 가 봐서: Your ship, Commander—which way does it lean? I have never once been there.
I don't know either. Someday come over and find it for me.
If I ever go, I will stand there quietly for a long while. So the ship can speak first.
If there is a level ship… I am a little jealous. But I would still like to see it.
I cannot ask someone I do not know. I would rather hear it from you, Commander.
오사가 뗏목 위에서 잠들었어~ 내 짐배 옆에서~ 깨울까 말까~?: Åsa fell asleep on her raft~ right next to my barge~ wake her, or let her be~?
Don't wake her. She says it's calmest next to your barge.
She'll wake up on her own.
Tell her to move that raft.
그럼 오늘은 짐배 안 움직일래~ 흐음~ 작게 불러야지~: Then I won't move the barge today~ hmm~ I'll sing it softly~
깨면 배고프다고 하겠지~ 간식은 벌써 옆에 놔뒀어~: When she wakes she'll say she's hungry~ I already left a snack beside her~
치우면 내 옆이 너무 넓어져~ 그건 좀 쓸쓸해~: If it's moved, my side gets too roomy~ that's kinda lonely~
짐을 사흘 먼저 싣는 거~ 나도 왜 그런지 몰랐는데~ 늦으면 누가 그냥: Loading three days early~ I didn't know why either~ guess it's 'cause I felt someone might just leave if I was late~
Nobody here just leaves. If you're late, I'll be waiting.
Doing it early is easier, right?
사흘이나 두면 짐 상하지 않아?: Doesn't the cargo go bad, sitting three whole days?
네가 기다리고 있으면~ 하루쯤은 늦게 실어 볼까~: If you'll be waiting~ maybe I'll load a day late, just once~
편하긴 해~ 근데 편해서 시작한 건 아닌 것 같아~: It is easier~ but I don't think that's why I started~
합금은 안 상해~ 기다림이 조금 익을 뿐이야~: Alloy doesn't go bad~ the waiting just ripens a little~
너는 흥얼거리는 노래 있어~? 하나 알려 줘~ 첫 소절만이라도~: Do you have a song you hum~? Teach me one~ even just the first line~
I do. One where the words are gone and only the tune's left. I'll hum it just for you.
방송 틀어 줄까?: Want me to put something on the PA?
가락만 남은 거 좋아~ 가사는 원래 금방 날아가거든~: I like ones with only the tune left~ words always fly off fast anyway~
그럼 입만 움직여 봐~ 소리 없어도 나한텐 들려~: Then just move your lips~ even with no sound, I can hear it~
방송은 남의 노래잖아~ 난 네 거가 듣고 싶었는데~: The PA's someone else's song~ I wanted to hear yours~
가끔 첫 소절을 부르면~ 뒤에서 누가 같이 부르는 것 같아~ 돌아보면 아: Sometimes when I sing the first line~ it feels like someone behind me is singing along~ but when I turn around, nobody's there~
Whoever that voice is, right now it carries on in yours.
녹음해서 들어 볼까?: Want to record it and listen?
이어지고 있구나~ 그럼 그 목소리한테도 안부 하나 실어 둘래~: It's carrying on~ then I'll load a little hello for that voice too~
기분이어도 좋아~ 혼자 부를 때보다 덜 조용하거든~: Even if it's just a feeling, that's fine~ it's less quiet than singing alone~
녹음하면~ 내 목소리만 남을까 봐 무서워~: If we record it~ I'm scared only my voice will be left~
베라 씨와 두고 온 컨테이너를 가지러 갑니다. 값은 안 나가는 물건입니다: I am going with Vera to retrieve a container we left behind. It is worth nothing. Do you find that strange?
Worth nothing or not, if someone left it behind, you're the one who goes back for it.
Just go easy on the fuel.
그 컨테이너 팔 수는 있어?: Can you even sell that container?
If that is the kind of person I am, my losses are great. I will go all the same.
I will conserve it. On the way there only. On the way back, the load is heavy.
The one going with me says it is the kind that cannot be sold.
You have never asked why I attach tags. Are you not curious?

팔려고 그러는 거 아냐?: Isn't it so you can sell things?
…I will write that on the back of the tag. The front is the price box.

I have never once sold one. I haggle, but I do not hand things over.
값을 매기지 않으면 손이 비는 것 같습니다. 지휘관님은 빈손일 때 무엇을: When I am not pricing something, my hands feel empty. What do you do with empty hands, Commander?

Ready to receive. …I will start by practicing keeping my hands open.

I always lose to you. But it never feels like a loss.

If it is a hassle, leave it to me. I will haggle for your share in your place, Commander.

로카가 금고 번호를 오늘 또 바꿨어! 근데 내 칸은 안 잠가 줘. 왜게?: Rocca changed the vault code again today! But she doesn't lock my compartment. Guess why?

띄울 거니까! 그럼 내 칸 문은 늘 열어 둘래. 돛 펴듯이!: 'Cause they're for floating! Then I'll keep my compartment door open all the time. Like spreading a sail!
금고지기는 깜빡 안 해. 하품은 해도!: The vault keeper doesn't forget. She yawns, sure!
잠그면 뗏목이 숨 막히잖아. 물결도 못 들어오고!: If it's locked, the rafts can't breathe. And the waves can't get in!
고물 집기 전에 똑똑 두 번 하는 거, 대답 들으려고 하는 거다? 근데: The knock-knock twice before I pick up junk—that's me listening for an answer, y'know? But nothing's ever answered yet.
Even without an answer, you fish it out. Next time I'll listen with you.
같이 들으면 귀가 넷! 작은 대답도 잡힌다!: Listening together makes four ears! We'll catch even a tiny answer!
Junk does answer. By floating! Even if it makes no sound.
Knock hard and it'll get scared and sink! Two soft ones is the rule.
내 선단 다 모이면 첫 항해 할 거야! 어디로 갈지 같이 정해 줄래?: When my whole flotilla's together, we're going on our first voyage! Will you help pick where to go?

Where are you going on a raft?
Buoys! Mark them for me. Then nobody gets lost.
멀리 안 가! 네 배 보이는 데까지만. 그 정도는 괜찮지?: Not far! Just as far as I can still see your ship. That's okay, right?
뗏목은 어디든 가! 대신 천천히. 엄청 천천히!: A raft goes anywhere! Just slowly. Super slowly!
난 뗏목이랑 이 배에 한 줄씩 묶여 있어! 너는 어디에 묶여 있어?: I'm tied by one line to my raft and one to this ship! What are you tied to?
One line, to your ship. And you're the one who tied it.
Spaceships dock. They don't get tied.
내가 묶었다! 그럼 안 풀리게 매일 확인할게!: I tied it! Then I'll check it every day so it doesn't come loose!
아무 데도? 그럼 둥실이네. 좀 무섭고, 좀 좋지?: To nothing? Then you're just floating along. A little scary, a little nice, right?
도킹도 묶는 거야! 이름만 어려운 거지!: Docking is tying too! It just has a fancy name!
소냐 선배가 상자에서 나온 순서로는 자기가 먼저래요. 그럼 저는 둘째일까: Sonya says that by the order we came out of the crates, she was first. Then am I second?
So what if you're second. It's good to have someone who came from the same place.
Ask her to call you by name, not by crate.
The same place… Then second is fine. It is right behind Sonya.
안 중요하면… 앞으로는 선배 옆에 나란히 서 볼까요?: If it does not matter… may I try standing side by side with Sonya from now on?
선배는 저를 꼬마라고 불러요. 이 키에요. 그냥 둘까요?: Sonya calls me "little one." At this height. Is it all right to just let it be?
작은 것도 두 손으로 드는 거요… 예전에 한 손으로 들다 뭘 부숴서 그런: The way I lift even small things with both hands… could it be because I once broke something lifting it one-handed? I do not remember, though.

Someone who takes care… I will accept those words with both hands. Since they are small.
습관이라면… 누구한테서 온 습관일까요?: If it is a habit… whose habit did it come from, I wonder?
It is faster… But one hand still scares me. I do not know why.
지휘관님, 손바닥 한 번만 대 봐 주실래요? 제 손이랑요. 크기를 알고: Commander, may I put my palm against yours, just once? There is a size I want to know.
Here. I won't ask what you're measuring.
Your hand size is on record in the medbay.
안 물어 주셔서… 다행이에요. 지휘관님 손이 더 작네요, 그렇죠?: I am glad… you did not ask. Your hand is smaller, Commander, is it not?
No reason… I only wanted to see if my hands are really my size.
기록 말고 따뜻한 쪽으로 재고 싶었어요. 안 될까요?: I wanted to measure the warm way, not by the records. May I not?
When you first saw me, Commander, what did you notice first? Besides my height.
Your voice, asking. I heard that before I took in your size.
All I could see was your height.
목소리가 먼저였다니… 그럼 앞으로 더 많이 물어볼까요?: My voice came first… Then may I ask you more things from now on?
It is actually better that you do not remember. I was a little embarrassed at first.
키가 먼저죠… (웃는다) 다음엔 키 말고 하나만 더 찾아 주실래요?: Height first, of course… (laughs) Next time, may I ask you to find just one more thing besides my height?
있잖아… 가비 말이야. 내 쪽지를 하나도 안 놓치면서, 그 얘긴 어디서도: Psst… about Gabi. She doesn't miss a single one of my notes, but she never mentions them anywhere, they say. That chatterbox…
가비가 근무 끝나고 쏟아내는 말에 네 쪽지 얘기만 쏙 빠져 있더라. 그게: When Gabi pours everything out after her shift, your notes are the one thing missing. That's her reply.

가비 입에 테이프 하나 더 붙여 줄까?: Want me to put another strip of tape over Gabi's mouth?
So it was a reply… then I'll write her a note too.
It's fine, but… I don't know where to hide a thank-you.
She says the tape's only for shifts… after, she talks till your ears hurt.
루바 방송 사이에 쪽지 끼우는 거… 걔도 알 거야. 근데 한 번도 안 물: The notes I slip between Lyuba's broadcasts… she must know. But she's never once asked. Why, I wonder…
She leaves room between the melodies. Just enough for your notes.
She's probably too busy to notice.
Ask her for your own airtime.
Leaving room… then my next note gets a line just for her.
Pretending not to know can't be that precise… the timing's always exact.
On my own, everyone would hear… it's only a secret when it's mixed in.
너는… 꼭 전하고 싶은데 못 전한 말 있어?: And you… is there something you really wanted to tell someone, but couldn't?
I do. I haven't decided who gets it, so I still carry it around. Like you.
If I had any, I'd just mail it.
Just carrying it gets heavy… I'll hold half until you find who it's for.
None… then your pockets have plenty of room for my notes.
There's no mail on this ship… that's why I'm here.
I dreamed of a mailbox… it had a slot to put things in, but no door to take them out.
Maybe the one who takes them out just hasn't come yet. Take me along in the next dream.
You could've pried off the back panel.
If I take you… you look for the door. I'll press my ear to it.
It was a dream, but it smelled of paper… a smell with noise mixed in.
I tried, but my hand wouldn't move… it felt like someone else's mailbox.
아가타가 요즘 나한테 안개 좀 내 달래~ 맞수라면서 왜 나한테 부탁하나~: Agata keeps asking me to put out some fog lately~ she calls me her rival, so why ask me~?
Some favors you only ask a rival. She trusts your fog.
믿는다고~? 그럼 진하게 내 줘야지~ 또 소리 지르겠다~: Trusts it~? Then I'll make it thick~ she'll be yelling again~
해 주긴 하는데~ 진하게? 옅게? 그게 늘 헷갈려~: I do it for her~ but thick? Thin? I always mix that up~
놀리는 거면 좋겠다~ 그럼 마음 놓고 흘리지~: Hope she is teasing~ then I can let it drift without worrying~
가비가 근무 중에 테이프 붙인 채로 나한테 뭐라고 웅얼댔어~ 이번엔 또: Gabi mumbled something at me on shift with the tape still on~ is she mad again this time~?

붙인 채면 부탁이구나~ 오늘은 방벽 피해서 흘릴게~: Tape on means a favor~ today I'll drift it around the barrier~
웅얼웅얼이었어~ 반은 안개가 먹었나 봐~: Just mumble-mumble~ guess the fog ate half of it~
떼 주려다 손이 젖어서~ 테이프가 더 안 떨어지더라~: I tried, but my hands were damp~ so the tape stuck even worse~
안개 샐 때~ 아주 낮게 웅 하는 소리 나는 거~ 너도 들려~?: When the fog leaks~ there's a really low hum~ can you hear it too~?
If I stay still, I think I could. Next time it leaks, I'll listen with you.
옆에서~? 그럼 일부러 조금 새게 둬야겠다~ 아, 이건 비밀~: Right beside me~? Then I'll let a little leak on purpose~ oh, that part's a secret~
엔진은 저쪽 끝이야~ 이건 안개 속에서만 나던데~: The engines are way at the other end~ this only shows up inside the fog~
귀는 멀쩡하대~ 안개 걷히면 소리도 같이 사라지더라~: They say my ears are fine~ when the fog clears, the sound goes with it~
안개를 마음대로 거두게 되면~ 너는 맑은 날의 나랑 흐린 날의 나 중에: If I could pull the fog back whenever I liked~ which would you like better, clear-day me or cloudy-day me~?
The you who gets to choose. I like the days you decide whether it's clear or cloudy.
Clear days. The radar's easier to read.
내가 정하는 날~ 오긴 하나~ 오면 첫날은 반만 흐릴래~: A day I decide~ will it even come~? If it does, the first day I'll be half-cloudy~
둘 다 나라고~? 그럼 오늘은 흐린 쪽으로 있을게~ 편하거든~: Both are me~? Then today I'll stay on the cloudy side~ it's comfier~
레이더 보는 애들은 좋아하겠다~ 나는 좀 심심할 것 같고~: The radar girls would love that~ I'd get kinda bored, though~
아가타가 반사 속 번호를 공책에 빠짐없이 남겨 둔대요. 제 얼굴은 한 번: Agata records every number in my reflection in her notebook, I hear. Yet she has never once drawn my face.
What she keeps is also a record that you stood there in front of it.
A record of my standing there… Then next time I shall stand there even more beautifully for her.
Observer or not, I would like her to look at my face a little. She looks only at the number.
If I kept records, I would draw a face beside the number first. Even a clumsy one.
레이더 화면 닦는다는 거, 반은 핑계예요. 호호. 나머지 반은 뭘 보러: Wiping the radar screens is half an excuse, you see. Oh-ho-ho. Do you know what the other half is for?
You go to see whether the you reflected there is still there.
Because the screen's dirty, I'd guess.
You have caught me. I only feel at ease after looking several times a day, you see.
Dust is the loveliest of all excuses, is it not?
If I did, I would have no reason to slip in and out. That would not do.
Commander, what do you check first in front of a mirror? I find myself looking for the number first.
Whether I'm smiling. Look for that first too, instead of the number.
Whether I am smiling… Tomorrow, before wiping the screen, I shall check the corners of my mouth first.
A glance? Then yours is a face that can afford it. How enviable.
If it is your hair, I shall tend to it for you. I always carry a comb.
어느 날 반사 속 번호가 제 것으로 바뀌면, 그다음엔 무얼 보며 살까요?: If one day the number in the reflection became my own, what would I live looking at after that?
