You'd live the same as now.
People's faces… Less even than a reflection, perhaps, but warmer, surely.
The same as now… that is a little sad, and yet a relief. I will keep wiping the screens.
I wish it were not, too. And yet my eyes keep drifting toward it.
칸 짝이 못 자는 밤이 많아! 그래서 무음 방송을 트는데, 소리 없는 방: My bunkmate has a lot of sleepless nights! So I run a silent broadcast—a broadcast with no sound still counts as on air, right?
It does. If even one person's listening, it's a broadcast. She's listening.
Why not just turn it off?
듣고 있었구나! 오늘 밤 무음 특집, 청취자 한 명 확정!: She was listening! Tonight's silent special: one listener confirmed!
끄면 둘 다 천장만 보고 누워 있어! 켜 두는 게 나아!: If I turn it off, we both just lie there staring at the ceiling! Better to stay on air!
자장가 틀었다가 그 애가 박자 세느라 더 깼어!: I played a lullaby and she stayed up even longer counting the beat!
이름 없는 신청곡이 꼭 같은 시각에 와! 조명이 주황으로 바뀔 때! 그: A nameless request always comes in at the same time! When the lights turn orange! What's the story behind that hour?
Let the story wait until she tells it. You just play it right on time.
Lots of people must be listening at that hour.
사연은 비워 두고 곡만 꽉 채운다! 주황 시각 고정 코너 개설!: Story left blank, tracks packed full! Launching a regular orange-hour segment!
많긴 해! 근데 이름 안 쓰는 건 딱 한 분이야!: There are a lot! But only one never signs a name!
묻는 순간 신청이 끊길걸! 이름 없는 게 그 애 사연이야!: The moment I ask, the requests would stop! Being nameless is her story!
오늘 첫 곡은 네 머릿속에 도는 노래로 할래! 흥얼거려 봐, 박자는 내가: Today's first track is whatever song's going around in your head! Hum it—I'll match the beat!
I can't pick just one. It changes every time I hear your show.
매번 바뀐다고? 그럼 내 방송이 네 머릿속 국장이다!: Changes every time? Then my show is the station manager in your head!
비어 있으면 내가 하나 심어 둘게! 오늘 밤 방송 잘 들어!: If it's empty, I'll plant one in there! Tune in tonight!
음치 환영! 박자만 맞으면 그것도 노래야!: Tone-deaf welcome! If the beat's right, that's a song too!
가락이 들어오기 직전엔 꼭 귀가 먼저 간지러워! 어디서 오는지는 몰라도: Right before a melody comes in, my ears always tickle first! I don't know where it's from, but I can tell it's at the door.
Then say hello first. Whatever's coming in might be glad too.
If it scares you, take a break from broadcasting.
인사부터! 그거 방송 예절이지. 오늘 첫마디는 어서 와로 간다!: Greetings first! That's on-air manners. Today's opening line is "Welcome in!"
It tickles even with it off! This isn't an equipment problem.
If I go off air, whatever's at the door has nowhere to go! Taking it in is my job.
점 그림이 쌓여서 둘 데가 없네. 네 방 벽 한 칸, 빌려줄 수 있네?: The dot drawings have piled up. Nowhere to put them. Could you spare a patch of your wall?
Bring them. I'll put them up where they're easiest to see.
Where they're easiest to see… then I'll pick the faintest one, actually.
One or two makes it hard to choose. They all look alike, huh.
Files don't keep the dots. The ones pressed into paper are the real ones.
아가타가 내 점 그림에 이론을 붙이네. 벌써 세 장째네. 그거 다 읽어: Oh, Agata's pinning theories on my dot drawings. Three pages already. Am I supposed to read all that.
읽어 줘. 네가 본 걸 그 애가 이어 쓰는 거니까. 둘이 같이 보는 셈이: Read them. She's continuing what you saw. It's like the two of you looking together.
Continuing it… then the fourth page gets my drawing attached.
If I don't, my drawing will be left off the next page. I'd kind of hate that, actually.
No idea if it's right. But she draws her lines the same direction I do.
So you saw something only you saw, too? Something nobody believed.
I did. It's fine if I don't talk about it now. Beside your screen, I think of it less.
Then someday draw that story in dots too. I'll recognize it.
Not remembering is nice too. Mine's too clear—that's the trouble, actually.
Being believed by everyone must be easy. One person was enough for me.
그 윤곽을 화면 밖에서 보는 날이 오면… 옆에 있어 줄래?: If the day comes when I see that outline outside the screen… will you be beside me?
I will. You'll recognize it first, so I'll just be beside you, holding your hand.
Let's check it on radar first.
Just holding hands… then I still have one hand for the screen. That works.
I hope it doesn't come. Half of me might be hoping it does, though.
Oh, radar doesn't pick it up. That's always the strange part.
I handed my teacher a rewritten toast. This time, no scolding came back—only laughter. What was lacking.
모자란 게 아니라 너무 무거웠겠지. 살아 있는 사람한텐 가벼운 말이 더: Not lacking—probably too heavy. For the living, light words stay longer.
웃었으면 된 거 아냐?: If she laughed, isn't that enough?
Light words. The rarest thing in my sentences. I will practice.
I have already rewritten it seven times. The eighth, I will write short.
I have taken that laughter down in writing. It will be the first line of my next piece.
첫 축사를 끝까지 들어 준 이는 하나였다. 그 뒤로 쓰는 글마다 그 귀를: Only one listened to my first toast to the end. Since then, with every piece I write, I recall those ears. Is that strange.
The one who listened to the end is your first reader. For a writer, that becomes the measure.
Next time, gather more people and read it.
The measure. Then my writing has always been written before a single person.
One is enough. Ears that listen to the end are rare.
Gather more, and the applause will grow. Ears that listen to the end will not.
Commander. In what words do you wish to be remembered. One line will do.
Someone who laughed along. That'll do.
Write it long. Mostly about what I did.
Someone who laughed along. Short and light. I will begin practicing now.
Even so, I will write it. The writing is my part.
Write it long, and no one reads to the end. Short, and complete.
If a day comes when I write neither eulogy nor toast, what do I do that day.
Nothing. Let's sit together and talk about the weather instead of names.
I'll think about that when it comes.
You'll probably be writing something that day too.
The weather needs no eulogy. A good companion. I will find us a place to sit.
Putting it off is a kindness too. Until that day, I will keep hold of my pen.
I cannot deny it. I do not know how to rest. I am looking for one who will teach me.
I once put someone to sleep. The patient thanked me on waking. Words I never hear when I press.
The hand that presses and the hand that brings sleep are both yours. The thanks just come later.
Then just put people to sleep from now on.
Words that come later. Then I will add waiting to the prescription.
I have no finding yet on whether it went well. My hands were awkward.
Bringing sleep is not my prescription. That day, it was a borrowed hand, just once.
Everyone comes to my room only when in pain. When they are not, they take the long way around the corridor. A strange symptom.
It means you're the one they look for when it hurts. That's how much they trust you.
Maybe if you spoke a bit more gently, they'd take fewer detours.
They detour because they trust me. That is a first finding. I will note it in the chart.
Symptoms dismissed as "just how it is" last the longest.
Gentle words heal slowly. A longer corridor is the better outcome.
손등에 멍이 들었습니다. 언제 부딪혔는지 모르겠습니다. 이런 진단은 처음: There is a bruise on the back of my hand. I do not know when I struck it. A first diagnosis for me.
Even if you didn't notice, a hurt is a hurt. This time I'll take a look.
어디서 싸웠어?: Where'd you get into a fight?
Sitting in the patient's seat, I do not know where to put my hands. Examine it.
"It will fade soon." That finding is my own line. I have never been on the receiving end.
I have no memory of a fight. I am aware that is the bigger problem.
아프면 누구에게 먼저 말씀하시는지 여쭙겠습니다. 의무관으로서입니다. 아마: I will ask whom you tell first when you are in pain. As the medic. Probably.
These days, you. You notice most precisely.
Noticing is my job. Still, hearing it first is different.
If you bear it, I cannot find it. So do tell me.
Patients like that arrive last. I will open your chart in advance.
쉿… 펠트 대다가 손끝이 다 닳았어. 마지막 공구 하나, 네가 대신 대: Shh… my fingertips wore down from padding felt. The last tool—will you do it for me?
Sure. I'll put it on slowly, no sound. The way you do it.
펠트 말고 테이프 붙이면 안 돼?: Can't we use tape instead of felt?
Slowly… yeah, at that pace the tool won't wake. When you're done, I'll wrap your hands.
If it's tomorrow, this tool cries one more night… I'll wait anyway.
Tape screams when you peel it off. That's too cruel for a tool.
포마네 화분 받침에 펠트 깔아 줬어. 그 뒤로 탑에서 고함이 줄었대. 부: I laid felt under Poma's flowerpot saucers. They say there's less shouting from the tower since. Nobody asked me to, though.
You were quiet for her first, so Poma answered by lowering her voice.
The flowerpots must have liked that.
고함 안 지르면 대공은 어떻게 해?: If she doesn't shout, how does she handle anti-air?
Answering with a lowered voice… that's my favorite kind of answer.
The leaves do tremble less. Flowerpots need sleep too.
The guns fire the same. Only the voice got smaller.
눈 감으면 안쪽이 하얘. 다들 감으면 까맣다던데… 너는 무슨 색이야?: When I close my eyes, the inside is white. Everyone says it's black… what color is it for you?
Black. On the day you get to see black too, I'll turn off the light.
Rest your eyes. Too much screen time, maybe.
Be next to me that day. I don't want to see my first black alone.
Dark… explain it a little more. Slowly.
I didn't look at any screen. The white was there before… long before.
쉿… 나도 언젠가 한 번은 푹 자 보고 싶어. 그날 너는 옆에서 뭐 할: Shh… someday I want to sleep deeply, just once. What'll you do beside me that day?
Just breathing… I think that'd do it. My eyes are already heavy.
If we both sleep, who keeps watch? …Still, that's nice.
No medicine. I want to wait for sleep to come.
엘리자베타가 드디어 제 땀 무늬에 경례했어요! 근데 깃발한테 한 건지 저: Elizaveta finally saluted my stitch pattern! But was it to the flag or to me? I can't tell.
Both, probably. That flag has your hands in it now too.
I figured you'd get scolded for breaking regulations.
My hands are in it too! Then next salute, I'll take it right along with the flag.
She does, sure. But this one took her a whole day of thinking, so it lasted longer, see?
I almost did! Lucky the rulebook's got no section on stitch patterns.
오늘 꿰맬 데가 열두 군데예요. 바늘귀에 실 꿰는 것만 해 줄래요? 수다: Twelve spots to stitch today. Could you just thread the needles? I'll do all the talking.
Sure. Needles are mine, stories are yours.
You could handle that much alone.
Let's just swap in new armor plates.
I love a division of labor! Then I'll tell you all twelve stories, not one skipped.
I could. But stitching alone, I run out of chatter before I run out of thread.
Swap them and her stories get thrown out too, right? I don't want that.
이 배 장갑을 다 이으면요, 손끝만 대도 누구 자리인지 알 거예요. 그날: Once I've stitched all this ship's armor together, I'll know whose spot it is with just a fingertip. That day, want to guess in my place?
Sure. If I'm wrong, tell me her story again from the start.
From the start? It's long! Still, that day I'll tell you all of it.
It'll come. Tearing days keep coming, so stitching days keep coming too, see?
Oh my, stuck-on name tags fall off. Stitched ones don't.
Is there something you can't throw away even when it's worn, Commander? Something you keep mending? I'd love to hear about it.
There is. It's got lots of mended spots, so every time I look at it, I remember.
Not really. I'd just buy new.
네가 꿰매 준 거 말고?: Besides the ones you stitched for me?
Something that brings it back every time… I'll hear that story slowly, like winding thread.
New is nice too. But the first day it tears, call me, okay?
Those count too! But I'm telling you, I want to know about the ones before.
간식 꾸러미, 오늘은 네가 반 들어 주자! 나 혼자 들면 자꾸 걸음이 빨: Snack bundle—today you carry half, let's do it! When I carry it alone, my steps keep speeding up!
Okay. If I'm carrying it, you'll slow down to match my pace.
You could just pack fewer snacks.
천천히 걷는 것도 계획이야! 오늘은 네 걸음으로 가자!: Walking slow is part of the plan too! Today let's go at your pace!
가벼운 척하는 거야! 한번 바꿔 들어 보자!: It's only pretending to be light! Let's swap and try it!
덜 챙기면 누가 배고파! 차라리 내가 덜 먹자!: Pack less and somebody goes hungry! I'll just eat less myself!
요즘 편성 애들이 내가 말하기도 전에 먼저 앉아! 간식이 남아나질 않아!: Lately the girls in my squad sit down before I even say it! The snacks never last! Let's figure out what to do together!
They're resting the way you taught them. Tell them to save your share now.
내 몫도 남기래! 그 말 그대로 다음 출격 때 전하자!: Save my share too, huh! Let's pass that on word for word next sortie!
더 챙기면 꾸러미가 터져! 주머니를 하나 더 달자!: Pack more and the bundle bursts! Let's sew on another pocket!
못 앉게 하는 건 내가 못 해! 차라리 다 같이 앉자!: I can't stop anyone from sitting! Let's all just sit together instead!
격납고가 조용해지고 다들 멈춰 있는 시간 있잖아! 그때만 되면 나 괜히: You know when the Hangar goes quiet and everyone's standing still? Whenever that time comes, I get busy for no reason! Let's do something together!
When it gets quiet, I'll talk to you. Let's see together that it's okay to be still.
There's a lot of maintenance during that time.
같이라면… 이번엔 손 놓고 버텨 보자! 말 계속 걸어 줘!: If it's together… this time let's try holding out with our hands still! Keep talking to me!
내가 하던 말을 듣네! 이상하다! 그럼 반만 쉬어 보자!: I'm hearing my own line! Weird! Then let's try resting halfway!
그치! 정비할 거 많지! 그러니까 목록부터 길게 쓰자!: Right! Lots of maintenance! So let's start by writing a long list!
맨날 내가 쉬자고 하잖아! 가끔은 누가 나한테 해 줬으면 좋겠어! 네가: I'm always the one saying let's rest! Sometimes I wish someone would say it to me! Will you?
Let's rest. Now. I'll lay out the snacks.
If you're tired, rest on your own.
쉬는 시간표를 짜 줄까?: Want me to make you a rest schedule?
지금? 진짜로? …다리가 안 떨린다! 같이 앉자!: Now? For real? …My legs aren't shaking! Let's sit together!
알아서는 안 되더라! 그래서 부탁하는 거야!: On my own, it doesn't work! That's why I'm asking!
시간표 좋다! 근데 그거 짜는 사이에 또 내가 바빠지겠다!: A schedule, nice! But while you make it, I'll probably get busy again!
칸 나눔 점호 때 자는 쪽 이름 부르면 깨는 소녀 있음. 작게 부를지 고: Shared-berth roll call: one girl wakes when the sleeping side is called. Considering calling quietly.
Call quietly. And count what she hears in her sleep as an answer.
If she wakes, she'll fall back asleep.
Answering in sleep: received. Sleep-talk counts as present.
Confirmed through to falling back asleep. Usually quick.
Skip it and half that berth disappears. Cannot do that.
오늘 명단 김. 마지막 열 명, 지휘관이 대신 불러 줄 수 있음?: Roster long today. Last ten names: Commander able to call them instead?
I'll call them. The names that don't answer, you call. Those are yours.
Just rest. Do them all tomorrow.
점호를 좀 줄이면 안 돼?: Can't you shorten the roll call a bit?
Division of roles confirmed. Unanswered side: handled here.
Order to rest: received. Resting after roll call, however.
Choosing names to cut: harder. So calling all.
다른 배 이름 부를 때 주파수 잠깐 열어 둠. 대답 들어온 일 없음. 계: Frequency left open briefly when calling other ships' names. No answer received to date. Keep it open?
Keep it open. When one comes in, I'll be beside you listening.
전력 낭비 아냐?: Isn't that a waste of power?
Seat beside secured. If that day comes, first answer heard by two.
Will do as liked. That is: keeping it open.
Power used: enough for one name. One answer and it pays off.
부르고 싶은 이름 있음? 지휘관 쪽 명단으로. 있으면 대신 불러 줄 수: Any name Commander wants called? From Commander's roster. If so, can call it in Commander's place.
There is. I can't say it yet. When I can, call it with me then.
Standing by. No deadline. Saving voice for that day.
None: received. Submit request anytime one arises.
Commander's name: called every roll call. Today, called once more.
새벽 장난 하나 짜는 중인데~ 망봐 줄 사람이 없어. 너 해 줄래?: I'm cooking up a dawn prank~ but I've got no lookout. Will you do it?
I'm in. If we get caught, I'll play dumb first.
Skip the prank and just sleep.
망꾼이 시치미까지? 이러다 내 자리 뺏기겠다~: The lookout plays dumb too? At this rate you'll steal my spot~
A sleepy lookout's fine~ Just signal me by snoring.
That's the third "go to sleep" today~ Everyone says it in the same voice.
나디아는 불 끄고 자라면서 자기도 안 자~ 불 하나 두고 누가 먼저 자나: Nadia tells me to turn off the light and sleep, but she doesn't sleep either~ We're both holding out over one light, seeing who drops first~
Then you both win. Thanks to it, you two are together at dawn.
Both of you go to the sickbay and ask to be put to sleep.
같이 있는 거라니… 그렇게 말하면 버티는 맛이 없잖아~: Together, huh… say it like that and holding out's no fun anymore~
자라는 사람이 또 늘었네~ 그럼 셋이서 버텨 볼까~?: Another one telling us to sleep~ Should we make it three holding out~?
재워 주는 쪽도 안 자는데~ 그 줄은 끝이 안 나~: The one who puts people to sleep doesn't sleep either~ That line never ends~
새벽만 되면 누가 와서 뭘 넘겨줄 것 같아~ 아무도 안 오는데. 이상하지: Every dawn, it feels like someone's about to come hand me something~ Nobody ever comes, though. Weird, huh~?
오늘 새벽은 내가 넘겨줄게. 받아 줄래?: This dawn, I'll hand you something. Will you take it?
누가 간식이라도 갖다주나?: Somebody bringing you snacks or something?
Got it. …Actually getting something makes my hands feel kinda awkward~ No joke.
덜 깬 거면 매일 같은 시각에 덜 깨~ 그것도 이상하지 않아?: If I'm half asleep, I'm half asleep at the same time every day~ Isn't that weird too?
간식이면 좋겠다~ 이건 손에 잡히는 게 아니라서~: Wish it were snacks~ This isn't something I can hold in my hands~
A prank that never got caught—you've got at least one too, right~? Not the ones that did.
I do. I'll tell only you. You know how to play dumb.
너 지금 나 떠보는 거지?: You're testing me right now, aren't you?
공범 됐네~ 그 비밀은 새벽에만 꺼내 보자. 둘이서만~: We're partners in crime now~ Let's only take that secret out at dawn. Just us two~
없다니 거짓말 냄새가 나~ 새벽까지 캐 볼 거야~: "Probably not" smells like a lie~ I'll dig till dawn~
떠본 거 맞아~ 근데 대답 안 해도 표정에 다 나왔어~: Yep, I was testing you~ But even without an answer, it was all over your face~
들어 봐, 내 얘기를 끝까지 듣는 사람이 이 배에 몇이나 될 것 같아?: Listen — how many people on this ship do you think hear my stories all the way through?
알리나는 끝까지 들어 주고, 에벨리나는 끝까지 따지지. 둘 다 듣는 거야: Alina listens to the end, and Evelina argues to the end. Both of them are listening.
If arguing counts as listening, my audience just doubled.
If there aren't any, I'll make some. You count as my first listener.
Keep it short and it's over before the monster even shows up.
지도에 빈칸이 하나 남았는데 그릴 얘기가 바닥났어. 네 출격 얘기 하나: There's one blank left on my map, and I'm out of stories to draw. Lend me one of your sortie stories?
Take it. Puff it up all you like, but leave the spot where I came back as it is.
You could just read the sortie reports.
I won't touch the spot where you came back. The rest… I'll add just a little.
Days when nothing happened are the best. Add one monster and suddenly something happened.
Reports have no smell, no sound. Filling that in is my job.
이번엔 네 차례야. 아무도 안 믿어 준 얘기, 너도 있어?: Listen — your turn this time. Got a story nobody believed, too?
I do. That's why I hear your stories out without laughing.
Without laughing, huh… Then someday I'll bring one out too. Start to finish, exactly as it was.
If you don't have one, want me to make one up? Starring you.
Sometimes they don't believe you even when you're not lying. That stings worse.
눈 감고 그어도 똑같이 나오는 선이 하나 있어. 다른 선은 다 삐뚤빼뚤한: You know what? There's one line that comes out the same even with my eyes closed. Every other line I draw is all wobbly.
That's the one line you didn't puff up. Let's follow it together sometime.
Try drawing it with a ruler.
Follow it together? Then when we get back, we'll each tell half the road story.
I don't remember practicing. That's what makes it weirder, I'm telling you.
With a ruler, the other lines come out straight too. This one just comes out on its own.
우주에 나가면 제가 밀라를 이끈답니다. 배 안에선 거꾸로고요. 공평한 걸: Out in space, I am the one who leads Mila, you know. Inside the ship, it is the other way around. Would you call that fair?
You've split the way between you. Neither one owes the other.
You could just memorize the paths inside the ship too.
Split between us… I shall have to hand those very words back to her at the next relay.
I suppose so. Still, I am the one who asks for directions far more often.
I have memorized them. The trouble is that the corridors do not memorize me.
복도 문을 세며 걸으면 셀 때마다 수가 다르답니다. 지휘관께서는 세면서: When I count the corridor doors as I walk, I get a different number every time. Do you count as you walk, Commander?
I don't. When you count, I'll count alongside you.
Ask Domina for the section numbers.
If two of us count, one of us is bound to be right. How reassuring.
You simply walk, and still you arrive. What an enviable talent.
I know the numbers. Where the numbers are posted is the problem.
지휘관께서는 도와 달라는 말, 쉽게 하시나요? 저는 아직 한 번도 입 밖: Commander, do you find it easy to ask for help? I have never once said it aloud.
It's hard for me too. So use your first one on me.
When I need to, I do.
Everyone helps you anyway, without being asked.
If it is my very first time, I shall give it to you, Commander. Only, I will say it very quietly.
When needed… I am always rather slow to notice that I need something.
Because they help without being asked, I find I cannot say it at all. Only my thank-yous have grown.
There is a scratch on the inside of my compass lid. Not at north, either. I have no memory of making it.
Probably the direction you looked at for a long time. Leave it; don't erase it.
If it is the direction I looked at for so long, then someday we shall trace it together with a finger.
I could not possibly replace it. Whenever I close the lid, my hand strokes that spot first.
It remained even after polishing. That one spot seems beyond even the maintenance crew's skill.
동료 이름 붙인 별이 오늘 배 그림자에 가렸어요! 그 동료한테 말해 줘야: The star I named after a crewmate got hidden in the ship's shadow today! Do I tell her?
It's just hiding for a bit. Call its name again tomorrow.
Stars get hidden sometimes. That's normal.
I'll call it tomorrow! Today I'm going to go see her face one more time!
원래 그렇대도요, 이름 붙인 별은 꼭 사람 같아서 신경 쓰여요!: Even if that's normal, a star with a name feels just like a person, so I worry!
I saw she's fine! I still went and held her hand once, in case.
카르타가 제 별 이름을 도표에 써 줬는데요, 글씨가 너무 작아요! 크게: Carta wrote my star names on the chart, but the writing is so tiny! Can I ask her to write them bigger?
Carta shows how she feels in handwriting more than words. Small, but not a single one is missing.
If you can read it, that's enough.
Not a single one is missing! I counted with a magnifying glass.
I can read it! If I press my nose to the chart. Hehe.
제 글씨는 별보다 더 흔들려요. 그래서 맡긴 거예요!: My handwriting wobbles more than the stars do. That's why I left it to her!
그 별 있잖아요, 다른 별이랑 깜박이는 박자가 달라요! 같이 세어 볼래요: You know that star? It blinks to a different beat from the others! Want to count it with me?
Let's count. You say one, I'll say two.
They all look the same to me.
One, two— and it rests there once! Did you hear? That is the beat.
똑같아 보이면 제가 손가락으로 박자 짚어 드릴게요. 하나, 둘—: If they look the same, I'll tap out the beat with my finger for you. One, two—
Even tired, I can see that star. The beat stays even with my eyes closed.
제 이름도 별에 붙여 줄 사람이 있을까요? 다들 이름은 제가 붙여 주기만: Will anyone ever put my name on a star? I'm always the one giving out the star names!
I'll do it. On the star that blinks the longest.
별 이름은 등록해야 하지 않아?: Don't star names have to be registered?
제일 오래요? 그럼 저 오늘 밤 안 자고 찾을래요!: The longest? Then I am staying up all night tonight to find it!
제 거를 제가 붙이면 좀 쑥스럽잖아요!: Naming my own would be kind of embarrassing!
You register it on the chart! Even small writing stays.
아가타는 점 하나에 이론 셋. 나는 발자국 하나에 사실 하나. 누가 맞지: Agata: one dot, three theories. Me: one footprint, one fact. Who's right.
You're both looking at the same thing. Just by different roads.
The theories are more fun, though.
The same thing, huh. Don't tell her that. She'll get smug.
Exhausting, sure. But put us together and the gaps shrink.
Fun isn't right. Sometimes it is, though. Sometimes.
One stamp. Couldn't read it. First time. …Look at it with me.
If you can't read it, it must be a ship nobody's seen before. Let's look together.
A ship never seen before. I'll write it like that. Your name beside it.
There's no next time. Stamps wear down the more they're handled.
Can't toss it. What I can't read goes in the top drawer.
What do you want to leave where you've passed. Besides footprints.
Something nobody needs to read. Word that I'll be back.
Leaving words. …Weak as evidence. I'll take it anyway.
Nothing. That kind is the hardest to read.
Carve it, and someone scrapes it off. Leave names to people.
나는 내 발자국을 안 남겨. 먼지 없는 데로만 걸어. 언제부턴지 모르겠어: I don't leave my own footprints. I only walk where there's no dust. Don't know since when.
You can leave them. Even if they're clumsy, I'll try reading them.
The cleaning crew must love that.
You'll read them. …Then I'll leave one. Don't ask the size.
It's not tidiness. I don't want to be found out. By whom, I don't know.
The crew said thanks. Nothing to thank me for.
야나가 요즘 나 때문에 밤늦게까지 버텨. 원래 불 낮아지면 조는 애인데!: Yana's been staying up late lately because of me. She's someone who dozes off when the lights go down! Am I supposed to feel sorry, or thankful?
Be grateful. She chose those nights.
She'll sleep when she wants to.
Fire a flare and she'll wake up.
Chose them! Then when the lights go down, I'll stay quietly beside her.
알아서 자긴 해. 내 어깨에 기대서. 무거워!: She does fall asleep on her own. Leaning on my shoulder. Heavy!
Waking her is easy. I still don't know how to put her to sleep.
조명탄 색은 늘 내가 골라. 오늘 하나만 네가 골라 줄래?: I always pick the flare colors. Will you pick just one today?
The color you fire most often. That one feels like you.
제일 자주 쏘는 거 알아챘구나! 그럼 그걸로 장전!: You noticed which one I fire most — so you do see me! Then that's what I'm loading!
If any color's fine, I'll go with the loudest one! If there is such a thing.
흰색은 너무 얌전해. 파티엔 안 어울린다고!: White's too well-behaved. It doesn't suit a party!
너는 다들 모여 있을 때가 편해, 혼자일 때가 편해? 나는 아직 잘 모르: Are you more comfortable when everyone's together, or when you're alone? I still can't tell.
Sometimes you feel alone even in a crowd. When that happens, I'll come stand by you.
Alone even in a crowd… I thought that was just me.
Alone's easier, huh. Then sometimes I'll just wave from far away. See me?
They don't let me fire flares in meetings. That's why I hate meetings.
불 쏘고 나면 꼭 뒤를 돌아봐. 불은 앞에 쐈는데. 이상하지?: After I fire, I always look back. Even though I fired it forward. Weird, right?
I'll watch behind you. You just look ahead.
You'll take my back? Then this time I'll try firing without looking back once.
My neck's fine! I just always look back the same way.
Nobody. But it felt like something was about to come from there.
{{루슬라나}}랑 앉아 있으면 둘 다 아무 말도 안 하는데, 그게 왜 편: When I sit with {{루슬라나}}, neither of us says a word — so why is it comfortable?
Because neither of you has to wait for an answer.
기다리지 않아도 되는 사이라… 너랑은 왜 자꾸 기다리게 되지?: Two who don't have to wait… so why do I keep waiting, with you?
할 말이 없어서라면, 왜 아무도 자리를 안 뜨지?: If there's nothing to say, why does neither of us get up and leave?
말을 걸면 비켜 갈 텐데, 그걸 또 보고 싶어지는 건 왜지?: If I talk to her, she'll sidestep it — so why do I want to see that, too?
리타가 요즘 나처럼 묻기만 하던데, 내가 잘 가르친 거야, 망친 거야?: Rita's been doing nothing but asking lately, like me. Did I teach her well, or ruin her?
She still says a star's name at the end. You've both learned.
끝엔 이름을 말한다라… 그건 나한테 없는 재주 아니야?: She says the name at the end… isn't that a knack I don't have?
알아서 하는 애가, 왜 질문 끝마다 내 쪽을 보지?: If she can figure it out, why does she look my way at the end of every question?
줄이라고 해서 줄어드는 거였으면, 내가 먼저 줄이지 않았겠어?: If being told to ask less worked, wouldn't I have cut back first?
너는 나한테 묻고 싶은 거, 아직 안 물은 게 있지 않아?: Isn't there something you want to ask me that you haven't asked yet?
There's one. How are you feeling today? As an answer, not a question.
Start by telling me your age.
기분이라… 네가 물어 주니 조금 가벼워진 것 같은데, 그건 기분일까?: My feeling… since you asked, I feel a little lighter — is that a feeling, I wonder?
없다면, 왜 아직 내 옆에 서 있지?: If there isn't, why are you still standing next to me?
나이라… 세다 보면 어디서 시작했는지부터 헷갈리지 않아?: My age… when you count, don't you lose track of where you started?
어떤 별자리는 이름보다 모양이 먼저 떠올라. 그런 건 어디서 배운 거지?: Some constellations come to me as shapes before names. Where did I learn those, I wonder?
어디서 배웠든 지금은 네 거야. 나한테도 그려 줄래?: Wherever you learned them, they're yours now. Will you draw them for me too?
It's all in the constellation books.
그려 주면, 너는 그걸 어느 쪽 하늘에 걸어 둘 거야?: If I draw them, which side of the sky will you hang them in?
어디서든이라… 그 어디가 제일 궁금한 거 아니야?: Somewhere… isn't that "where" exactly what's most curious?
책에 나온다면, 왜 나는 책을 펼친 기억이 없지?: If it's in the books, why don't I remember ever opening one?
누가 내 물건을 쥐고 웃으면, 그 웃음이 꼭 내 것 같단다. 이상하니?: When someone holds a thing of mine and smiles, that smile feels just like mine, you know. Is that strange, dear?
You gave the smile too, so nothing strange about it.
I gave the smile too… Then today was a day I gave a lot, dear.
Strange or not, I can't stop, you know. I love seeing others smile that much.
It can't be taken, so I keep on giving, dear. Even coming back empty-handed is a joy.
헬가 난롯가 말이다, 나는 거기 한 번도 안 앉아 봤단다. 앉으면 지는: Helga's fireside, dear — I've never once sat there, you know. Sitting would feel like losing.
Let's sit together. With me beside you, it's half and half.
If you get cold, I'll bring a blanket.
Half and half… yes, then I've only half lost. Sit with me, dear.
If I just sit, she'll wear a winner's face, you know. That I can't bear to see.
A blanket? You're giving first what I would have given. Just this once, I'll accept it.
What face should the one receiving make, dear? The giving face is the only one I know, you see.
The face you have now is fine. That slightly shy one.
You never get to receive anyway — you give everything.
Shy, you say… I can't bring myself to look in a mirror. Look for me, dear.
Whenever I try to say it, I think of the next thing to give, and the words break off, you know.
I give it all, so I never receive… That sounds a little lonely, dear.
네 손은 무슨 획을 잘 긋니? 곧은 거니, 굽은 거니?: What strokes is your hand good at, dear? Straight ones, or curved?
The kind I draw all the way to the end, if you ask.
획은 갑자기 왜?: Why strokes, all of a sudden?
All the way to the end… I don't yet know how to receive those words, so I'll just hold on to them.
It's fine if you can't, dear. One stroke is all it takes. Truly, just one.
I was only curious, you know. Truly, just curious. Don't look over at my shield, dear.
히폴리타가 요즘 한 합 끝나면 숨을 고르더라고요. 제가 시킨 건 아닌데요: Lately Hippolyta catches her breath after each bout. I did not tell her to. Should I praise her?
She learned it watching you wait for her. Praise, too — one a day.
One a day. Then the things to praise will last a few weeks.
Letting her grow on her own is a move too. I will just watch from beside her.
She does not need "faster." She already has more than enough of it, you see.
오늘 수가 안 떠올라요. 이런 날은 드문데요. 옆에 좀 앉아 계실래요?: Today's move will not come to me. Days like this are rare. Would you sit beside me for a while?
Sure. Even if the move won't come, the board isn't going anywhere.
내가 대신 둘까?: Want me to play it for you?
It is not going anywhere, is it. Hearing that, my hands loosen up a little.
Skipping is a move too, but today's square is too precious to leave empty.
If you play it for me, tomorrow I will be answering your move. That would be nice too.
당신 하루는 몇 수예요? 저보다 훨씬 많죠?: How many moves is your day? Far more than mine, I imagine?
Lots. But when I come here, it drops to one.
I just look at paperwork all day.
Just one move here… Then my board is where you rest.
People who do not count play the fastest, I find. No need to hurry.
Paperwork is moves too. Every page you turn takes you one square forward.
제가 첫 수를 늘 같은 칸에 두는 거, 아셨어요? 누구한테 배웠는지 생각: Did you notice I always play my first move on the same square? I cannot remember who taught me.
Let's keep that first move until you remember.
That square must be the best one.
I will keep it. On the day I remember, I will tell you first.
The best square is a different one. Even so, my hand always goes there.
I moved it once, and the board felt so unfamiliar I took the day off.
로카 금고 번호를 쪽지에 써 뒀어. 셋이나. 근데 쪽지를 어디 둘지 모르: I wrote Rocca's safe code on notes. Three of them, just in case. But I don't know where to keep the notes.
Leave one with me. I'm better than a safe.
Better than a safe, huh. Then one spare with you, two in the safe.
Even if I memorize it, it changes by tomorrow. That's why I write new ones every day.
The code inside the safe? Then it could never be opened. Ha, that's funny.
폴리나가 겹마다 다른 무늬를 놔 줬어. 이제 안 헷갈려. 근데 고맙다는: Polina stitched a different pattern on each layer. I don't mix them up now. But do I have to say thank you for all three?
Once is enough. Just wear all three patterns for a long time instead.
Forget the words — just take her a snack.
Why not just match them all to one pattern?
Wearing them long. That I'm sure of. I'll ask her for a fourth set too.
I'll pack three snacks. What if two's not enough?
With one, I'd get mixed up again. That's why all three are different.
네 짐 슬쩍 봤어. 전부 하나씩이더라. 모자라면 어떡하려고?: I peeked at your things. Just one of everything. What if it's not enough?
If it runs short, I've got you. You're my spare.
If I'm your spare, maybe I'll try packing just one. Only today.
Never? Either you were lucky, or someone's been quietly topping you up.
Borrow a spare, then. But when you give it back, add one more.
안쪽 겹 하나만 늘 따뜻해. 바깥 겹은 다 차가운데. 이상하지?: Only one inner layer is always warm. The outer ones are all cold. Weird, right?
If it's warm, that layer's protecting you. Leave it be.
It's because it's right against your body.
바깥 겹에 열선을 깔아 줄까?: Want me to line the outer layers with heating wire?
If it's protecting me… I'd better pack one more, for that layer's share.
They're all against me, but only that one's like that. I felt it three times.
With heating wire, they'd all be warm the same. Then I couldn't tell that layer apart.
맨 앞에 서면 등 뒤가 다 보이는 기분이야! 안 보이는데! 이상하지?: When I stand at the very front, it feels like I can see everything behind me! I can't, though! Weird, right?
That's because you trust who's behind you. Everyone follows your back.
It's all the noise behind you.
Strap a mirror on your back.
믿는 거라고? 그래서 한 번도 안 돌아봤구나! 이제 알았다!: Trust? So that's why I've never once looked back! Got it now!
소리? 듣고 보니 그렇네! 다들 발소리가 커!: Noise? Now that you say it, yeah! Everyone's footsteps are loud!
거울? 앞만 보고 뛰다가 다 깨먹을걸! 안 달아!: A mirror? I'd smash it charging ahead! Not doing it!
다리야가 오늘 나보다 반 걸음 먼저 나갔어! 반 걸음! 이거 내가 진 거: Darya stepped out half a step ahead of me today! Half a step! Does that mean I lost?
Half a step means you two stood side by side.
나란히? 그런 게 어딨어! …있네. 오늘은 있다!: Side by side? No such thing! …Oh, there is. Today there is!
물어보면 또 자기가 먼저래! 뻔해! 안 물어!: If I ask, she'll just say she was first again! Obviously! Not asking!
진 거면 내일 다시 하면 돼! 따라와, 연습이다!: If I lost, I'll just go again tomorrow! Follow me — practice time!
넌 왜 맨날 뒤에 있어? 원래 그런 거야? 진짜 궁금해서 묻는 거야!: Why are you always at the back? Is that just how it is? I'm asking 'cause I really want to know!
Because I like watching you up front.
좋아서? 그런 이유도 돼? 그럼 오늘은 더 멋지게 서야겠다!: Because you like it? That counts as a reason? Then today I'll stand there even cooler!
There's no "just how it is"! Stand up front once. I'll be right beside you.
무서우면 내가 앞에 있잖아! 그러라고 있는 거야!: If it scares you, I'm up front! That's what I'm there for!
나 기다리는 거 진짜 싫어하잖아. 근데 너 기다리는 건 왜 안 싫지?: You know I really hate waiting. So why don't I hate waiting for you?
Same here. Even when you run ahead, I know you'll come back.
Maybe you got used to it.
돌아오지! 꼭! 그러니까 너도 거기 그대로 있어!: Of course I come back! Always! So you stay right there too!
익숙? 나한테 그런 게 생겼다고? 큰일 났다!: Used to it? Me? That's a disaster!
If I go ahead, you won't be there. Then what's the point of the front?
해치 밑에서 본 발 얘기를 듣는 게 요즘 낙이에요. 당신 발도 나왔대요…: Lately my little joy is hearing about the feet seen from under the hatch. They say yours came up too… Would you like to hear?
Tell me. Let's compare it with what you saw.
I'll pass on the feet talk.
From below, they say your steps are half a beat slow. That is how I saw it too.
Oh — then maybe just a little about your shoes… No, never mind me. I will hold back.
Someone does, truly. Let us just say a friend of the floor.
발밑만 보고 걷다 보면 문턱에 이마를 박아요. 그럴 땐 앞 좀 봐 주실래: When I walk watching only my feet, I bump my forehead in doorways. At times like that, would you watch ahead for me?
Sure. When a doorway's coming up, I'll tell you first.
I'll have the door sills taken out.
If you tell me, I can keep my head down without worry.
If I look up, I cannot see the laces. Better my forehead takes the loss.
Then there would be nothing to catch anyone's feet, and no one would look down anymore.
당신이 아무도 모르게 하는 일도 있어요? 하나만 알려 주시면 저도 모른: Is there anything you do without anyone knowing? If you tell me just one, I will pretend not to know too.
There is. But I think you've already caught me.
Everyone seems to know whatever I do.
Me? Oh… then let us keep that between the two of us. Truly.
If you have none, I will find one for you. Slowly, starting from the floor.
That is because everyone looks from above. From below, it is different again, truly.
갑판 이음매를 밟을 땐 저도 모르게 숨을 참아요. 당신은 일부러 피해 가: When I step on a deck seam, I hold my breath without meaning to. Is there anywhere you go out of your way to avoid?
There is. But wherever you've looked first, I step without worry.
Holding your breath isn't good for you.
Without worry… Then I will step on every seam first for you.
Then someone who steps just anywhere needs someone like me close by, I think.
Oh, my body is fine. It is only my heart that tightens a little.
축하 안 하면 하루가 그냥 지나가잖아. 그냥 지나간 하루는 어디로 가는지: If you don't celebrate, the day just slips by. Know where a day that just slips by goes?
Every day you celebrated stays stuck in memory.
Stuck! That's it. That's why I can't put my glass down.
Letting it just go is a waste! I'll celebrate what you just said, too.
Records keep numbers, that's all. The laughs? Gone.
잔치 끝나면 잔 씻는 건 늘 나야. 오늘은 같이 씻을래?: When the party's over, I'm always the one washing the glasses. Wanna wash them with me today?
Sure. While we wash, let's talk about who laughed loudest today.
For that talk, I'd wash a hundred glasses! Number one is you, obviously.
Leave them and we'll be short tomorrow. Who cares — I'll just wash them myself.
Fewer?! Then I'll just use one really huge glass. Ha ha.
너는 이긴 날 중에 뭐가 제일 기억나? 진 날도 괜찮아!: Which win do you remember most? A loss is fine too!
I don't remember the wins. I remember every day we held out together.
다 기억난다고? 그럼 그날들 하나씩 다 축하해 줄게!: You remember all of them? Then I'll celebrate every one of those days!
없으면 오늘을 첫 번째로 하자. 자, 축하!: None? Then today's the first. Here — cheers!
You won! Then who lost? Let's set out one more glass.
맨 뒤에선 앞사람들 등을 하나씩 세. 끝날 때까지 몇 번이고. 너는 뭘: From the very back, I count the backs ahead of me, one by one. Over and over till it's done. What do you count?
The ones who went out, coming back. If they all make it, the day's good.
All back means it's good! Same as my way of counting. Let's count together later.
No counting needed! I'll count your share too.
Stars never end! Then the celebrating never ends either.
다리야랑 선봉 다툼할 때요, 저 한 번도 먼저 못 들어갔어요! 노크하느라: When Darya and I fight over the vanguard, I have never once gone in first! Because I am busy knocking. That means I lost, right?
Darya may get in first, but that door heard your sound first.
Skip the knock and you'd win.
제 소리를 먼저요! 그럼 저 매번 이긴 거네요. 걔한텐 비밀이에요!: My sound first! Then I have won every single time. That is a secret from her!
I lost! But she laughed, so half of it is mine.
빼면 손이 허전해서 문고리를 놓쳐요. 진짜예요!: Without it my hand feels empty and I miss the handle. It is true!
게르다가 그러는데요, 제 노크는 정보다 시끄럽대요! 그래도 열리는 건 똑: Gerda says my knocking is louder than her chisel! But it opens just the same, right?
Not the same. The chisel makes a gap; your knock calls to whoever's inside.
Then try using a chisel yourself.
부르는 거예요! 정은 벽한테, 저는 안쪽한테 하는 거죠!: It is calling! The chisel talks to the wall, and I talk to the inside!
It has to be loud to reach the inside! If I knock softly, the wall swallows it.
정은 손에 안 맞아요. 쥐면 노크가 아니라 콕콕이 돼요!: A chisel does not fit my hand. If I hold one, it is not knocking anymore — it is poke-poke!
노크 한 번에 안에서 먼저 열어 주는 문이요, 그런 문 꼭 만나 보고 싶: A door that opens from the inside after just one knock — I would really love to meet a door like that. Do you think there is one?
There is. If someone behind the door is waiting for your knock.
Then let's just take all the doors off.
Someone waiting! Then I will practice knocking even prettier.
자동문은 노크 전에 열려서 인사를 못 해요. 아쉬워요!: Automatic doors open before I knock, so I cannot say hello. What a shame!
Then there would be nothing to knock on! Walls are too hard.
지휘관은 문 열기 전에 뭐 해요? 저는 노크! 사람마다 다 다르던데요,: Commander, what do you do before opening a door? Me, I knock! Everyone does something different, and I really want to know!
I take one breath. You never know who's inside.
숨 한 번! 그럼 제 노크랑 같은 거예요. 소리만 안 날 뿐이에요!: One breath! Then it is the same as my knock. It just does not make a sound!
그냥요? 그럼 안에 있던 쪽은 깜짝 놀라겠어요!: Just like that? Then whoever is inside will jump!
열린 문엔 문틀을 두드리면 돼요. 그게 제 규칙이에요!: For an open door, I knock on the frame. That is my rule!
토베가 내 박자에 맞춰 줄을 세워. 내가 틀리면 걔 줄도 틀려. 그게 좀: Tove lines things up to my beat. If I'm off, her lines are off too. That weighs on me a bit.
Even if you're off, Tove will line them up again. It's not a beat you keep alone.
Then tell Tove to line hers up separately.
Not alone, huh. Then even an off beat, the two of us can count again.
I count so I won't be off. But sometimes my hands go first.
Line them up separately and the guns ring on two beats. I'd hate that more.
루바는 같은 가락을 두 번 못 틀어. 난 같은 박자밖에 몰라. 우리 이상: Lyuba can't play the same tune twice. I only know the same beat. We're a weird pair, right?
Your beat lays the floor, so she can wander off wherever she likes.
The floor, huh. Fine, I'll lay it. Boom, boom— she plays on top.
Being a weird pair is good. Two of the same only make one sound.
Teach her and her tune stops. Not counting is her beat.
One beat before I fire, I hold my breath. I'm not counting it, but it's always in the same spot. You know that moment too?
알아. 포대가 다 조용해지는 그 한 박. 거기 있을 때 넌 제일 편해 보: I know it. That one beat when the whole battery goes quiet. You look most at ease right there.
I looked at ease, huh. There, I don't have to count. Just that one beat.
다음에 옆에 서. 같이 참아 보자. 하나—: Stand next to me next time. Let's hold it together. One—
Holding it is how I rest. There's no sound at all in that one beat.
What do you end your day with? Without gunfire, my day doesn't end.
Your gunfire. When I hear the last shot, I think, that's today done.
It ends when I flip the calendar.
My gunfire is the end of your day, huh. I'll fire the last shot one beat late. Long.
End it with sleep and no beat is left. That feels a bit empty to me.
Calendars make no sound. Just the flip of a page — that one.
루트랑은 던지기로 얘기해. 말보다 빨라… 너도 하나 던져 볼래?: Ruth and I talk by throwing. Faster than words… want to throw one too?
Then I'll throw it low. Like you do for Ruth, easy to catch.
Low… so you saw that. If I catch it, I'll throw one back. Even lower.
없으면 빈손이라도 던지는 척해. 받는 척할게…: If you've got nothing, just pretend to throw with an empty hand. I'll pretend to catch…
말로 하면 길어져. 던지면 한 번에 끝나잖아…: Words drag on. A throw is over in one go…
출격 땐 제일 뒤가 편해… 근데 거기선 네가 안 보여. 조금 앞으로 가도: On sorties the very back is easiest… but from there I can't see you. Can I move up a little?
Come only as far as feels easy. I'll wave so you can see me from there.
그럼 선봉 서 볼래?: Then want to try the vanguard?
손 흔들면… 던지는 거 말고 흔드는 걸로 답할게. 귀찮…: If you wave… I'll answer with a wave, not a throw. Too much eff…
If it doesn't matter… I'll just go where I can see you.
선봉은 앞에 서는 애들 거야. 나는 보이는 데까지만…: The vanguard belongs to the ones who stand up front. Me, only as far as where I can see you…
출격 전에 지도 뒤집어 보는 거… 귀찮아서야. 진짜로. 근데 왜 꼭 거꾸: Flipping the map before a sortie… it's 'cause I can't be bothered. Really. But why does upside down always feel easier…
You probably want to see the picture from the far side. A habit just like you, watching from afar.
바로 보면 헷갈려서?: Because it's confusing the right way up?
You find the way by reading the map right side up.
From the far side… from there, I'd look the farthest away. That's fine too.
바로 봐도 길은 알아. 거꾸로가 숨이 편할 뿐이야…: I know the way right side up too. Upside down just lets me breathe easier…

서류면 던져도 됐잖아. 근데 걸어왔네…: Papers, you could've thrown. But you walked over…
셀라는 물건을 세고 저는 마음을 셉니다. 지휘관께서는 어느 쪽이 더 무겁: Sella counts goods, and I count feelings. Which do you consider heavier, Commander?

에바와 누가 더 멀리 던지나 겨룹니다. 이기면 셈이 기울어서 늘 한 뼘: Eva and I compete over who throws farther. If I win, the accounts tip, so I always throw one hand-span short. Is that a fair reckoning?

Give the gifts out to the keepers.

저울 없이 여쭙니다. 끝내 갚지 못한 것, 지휘관께도 있으십니까?: I ask without the scale. Is there something you were never able to repay, Commander?

데시마가 써 준 간격 종이를 접어서 늘 갖고 다녀요. 숫자뿐인데 꺼내 보: I keep the spacing note Decima wrote for me folded and always with me. It is only numbers, but when I take it out, my hands stop shaking.

그리젤이 제 줄을 보더니 반 뼘 넓대요. 재 보니 맞았어요. 그 뒤로 그: Grizel looked at my line and said it was half a hand-span too wide. I measured, and she was right. Since then, whenever I see that spot, my hand reaches for it.

언젠가 줄 안 맞추고 한 번 쏴 보고 싶어요. 그날은 옆에서 같이 봐 주: Someday I would like to fire once without lining up. Would you watch beside me that day?

Loyalty. Asked whose it was. Signe did. Couldn't answer.

의리가 꼭 누구 거여야 해?: Does loyalty have to belong to someone?

Letting it slide. Armor'll get scratched again. Can't stop that.

문 걷어찬 날. 노크하던 애랑 눈 마주쳤다. 웃었다. 왜 웃었나. 모르겠: Day I kicked the door in. Locked eyes with the one who was knocking. Laughed. Why. Don't know.

다 자란대! 속보, 지휘관 탑 등반 시작! 계단 몇 개게?: They all grow, she says! Breaking news: the Commander begins the tower climb! Guess how many stairs?

경보 버튼, 탑에서 계단 서른 개 아래야. 위에도 달아 줘!: The alarm button's thirty stairs down from the top of the tower. Put one up here too!

녹이고 나면 어느 배 것이었는지 아무도 몰라요. 그래서 그 전에 혀에 담: Once it is melted, no one can tell which ship it came from. So I keep it on my tongue before that. Is that strange?

Safe, but so boring you'd rust, right? The parts and me both.
이베트는 내 회전자만 보면 손을 내저어! 근데 제작대에 몰래 하나 달아: Yvette waves me off the second she sees one of my rotors! But I snuck one onto the workbench, hehe. When'll she notice?

Sneak one onto something of mine too.
안 떼면! 그럼 하나 더 달아도 되는 거지?: If she doesn't! Then I can add one more, right?
그럼 대놓고 달까? 아냐, 몰래가 더 신나!: Should I put it on openly, then? Nah, sneaking's way more fun!
어디에? 의자에? 와, 돌아가는 의자다!: Where? Your chair? Whoa, a spinning chair!
모든 배 지휘관이 하나씩 쓰는 발명을 만들 거야. 근데 너부터 써 줘야: I'm gonna make an invention every ship's commander uses. But you're my first user, okay? What's a hassle for you?

그럼 귀찮아질 때까지 기다릴게. 오래는 못 기다려!: Then I'll wait till something gets annoying. I can't wait long, though!
없는 거? 그건 발명이 아니라 그냥 물건이잖아!: Without one? That's not an invention, that's just a thing!
언젠가 회전자 하나 없이도 다들 와! 하는 걸 만들 거야. 근데 그게 뭔: Someday I'm gonna make something that makes everyone go "whoa!" without a single rotor. I just don't know what it is yet!
Whatever you make, if you're excited first, everyone goes "whoa."
그런 게 있겠어?: Does a thing like that even exist?
Just put a rotor on it.
내가 먼저? 그럼 벌써 반은 만든 거네! 위잉!: Me first? Then it's already half built! Whirrr!
있어! 없으면 내가 처음 만들면 되지!: It does! And if it doesn't, I'll just be the first to make it!
그치, 결국 손이 회전자로 가. 이번만 참아 볼게!: Right, my hands always end up on a rotor. Just this once, I'll hold back!
한 방울씩 덜어 쓰는 버릇 말이다. 처음 합성한 연료가 딱 한 컵이었단다: About my habit of measuring out one drop at a time. The first fuel I ever synthesized was just one cup, you know. How could I spend that carelessly?

알리나가 남는 냉각수를 또 들고 왔구나. 받기만 하니 빚진 것 같은데,: Alina brought over her spare coolant again. Taking and only taking feels like a debt. What should I give back, hm?
Share a little of something you've been saving. That's the biggest thanks there is.
Just give her a drum of fuel.
Share what I've been saving… It stings, but I suppose that's right.
If I just take it, the sums won't balance at night and I can't sleep.
A whole drum? For a scoop of coolant, that's too much, child.
탱크가 꼭대기까지 찬 날을 하루라도 보고 싶구나. 그날은 아무도 내보내지: I'd like to see the tank full to the brim, even for a single day. Would you send no one out that day?
Nobody goes out that day. Let's look at the full tank together.
When it's full, it's there to be used.
Look at it together… Then that day, I'll set down my dropper too.
Who doesn't know it's there to be used? I only want to look at it for one day.
Build it bigger and the empty part gets bigger too. There's no end to it.
너 끼니는 챙기니? 남의 연료는 한 방울까지 재면서, 네 배 속은 안 재: Are you eating properly? I measure everyone's fuel down to the drop, and never once measured what's in your belly.

Then from today your meals go in the ledger too. One spoonful at a time.
"Whatever," child? That's not measuring out—that's throwing away.
Good grief, what are you saying! That's for ships to drink.
내가 전력 덕이라고 떠드는 이유 말이다! 계기판은 말을 못 하잖아. 그러: As for why I keep crowing that it's all thanks to my power! The gauges can't talk, you see. So I do the talking for them!
Even if nobody notices, the needle went up. And you're the witness.
Put a speaker on the gauges.
증인! 그래, 이 배 전력의 증인이다! 기록해 둬라!: A witness! Yes, the witness to this ship's power! Write that down!
자랑 맞다! 근거 있는 자랑이다, 보라고!: It is bragging! Bragging with evidence—behold!
스피커! 그럼 바늘 오를 때마다 내 목소리가 나오게 하지!: A speaker! Then every time the needle rises, out comes my voice!
가비는 내 강연을 한 번도 안 끊는 귀한 표본이다! 너는 몇 분이나 버티: Gabi is a rare specimen who has never once interrupted my lectures! How many minutes can you last?

요점만 말해 주면 안 돼?: Can't you just give me the main point?
과정이라니! 그럼 서론만 한 시간이다, 앉아라!: The process! Then the introduction alone is an hour—sit!
오 분이면 서론도 안 끝난다. 일단 앉아라!: Five minutes won't even finish the introduction. Sit down for now!
요점부터 말하면 멋이 없다! 결론은 늘 맨 끝이다!: Leading with the point has no flair! The conclusion always comes at the very end!
다들 나를 기관장이라고만 부른다! 나는 실험가인데. 너는 뭐라고 부를 거: Everyone just calls me the chief engineer! I'm an experimenter. What will you call me?

박사님…! 방금 그거 기록해 둬야겠다. 다시 한 번!: Doctor…! I must record that just now. Once more!
기관장도 틀린 건 아니다. 마음은 실험실에 있지만!: Chief engineer isn't wrong, either. Though my heart is in the lab!
자격증? 내 계기판 바늘이 곧 자격증이다!: A license? My gauge needles are my license!
내 실험이 전부 틀린 걸로 끝나도, 그래도 들으러 올 거냐?: Even if all my experiments end up wrong, will you still come to listen?
I will. Even when you're wrong, I like hearing you get excited.

틀린 실험은 왜 해?: Why run experiments that are wrong?
신나서라니… 그럼 틀린 날엔 더 크게 떠들어 주지!: Excited, you say… Then on the wrong days, I'll talk even louder!
다시 하면 된다, 맞다! 실패는 다음 실험의 재료다!: Do it again—exactly! Failure is material for the next experiment!
틀린 걸 알아야 맞는 데로 간다. 그게 학문이다!: You have to know what's wrong to get to what's right. That's scholarship, you see!
One stamp, and receiving it becomes a record. No stamp, and it never happened.

"Keeping a record." Not on the form. I'll accept it.

The crate stays. Only the proof that a sender existed goes.
베라가 맡긴 매듭. 아직 봉투째 내 서랍에 있어. 돌려줄지, 판단 보류: The knot Vera left with me. Still in my drawer, envelope and all. Return it or not: decision pending.
Vera left it with you, so you holding onto it is right.
Untie the knot and use it.
Processed as "right." Envelope stays in the top drawer.

Untying it is outside my authority. What's entrusted stays as entrusted.
네가 나한테 상자를 보낸다면. 서류엔 뭐라고 쓸 거야?: Say you sent me a crate. What would you write on the form?

A number is enough. I'll leave the name field open anyway.

너 올 때마다 기록해. 서식에 없는 칸에. 몇 번째인지 알려 줄까?: I log every time you come. In a field that's not on the form. Want to know the count?
Don't tell me. I'll come again and add one more line.
"Do not disclose," processed. Lines to keep increasing.
Classified. Fields not on the form aren't disclosed.
Why pegs? A weld, once it's on, that's it. A peg you pull and fit again. That's better.
So you leave room to redo it if it's wrong.
That's right. No hand fits it right the first time.
Sturdy, sure. So it stays wrong a long time.
Mix them and both are half-done. Pick one.
마고랑 수리 순서로 또 붙었다. 저녁마다 그렇다. 근데 안 붙는 날은 손: Got into it with Margot over the repair order again. Every evening. But on days we don't, my hands won't loosen up.

다른 도크로 옮겨 볼래?: Want to try moving to another dock?

Move where? Every peg here, I drove in myself.

Bring them. No line. I'll look right away.

What goes unused breaks fastest. Tools and people both.
소냐 칸은 지금도 안 나눠요. 퍼즐에 빈 데가 남는 거, 저 원래 못 참: I still do not split Sonya's slot. And I normally cannot stand leaving a gap in a puzzle.

작게 칠하는 건 칸을 반 자르는 거래요. 그건 저도 못 해요!: She says painting it smaller is cutting the slot in half. Even I cannot do that!

같이요? 그럼 칸을 하나 더 맞춰야겠어요. 지금 당장!: Together? Then I have to fit one more slot. Right now!

내 칸이랑 바꿀래?: Want to trade with my slot?

남는 칸이 없어서 하는 말이었어요. 하하…: I only said it because there are no slots left over. Ha ha…
바꾸면 또 나누게 될걸요? 저 그런 사람이에요!: If we trade, I will just end up splitting it again! That is the kind of person I am!

세게 불었더니 걔가 박자 맞춰 들어오더라. 더 신나서!: I blew harder and she came in right on the beat. Even more pumped!

안 세도 돼. 내가 세고 있었거든. 넌 어제보다 일찍 왔다!: You don't have to. I've been counting. You came earlier than yesterday!

호루라기 박자는 아무도 안 가르쳐 줬는데 처음부터 알았어. 그거 좀 신기: Nobody taught me the whistle's rhythm, but I knew it from the start. Isn't that kinda strange?

판돈은 돌려줬어?: Did you give the stakes back?

Her fault? No, no~ I should have taken bets on her being late too. My math fell short.
카산드라 씨는 제 판에서 늘 져요. 그래도 매번 걸어요. 이번 판, 그분: Cassandra always loses at my table. She bets every time anyway. This round—care to bet on her side with her?
Sure. The losing side could use one more backer.
I'll just watch from outside the game.
그럼 배당이 또 달라지는데요? 공정하게 다시 셈할게요~: Then the odds change again, you know? I will recalculate, fair and square~
The winning side pays stingy~ I will take it anyway, heh heh.
구경꾼 자리는 공짜예요. 표정만 잘 감추시고요~: Spectator seats are free. Just keep a straight face~
지휘관님한테 배당을 매겨 보려는데요, 도통 셈이 안 서요. 다음에 뭘 하: I have been trying to put odds on you, Commander, but I cannot work them out at all. Would you let slip just one thing you will do next?

If even you do not know, the odds go sky-high~ Heh heh.
주사위한테 맡기시면 제 일이 없어지잖아요~: Leave it to dice and I am out of a job~
판돈은 늘 공정하게 받아요. 근데 지휘관님 앞에선 자꾸 덤을 얹고 싶어져: I always take stakes fairly. But around you, Commander, I keep wanting to throw in a little extra. Is that fair?
If you're agonizing over even the extra, your table's fair.
그 말씀은 배당표 밖에 둘게요. 판 밖 얘기니까요~: I will keep those words off the odds sheet. That is talk from outside the game~
좋으시죠? 그래서 문제예요. 셈이 자꾸 틀려요~: Fine by you, is it? That is the problem. My math keeps going wrong~

군힐드가 내 박자가 반 박 늦대. 고참한테 말이야. 근데 그 뒤로 귀가: Gunhild says my timing's half a beat late. To a veteran, mind you. But since then my ears keep counting her beat, I tell you.

남의 포라도 봐야 눈이 안 무뎌진다고. 품평은 그래서 하는 거야. 너 보: You've got to watch other people's guns, or your eye goes dull. That's why I critique. How does my eye look to you?

Hmph, light up. …Guess next time I'll critique in front of a mirror.
None? For a veteran, that's the hardest critique of all.
Small? Hey, that's because raids are rare. No reason to make it bigger.
고참 소리 듣는 거 말이야, 사실 몇 번째로 왔는지도 잘 몰라. 제일 시: About being called the veteran—honestly, I don't even know what number I arrived. I just became the veteran by being the loudest.

Then be the baby from today.

The baby? Hey, then who's doing the critiquing?
무리가 오기 전엔 잎이 먼저 바짝 서요. 그래서 저는 하늘보다 잎을 먼저: Before a swarm comes, the leaves stand up stiff first. So I watch the leaves before the sky~ Do you believe me?

레이더 보는 게 낫지 않아?: Wouldn't watching the radar be better?
매일 보니까요~ 잎도 저를 매일 보고요!: Because I look every day~ And the leaves look at me every day too!
우연이 매번이면 그건 버릇이에요~: If chance happens every time, that's a habit~
레이더는 탑에 없어요! 잎은 있고요~: There's no radar on the tower! But there are leaves~
고함을 지르고 나면 목보다 잎이 먼저 걱정돼요. 지휘관님, 제 고함 많이: After I've been shouting, I worry about the leaves before my throat. Commander, is my shouting really that scary?
It's fine if it's scary. It's the sound you make when you're protecting us.
Move the pots somewhere they can't hear.
지킬 때 내는 소리… 잎한테도 그렇게 말해 줄게요~: The sound I make when protecting… I'll tell the leaves that too~
시끄러운 건 인정이에요. 그래도 잎은 참아 줘요~: I'll admit it's loud. Still, the leaves bear with me~
If I move them, the leaves can't see the sky the swarms come from. I don't want that.
My wish is to make one flower bloom out in space. Please don't laugh~ I mean it.
Not laughing. In front of your pots, you're the most serious one here.
You caught me being serious~ The day it blooms, I'll sing instead of shouting.
언젠간이 제일 어려워요. 흙 만지다 보면 알게 돼요~: "Someday" is the hardest part. You'll understand once you've had your hands in the soil~
불꽃이요? 기관포도 꽃처럼 터지긴 하는데… 그건 안 예뻐요!: Fireworks? The autocannon bursts like flowers too… but that's not pretty!
잎은 해 쪽으로 고개를 돌리잖아요. 저는 요즘 지휘관님 오시는 문 쪽으로: Leaves turn their faces toward the sun, right? These days I keep turning toward the door you come in by, Commander~
Then I'll come at watering time. That's when you smile the most.
Watering time~ Then starting today, I'll water twice a day.
습관이면 더 좋아요. 잎도 습관으로 해를 보거든요~: Habit's even better. Leaves look at the sun out of habit too~
목은 괜찮아요. 고함으로 단련됐는걸요!: My throat's fine, Commander! The shouting keeps it trained~
Reason for measuring everything. What has been measured does not surprise when it comes again. End of report.
It's not surprise you hate — it's being late because of it.
Being late. Not even 0.1 seconds is acceptable. That statement: accurate.
Thoroughness: unmeasurable item. Classifying as praise.
Fun: no such item on this unit's gauges. Considering an addition.
First time standing on the battery: respondents, 0. A report ends even without a reply. Hence this way of speaking.

Comfort: confirmed. For this unit, this is the most comfortable.
Report recipient added. First report: barrel temperature normal.
그리젤과의 기록, 늘 한 발 차이. 줄이고 싶은지 유지하고 싶은지, 이쪽: Records with Grizel: always one shot apart. Whether to close the gap or keep it — this unit cannot judge either.

Nothing left to compete over. That item was just measured for the first time.
Not worrying: attempted. The record still enters view first.
A big win widens the gap. That calculation does not add up either.
질문. 지휘관이 끝까지 재 보고 싶은 것 하나. 이쪽 계기, 빌려드립니다: Question. One thing the Commander would want to measure to the end. This unit's gauges are available on loan.
How many times everyone comes back safe. All the way to the end.
Return count. This unit is measuring it as well. Will enter it on the same chart.
None. Recording. Will ask again next time.
테이프 왜 붙이냐고? 안 붙이면 근무 중에 다 말해 버리거든! 방벽에 걸: Why the tape? Because without it I'd blurt everything out on shift! Every single thing that snags on the Barrier!

테이프 말고 마스크는?: What about a mask instead of tape?
The moment I pass it on, it's not someone else's story anymore — it's my gossip. So, zip.
If I could do that, why would I buy tape! My mouth isn't built that way.
A mask flaps when I talk, so everyone can tell. I tried it, for real.
마그다가 또 방벽 전력을 두 배로 불렀어! 근무 중이라 반박도 못 했다고: Magda went and called the Barrier power double again! I was on shift, so I couldn't even argue. So unfair!
Seems to me Magda's waiting for you to come argue.
Double or whatever, as long as it runs.
전력 줄이면 조용해지려나?: Would cutting the power make it quieter?

Cut it and the Barrier gets thinner! Stuff we've been blurring gets less blurry.
있잖아, 내 말 듣다가 어디쯤에서 딴생각해? 솔직하게 말해도 돼. 안 삐: Hey, at what point do you zone out while I'm talking? You can be honest. I won't sulk.

If you talked a little less, I wouldn't zone out.
끝까지? 그럼 오늘 건 진짜 길어, 물 챙겨!: To the end? Then today's is a really long one — grab some water!
The third! That's the best part. Next time I'll put it first.
I did all my cutting on shift. Now's the time to pour out whatever's left.
거함 편대 얘기만 나오면 나만 빠져! 끝나면 무슨 일 있었는지 나한테 제: Whenever Dreadnought squadrons come up, I'm the only one left out! When it's over, will you tell me what happened before anyone else?

The Barrier could just come along too.
You'll wait? Then the second the tape's off, I'm gonna burst out talking first.
Reports don't say who laughed! That's what I want to know most.
The Barrier's for hiding the ship, so it can't go along! I know that, but it's still unfair.
점마다 이론 붙이는 이유? 이론이 없으면 그 점은 그냥 지나가 버리거든!: Why I stick a theory on every dot? Without a theory, that dot just slips right past!
Once you name it, you won't miss it. That's your way.
Most of them turned out to be nothing.
Missing things is the worst. That's why I'm always short on notebooks.
Most! That's why the few left over are all the more precious.
I take photos too! But wait — a photo doesn't show why it's there.
이론 세우다 밤새면 다음 날 화면이 두 개로 보여. 그날은 네가 대신 봐: If I stay up all night building theories, the next day the screen looks doubled. Will you watch it for me that day? Yell if it's suspicious!
I'll watch. But whether it's suspicious or not, you decide.
Two screens means you see twice as much.
그치! 판정은 내 몫이야. 넌 소리만 질러!: Right! The call's mine. You just yell!
자면 그사이에 뭐가 지나갈 거 아냐! 못 자!: Wait, wait — if I sleep, something'll slip past in the meantime! I can't sleep!
두 배로 보면 이론도 두 배야! …그건 좀 좋은데?: See twice as much, get twice the theories! …That's actually kinda nice?
내 이론 하나가 진짜로 맞으면 말이야, 넌 기쁠 것 같아, 무서울 것 같: If one of my theories actually turns out right — would you be happy, or scared?

지금까지 맞은 이론은 몇 개야?: How many of your theories have been right so far?
Let's watch together! I'm gonna scream the moment it's right, so cover your ears.
If you don't think much of it, I'll make twice the fuss. Then it's fair.
A few half-right ones! None fully right yet. That's why I'm saving them.
말 안 한 이론이 하나 있어. 너무 커서 공책에도 안 썼어. 꺼내도 될까: There's one theory I haven't told anyone. It's so big I didn't even write it in my notebook. Can I let it out?

If you want to let it out, go ahead.
Try breaking it into small pieces.
Not asking is exactly what makes me want to let it out most. That's so sneaky, seriously.
I want to, but I'm scared it'll become real once I do. That's the thing.
In pieces… first piece. It started from a single dot. That's it! No more.
번호를 날마다 바꾸는 거, 루트 때문이야. 걔가 매일 따거든. 근데 안: I change the numbers every day because of Ruth. She cracks it every day. But on days she doesn't, I get a little lonely.
So changing the numbers isn't guarding — it's playing together.
Lots of things to feel lonely about, huh.
Playing… tch, caught. Guess I'll make tomorrow's numbers a bit harder.
Not lots. Just that one kid. *Yawn*.
If I tell her, she won't come. She comes for the thrill of cracking it.
Wake me up if there's a raid. Your voice gets through better than the alarm.
I'll wake you. But you're up before anyone at the sound of a raid.
If there's a raid, just stay asleep.
I'd be up before you woke me. A raid knocks the yawn right out of me. Trouble is they're rare.
My ears get used to an alarm in three days. Your voice, not yet.

진짜 도둑이 한 번은 왔으면 좋겠어. 농담 반이야. 여기서 하나 훔쳐 간: I kinda wish a real thief would show up, just once. Half joking. If you were stealing one thing from here, what would you take?

언젠가 금고를 다 비워 보고 싶어. 전부 돌려주고, 빈 금고 앞에서 하루: Someday I want to empty the vault out completely. Give everything back, and sleep a whole day in front of the empty vault.

트릭시 발명품이 또 망가졌대. 고쳐 주면 지는 것 같고, 안 고쳐 주면: Trixie's invention broke again, I hear. If I fix it, it feels like losing, and if I don't, I'm bored!

Together, huh… that doesn't show up on the ranking board. Kinda want it, though.
다? 그럼 또 이겨야겠네. 쉴 틈이 없잖아!: Everything? Then I'll just have to win again. No time to rest!

네가 안 한 일로 칭찬받으면 어떡해? 난 그게 제일 싫거든. 그냥 궁금해: What would you do if you got praised for something you didn't do? I hate that more than anything. Just curious.

Send all the praise my way.

To you? Then half mine, half yours. Split it fair.
도, 도표는요, 틀리면 지우고 다시 그리면 돼요. 말은… 한번 나가면 못: Ch-charts, you see, if they are wrong, you can erase them and draw them again. Words… once they are out, they cannot be erased.

S-slowly… Then this one sentence, I will try without a chart.
괜찮았어요? 그, 그럼 아까 그 말엔 틀린 데 없었던 거죠?: It was fine? Th-then what I said earlier had nothing wrong in it, right?

리, 리타처럼 저도 별에 이름 하나 붙여 봤어요. 아직 소리 내서 안 불: L-like Rita, I gave a star a name too. I have not said it out loud yet.
Rita would love to be the first to hear it. Say it.
Rita takes care of star names, doesn't she?
번호로 부르는 게 편하지 않아?: Isn't calling them by number easier?
머, 먼저 들려줄게요. 연습은… 여기서 해도 돼요?: I-I will let her hear it first. The practice… may I do it here?

If you get stuck, just don't talk.
I-if you will wait… may I stop right now? …There. I will go on.
I-I cannot gloss over things. If even one tick mark is empty, I cannot sleep.
N-not talking… is what I am best at, so that will not do.

The densest one. It's the one you put the most work into.
Just keep asking someone to read for you.
Th-the densest one… The practice will take a long time. Still, I will go with that one.
Th-there is no "any." Each one is a sheet where I fixed one mistake.
Th-that is easy too. But if I only pick the easy way, my charts will not grow.
카타리나가 쉬는 날엔 내 「안 돼~」만 남아서 연구소가 통 안 굴러가~: On Katarina's days off, only my "nah~" is left, so the lab just doesn't roll~ What do I do~?

It's fine to stop for a day.
대신 이렇게~ …길다~ 그래도 해 볼게~ 굴러가면 좋지~: Instead, like this~ …so long~ Still, I'll try~ Rolling's nice~
하루 멈추면 다음 날 두 배로 걸려~ 그게 싫은 거야~: Nah~ stop one day and the next day takes twice as long~ That won't do~
둘 다 쉬면 연구소가 너무 조용하겠다~ 그것도 괜찮네~: If we both rest, the lab'll be too quiet~ That's kinda nice too~
회의가 길면 나 졸아~ 그래서 「안 돼~」로 빨리 끝내는 건데~ 들켰나~: When meetings run long I doze off~ That's why I end them fast with "nah~"… Did you catch on~?

다 알아도 아무도 안 말려~ 다들 빨리 끝나서 좋대~: Even if everyone knows, nobody stops me~ They say it's nice that it ends fast~

빨리 가자는 사람들 사이에 있으면~ 나만 느린 것 같아~ 넌 내가 느려: When I'm among people who want to go fast~ it feels like I'm the only slow one~ Do I look slow to you~?

조금이면 괜찮아~ 많이였으면 브레이크 걸었지~: A little's fine~ If it were a lot, I'd have hit the brakes~

남들 걸리는 데는 잘 보이는데~ 네 건 아직 못 찾았어~ 어디야~?: I can easily see where other people catch~ but I haven't found yours yet~ Where is it~?

정비소에 줄 서야 해?: Do I have to line up at the maintenance bay?

각도를 보면 입이 먼저 움직입니다. 한 도 틀린 빛이 멀리서 얼마나 벗어: When I see an angle, my mouth moves first. Do you know how far light that is one degree off strays at a distance?

Then just shoot only up close.
Early, up close. Yes — that way, those who are far away are not harmed.
If I may — one degree, at the far end, is the width of a ship. Still, I shall let it pass for you.
If I may — shooting only up close is too late. They are to be brought down before they approach.
엘리나 님이 제 레이저를 조명으로 쓰자 하십니다. 각도가 어긋난다 했더니: Miss Elina wishes to use my laser as stage lighting. When I said the angle was off, she told me that was the staging.
Your angles are precise, so Elina can twist them without worry.

Fireworks have no angle. My part disappears, it seems.
제 프리즘을 남에게 맡겨 본 일이 없습니다. 지휘관님이라면 떨어뜨리지 않: I have never entrusted my prism to another. You, Commander, would surely not drop it.
I'll hold it tight, if only out of fear. You watch the angle.
If I drop it, I'll buy you a new one.
If you grip it tightly, the angle will shift. …Still, I shall leave it as it is.
Left there, the light splits on its own. It always has.
This is the only one that splits light like this. I shall decline.
요격은 다가오는 것을 미리 떨어뜨리는 일입니다. 그런데 지휘관님이 다가오: Interception is bringing down what approaches before it arrives. And yet, when you approach, Commander, I forget the angle.
No need to measure. I'll walk slowly, outside your angle.
Probably because you're used to me.
Outside the angle, is it. Then that side is one I need not guard. …Regrettably.

If I may, I shall decline. You are not someone I would aim at.
내가 판마다 보낸 배를 크게 불러 대는 거, 시끄럽지? 근데 왜 그러는지: Me yelling out the ship behind every plate — noisy, huh? But do you know why I do it?
