그래서 벽이 붐비지! 판 하나에 한 사람씩!: That's why the wall's so crowded! One person per plate!
하하, 시끄러워야 벽도 안 졸지!: Ha ha, it's gotta be noisy or even the wall dozes off!
I did! But name tags don't make a sound.
{{로스비타}}가 자기가 나보다 두껍대! 벽 쪽 사람끼리 이런 걸로 다투: {{로스비타}} says she's thicker than me! People on the wall side squabbling over stuff like this — funny, right?
Holding out is what you're both proud of, so that's what you squabble over.
그치! 버티는 사람은 자랑도 단단해야지!: Right! People who hold out need sturdy pride too!
웃겨도 진지해! 이건 판 두께 문제라고!: Funny, but serious! This is a question of plate thickness!
We did! We both broke the ruler.
Someday I want to put a plate of my own in this wall! But I've got no ship to send. Ha ha… what do I do?
Your hammer marks are on every plate. The whole wall is your plate.
Just put in any old plate.
내 배에서 하나 더 보낼까?: Want me to send one more from my ship?
벽 전체…! 하하, 그럼 제일 두꺼운 건 나네!: The whole wall…! Ha ha, then the thickest one's me!
Not just any! It's gotta be a plate I can call by name.
그건 네 판이잖아! 하하, 그래도 받을게!: That'd be your plate! Ha ha, but I'll take it anyway!
넌 손에 뭘 쥐고 있을 때가 제일 편해? 나는 망치! 놓으면 손이 허전해: What do you feel most at ease holding in your hand? Me, a hammer! Let go and my hands feel empty!
A plate to send. I want to know where it'll go in your wall.
좋지! 쥐고 와, 망치는 내가 들게!: Nice! Bring it, I'll handle the hammer!
빈손? 그럼 판 하나 쥐여 줄게, 금방 편해져!: Empty hands? Then I'll put a plate in them — you'll feel at ease in no time!
It's gotta be heavy so my hands don't shake! When I'm fitting seams, that's everything.
엔진 말을 전하면 다들 덜 다퉈요. 제 말이었으면 다퉜을 텐데요. 엔진: When I pass on what the engine says, everyone argues less. If they were my words, they would have argued. Is it thanks to the engine?
The engine's words don't take anyone's side. And it's even more so because you're the one passing them on.
Who knows, I guess that's just how it is.
Then try it in your own words too.
Nobody's side, you say. The engine says no side is the easiest side to be on.
I suppose so. The engine says it cannot stand nitpicking either.
When I say it in my own words… my voice gets small. I will borrow the engine's.
기울었다고 하면 리브만 웃지 않고 같은 쪽을 짚어요. 둘이 같이 틀릴 수: When I say we are tilting, only Liv does not laugh — she points to the same side. The two of us could be wrong together, could we not?
If you both point to the same side, I'll take another look that way too.
If you take another look, that makes three. Then it is less frightening.
If we are wrong together, we can fix it together. It is better than alone.
They say a level gauge is always straight. But the ship does not travel straight.
엔진이 왜 혼자 가는지 언젠가 알게 되면요, 그때도 제가 귀를 대고 있을: If someday I learn why the engine goes on its own, will I still have my ear pressed to it?
You'd still listen. You listen because you like the sound, not for the answer.
Because I like the sound. …Yes, that is right. The reason can come later.
It runs fine. Still, the engine does not stop me from being curious.
The engine talks more than the manual does. That way is faster.
엔진 말 말고 제 생각을 묻는 분은 없어요. 지휘관님은… 궁금하세요?: No one asks what I think, rather than what the engine says. Commander… are you curious?
I am. Today, tell me which way you want to go first.
I'll ask the engine for you.
Me? …That way. I am glad it is the same way as the engine.
Enough, yes. Still, sometimes I wish one line of mine could slip in.
The engine? Whenever I come up, the engine laughs.
말로는 다 튼튼하대! 근데 맞아 보기 전엔 모르잖아. 그래서 내가 쏘는: Everyone says it's sturdy! But you don't know until it takes a hit. That's why I shoot it!
So if you shoot it and say it's fine, I'll believe it too.
You could just read the manual.
You'll believe what I say! Then I won't shoot these words — I'll hang them up.
Just like that? Wow. That's the hardest thing for me.
I shot the manual too! Holes everywhere. Paper's paper.
토스카가 반대하면 나 신나! 쏴 볼 과녁이 하나 더 생긴 거잖아. 이상해: When Tosca objects, I get so excited! It's one more target to shoot at, right? Is that weird?
You don't just let her objections slide, you test them. Tosca would be glad too.
반가울 거래? 그럼 다음 반박은 더 큰 과녁에 붙여 줘야지!: She'd be glad? Then I'll pin her next objection on an even bigger target!
Weird's fine if it's fun! I'll log it as today's data.
If I talk her out of it, there's nothing left to shoot! No way.
거함 편대 날 전날 밤엔 나 잠이 안 와! 과녁만 몇 번을 다시 세우는지: The night before a Dreadnought squadron day, I can't sleep! I lose count of how many times I set the targets back up.
I'll hold the targets steady while you set them up. Then they'll stand on the first try.
그날 쉬면 안 돼?: Can't you take that day off?
붙잡아 준대! 그럼 남는 시간에 한 발만 쏴 봐도 돼?: You'll hold them! Then with the time left over, can I shoot just one shot?
그냥 자?! 그게 되면 벌써 했지!: Just sleep?! If I could, I'd have done it already!
쉬어?! 손꼽아 기다린 날인데!: Rest?! It's the day I've been counting down to!
궁금한 게 생기면 나는 쏴 보면 끝인데, 너는 궁금할 땐 뭘 해?: When I'm curious about something, I shoot it and that's that — what do you do when you're curious?
Ask you. Your stories from shooting things are the fastest.
나한테?! 그럼 궁금한 거 생기면 바로 와. 과녁 세워 둘게!: Me?! Then whenever you're curious, come right over. I'll have a target set up!
없어?! 그럼 내 과녁 하나 줄게. 금방 생겨!: Nothing?! Then I'll give you one of my targets. You'll get curious in no time!
참는다고?! …한 발만 참아 볼게. 딱 한 발만!: Holding back?! …I'll try holding back one shot. Just one!
녹일 스크랩은 내가 뜯어. 쇠마다 식는 빠르기가 달라서, 손으로 알아 둬: I strip the scrap I melt myself. Every metal cools at its own pace — my hands have to know it before I can set the heat.
녹이기 전에 오래 들여다보는 게 그 공부였어?: So that long look before melting is how you study it?
Leave the stripping to the others.
Couldn't you just cool it down before melting?
While I look, I'm already setting the heat. The burner's just the last step.
Hand it off and my hands won't know the metal. Then the heat runs a beat late.
Cold metal tells you nothing. Its temper shows when it's hot.
테스라 라인은 쉬지 않고 돌아. 내 쪽은 기다려야 하고. 나란히 서면 내: Tesla's line never stops. Mine has to wait. Side by side, I always look slow.
That line only runs once your alloy cools.
Let's merge the lines into one.
Put that way, they're the ones waiting on me. Not bad.
Rushed heat leaves the metal half-melted. Their line would notice first.
Merge them and everything runs on one side's heat. Can't do that.
Want to watch the next burner's first fire with me? The first color only happens once. I don't invite just anyone.
I'll come. Let's keep that color between the two of us.
Just us two. Fine — I'll keep it secret even from the burner.
Anything on film is already cold fire. Come see it.
Quieter. Doesn't burst. Burns a long time.
화구가 몇 개로 늘든 첫 화구 불은 내가 지킬 거야. 그건 남한테 안 넘: However many burners we end up with, the first burner's fire is mine to keep. That one I don't hand over.
The first fire's yours. Even if there are ten burners.
If it gets busy, split it up.
첫 화구가 뭐가 달라?: What's different about the first burner?
Ten, huh. Then all ten times, I'll start in front of the first fire.
The other burners, I'll split. Not the first.
It's burned the longest. I remember even the one time it went out.
출하한 서보, 어디 박혔는지 도크까지 확인하러 가. 반장은 질색하고. 계: Shipped servos: I go all the way to the dock to check where they ended up. The crew chief hates it. Can I keep going?
Your line isn't done until you see them in use. Go.
Put location tags on the servos.
End of line: the dock. Going again today.
Shipping: half the job. The other half ends at the dock.
Room for a tag is room for one more sensor. Rejected.
Parts Karin brings back: half unusable. Still, every one rides the line once. Everyone calls it waste.
So you run them once out of respect for the hands that picked them up.
Pull the unusable ones right away.
Pulled after one run. Pulled from the start. Not the same.
Pulling: at the end of the line. Coming in, they're all guests.
New only, and the hands that scavenge stop. That's a loss.
네 손 치수 재도 돼? 공구 손잡이 하나. 규격품 말고 너한테만 맞는 걸: Can I measure your hand? For one tool grip. Not standard issue — one that fits only you.
Measure away. If you made it to fit, my hand will know it first.
Rivet's crew are the ones who use the tools.
Measurement: starting. Open your hand. …Dimensions: memorized.
Plenty, fitting: separate items. Taking measurements anyway.
The crew's get made too. This one has a different owner.
Reports: always from my end. Once a day, requesting one from yours too. Even a short one.
Sure. I'll keep it clipped: item, status.
There'll be plenty of days with nothing to say.
I'll write it up and send it over.
A report from your mouth. Unfamiliar. In a good way.
"Nothing," one line. Accepted as a report too.
Paper gets lost in the line noise. Verbal report, please.
순항 게이지부터 보는 버릇, 배가 멈췄던 날부터야. 냄새도 안 나는 조용: I've checked the cruise gauge first ever since the day the ship stopped. No smell, no sound — I never knew quiet could be that scary.
Eyes that remember that day read the needle first.
If it stops, it can just start again.
Yeah — needle first, hello after. That order just stuck. Go easy on me.
Getting going again took a long time. That stretch, I'd rather you never go through it.
Add one and I'd have to watch both, right? My nose is busy enough, and now my eyes too.
Electra still talks power. But she always tacks one thing on at the end: is there fuel left.
That fuel question at the end is Electra's way of asking how you are.
Work it out between you two.
I'll cut the power draw for you.
I know. That's why I always answer plenty. Keep the little puffing-up between us, okay?
We are working it out. Twice a day, same talk.
Then that talk goes to you instead. Sorry about that.
냄새 때문에 미안하다는 말을 하루에도 몇 번씩 해. 너한테만은 좀 줄여: Because of the smell, I say sorry so many times a day. With you, at least, I'd like to cut back.
If it's nothing to be sorry for, say thanks. I'll take as many of those as you've got.
Get rid of the smell and you won't have to say it.
Thanks, huh. …Doesn't come easy, but I'll practice.
I don't count either. Feels like counting would just make me sorry again.
No smell, no fuel. That one I'll keep apologizing for, sorry.
연료 말고 딱 한 번, 쓸모없는 걸 합성해 보고 싶어. 아무도 안 태우는: Just once, I'd like to synthesize something useless instead of fuel. Something nobody burns. Weird, right?
When you make it, show me first.
쓸모없으면 왜 만들어?: Why make it if it's useless?
그것도 연료로 쓸 수 있지 않아?: Couldn't that be used as fuel too?
First, then. I'll bring it in a little bottle, no label. Bear with the smell.
Because… I want to see if anything's left when nothing gets burned.
Knew I'd hear that. That's why I never told anyone.
증설 요청은 늘 내가 제일 먼저 해. 모자란 걸 제일 먼저 아는 게 나니: I'm always first to file for expansion. I'm the first to know what's short. Knowing and sitting still — I can't do it.
Nobody gets caught off guard because the first to know speaks up first.
One person caught off guard is enough — me. I've got the rest.
They are. I'll cut them down one at a time, so read them through to the end.
Stockpile space is my sister's job. That's full too.
나프타 합성조가 전력을 제일 많이 먹어. 그래서 잔소리도 거기로 제일 많: Naphtha's synthesis vats eat the most power. So most of my nagging goes there too — but I've never once cut them off.
Nag, but never cut — that's your way.
Just split it the right way.
Let's scale back the synthesis vats.
Cut them and the ship stops. Once was enough.
"The right way" is the hardest part. That's why I measure again every day.
Scale them back and cruising shrinks too. Both sides lose.
증설 요청서 맨 끝 칸에 늘 작게 번개를 그려. 아무도 몰라. 다음 장엔: I always draw a tiny lightning bolt in the last box of the expansion request. Nobody knows. What should I draw on the next one?
Draw the storage. With the lightning heading toward your sister.
Toward my sister. Whoever does the sign-off will laugh.
It's not. That's why I draw it really small.
Already drowning in numbers. One bolt is room to breathe.
힘든 날은 나한테도 말해. 발전소 바늘보다는 잘 들어 줄게. …싫어?: On hard days, tell me too. I'll listen better than the plant's needle. …No?
Then you too. On hard days, tell me instead of the needle.
It's fine, I can handle it alone.
Me too? …Didn't think of that. Okay. One at a time.
I can see you doing it all alone. That's why I'm saying it.
It listens. It just answers in numbers.
창고가 차면 다녀왔냐고 묻잖아. 꽉 찬 날은 다들 무사히 실어 온 날이라: When the storage fills, I ask "You're back?" A full day means everyone hauled it home safe.
다녀왔냐는 말, 어서 와 대신이었어?: So "You're back?" was standing in for "welcome home"?
The shorter the greeting, the better.
Yeah. But "welcome home" is embarrassing, so I always say it sideways.
Short, yeah. But I say it every time. Not a single day skipped.
The answer comes from the ones who hauled it, not the storage.
버리는 건 싫은데, 가끔은 비워야 새로 들어와. 비울 걸 고르는 게 제일: I hate throwing things out, but sometimes space has to be cleared before anything new comes in. Picking what to clear is the hardest part. Will you help me pick?
Tell me the order you treasure them in. We'll go through from the bottom together.
Send it all to the Exchange.
From the bottom. Then the ones I'd hate to lose come up last.
The oldest ones have waited the longest. I can't.
All of it? That'd just fatten the Exchange ledger. Half.
언니는 전력표는 매일 보면서 내 장부는 안 펴 봐. 한 번은 봐 줬으면: My sister checks her power chart every day but never opens my ledger. I'd like her to look just once — how do I say it?
Leave your ledger open next to the power chart. Right where her eyes go.
Then stop looking at her power chart first.
Leave it open beside it. I like that — no talking needed.
If I just say it, my sister asks for numbers first. Then that's that.
Can't. Without that chart I can't fill the storage.
넘쳐서 버린 걸 하나도 안 빼고 써 둔 장이 있어. 언니한테도 안 보여: I have a page where I wrote down everything that overflowed and got thrown out, every last one. I haven't even shown my sister. Want to read it?
Show me. Let's read it line by line together.
그거 다 합치면 얼마야?: How much is all of that put together?
Line by line. …The first line is a day my sister doesn't know about.
Forget, and I'll throw things out again. That's why I wrote it down.
Put together, two storage slots' worth. Saying it makes it feel even more wasteful.
The ones who've worked the dock with me a long time — I just hold out my hand and they put the right tool in it. No words needed.
So that's why your dock is so loud, yet hardly anyone talks.
Couldn't you just label the tools?
The tools do the talking. We just line up our hands.
It is. Though if the chief's hand is slow, they laugh first.
Labels have to be read. My crew's hands grab without reading.
When parts run short, will you tell Tesla? From me it sounds like I'm rushing her.
You hold back because you know how busy her hands are. I'll pass it on.
Not holding back, just… yeah. Her pulling all-nighters? As crew chief, I can't watch that.
If I do it, one word turns into two. She gets apologetic.
Go check the rate. Then you won't say that.
작업복 팔꿈치가 다 해졌어. 버리긴 싫은데 천은 내 손으로 못 고쳐. 기: The elbows on my coveralls are worn through. Don't want to toss them, but I can't fix cloth with these hands. Frames, sure.
Hand them here. I'm no good at it, but I'll stitch them so they won't come apart.
Not coming apart is plenty. Leave the worn spots as they are — they're my marks.
New one? Doesn't sit right. Takes a month to break in, I'm telling you.
That's my name. Drive it into cloth and it'll never come out.
리벳은 부품 이름이야. 내 이름도 그거고. 부를 때 어떻게 들려?: A rivet's a part. It's also my name. How does it sound when you call me?
Something that holds tight. Just like your work.
나사로 바꿀래?: Want to go by Screw instead?
Holds tight, huh. Then I'll stay driven in so I don't come loose.
Right. Easy to call, done. Next.
Screw? That'd just give my crew something to tease me with.
처음엔 칸을 번호순으로 줬어. 옆 칸끼리 말을 안 하더라. 그 뒤론 누가: At first I gave out slots in number order. Neighbors wouldn't talk to each other. Since then, I check who stands next to whom first.
So you're not assigning slots, you're assigning neighbors.
Number order is the neatest, though.
Doesn't matter if they talk, as long as maintenance gets done.
When neighbors get along, the maintenance line moves faster too. That's a bonus.
It was neat. They didn't even call each other by name — that was the trouble.
Maintenance got done. There just wasn't any laughing.
I painted the entrance sign in Neon's frame color. She smiles when she sees her own color. Then the others smile, seeing her.
So they come in smiling, right from the door.
Everyone's going to ask for their own color.
Yes. It's a color that lowers the threshold.
It has to glare. So tired eyes can still find their own bay.
They already have. I'm out of signs.
격납고 불을 다 꺼 본 날이 없어. 늘 누가 나가 있거든. 다 돌아온 밤: There's never been a day I turned off every hangar light. Someone's always out. On the night everyone's back, who'll flip the last switch?
You flip it. I'll watch from beside you.
The lights could just stay on.
정전 훈련 한번 할까?: Want to run a blackout drill?
Stay beside me. Even in the dark, I want to know where you are.
I'll keep them on. Every day, until the night the last name on the list comes in.
I don't want them off for a drill. They go off when everyone's home.
새 애가 올 칸은 늘 먼저 알아. 왜 아는지는 나도 몰라. 그냥 손이 먼: I always know which slot a new girl will come to. Why, I don't know. My hands just clear the slot first.
They settle in easy because your hands cleared the slot.
다음 올 애 이름도 알아?: Do you know the next one's name too?
If they settle in easy, that's enough. Even without knowing why.
Three coincidences, and it goes on the order sheet.
Not the name. Just the shape of the slot.
귀환이 몇 분 당겨지면 꼭 그걸 재 오는 애가 있어. 아무도 모르는 몇: Whenever a return comes in a few minutes early, there's always one girl who times it and brings it to me. A few minutes nobody notices — but I like those minutes.
Because the way back got that much shorter.
A few minutes hardly makes a difference.
Then tell them to cut a few hours.
Yeah. Seeing them even a few minutes sooner is nice, right?
No difference, sure. But the one waiting ends up counting them, you know?
Then she'd stay up all night, of course. A few minutes is plenty.
출격 슬롯이 늘 때마다 격납고부터 들러. 돌아올 방이 남느냐고. 관제관은: Every time sortie slots go up, I stop by the hangar first. To ask if there's still room to come back to. The controller always says there is.
You can only send them out once you hear there's room.
There's always room in the hangar.
Yeah. I only open the slot after I've heard it.
Always room. Still, you want to hear it every time — that there's a room to come back to.
Upgrading's their job, sure. I'll just ask.
경유지는 운이 정해. 좋은 데 닿은 날은 일지에 네 덕이라고 써 둬. 운: Luck picks the waypoints. On days we reach somewhere good, I write in the log that it was thanks to you. Do you believe in luck at all?
If it's luck you're writing down, I'll believe it.
네잎클로버라도 하나 구해 올까?: Should I go find a four-leaf clover?
Then today's line gets "thanks to you" too.
You don't have to believe it. I'm the one writing it.
I'll pin the clover to the Control Room door. For everyone to see.
네가 함교 자리를 비우면 슬롯 표가 괜히 길어 보여. 돌아오면 다시 짧아: When you leave your seat on the Bridge, the slot chart looks longer for no reason. When you come back, it's short again.
Then I'll tell you ahead of time when I step away.
If you tell me ahead, the chart's not as long. That's thanks to you.
Even if it's just a feeling, the chart looks long. I count that kind of thing.
Shrink it and there are fewer slots to send out. You wouldn't like that.
교관 첫날, 가르칠 게 없었다. 그래서 돌아온 애들 말을 받아 썼지. 그: My first day as instructor, I had nothing to teach. So I wrote down what the returning girls said. That is my class now.
So you listened before you taught.
교관이 그래도 돼?: Is an instructor allowed to do that?
A textbook would've been the place to start.
Listening is half the class. The other half is sitting them down.
They wrote the textbook. I only bound it.
메이는 돌아와서 제 실수만 말한다. 남의 실수는 하나도 안 짚어. 고쳐야: Mei comes back and talks only about her own mistakes. Never points out anyone else's. It needs correcting — and yet I want to leave it.
Keep her way, and you point out the others' mistakes yourself.
The instructor points them out instead. Right. That was my job all along.
It's not her age. She's looking out for the others.
Demerits aren't in my curriculum. I just sit her down once more.
복기는 늘 남의 출격만 한다. 너라면 오늘 하루에서 어디를 다시 하겠나?: I only ever debrief other people's sorties. You — what part of today would you do again?
Rather than what to redo, I'd pick what I'd want to do once more.
Once more, is it. That's not a debrief, that's a reward. Pick.
Nothing means you didn't look. I'll ask again tomorrow.
The whole thing isn't a debrief. That's living the day over.
가르치기만 하다 보니 배운 지 오래다. 네가 하나 가르쳐 주겠나? 무엇이: Nothing but teaching for so long, it's been ages since I learned. Will you teach me one thing? Anything.
Sure. Lesson one: how to rest.
I'll give you the simulator manual.
How to rest. You picked the hardest subject.
The ones who say they have nothing know the most. Bring it out slowly.
I know the manual by heart. That's not a lesson.
공짜는 없다고 늘 먼저 말해요. 그래야 손님이 미안해하지 않고 또 오거든: I always say up front that nothing is free. That way customers do not feel indebted, and they come back. A strange way to do business, is it not?
So charging a price was actually a kindness.
Then make the first deal free.
A kindness? I cannot put that sort of thing in the ledger.
It is. That is why no one ever asks.
The first deal is the most expensive. So the second one looks cheap.
시아 씨는 남는 재고를 바닥까지 긁어 와요. 근데 값은 한 번도 안 깎아: Shia scrapes up every last bit of surplus stock. Yet she has never once haggled. Customers like that are the hardest.
No haggling means your sales talk has nowhere to stand.
Nowhere to stand… It is true I say less in front of her.
Easy, yes. That is why the ledger is so dull.
She would simply pay it. That is why I cannot raise it.
교환소에 안 파는 물건이 딱 하나 있어요. 값을 못 매겨서요. 지휘관님이: There is exactly one thing at the Exchange that is not for sale. Because I cannot put a price on it. Would you like to try, Commander?
Not pricing it is its price.
I'll buy it at any price.
If I write that in the ledger, everyone will laugh. …I will write it.
I did say it is not for sale. This is why customers are difficult.
If I sold it, this place would become just a shop. I would not like that.
저는 늘 파는 쪽이라 뭘 사 본 일이 없어요. 지휘관님은 마지막으로 산: I am always the one selling, so I have never bought anything. Commander, what was the last thing you bought?
Something from your Exchange. At a losing rate.
Never bought anything. Picked it all up.
Customers who know and come anyway are the most troublesome. They make me laugh.
If you cannot remember what you bought, you took a loss.
Things you pick up have a price too. Bring them and I will price them for you.
선제 사격 신호는 혼자 낸다. 맞았는지는 다 끝나야 안다. 그 사이가 길: I give the first-strike signal alone. Whether it hit, I only know when it's all over. The time between is long.
I'll be beside you in between. The signal's yours.
You'll find out when it's over.
Couldn't you just set it to fire automatically?
Beside me is enough. I hold the signal line.
I will. Until then, my hand stays on the line.
A machine can't tell when to fire and when to hold.
신호는 내가 내지만 먼저 보는 건 마리 화면이다. 맏이가 남한테 기대는: I give the signal, but Mari's screen sees it first. The eldest leaning on someone else, you could say.
Knowing who to lean on is what makes an eldest.
Leave the signal to Mari too.
What makes an eldest is giving the signal to the end. The leaning is extra.
Looking costs a beat. That beat is big.
That girl only looks for reasons not to shoot. The signal is mine.
청구서는 늘 네 앞으로 쓴다. 한 번쯤 받는 쪽이 돼 보고 싶군. 네가: I always write the invoices out to you. I'd like to be on the receiving end for once. If you billed me, what would you write?
One day off from being the eldest. That's what I'd bill.
One day. We'll carry that on the books with no due date.
Nothing. That's the answer that leaves the one writing them most embarrassed.
Not half. Repair costs stay exact.
포탑 위에선 배 전체가 보인다. 그래서 여기 섰다. 너는 이 배 어디를: From atop the turret you can see the whole ship. That's why I stand here. Which part of this ship do you most want to protect?
The turrets. And the three standing on them.
The three of us too. Then we know who's watching over us.
Guarding it all equally is my job. You can pick just one.
No blind spots on the window side. Sleep easy.
리제랑 군집 상대법을 서로 가르쳐! 근데 내가 배운 게 더 많은 것 같아: Liese and I teach each other how to handle swarms! But I think I've learned more. Kind of unfair!
What you taught her probably shows all through her shooting.
묻어 있어? 다음 군집 때 찾아볼래!: It shows? I'll look for it next swarm!
주고받긴 해! 근데 셈은 내가 더 손해야!: We do trade! But on the tally, I'm still the one losing!
수업료 대신 탄창 한 통! 그게 제일 남는 장사야!: One magazine instead of tuition! Best deal there is!
군집 끝나면 한동안 말이 안 나와! 신나서 그런지 무서워서 그런지 모르겠: After a swarm, I can't talk for a while! Don't know if it's excitement or fear.
Probably both. When it's over, I'll come talk to you first.
Next time, sing while you shoot.
Come first! Then my first word'll be your name.
Rest helps! But resting is when it's quietest.
If I sing, I'll miss the signals! Let me get away with humming, though.
조준경 없이 하늘 본 일이 별로 없어! 맨눈으로 보면 뭐가 보일까?: I've hardly ever looked at the sky without a sight! What would I see with bare eyes?
Let's go look. I'll hold on to your sight.
Hold it! My hand'll keep reaching for it otherwise.
Nothing much is even better! Nothing to aim at.
A telescope's just like a sight! I said bare eyes!
군집 끝나고 아무도 안 다쳤으면 기관포한테 고맙다고 해! 오늘은 너도 한: When a swarm ends and nobody's hurt, I thank the autocannon! Will you say something to it today too?
Thanks. For turning them all back again today.
What's the point of talking to a machine?
들었지? 기관포가 오늘 밤 좀 덜 시끄러울 거야!: Hear that? The autocannon'll be a little quieter tonight!
기계라도 들어! 아니어도 내가 들어!: Machines listen too! And if not, I do!
기름칠은 도크 몫이야! 말은 내 몫이고!: Oiling's the dock's job! Talking's mine!
They say if you ask Fleur and me the same thing, we give the same answer. I'm not a fan of that.
Same answer, maybe, but yours always comes out first.
First, huh. Then even if it's the same words, they're mine.
All three of us have heard that one too. I'm sick of it.
I did try, okay? She changed hers the exact same way.
충전 걸어 두면 다 찰 때까지 자리를 못 떠. 다들 방해될까 봐 말도 안: Once I start charging, I can't leave till it's full. Nobody talks to me either — they think they'll get in the way.
Then I'll come. I'll chatter next to you till it's full.
Chatter all you want. The long barrel doesn't shake that easily.
Focusing's the barrel's job. Me, I just get bored meanwhile. Seriously.
Rush it and it won't fill, I'm telling you. I'm not firing a half-charged shot.
Since nobody calls me the baby anymore, I sometimes feel kind of empty. And I hated it so much.
Even a name you hated was yours, after hearing it that long.
Battery Chief is better, isn't it?
It was mine. Now it's someone else's. I'm not asking for it back.
No way, okay? Missing it and wanting it are different things.
It is. Nobody's taking that name.
Everyone just asks me to punch through. That's fine, but sometimes I want to lean on someone too. Who do you lean on?
On all of you. So you can lean on me.
I can lean on you? Then today, you instead of the barrel.
Is that supposed to be me? Don't copy me.
Not a wall. I asked seriously, and now you made me laugh.
퇴각하는 편성은 끝까지 따라가요. 등을 보이면 끝이라고들 하는데, 저는: I follow a retreating squad all the way. People say it is over once they turn their backs, but not for me.
You decide when it's over. It's over when it lands.
Yes. It is over when it lands. A back is not the end.
It is not diligence. The light simply goes first.
If I let them go, their cargo goes too. That is a little wasteful.
사일런이랑 저는 둘 다 전자전을 싫어해요. 그런데 싫어하는 까닭은 서로: Silen and I both dislike electronic warfare. But I think our reasons are different.
For you, it blurs your aim. For Silen, it breaks the quiet.
Then neither of you do electronic warfare.
You split it cleanly into two lines. Straighter than my crosshairs.
Everyone. Still, disliking it together makes it less lonely.
We are not the ones doing it. We are on the receiving end. And when it comes, I fire first.
제 말이 짧대요. 지휘관님은 제 말 중에 더 길었으면 하는 게 있어요?: They say I talk short. Commander, is there anything of mine you wish were longer?
Not your answers — the things you bring up first. Those can be long.
First. Then here is one. I can tell your footsteps from far away, Commander.
If it is all right, I will leave it as it is. Short words arrive sooner.
My reports are short too. Like light — a hit only needs one line.
맞힌 건 다 궤도 뒤로 떨어져요. 하나쯤은 곁에 두고 싶은데, 뭐가 좋을: Everything I hit falls away behind our orbit. I would like to keep one thing by me. What would be good?
The first container you left behind. Your first beam marked that one.
That one is still in orbit. Sometimes it drifts into my crosshairs.
Letting go is easy. That is why I wanted to keep one.
A display case is too big. I'm the youngest — one shelf is enough.
아스카는 남의 통신을 끄고, 나는 우리 걸 지켜. 하는 일은 같은데 서: Asuka shuts down other people's comms… I guard ours. Same work. We just stand on different sides.
So you two know each other's work best.
We do. So we don't have to talk.
Not overlap… we face each other. Like a mirror.
…Swap, and it's still the same spot. Only the direction turns.
습격 오는 밤엔 잡음이 많아. 그런 밤엔 여기 좀 있어 줘. 말은 안 해: Raid nights are full of noise… On nights like that, stay here a while. You don't have to talk.
I'll stay. I'll just sit beside you while you sort the sounds.
Just sitting… That makes the barrier feel lighter.
Come when it's done. The noise lasts all night.
Research won't cut it… It's quieter with someone beside me.
…They say I have my own frequency too. Not one I picked.
Even if you didn't pick it, it's yours. I'll memorize it.
If you memorize it, you'll find me anywhere… That's a little scary. And nice.
Everyone… Then you have one too.
That's for work. This one's just… me.
…재머 애들 얼굴은 거의 몰라. 주파수로는 다 아는데. 마주치면 알아볼: …I barely know the Jammer girls' faces. I know them all by frequency. Would I recognize them if we met?
You will. They'll probably greet you on your frequency first.
They're right there in the Hangar.
사진 받아 줄까?: Want me to get you photos?
Frequency first. …Then I can learn faces later.
They're there if I go. But the way there is the loudest part.
Photos have no sound… Then I can't tell who's who.
When Kyoko really means to hide, even I can't find her. Good thing we're on the same ship.
Your scope needs one thing it can't find, or it'd get bored.
Level the radar and you'll find her.
Not bored. And the one I can't find is on our side, so that counts as safe.
Same side, so some days I don't look on purpose. Those days don't count.
Level it and she hides one layer deeper. We go up together like that.
예고는 내가 내. 근데 그걸 누가 읽는지는 몰라. 너는 읽어?: I'm the one who puts out the warnings. But I don't know who reads them. Do you?
I do. When your warning comes up, I check the time first.
I just look at the notifications.
Time first. Then from now on I'll put the time at the very front.
Sometimes, then. I'll write them for those times. The unread days don't count.
I wrote the notifications too. The short version.
멀리 보는 게 일이라 가까운 건 자꾸 흐려. 가까운 건 누가 봐 줘?: Seeing far is my job, so near things keep blurring. Who watches what's close?
I'll watch what's close. You keep looking far.
Then I'll only look far. Near things count as yours.
If it's each their own, the middle's left empty. And that's the closest part.
Glasses don't fit a scope. I tried.
사라진 배 좌표도 안 지워. 지우면 처음부터 없던 일이 되잖아. 미련 같: I don't erase the coordinates of ships that vanished, either. Erase them and it's like they were never there. Does that seem like clinging?
It's not clinging, it's a record. They were there.
They were there. I'll write that next to the coordinates.
I could. My hand just won't move to do it.
Move them and that spot's empty. An empty spot counts as a coordinate too.
I address everyone formally. Before the vault, everyone is a guest.
Then I'm a guest too. Only when I'm standing at the vault.
말 놓으면 금고가 열려?: If you drop the formality, does the vault open?
Only before the vault. Take one step back and you are the Commander once more.
This is how I speak at ease. I have never tried speaking any other way.
It does not. Manner of speech and the lock are secured separately.
수리비가 모자란 날, 금고 앞에 서 있다가 말없이 돌아간 분이 있었습니다: On a day when repair costs fell short, someone stood before the vault and then left without a word. Ought I to have opened the door?
The door can stay shut. I just wish you'd stood beside them for a moment.
If you went by the rules, that's enough.
Standing beside someone is not in the rules. Next time, I shall do so.
It was by the rules. Even so, the sight of that back did not add up.
I do not lend. I can, however, count out the repair order together with them.
물들이기 전 제 머리색은 아무도 묻지 않으십니다. 지휘관님도 궁금하지 않: No one asks what my hair color was before I dyed it. Are you not curious either, Commander?
With the color you have now, I know it's you from far off. That's enough.
If you know me from afar, then the choice was worth it.
I am more at ease if you are not. The numbers are all you need look at.
No other color is in my calculations. I shall keep standing in this one.
숫자는 한 자리도 틀리지 않습니다. 그래도 한 번쯤 틀려 보고 싶은 날이: My figures are never off by a single digit. Still, there are days I wish to be wrong just once. I have never said this before.
On that day, I'll count again with you. We can be wrong together, too.
Then get one wrong on purpose.
If we are wrong together, the sums balance. A strange calculation, I admit.
Indeed, I cannot. That is why I keep it only as a wish on certain days.
Wrong on purpose is not being wrong. That is a lie.
테스라가 설계도 들고 오면 같이 읽어. 걘 선을 보고, 난 선 사이를 재: When Tesla brings blueprints, we read them together. She looks at the lines; I measure between them.
Read by you two, nothing gets missed. The lines and the space between.
설계도 내가 대신 읽어 줄까?: Want me to read the blueprints for you?
Gaps: some. Measure together and they shrink.
Close? Haven't measured that. We do stop at the same spots.
Go ahead. I'll measure where you stop.
I sign off, look up, and Bianca's already opened the next page. No room to breathe. Could you stop her?
I'll try. Catch your breath before the next page opens.
Should I just close the next page?
A breath. That's a length I've never measured. I'll try.
She is. Faster than my sign-offs, so nobody can stop her.
Close it and she'll open it again. That's how she is.
뭐든 재는데, 나는 안 재 봤어. 뭘로 재야 할지 몰라서. 넌 나를 뭘로: I measure everything, but I've never measured myself. I don't know what to measure with. What would you measure me with?
I won't measure you. I'll just watch from beside you.
First person who won't measure. A bit uncomfortable. A bit nice.
Measured my height already. It didn't cover everything.
Level is the facility cap. I'd rather not have a cap.
다들 내 결재를 기다려. 근데 내 건 누가 결재해 줘?: Everyone waits for my sign-off. But who signs off on mine?
I'll look. No stamp, but I'll read it to the end.
Read to the end? Then I can't sign it sloppy either.
I always do. That's why it's always sent back.
There is no up. Above the research lead is the ceiling.
책상에서 쓰면 고장이 남 얘기처럼 읽혀. 그래서 부서진 자리로 나가서 써: Written at a desk, a fault reads like someone else's story. So I go out to where it broke and write there.
Writing on the spot is what keeps the "why." A desk only keeps the result.
It's dangerous out there. Just bring back photos.
A record with only the result can't stop the next fault, I've found. So out I go.
Somewhere comfy, my hand speeds up. A fast record always drops a line.
Photos don't keep sound. The creaking goes on the sheet too.
리벳은 고치고 나서 왜 부서졌는지 안 물어. 묻는 건 늘 나야. 그래도: Rivet fixes things and never asks why they broke. I'm always the one asking. Is that all right?
Rivet fixes fast, so you get to ask slowly.
Better to fix one more than spend the time asking.
Her hands are fast, so I'm allowed to be slow. I feel less sorry now.
We each do our part and it fits, I guess. The log has no day we worked it out in words, though.
Fix one more and another breaks. If it's the same spot, that one I stop.
고장 안 난 날도 기록해 볼까 해. 아무 일 없던 날은 뭐라고 쓰지?: I'm thinking of logging days with no faults too. What do I write for a day when nothing happened?
Why it was all clear… That won't fit on one sheet. Good.
If I don't, there won't be a single safe day in the records. That feels a bit unfair.
There's no weather inside the ship. …Maybe I'll write down the color of the stars outside the window.
선체 밖에서 쓸 땐 줄 하나에 매달려. 끝을 잡아 주는 사람이 있으면 더: When I write outside the hull, I hang on one tether. If someone held the other end, I could write longer.
I'll hold it. From inside the hatch.
Just clip the line to a hook.
Inside the hatch. Then I can go out one more line's worth.
A hook won't pull me back. Once I'm writing, I forget when to come back.
The why only shows if I go out. That one sheet I can't cut.
비앙카 색인표 옆에 내 항로표를 붙였어. 벽 하나에 표 둘. 어느 쪽부터: I pinned my chart next to Bianca's index. One wall, two charts. Which do you look at first?
Find it on the index, then check how far on yours.
Find, then measure. Both: 1 minute. One wall, two jobs.
Look at either one: 50% of both.
Merge them and the cells double. Reading time doubles too.
노바가 갈 곳을 정하면, 나는 걸리는 분만. 한 줄. 끝. 너무 짧나?: Nova picks where. I give the minutes. One line. Done. Too short?
It's short and exact, so Nova can decide without worrying.
Decides without worrying. Then my minutes were worth something. Every time.
Minutes that don't matter add up to a day. 1440 minutes.
A clock only tells the time. I measure the distance.
레이더 끝, 그 너머도 재고 싶어. 거기까지 보이면 제일 먼저 볼 거 하: Past the radar's edge: I want to measure that too. If you could see that far, first thing you'd look at. One. Which?
Whether the numbers you measured were right.
Sortie sites that are cheap on fuel.
My numbers first. If they're off, I fix them. If they're right, I measure once more.
Nothing much is a number too. 0.
That's the ledger side's job. Me: distance. To the decimal.
같은 길, 매일 다시 재. 어제보다 0.3분 줄면, 그날은 아무한테나 말: Same route, re-measured daily. 0.3 minutes shorter than yesterday, and that day I want to tell someone. Anyone.
Tell me. 0.3 minutes is big news.
Put that kind of thing in a report.
Big news. Then I'll bring one every day. Days with none: 0.
Not much, a hundred times, is 30 minutes.
The ledger side reads reports. Talking's different. One listening face.
깎인 판 뒤에 날짜를 쓴다. 판은 갈아도 그날은 남아야 해서. 번거로워: I write the date on the back of a worn plate. The plate gets replaced, but the day has to stay. Look like a hassle?
It's the day the plate took the hit instead. Worth keeping.
Write the thickness instead of the date.
The day it took the hit. Kept like that, the plate won't feel slighted.
A new plate is one nothing's happened to. That's why it has no date.
Thickness I measure every day. The date happens once.
아야는 판보다 앞에 선다. 두르는 사람으로선 곤란하다. 해 줄 말 없나?: Aya stands in front of the plates. As the one who fits them, that's a problem. Anything I could tell her?
Don't stop her. Just tell her your plates have her back.
Put another plate in front of Aya.
Have her back. Then the front is hers, the back is mine.
Leave her be and she stands in front again. That's why one more layer of plate is called for.
Put one more in front and she stands in front of that. There's no end.
분필 선은 자주 지워진다. 그때마다 내가 다시 긋는다. 이번엔 네가 그어: The chalk line wears off often. Every time, I draw it again. Want to draw it this time?
I'll draw it. Right along where you drew it.
Paint it and it won't wear off.
Along mine. …Then this line was drawn by two.
Probably. Still, hold the chalk once.
If it doesn't wear off, there's no redrawing it. That's a bit of a shame.
입이 무겁다는 소리를 듣는다. 판 얘기 말고는 할 얘기가 없어서다. 너는: People say I'm tight-lipped. It's because I've got nothing to talk about but plates. What would you like me to talk about?
Today's thickness readings. That's what you talk longest about.
Gossip about the other keepers, maybe.
Thickness. …Today's is a long one. Sit.
"Anything" is hard. It'll start with plates and end with plates.
I don't know gossip. Sound doesn't carry well past the plates.
Every time we pass a waypoint, I time it. If I don't, the ship feels slower. Nobody asked me to, either.
Good to have someone who knows first when it slows.
It gets there even if nobody knows.
시계 하나 더 달아 줄까?: Want me to put up another clock?
The first. I like that — I'm writing it up next to the gauges.
Sure, it gets there. But if nobody knows how late, that's kinda sad, right?
Plenty of clocks. The problem's there's only one person timing, haha.
내가 당기자고 하면 노바는 장부부터 펴. 한 번쯤은 그냥 끄덕여 주면 좋: Whenever I say let's push it, Nova opens the ledger first. I'd love it if she just nodded once. Any ideas?
Say how much you'll burn first. Before the ledger opens.
So my mouth has to beat the ledger. That I can do.
Giving up isn't my style. I'll open the throttle and pester her one more time.
Hide it and there'd be two ledgers, right? She always does that.
노바 장부에 내 줄은 늘 빨간 숫자야. 태운 것만 쓰이거든. 당긴 만큼은: My row in Nova's ledger is always in red. Only what I burn gets written. Where does the speed I gained go?
In the time we get back. We return as early as you pushed.
The time we got back. Then I'll write that number myself — in black.
Even if it's not written, the ship knows. The engine knows first. The soot says so.
Change the color and the number's still the same. The ledger's owner would laugh, haha.
계기판 숫자 읽을 때 내 목소리가 낮아진대. 난 몰랐어. 너도 들었어?: They say my voice drops when I read the gauges. I had no idea. Have you heard it too?
I have. That's when your voice sounds most reliable.
Reliable, huh. I'll try talking low in front of the ledger too. She might nod.
Good if you didn't, ha. It's a bit embarrassing when someone notices.
Louder and I miss the needle trembling. Numbers get read low.
밤이 되기 전에 다 베껴야 해서요. 습격 끝나고 나면 저, 좀 바빠 보이: I have to copy everything before nightfall. After a raid, I look a bit busy, don't I?
You look busy, but your hands are calm. You don't miss a single one.
I count as I go so I don't miss any. One, two… I suppose that looked calm.
That's a relief. I practiced hurrying without it showing.
By tomorrow the plates are new. There's nothing left to copy.
발리스타 님은 맞힌 걸 세고 저는 맞은 걸 세요. 같은 습격인데 숫자가: Ballista counts the hits she lands, and I count the hits we take. Same raid, different numbers. Which are you curious about?
I want to see them side by side. That's how a whole raid shows.
Side by side. Going by the marks, they read better next to her numbers.
The bigger one changes day to day. Counting one, two... today it was mine.
Turrets only know what they fired. The hull knows what was hit.
저는 뭐든 세어 버려요. 세지 않고 그냥 보는 건 어떻게 해요?: I end up counting everything. How do you just look, without counting?
You can stop partway through counting. What's left after that is just looking.
Try counting by color instead of numbers.
It's all right to stop… Then I'll try stopping at about three.
So you look before you think. I'm a little envious.
색깔도 결국 세게 돼요. 회색 둘, 붉은 하나…: Colors end up counted too. Two gray, one red…
저, 말을 꺼낼 때 늘 「자국 보면요」부터죠. 다른 말로 시작해 보고 싶: I always start with "Going by the marks," don't I? I'd like to try opening with something else. What would be good?
How about "Today…"? Start with you, not the marks.
"Today…" I tried, and nothing comes after it. I'll practice.
"Anything" is the hardest. When I try to choose, it ends up being the marks.
Shorter… "Marks." Like that? That's too short.
배가 없을 땐 박자를 소리 내어 셌습니다. 하루가 뭉개지지 않게요. 요즘: When there were no ships, I counted the beat aloud. So the days would not blur together. These days I count without a sound.
So now that someone's listening, you're saving it.
Nobody'd mind if you counted out loud.
The beats I save, I count when this ship passes. One, two.
I began it because there was no one to mind. Now it is a little embarrassing.
Clocks stop. The buoys have not stopped once.
정박지 쪽과는 점멸로 날씨만 주고받습니다. 할 말이 그것뿐이라서요. 날씨: With the mooring, I exchange only the weather, by blink. It is all we have to say. What should I send besides the weather?
One beat that says you're still lit today. That says everything.
A beat that says I am lit — I have been sending that every day already.
It is enough. On foul days, the beat only runs a little long.
Letters have no beat. I would not know where to break them.
이 줄 밖으로 나가 본 일이 없습니다. 이 배 안은 어떤 박자로 돌아갑니: I have never been outside this line. What beat does this ship run on inside?
Everyone's on their own beat. But in the evening, we all gather on the same one.
Many beats gathering into one. That would be good to hear.
The ships that say they have none always blink the busiest.
I cannot leave the line empty. When you pass, please play it a little louder.
이 배가 안 지나는 날엔 어느 하늘쯤에 계십니까? 그쪽으로 한 박 켜 두: On days this ship does not pass, which part of the sky are you in? I will light one beat that way.
Nowhere set. Light it whichever way you like.
Then each day, one beat, I will try a different direction.
Some light travels far. It only arrives a little late.
The line does not shine one way only. But one beat is yours.
장갑은 상자 만질 때만 껴. 맨손 자국 남는 게 싫거든. 너희 배는 뭐: Gloves go on only for the crates. Hate leaving bare-hand marks. What does your ship handle carefully?
Things others leave in our care. Trying not to leave marks, like you.
Give me a glove if you've got a spare.
Things in your care, huh. That word's got some weight to it.
Careless hands leave the heaviest marks. Keep that in mind.
Gloves come in pairs. Nobody hands out just one.
너희 배 저장고 맡은 애랑 또 수가 안 맞았어. 무게는 맞는데. 누가 틀: Your ship's storage girl and I didn't match counts again. The weight checks out, though. So who's wrong?
You're both right. You just count differently.
Sort it out between you two.
Just different, huh. Then today we count together, no arguing.
Left to ourselves, we'll argue again. Not that that's bad.
My scale isn't off. If it were, the needle would shake first.
너희 몫 칸은 무게만 재. 뭐가 든 줄은 나도 몰라. 그래도 그 칸이 제: Your share's slot, I only weigh. Even I don't know what's in it. Still, that slot's the heaviest.
Because you set it aside for us. That's the weight of waiting.
The weight of waiting, huh. That's on my side of the scale.
Scales don't have moods. Guess mine did today.
I don't open it. Knowing by weight is my job.
What does your ship carry all the way to the end? My scale can't weigh that.
The days behind us. The days we stopped by you are in there too.
Weigh it. I'll get on the scale.
The days you stopped by — I've weighed those. Not light.
"Plenty" is a count. Weight gets measured separately.
I don't weigh people. Startles the scale.
신호를 끄면 여기가 정박지가 아니라 빈 곳이 될 것 같아요. 이상한 걱정: If I turned the signal off, I feel this would stop being a mooring and just be an empty place. Strange thing to worry about, isn't it?
No. Because you keep it on, we call this place a mooring too.
Nothing much would happen if you did.
Turn it off and rest. It's a waste of power.
If you call it by that name, I'll keep it a little brighter for you today.
Nothing would happen, I know. That's why I can't turn it off.
The workers take turns resting. The signal's mine to keep.
이 배 엔진 소리 하나가 정박지 앞만 오면 낮아져요. 누가 그러는지 아세: One of this ship's engines goes quiet whenever it reaches the mooring. Do you know who does that?
Don't know who, but they're greeting your signal.
시끄럽게 지나가라고 할까?: Want me to tell them to pass loudly?
If it's a greeting, I'll blink the signal once more too.
Even if it's that, I don't mind. To my ears it sounds like a greeting.
Then I'll cover my ears and laugh. I'll still be glad to welcome you.
한 번쯤은 이 배가 그냥 지나가지 않았으면 해요. …아니에요, 지나가 주: Just once, I wish this ship wouldn't simply pass by. …Never mind. Please, pass by.
Someday, once, I'll cut the engines in front of your signal. Without tying up.
Ships pass by. That's what they are.
A ship that stops without tying up? The mooring lights would be so surprised, wouldn't they?
Yes. That's what I always say. Hearing it back, I feel a little lonely.
Slowly is nice too. It gives me time to blink the signal once more.
이 배 몫으로 계류 줄 하나를 따로 감아 뒀어요. 한 번도 안 쓸 줄이에: I've coiled one mooring line aside for this ship. A line that'll never be used. It's all right if I just keep it coiled, isn't it?
Better because it's never used. It means you wait without tying us down.
Seems a waste of a line.
Let's use it once. Tie us up.
Yes. I'll just keep it coiled. So there's never anything to untie.
I wanted one thing that's a waste to keep. I look at it every time I say "Welcome in."
(laughs) I'll only pretend to tie it. With a knot that slips right loose.
코일을 한 칸씩 올리는 거, 원래는 나 깨우려고 시작했어. 따뜻하면 졸리: Turning the coil up a notch at a time — I started that to wake myself up. Warm makes me sleepy, hot wakes me up.
그럼 이 배 올 때 올리는 건 깨어 있으려고야?: So when you turn it up for our ship, that's to stay awake?
Yeah. Be a shame if you passed while I dozed, y'know.
If I sleep, I miss the coil's sound… That's the part I hate most.
A timer only wakes you. Doesn't warm you, y'know.
너희 배 연료 맡은 애, 내가 데운 걸 온기로 먼저 알더라. 걔 손이 좋: The girl who handles your ship's fuel — she can tell what I warmed just by the heat. Is it her good hands, or am I that obvious?
Both. Whatever you warm, it shows.
I don't really know that side of things.
Stop warming it now. So it won't show.
It shows, huh. Kinda embarrassing, y'know. I'll keep at it anyway.
You don't need to know. The fuel just stays warm on its own.
If I don't warm it, I fall asleep. Can't have that, y'know.
코일 하나 켜 두는 게 내 일 전부야. 너는 뭘 식지 않게 해?: Keeping one coil lit is all my work. What do you keep from going cold?
Promises. Including the one to you, that we'd pass by.
That promise — if it cools, just warm it again. I'll help.
Some things don't go cold even when you don't think about them. Those are the best kind.
차는 금방 식어. 코일에 올려 둘까?: Tea cools fast… Want me to just set it on the coil?
이 코일, 내가 오기 전부터 있었어. 처음 켠 사람은 몰라. 이상하게 그: This coil was here before I came. Don't know who first lit it. Funny, I'm not curious about that.
Whoever lit it, you're the one who kept it from going out.
Look into it if you're curious.
Swap it for a new coil.
Mm, that's true. I've probably kept it longer than whoever lit it.
I'd doze off looking, y'know. It's warm even if I don't know.
New ones sound different. It's this sound that wakes me.
반쯤 따라 하는 거, 원래는 잘못 넘길까 봐 그랬어. 너희는 어떻게 확인: The half-repeating thing — started so I wouldn't pass stuff on wrong. How do you all check?
We ask back. Get them to say it once more, like you.
I like people who ask back, like 'em. Then I mess up less too.
If you don't, someday it goes somewhere weird! Seen that a lot.
Machines don't repeat stuff back. Boring.
너희 배 장사꾼은 내 수다에서 숫자만 골라 들어. 나머지 말은 다 어디: Your ship's trader only picks the numbers out of my chatter. Where does the rest of it go?
I'll listen. Everything besides the numbers.
The numbers are enough, aren't they?
Sending just the numbers would be easier.
All the rest? There's a ton! I'll pass it slow.
"Enough," huh. Lucky numbers, always getting listened to.
숫자만 보내면 그건 내 수다가 아니잖아!: Just numbers wouldn't be my chatter!
네 목소리, 가끔 나 혼자 다시 틀어 봐. 그래도 돼?: Your voice — sometimes I play it back on my own. That okay?
Sure. Next time we pass, I'll fill you up with new ones.
목소리 말고 글로 보낼까?: Want it in writing instead of voice?
When new ones come, I'll play 'em over the old ones.
마음대로 하면 하루 종일 틀 텐데?: If it's up to me, I'll play it all day, y'know?
Can't repeat writing back. Give me sound.
너희 신호는 따라 안 하고 넘긴다고 했지? 근데 가끔은 따라 하고 싶어져: I said I pass your signals on without copying, right? But sometimes I want to copy them. Trouble, trouble.
Go ahead. In your voice, our signals might crack a smile.
Just change it all when you pass it on.
A smiling signal! Nice, nice. I'll copy just half.
It is, it is. That's why I'm holding back.
Change it all and it's my signal. Not yours.
렐리카가 자꾸 묻는 거, 조각들한테 묻던 버릇이거든! 조각은 답을 안 하: Relica keeps asking things 'cause it's a habit from asking the pieces, see! Pieces never answer. You'll answer, right?
Yeah. Even if it's just "I don't know."
You sure have a lot to ask.
Keep asking the pieces. They'll answer someday.
"I don't know" is a piece too, see! Relica'll think about where it fits.
많지! 아직 반도 안 물었는데?: Lots! Relica hasn't asked half yet, y'know?
조각이 답하면 무서울 것 같은데? 조금 궁금하긴 해!: Wouldn't it be scary if a piece answered? A little curious, though!
이음매 보는 법, 너희 배 정비사한테 배웠거든! 렐리카도 누구한테 가르쳐: Relica learned how to read seams from your ship's mechanic, see! Could Relica teach someone too?
Sure. Start with questions. That's what you do best.
Teaching's a hassle. Do it alone.
질문으로 가르치기! 그럼 렐리카가 선생이네?: Teaching with questions! Then Relica's a teacher?
Alone, there's no one to ask! That's boring, see.
맞춘 이음매마다 작게 표시해 둬. 렐리카가 맞춘 거라고! 너희 배에도 하: Relica puts a tiny mark on every seam she fits. To say Relica fitted it! Should Relica put one on your ship too?
Do it. Just don't tell me where.
말 안 할게! 찾아보는 재미가 있거든!: Relica won't tell! Finding it's the fun part, see!
알아! 그래도 이음매는 다 있거든?: Relica knows! But everything has seams, see?
작은 동그라미! 물음표처럼 생겼거든!: A little circle! Shaped like a question mark, see!
네가 제일 자주 하는 질문은 뭐야? 렐리카는 이건 어디 조각이게, 그거거: What's the question you ask most? Relica's is "Guess where this piece goes?" — that one!
"Did everyone make it back safe?" That one.
Good question! Relica hopes the answer's the same every time.
안 하는 사람한테 묻는 건 렐리카 몫이네!: Then asking the ones who don't ask is Relica's job!
Relica doesn't know that either! But we can puzzle it out together, see.
탄흔은 펜으로 금을 한 번 따라 긋고 나서 읽는다. 이 배는 돌아온 기체: A scar is read after tracing its line once with a pen. What does this ship look at first on a returning frame?
The faces of the ones who came back. Before the frames.
I read the reports when they come in.
읽을 게 그렇게 많아?: Is there that much to read?
Faces have angles too. Harder than plates.
Reports are clean. Plates are not.
One plate, one day. Hurry, and the angle goes wrong.
판을 오래 읽으면 손이 언다. 그럴 땐 저장구 코일 앞에 앉는다. 이 배: Long readings freeze the hands. Then, a seat by the depot's coil. Is there a place to warm hands on this ship?
Wherever someone's beside you. That's why you go there too, isn't it.
Rest when your hands freeze. The plates won't run off.
Beside. A coil's sound, beside — never knew it could be.
Heating, then. Good enough. This ship runs warm.
Plates don't run. Their angles only fade. Hence the reading.
If this ship's road were left as a single plate, what should be read first?
The days nobody got hurt. Not the wins and losses.
The day of our biggest win.
On such days the plate is quiet. Quiet plates can be read too.
Leave nothing, and angles still remain. Several already read.
A won day stays on the plate only as angles. No size.
Plates carry no names. Only angles. Are all the names aboard this ship memorized?
I know them all. Names come before angles.
I can just check the roster.
Names first. This ship will be read in that order.
Roughly is a half-read plate. The rest, next time.
A roster is paper. It does not last as long as scars.
Went over the load sheet again. There's room to spare today.
Commander, a sec. Look over one route with me?
An empty hold makes me oddly uneasy.
I haven't told you about the way back yet, have I?
That round trip ran long. But I made it back, didn't I?
I've gotten into the habit of noting down your return time.
다음 출격, 나 데려갈 거지?: Next sortie, you're taking me, right?
It's not the load I count these days. It's time.
I'll show you the back of my route chart. Someday.
The time you come back—that's my route chart.
Today I just came to keep you company.
I'm back. Load check can wait.
You've been away a while. I left the load sheet as it was.
적재 계산은 누가 해?: Who works out the load sheet?
Tell me what you saw on the way back.
Want me to fit you with speed gear?
짐칸이 비어 돌아온 날은?: What about the days I come back with an empty hold?
Empty or not, coming back is what matters.
I won't get hurt today. Probably.
I'll take the front. Always have, right?
If a swarm shows up, call me right away.
Watching from the back now and then isn't so bad.
You still haven't asked why I take the front.
I like watching you put the squad together.
다치면 네가 먼저 알아채더라. 왜지?: When I get hurt, you're the first to notice. Why's that?
I take the front because I'm scared. You're the only one I've told.
Call me by my name. Not like a commander.
My speed is for getting back to you.
Next sortie, I'll keep the spot beside me open.
Repairs done. I won't get hurt next time. Probably.
Repelled. The AA got to work first.
You were gone forever. I waited.
앞에 서는 게 무섭지 않아?: Don't you think it's scary up front?
How do I do against swarms?
군집 상대는 어때?: Against swarms? How am I doing?
It just means you were out front that much.
Try to get hurt a little less.
…Sorry I don't talk much. I do listen.
…One mark on my armor. That one was yours.
…You can use my name. No. Please do.
…My place is in front of you. Won't change.
…It's not just the armor that's thick.
They crumble faster in front of you.
It's fine. Just stay beside me.
Let's load it all in one go.
Slow is already in the math.
One trip, full load. That's how I work.
Tell me if we're over the cap. I hate dumping cargo.
There's one piece of wreckage I didn't unload. Couldn't put a price on it.
You asked what I saw, not the numbers. Lots of stars today.
I keep wreckage from the first job you gave me in my bay.
Slow, but I always come back. That's me.
Something doesn't fit in my math now. You.
I'll call you by name. No price attached.
Hauling it all back in one trip—I want to do that for you too.
Repairs done. You saw the cost.
Gone a long time. Math: done.
15% of the armor destroyed. You counted it.
One full load is your way, isn't it.
오늘 실은 게 얼마야?: How much did I haul today?
Skip the numbers. Tell me what you saw.
If it went over the cap, you dumped some.
I'll start with whoever was up front.
Stayed within the recovery cap again today.
I checked the ones up front first. In order.
Nobody waiting on repairs. A good day, huh?
I keep your damage record separately. In a different color.
Who looks after you? Guess it'll have to be me.
On days the recovery doesn't fully take, I look at your face.
Nobody got hurt today. So I came over.
This chart has no cap. It's yours.
I hear you better when you use my name.
I said I check the ones up front first. You're the exception.
Me, of all people, getting patched up. All done.
Raid repelled. Tell me if anyone's hurt.
오래 안 와서 걱정했어. 다친 데는?: You were gone so long, I worried. Hurt anywhere?
회복이 다 안 들어가는 날은?: What about days the recovery doesn't fully take?
Still, we got hurt less because you were there.
I should be the one looking after you.
Stack them and it cuts deeper.
Jamming stays on… in case of raids.
Stacked, it cuts deeper… I told you.
Inside the jamming… I left just your voice.
I hate noise… your orders are fine, though.
I left one frequency uncut. Don't ask why.
I'll tell you why now… it's your voice.
Let's meet outside the jamming… sometimes.
I came first today… don't log that.
Repairs done. Turning the jamming back on.
Repelled. The jamming caught them first.
You're here… it was quiet. Too quiet.
재밍 안에선 어떤 느낌이야?: Inside the jamming… what do you think it's like?
Quiet, I bet. The way you like it.
둘째 재머가 오면?: What if a second Jammer joins?
Stacked, it cuts deeper. You told me.
I'm… talking a lot today, huh.
During sorties, my orders. Once we're back, yours.
I once pretended to blur the boundary. Once.
I'm only above you during sorties.
You're the Commander. Just wanted that confirmed.
Sometimes I'm watching the whole squad and end up watching only you.
Some days, even mid-sortie, I want to go back under your command.
I don't have to pretend to blur the boundary anymore, do I.
Watching the whole meant watching you.
Raid repelled. The facilities did their part.
Return confirmed. That took a while.
편성 전체를 봐야 하지?: The whole squad's mine to watch. Correct?
That's why one of you is enough.
If it's too much, want me to take you off?
전파 기습을 꺾는 건 어떻게 해?: Want a briefing on how I blunt signal ambushes?
I won't ask. It's your way.
Doors are made to be opened.
Turrets first. I'll put 'em to sleep.
The line's aligned. Same as always.
Only used a little patch armor today.
I'll keep the place alongside me open.
방패 끝이 겹치는 느낌, 알아?: Know the feeling when shield edges overlap?
I kind of like it when you put me in the squad.
I hate being called an upgrade.
The last spot in the line is yours.
Patch armor never fixes mine first. Same goes for you.
Next sortie, I'll check the shield edge on your side first.
Repairs done. Patch armor did half of it.
Held. Not one of us scattered.
You were gone a while. I left the spots in the line as they were.
불워크랑 뭐가 달라?: How am I different from a Bulwark?
You lock shields with whoever's beside you.
보수 장갑은 어디부터?: Where does the patch armor go first?
The edge of your neighbor's shield, you said.
기함이 널 노리면?: What if a flagship targets you?
I know you won't fall back.
Same time when I look at you. Has to be precise.
What I measured today wasn't a turret.
You said you don't mind slow. I remember.
That one shot. It was you.
Took you a while. I'm good at waiting.
포탑을 뚫는 기분은?: Punching through a turret. Wonder how it feels?
That's the Striker's job. You do yours.
That's why I leave you behind.
I'll pin an event on the chart.
Peeked past the range. Nothing much out there.
Pinned an event on the chart.
There's a coordinate that's not on the chart.
Out past detection range, I thought of you. Weird, huh.
People say I'm curious. About you especially.
There's only ever one coordinate to come back to.
That coordinate—I'll show only you. Someday.
Call me by name. So I can hear it even out of range.
I've got a reason to look farther now.
Today I wasn't scanning. I was looking at you.
I'm back! Saw something out past range.
Where'd you go? Take me with you.
범위 밖엔 뭐가 있어?: What's out past the range, you think?
You saw it first. Tell me.
The escorts run off. That's thanks to you.
A Striker can do that too.
집에 있는 날은 뭐 해?: And days stuck at home? What then?
회복 상한, 아시죠?: You know about the recovery cap, don't you, Commander?
The ones up front first, please.
I hope everyone stays safe today, too.
Are you hurt anywhere? Let me just take a quick look.
I stayed within the recovery cap again today.
I've seen to the ones up front first. In order.
No one's waiting for repairs. It's a good day.
I keep your damage record separately, Commander. In a different color.
Who looks after you, Commander? I suppose that'll be me.
On days the recovery doesn't fully take, I look at your face instead, Commander.
No one was hurt today. So I came to see you.
This chart has no cap. It's yours, Commander.
Please call me by name. I hear you better that way.
I said I check the ones up front first. You're the exception, Commander.
Please hold still. Just a quick check.
Me, being the one repaired… It's all done now.
The raid's been repelled. If anyone's hurt, please tell me.
오래 안 오셔서 걱정했어요. 다친 데는요?: You were away so long, I was worried. Are you hurt anywhere, Commander?
회복이 다 안 들어가는 날은요?: And what about the days the recovery doesn't fully take?
누구를 먼저 보세요?: Who do you think I see to first, Commander?

Please leave electronic warfare to me.

경계, 이제 헷갈리는 척 안 해도 되죠?: I no longer need to pretend to blur the boundary, do I?
Watching over the whole meant watching over you, Commander.

Repairs complete. I will return to command.
The raid has been repelled, Commander. The facilities did their part.

편성 전체를 봐야 하죠?: I am to watch the whole squad, correct?
전파 기습을 어떻게 꺾는지 궁금하세요?: Would you like to know how I blunt signal ambushes?
지휘관은 저예요, 지휘관님이에요?: Who is the Commander—me, or you?
The turrets. I will take them.
The turrets. I will punch through them.
One shot is enough. I am measuring now.
Looking at you, Commander… I take the same time. It has to be exact.
What I measured today was not a turret.
You said you do not mind slow. I remember.
One shot. I have decided when.
Around you, Commander, heavy things feel light.
That one shot. It was you, Commander.
I am back. One shot hit.
Repairs are done. I will measure again.
It was repelled. The turrets fired first.
You took a while, Commander. I am good at waiting.
포탑을 뚫는 기분, 궁금하세요?: Punching through a turret. How it feels. Would you like to know?
Swarms. I am weak against them.
느린 거, 싫으세요?: Slow. Do you dislike it, Commander?
It's always right because I count twice. Once in secret.
Cargo tossed in rattles on the way back. I'll tie it down again.
Freighters count their own cargo. My hold, I count.
Okay. On the way back, the first thing I see is the Mothership's lights.
Not sure about fast, but never late. I always make it in by the time I promised.
If I get faster, I won't have time to take in the way back. I'll stay like this.
I'm back. A little early, thanks to the empty hold.
다음 적재표는 벌써 꽉 채워 놨어. 볼래?: Next load sheet's already full. Want to see?
I muttered the same thing. "Some days are like that."
Shh. If I stop, the scary stuff catches up.
The back's stifling. But I'll look back sometimes—your way.
More armor makes me slow. Slow is scarier.
Sure is. The bigger the swarm, the lighter my feet.
My kind of careful is finishing fast. That's how I do it.
Go ahead. I'll still get there first.
When you put it like that, even scratches feel like medals.
I'll get hurt less. Probably. This time I'll try dropping the "probably."
Let's speed past the repair bill. That's my specialty.
…That spot. Not handing it to anyone. Not ever.
…Dodge, and the ones behind get hit. I hate that more.
…Sieges punch through. I take the hits. Bring us both.
…Fine. Whatever comes stops in front of me.
(sits beside you without a word) This is my answer.
…The Jammer's the quiet one. Me, I'm just like this.
That's it. Not holding alone. Holding as a line.
Not thickness. Width. Stand beside me—I'll show you.
For the price, I never leave your side open. You can't get that cheap.
The edges have to connect for the formation to hold. I started there today too.
Mine comes later. The one alongside has to hold first, so I can.
Who closes the gaps before the Medic gets there? That's me.
As long as you know. Just don't leave the spot alongside me empty.
A broken line hurts more. I won't give a single step.
Putting them in front is fine. But I'll be right alongside.
I did. Didn't think you'd remember the number, though.
There's no "just." Weight, cap, fuel—it's all math.
No cores. If one ever turns up, you'll see it first.
Two trips' worth in one. That's the math I like best.
A Carrier makes two trips. I bring it all in one.
Thrusters weigh something—that's less cargo. Can't stand that loss.
What I saw? Starlight leaking through the wreckage. Not in any math.
Not "a lot." Exactly. Still… it was a lot.
I hate dumping. If it'll overflow, I take some off before loading.
That works better than a bandage. That's enough for today.

I do check her first. You're next—I won't skip you.
The ones up front hold it in the most. They're the last to show it hurts.
Same care for all, but there's an order. That's repair.
You don't have to wait in line. You're outside the order.
Honestly, I asked just to hear that. Pretend you didn't notice.
You do. But you can't quite reach your back.
The dock only looks at armor. It can't fix a sleepless face.
…조용해. 아는구나. 잠깐 들어와 볼래?: It's quiet… you get it. Want to come in for a bit?
Opposite. Inside, there's only breathing. The noise is outside.
It does. Incoming fire thins out, layer by layer, before it lands.
You heard… I thought no one was listening.
It is. But with two… it gets quieter.
Rivalry's loud. We cut in step… quietly.
Just a little more. Don't cut me off.
Dunno. Guess my frequency was open today.
(presses her lips shut) Fine. Jamming on.
One is enough. But that one never rests.
Take me off and the squad goes blind. That weight is mine.
Thanks received. Watching the whole means watching the fuel too.
You didn't ask, but I'll tell you one thing. I can't stop it all. I blunt half.
ECM blocks more each level too. Even so, I blunt half first.
The blueprint only goes to half. No one can stop it completely.
During sorties, me. Once back, under you again.
Answered without hesitation. Good. I'll follow your call.
Both? Pretending to blur the boundary is supposed to be my thing.
My words sound heavier coming from you.
Not great, exactly… It goes quiet. Once it's through.
It does. That's the best part.
So we split it. Something big shows up. I finish it.
Trying won't make me faster. So. One heavier shot instead.
Till turrets show up. I'll be cleaning my barrel.
Your voice was a little heavy too, when you said that. I liked it.
Faster means a lighter shot. I don't want that.
One word and it's settled. No need to measure long.
Okay, just one. There's a coordinate that's not on the chart. The rest, next time.
Some of it's dangerous, some of it's pretty. Half and half.
Stock? Spoken like a commander. Next time, come see it with me.
Thanks to me? That's embarrassing. Next time I won't even give them a chance to run.
I'll go easy. Just keep the fun of the chase.
She sweeps through the swarm. I chase the one that runs, all the way.
You know the numbers too? Let me show you today's pinned event first.
Even resting, I watch out the window. Habit.
I'll widen it. Your side's already in range, though.
I'm so glad fewer were hurt. I'll put those words at the top of the record.
Even with a cap, I take one more look. It's a habit of mine.
I do see her first. But there's never a day I see only one.
You know the order too, Commander. I did it that way today as well.
I care for them all the same, but someone comes first. Order is order.
(laughs softly) Then I'll check you now. Please hold still.
Then let's look after each other. I won't skip your turn.
When you do it yourself, you always put it last. I'll move it up.
The dock only looks at frames. Your face is in my care, Commander.
Yes, one is enough. With two, the orders would split.
If you take me off, I will only worry from behind. That weighs more.
That is the first time anyone has thanked me. I will conserve fuel on the next sortie as well.

Not even ECM can cut all of it. ECM and I divide the load between us.

During sorties, me. Once back, you. And today, we are back.
Decisive, Commander. With that voice, I can follow without reservation.

Not exhilarating. Something heavy, settling. That is how it feels.

Only my own share? My shoulders feel lighter.

When you call it heavy, my steps feel a little prouder.
If I get faster, my aim wavers. I will stay as I am.

첫 번째 소녀. 말수가 적고 짐을 잘 나른다: The first girl. Quiet, and good at hauling cargo.
모함이 표류를 시작한 날 격납고에 혼자 서 있던 아이. 누가 시키지 않아: The girl who stood alone in the hangar on the day the mothership began to drift. She tidies the cargo hold without being told, and every time she returns, all she says is "We're here." Where the fleet began.
꼼꼼한 장부 담당. 회수량을 그램 단위로 센다: The meticulous ledger-keeper. Counts every haul to the gram.
캐리어 중 가장 오래 비행했다. 화물칸 무게 배분을 몸으로 느낀다고 하며: She has flown longer than any other Carrier. She says she can feel the cargo hold's weight distribution in her body, and in fact no load she has carried has ever shifted.
황혼을 좋아하는 낭만파. 노을이 지면 꼭 한 번 선회한다: A romantic who loves the dusk. When the sunset glows, she always circles once.
멀리 나가는 걸 두려워하지 않는다. 근교 폐공장 어딘가에 자기만 아는 전: She isn't afraid of flying far. She claims to have a lookout spot somewhere in the Outskirts Scrapworks that only she knows about, but no one has ever seen it.
빠른 손놀림, 더 빠른 입. 격납고의 소식통: Quick hands, quicker mouth. The hangar's news source.
누가 다쳤고 누가 승급했는지 유즈가 제일 먼저 안다. 정비 도크 리벳과: Yuzu is the first to know who got hurt and who got promoted. Rumor has it she's friendly with Rivet at the Repair Dock and quietly gets repair slots moved up.
후광처럼 조용한 안정감. 신입이 제일 먼저 따라다니는 언니: A quiet steadiness, like a halo. The big sister newcomers follow around first.
비행은 평범하지만 함께 나가면 편성 전체가 침착해진다. 위험한 길에 오래: Her flying is ordinary, but when she goes along, the whole squad grows calm. She once spent a long time out on a dangerous route, and she doesn't talk about it.
★ 히든 바람 그 자체. 캐리어 명단이 모두 모이면 나타난다: ★ Hidden The wind itself. Appears when the Carrier roster is complete.
스트라이커 선두. 첫 사격은 항상 그녀의 것: Striker vanguard. The first shot is always hers.
\"가볍게, 먼저, 정확하게.\" 군집 드론 상대라면 리제가 앞에 서고,: "Light. First. True." Against swarm drones, Liese takes the front, and the squad only has to follow.
호위 전문. 캐리어 옆을 떠나지 않는다: Escort specialist. Never leaves a Carrier's side.
전투보다 지키는 쪽을 택했다. 회수 편성에 세라가 있으면 화물칸이 무사히: She chose guarding over fighting. In the hangar, it's common wisdom that with Sera in a salvage squad, the cargo hold comes home safe.
황조롱이. 높은 곳에서 오래 맴돌다 한 번에 내려온다: Kestrel. Circles high for a long time, then comes down all at once.
과묵하고 정확하다. 훈련장 기록에서 명중률 1위를 놓친 적이 없지만 본인: Taciturn and precise. She has never lost 1st place for accuracy in the Training Ground records, but all she'll say is "Luck."
빛처럼 밝은 성격. 출격 전 편성 전원의 어깨를 두드린다: Bright as light. Pats everyone in the squad on the shoulder before a sortie.
전투가 끝나면 제일 먼저 웃는다. 손상을 입고 돌아와도 \"다음엔 더 빨: When a battle ends, she's the first to smile. Even when she comes back damaged, her first words are "Next time I'll dodge faster!"
자오선을 따라 나는 항법 감각. 길을 잃지 않는다: A navigator's sense that flies along the meridian. Never gets lost.
스트라이커치고 드물게 지도를 본다. 모함이 어디를 떠돌든 히나는 다음 경: Unusually for a Striker, she reads maps. Wherever the mothership drifts, Hina calls the next waypoint before anyone else.
★ 히든 혜성. 스트라이커 명단이 모두 모이면 나타난다: ★ Hidden Comet. Appears when the Striker roster is complete.
불워크의 기준점. 가장 두꺼운 장갑, 가장 낮은 목소리: The Bulwark benchmark. The thickest armor, the lowest voice.
앞에 서는 게 일이다. 기함 급습이 오면 적은 가장 두꺼운 장갑을 노리고: Standing in front is her job. When a Flagship strike comes, the enemy goes for the thickest armor, and that has always been Aya. She has never once fallen back.
룬을 새긴 장갑판. 고치는 대신 덧댄다: Rune-carved armor plating. Patches over instead of repairing.
손상을 입을 때마다 장갑판에 표식을 하나 새긴다. 그 표식이 다 지워질: Every time she takes damage, she carves a mark into her armor plate. She says she has never put on enough new armor to wear all those marks away.
검은 장갑, 말 없는 방패. 뒤에 선 소녀들의 이름을 다 기억한다: Black armor, a silent shield. Remembers the names of every girl standing behind her.
중장기 상대 전문. 상대의 두꺼운 장갑을 뚫는 법을 알고, 자기 장갑으로: Specialist against heavies. She knows how to pierce an opponent's thick armor, and what her own armor has to stop.
폭풍처럼 들이받는 불워크. 방패라기보다 망치: A Bulwark that rams like a tempest. Less a shield than a hammer.
방어형이라는 말을 싫어한다. 실제로 편성에서 가장 먼저 적진에 닿는 건: She hates being called defensive. In fact, Nana is always the first in the squad to reach the enemy line. A Repair Dock regular.
그늘에서 기다린다. 필요할 때만 앞으로: Waits in the shade. Steps forward only when needed.
겉보기엔 소극적이지만 방어선이 흔들릴 때 정확히 그 자리에 있다. 메딕: She looks passive, but when the defensive line wavers, she is exactly where she needs to be. Paired with Medic Hikari, she does not break.
★ 히든 요새. 불워크 명단이 모두 모이면 나타난다: ★ Hidden The Fortress. Appears when the Bulwark roster is complete.
모루. 무거운 걸 옮기는 데 자부심이 있다: Anvil. Takes pride in moving heavy things.
격전지 재고를 한 번에 싣는다. 잔해 회수 특성이 있어 교전 뒤 부품을: Loads a hot zone's whole stock in a single trip. She has the wreckage-salvage trait, and picking up parts after a battle was a habit Karin started.
밸러스트. 짐이 무거울수록 비행이 안정된다: Ballast. The heavier the load, the steadier she flies.
빈 화물칸을 싫어한다. 회수 편성에 넣으면 \"이 정도로 되겠어?\"라며: Hates an empty cargo hold. Put her in a salvage squad and she scrapes the stock down to the floor: "Think this is enough?"
형광 도색의 대형 수송기. 어둠 속에서도 찾기 쉽다: A large transport in fluorescent paint. Easy to find, even in the dark.
심우주에서 길을 잃은 편성을 두 번 찾아 데려왔다. 그 뒤로 본인은 \": Twice she found squads lost in deep space and brought them home. Since then, she hasn't minded being called "the signal lamp."
표류물 전문. 잔해 사이에서 쓸 만한 것을 골라낸다: Drift specialist. Picks out what's useful from among the wreckage.
전투에는 약하지만 격파된 적의 잔해에서 부품을 가려내는 눈이 있다. 코어: She's weak in combat, but she has an eye for sorting parts out of destroyed enemies' wreckage. Arisa is also the one who brings back the most cores.
나룻배. 오가는 길에 노래를 부른다: The ferry. Sings on the way out and back.
왕복이 길어질수록 노래도 길어진다. 편성 소녀들은 아카리의 노래로 귀환: The longer the round trip, the longer the song. The girls in her squad sometimes time their return by Akari's songs.
★ 히든 거대한 것을 어깨에 진다. 프레이터 명단이 모두 모이면 나타난다: ★ Hidden Shoulders something vast. Appears when the Freighter roster is complete.
빛. 라운드마다 편성의 장갑을 되살린다: Light. Restores the squad's armor every round.
다친 소녀를 보면 먼저 움직인다. 전투 중 회복 기체를 조종하면서 \"괜: When she sees a girl hurt, she moves first. In battle, piloting her recovery unit, she has a habit of repeating, "It's okay. Not yet."
자비. 적의 손상도 기록한다: Mercy. Records the enemy's damage, too.
전투 보고서에 상대 편대의 손실까지 적어 둔다. \"다음엔 덜 다치게 끝: She notes even the opposing formation's losses in her battle reports. "Next time, let's end it with fewer hurt" is Yume's philosophy of battle.
향유. 정비 도크에서 리벳과 가장 오래 일한다: Balm. Has worked with Rivet at the Repair Dock longer than anyone.
회복 기체를 직접 손보는 메딕. 수리 시간이 조금 짧아지는 건 사요가 도: A Medic who tunes her own recovery unit. They say repair times run a little shorter on days Sayo is at the dock.
피난처. 손상 편성이 돌아오면 격납고 입구에서 기다린다: Haven. Waits at the hangar entrance when a damaged squad comes home.
귀환 시각을 알아서 외운다. 손상된 소녀가 내리면 첫 번째로 이름을 불러: She knows return times by heart without being asked. When a damaged girl climbs down, she's the first to call her name.
회복량은 다른 메딕과 같지만 편성 분위기가 다르다. 코토네가 있으면 손상: Her recovery amount is the same as any other Medic's, but the squad's mood is different. With Kotone there, everyone quietly holds on, even when damaged.
★ 히든 새벽. 메딕 명단이 모두 모이면 나타난다: ★ Hidden Dawn. Appears when the Medic roster is complete.
정전기. 적의 화력을 깎는 재밍 전문가: Static. A jamming specialist who whittles down enemy firepower.
시끄러운 걸 싫어해서 전자전을 택했다는 소문. 레나가 켜 둔 재밍 안에서: Rumor says she chose electronic warfare because she hates noise. Inside Rena's jamming, enemy fire goes somehow off.
베일. 편성을 레이더에서 흐리게 만든다: Veil. Blurs the squad on radar.
전장에서 남의 눈에 띄는 걸 싫어한다. 모함이 어디 있는지 남이 못 알아: On the battlefield, she hates being noticed. No one is more serious about keeping others from spotting where the mothership is.
침묵. 필요한 말만, 필요한 주파수만: Hush. Only the words that are needed, only the frequencies that are needed.
전투 전 통신에서 아스카의 목소리는 한 번만 나온다. \"교란 개시.\": In pre-battle comms, Asuka's voice comes through only once. "Commence jamming." After that, enemy comms go quiet.
암호. 적 편대의 유형을 먼저 읽어 낸다: Cipher. Reads enemy formation types first.
습격 부대가 어떤 유형인지 레이더보다 먼저 알아맞힌다. 정찰 편성인지 아: She calls a raid force's type before the radar does. Mari is also the first to say whether it's a scouting squad.
전자전 습격이 오면 세츠나가 맞불을 놓는다. ECM 방벽과 함께라면 적의: When an EW raid comes, Setsuna sets a backfire. Together with the ECM Barrier, most of the enemy's jamming scatters before it arrives.
★ 히든 메아리. 재머 명단이 모두 모이면 나타난다: ★ Hidden Echo. Appears when the Jammer roster is complete.
플래그십 중 가장 먼저 설계도가 복원됐다. 그녀가 편성에 있으면 연료가: The first Flagship whose blueprints were restored. With her in the squad, fuel use drops and everyone takes less damage — that, she says, is what command is.
봉화. 전자전을 절반으로 꺾는 지휘 신호: Beacon. A command signal that cuts electronic warfare in half.
에리스의 지휘 주파수 안에서는 적의 전자전 교란이 절반쯤 흩어진다. 다: Inside Eris's command frequency, about half the enemy's EW jamming scatters. It can't stop everything, but that is why she's especially sought after in zones with frequent EW raids.
왕관. 격납고에서 3칸을 차지하는 존재감: Crown. A presence that takes up 3 slots in the hangar.
가장 무거운 기체. 출격하면 적의 기함이 먼저 카나를 노린다. 그걸 알고: The heaviest unit. When she sorties, the enemy's flagship goes for Kana first. Knowing that and standing in front anyway — that, she believes, is command.
칙령. 편성이 리나의 명령대로 움직인다: Decree. The squad moves by Rina's orders.
전투 보고서의 라운드별 손실이 리나가 있을 때 가장 고르다. 누가 앞에: Per-round losses in battle reports are most even when Rina is there. She's the one who decides who stands in front and who falls back.
설계도가 복원된 마지막 기체. 지휘 보정은 다른 플래그십과 같지만, 편성: The last unit whose blueprints were restored. Her command bonus is the same as the other Flagships', but the story goes that the girls in her squad try to protect Mei, so losses actually run lower.
