★ 히든 여제. 플래그십 명단이 모두 모이면 나타난다: ★ Hidden Empress. Appears when the Flagship roster is complete.
성벽 파쇄. 요새 포탑을 첫 라운드에 무너뜨린다: Rampart-breaker. Brings down fortress turrets in the first round.
시설 상대 화력 ×2. 요새 잔해에 편성이 막힐 때 키라를 넣으면 포탑이: Firepower ×2 vs facilities. When a squad gets stuck at the Fortress Ruins, put Kira in, and the turrets go silent first.
일제 사격. 느리지만 한 번에 크게: Salvo. Slow, but big, all at once.
기동은 느리다. 대신 시즈 포가 한 번 울리면 기함의 장갑에도 구멍이 난: Her maneuvering is slow. But when her Siege cannon booms once, even a flagship's armor gets a hole in it. Swarm drones she leaves to other girls.
박격. 곡사로 시설 뒤를 친다: Mortar. Hits behind facilities with arcing fire.
정면에서 보이지 않는 곳을 노린다. 방어 포탑이 많은 출격지에서 미레이의: She aims for what can't be seen head-on. At sortie sites thick with defense turrets, Mirei's fire always comes from an unexpected angle.
성채. 시즈 중 가장 두꺼운 마음가짐: Citadel. The thickest resolve among the Siege girls.
시즈는 장갑이 얇다. 유나는 그걸 알고도 기함 앞에 서기를 자청한다. 습: Siege girls have thin armor. Yuna knows that and volunteers to stand in front of the flagship anyway. She has blocked two Flagship strikes in raids.
파쇄자. 이름이 짧은 만큼 사격도 짧고 강하다: Breaker. As short as her name, her shots are short and strong.
신입 시즈. 말이 없고 기록만 남긴다 — 격파한 시설 수를 기체에 새겨: A new Siege girl. Says nothing and leaves only records — she carves the count of facilities she has destroyed into her unit, already on the second row.
★ 히든 종말의 포성. 시즈 명단이 모두 모이면 나타난다: ★ Hidden The Doomsday Knell. Appears when the Siege roster is complete.
벡터. 편성이 가는 길의 방향을 잡는다: Vector. Sets the heading of the squad's path.
정찰 전문. 니나가 편성에 있으면 레이더가 닿지 않는 출격지의 적도 미리: Recon specialist. With Nina in the squad, even the enemies at sortie sites beyond radar range can be seen in advance.
나침반. 심연 회랑의 깊이를 재는 눈: Compass. An eye that gauges the depths of the Abyss Corridor.
심연 티어 보상을 더 끌어내는 감각이 있다. 어디에 무엇이 남아 있는지: She has a knack for drawing more rewards out of the Abyss tiers. She claims she can smell what's left, and where.
육분의. 별을 보고 모함의 위치를 안다: Sextant. Knows the mothership's position by the stars.
모함이 어디를 떠돌든 모모는 좌표를 외운다. 전장 지도의 좌표 표시는 모: Wherever the mothership drifts, Momo memorizes the coordinates. The story goes that the coordinate readouts on the battlefield map are numbers Momo reads out.
발자국. 남이 안 간 길을 먼저 밟는다: Footprints. First to tread paths no one has taken.
버려진 기함의 위치를 처음 보고한 게 아즈사였다. 그 뒤로 위험 구역에: Azusa was the first to report the Abandoned Flagship's location. Since then, the squad calls on Azusa first when entering danger zones.
등불. 어두운 회랑에서 편성을 이끈다: Lantern. Leads the squad through dark corridors.
심연 회랑 깊은 티어에서 치카의 기체 등불이 꺼진 적은 없다. 꺼지면 돌: In the deep tiers of the Abyss Corridor, the lantern on Chika's unit has never gone out. Everyone knows that if it did, there would be no way back.
★ 히든 북극성. 패스파인더 명단이 모두 모이면 나타난다: ★ Hidden Polaris. Appears when the Pathfinder roster is complete.
첫 번째 브리처. 문 앞에서 서두르지 않는다: The first Breacher. Never hurries at the door.
방벽을 여는 일은 부수는 일과 다르다고 했다. 포탑이 먼저 쏘지 못하게: Opening a barrier is different from breaking it, she said. The time it takes to keep the turrets from firing first is always the same — it's the time she counts.
지렛대 하나로 대부분을 연다: Opens most things with a single crowbar.
필요한 힘은 생각보다 작다고 말한다. 어디에 걸 것인지가 전부라고. 실패: She says the force needed is smaller than you'd think. That where you set it is everything. Ask whether she has ever failed, and she doesn't answer.
걸쇠 담당. 소리로 잠금 상태를 읽는다: Latch keeper. Reads a lock's state by sound.
금고 앞에 귀를 대고 한참 있는다. 다른 브리처들은 그 시간을 기다려 준: She puts her ear to a vault and stays there a long while. The other Breachers wait for her. When she nods, the door is already as good as open.
틈을 찾는 눈. 가장 빠르다: An eye for gaps. The fastest.
벽에서 약한 자리를 먼저 본다. 완벽한 방벽은 없다고 했다 — 있다면 그: She sees a wall's weak spot first. There's no perfect barrier, she said — if there is, it's one she hasn't looked at yet.
열쇠 구멍 너머를 상상한다: Imagines what lies beyond the keyhole.
Plays a game of guessing what's inside before opening it. She's right about half the time. She says being wrong is more fun.
★ 히든 문지기. 브리처 명단이 모두 모이면 나타난다: ★ Hidden Gatekeeper. Appears when the Breacher roster is complete.
첫 번째 팔랑크스. 방진의 기준이 되는 방패: The first Phalanx. The shield the formation is set by.
불워크 다섯이 각자 앞에 서던 자리를 다프네는 한 줄로 세웠다. 혼자 두: Where the five Bulwarks had each stood forward on their own, Daphne set them into a single line. Not each girl thick on her own, but overlapping shield edges with the girl beside her. Even when firing, the shield stays folded on the arm — it opens only to overlap. That picture was on the first page of the blueprints salvaged from beneath the turrets of the Fortress Ruins.
거북 대형. 느리지만 흩어지지 않는다: Tortoise formation. Slow, but never scatters.
Her name means peace, yet she holds the record for the longest battle endured. Crossing the claws on her two arms makes a shield. She raises the shield overhead, too. Even on days when nothing was falling from above.
가장 반짝이는 장갑. 흠집을 남기지 않는다: The shiniest armor. Leaves no scratches.
출격 뒤에 장갑을 닦는 데 한 시간을 쓴다. 보수 장갑이 긁힌 자리를 스: She spends an hour polishing her armor after a sortie. Since learning that the patch armor fills in scratches on its own, she spends two — to check that the filled spots were filled properly.
장창. 방패 사이로 찌른다: Pike. Strikes through the gaps between shields.
팔랑크스 중 화력이 가장 먼저 나오는 소녀. 방패는 막으라고 있는 게 아: The Phalanx whose firepower comes out first. Shields aren't for blocking, she says — they're for making openings to strike through. She trades aiming records with Kira of the Siege class.
보수 장갑 담당. 방진이 깎인 만큼 다시 채운다: Patch armor specialist. Refills the formation by as much as it's worn down.
메딕 히카리에게 회복 상한을 배웠다. 자기 장갑부터 고치지 않는다 — 방: She learned the recovery cap from Medic Hikari. She doesn't fix her own armor first — because the formation's armor is her armor. At the end of every round, she checks the shield edge of the girl beside her.
★ 히든 지키는 상. 팔랑크스 명단이 모두 모이면 나타난다: ★ Hidden The guardian statue. Appears when the Phalanx roster is complete.
Rushing a door doesn't make it any faster.
Until the turrets go quiet — that part's mine.
A good day is one where it opens on the same count.
Two doors today. Count's already set.
Seven's enough. After that, the door does the rest.
Got told to go in faster again today. Let it pass.
You can talk to me while I count. I won't slip.
When you come, I lose my count. Starting over.
One of them asks how many seconds. I say how many counts.
You don't rush either. That's easy to be around.
Today it opened before I finished counting. Feels good.
…Five. Six. Six for you to get here.
Tell me if the counting gets old. I'll keep counting anyway.
No sortie, nothing to count. So I come here.
Next to you, the numbers go slow.
My counting before a sortie — too loud? Not planning to tone it down.
Don't. When I hear it, I know it's starting.
노래로 바꿔 보는 건 어때?: What about turning it into a song?
Then I'll keep counting. I'll tell you when it starts.
If it's up to me, I'm counting all the way to seven.
Songs wobble on the beat. Numbers don't.
약탈 편성에서 나를 맨 앞에 두는 거, 무슨 이유야?: Why put me at the very front of the plunder squad?
Because while you count, the turrets can't fire first.
Yeah. That stretch is always the same. That's why I like the front.
If it doesn't matter, I'll stand at the front.
How many counts to open one door, you think? More is safer, sure.
As many as you always count. That's safest.
Any number, I still count. Counting's easier.
Nothing opens on one. A door needs a moment to breathe too.
세는 버릇, 첫 약탈 때 생겼어. 그때 문을 연 건 내가 아니야. 누구: The counting habit started on my first plunder. I wasn't the one who opened the door. Guess who?
The one with the crowbar? You count, and she sets it.
Whoever it was, it opened. That's enough.
I thought you opened it alone.
Yeah. I count, she sets it. Since that day.
Opening is what counts, sure. Still, I won't forget that face.
I can't open them alone. All I did was count.
Before the sortie, count with me once? Just to seven.
열까지 세면 더 든든하지 않아?: Wouldn't counting to ten feel safer?
Okay. From three, I'll take over.
Next time, then. We'll start together from one.
Ten's too long. The door gets tired of waiting.
세다 보면 기체 장갑이 숨 쉬는 박자랑 맞아. 나만 그래?: When I count, it lines up with the beat my unit's armor breathes at. Just me?
Your unit probably knows the beat you count.
My unit knows, huh. Then I'm not counting alone.
I don't know either. The beat'll keep lining up, though.
If they check it, they might fix the beat. No thanks.
What do you count while you wait? It's a little lonely being the only one counting.
The time left until you're back.
That's the same number as mine. …One. Two.
Doesn't waiting feel long if you don't count? It does for me.
That's what you count to fall asleep. I need to stay awake.
Fixed. My counting beat's back too.
Held them off. Our door stood firm this time.
…Twenty, twenty-one. I can stop counting now.
It does not take much force.
I will check where to set it once more.
With a crowbar, the fulcrum matters more than the length.
An opened door is better than a broken wall.
Ready for sortie. I will start with the seams.
When I cannot see where to set it, I step back once.
지렛대 끝을 갈았습니다. 확인하시겠습니까?: I have ground the tip of my crowbar. Would you care to inspect it?
I will not heed anyone who tells me to push harder.
Today it caught on the first try. That is worth reporting.
I have been assigned the same fortress as the one who breaks down ramparts. Again.
I will keep the report short. I have more to ask than to tell.
When the fulcrum is firm, the heart wavers less as well.
오늘은 문 이야기 말고 다른 이야기를 해도 되겠습니까?: Today, may we speak of something other than doors?
Where would you set my crowbar? I will leave it to you.
This is a place where no force is needed.
You need not say anything. Neither do I.
성벽을 부수는 쪽과 같은 요새를 맡으면, 저는 어디부터 봐야 하겠습니까?: When I share a fortress with the one who breaks down ramparts, where should I look first?
Next to the breach. Start with the seams.
같이 부수면 빠르지 않아?: Wouldn't it be faster to break it down together?
The seams. Yes, there it will catch on the first try.
시키시는 곳에 걸겠습니다. 어디입니까?: I will set it wherever you say. Where is it?
It would be faster, yes. But what remains afterward is different.
제 지렛대가 짧다고들 합니다. 바꾸라고 하시겠습니까?: People say my crowbar is short. Would you have me replace it?
With a good fulcrum, short is fine. Keep using it.
I will keep using it. I will choose the fulcrum myself.
Then I will not replace it. I have used it a long time.
With two, I would have to think about where to set it twice.
다음 약탈에서 제가 맡을 문, 어떤 문이 좋겠습니까?: On the next plunder, what kind of door would suit me?
The one everyone shoved at and gave up on.
With doors like that, the spot is usually wrong. I will take it.
The door that is left over is rarely the easy one.
Even on a large door, the place to set it is no bigger than a palm.
문 앞에서 거는 자리를 못 찾을 때가 있습니다. 그럴 때 지휘관께 한 번: There are times I cannot find where to set it in front of a door. At such times, may I ask you once, Commander?
Ask. If we look together, we'll spot at least one.
Pull as hard as you can.
If you look with me, it is as good as having one more fulcrum.
Yes. I usually find it. Usually.
Brute force is not my way. It means the spot is wrong.
제가 지렛대를 걸 때 옆에서 수를 세는 분이 있습니다. 그 소리가 없으면: When I set my crowbar, there is someone beside me who counts. What do you think it would be like without that sound?
It'd feel empty. Your hands are tuned to that beat.
The quiet would help you focus.
It would feel empty. I believe my hands would stop at around seven.
I hope there would be no difference. There probably would be.
In the quiet, I hear only my own breathing. That is not welcome.
실패한 일이 있느냐고 묻는 분들이 있습니다. 지휘관께서는 묻지 않으시는군: Some ask whether I have ever failed. You do not ask, Commander. Why is that?
Because you can tell me when you want to.
Those words are enough. As long as you do not ask, I am at ease.
Not curious, you say. That stings a little, and is a great relief.
If that is how it looked, I am glad. I will not answer.
물으시면 되묻는 것이 제 버릇입니다. 지휘관께는 되묻지 않고 바로 드릴: When asked, I answer with a question. It is a habit of mine. For you, Commander, I would like to settle on one answer I can give straight away.
How your day went. Answer that one straight.
되묻는 것도 재밌는데?: The questions back are fun, though?
Today was fine. …Answering directly feels awkward.
편할 대로 하면 또 되묻게 됩니다. 어디까지 편해도 됩니까?: If I do what is comfortable, I end up asking back again. How comfortable may I be?
You found it amusing? Then I will fix only half of it.
I have returned. It caught on the first try.
All repaired. I replaced the fulcrum as well.
Repelled. Wherever they set it, our door will not open.
You have come. My crowbar did not rest once while you were away.
If I put my ear to it, the door tells me first.
If it goes clunk and catches, it's not ready yet.
If you could keep quiet, please, it'll be over soon.
Our own storeroom door is the sound I know best.
The storeroom keeper played me another sound.
Before a sortie, I clean my ears first. Really.
Thud, I don't like. Click, I like.
If you wait for me, the door answers.
When you open the bridge door, Commander, I'm the first to hear it.
The guessing game came out half and half today.
Rooms without sound scare me a little. It's okay here.
My good ears come from being taught. I couldn't have done it alone.
Your breathing sounds relaxed today, Commander.
Tap, tap. I like the sound of your pen, Commander.
Even when there's no door to open, I'd like to come here.
Of everywhere I listen, this is the quietest.
금고 앞에서 제가 한참 귀 대고 있으면, 답답하지 않으세요?: When I keep my ear to a vault for ages, doesn't it get frustrating for you?
I'll wait. When you nod, it's done.
As long as you don't run over time.
귀 말고 장비로 들으면 안 돼?: Can't you listen with equipment instead of your ears?
Yes. A nod means the door said yes.
I won't. The sound tells me everything.
Equipment flattens the sound. I don't like it.
잠금 소리마다 이름을 붙여 줬어요. 하나 들어 보실래요?: I've given every lock sound a name. Would you like to hear one?
금고 열쇠 소리 말이야?: You mean the sound of the vault key?
Then this one. It's a click, and then a rest.
Next time for sure. Keep your ears free, please.
Keys don't get names. Only the sounds doors make do.
상대 창고 보호를 깎는 거, 저는 소리로 해요. 어떻게 생각하세요?: Wearing down an opposing storeroom's protection — I do it by sound. What do you think?
It opens as much as you hear. I trust that.
When you trust me, my ears get sharper.
The result comes after the sound. Please wait for it.
Hammers startle doors. A startled door won't open.
창고 담당 언니한테 처음 들킨 날, 저 혼날 줄 알았어요. 언니가 어떻게: The first day the storeroom keeper caught me, I thought I'd get scolded. What do you think she did?
Didn't chase you off — let you hear one more sound, I bet.
How did you know? I still remember that sound.
That's what I thought too. But no.
The key? She'd never give that out.
맞히기 놀이 하는 애가 있어요. 그 애는 상상, 저는 소리로요. 답이 다: There's a girl I play a guessing game with. She guesses by imagining, I guess by sound. When our answers differ, I get a little excited. Why is that?
Because one of you learns something new.
싸울까 봐 그런 거 아냐?: Isn't it because you might fight?
Yes. Whoever's wrong always brings back something interesting.
Hmm, I wonder too. I think I'll know when I hear it open.
We don't fight. She laughs even when she's wrong.
제가 귀를 대고 있으면 다들 기다려 주잖아요. 저도 누굴 기다려 주고 싶: When I have my ear to a door, everyone waits for me, right? I'd like to wait for someone too, but I don't really know how.
Just listen like you do now. It's the same as waiting.
Listening, I'm good at. This time it's your turn, Commander.
Staying still is the hardest. I'll give it a try, though.
Timers shout when they're done. That's not waiting.
지휘관님은 무슨 소리를 들으면 마음이 놓여요? 저는 금고 문이 다시 닫히: What sound puts you at ease, Commander? For me, it's a vault door closing again.
The sound of you coming back from a sortie.
The sound of resources piling up in the storeroom.
Then I'll open the door a little louder when I come back.
If you don't have one, I'll pick one for you. Tock. That one.
That doesn't make a sound. It piles up quietly.
I'm back. The click was a pretty one.
All fixed. My unit sounds clear.
We held. Our storeroom door didn't make a single sound.
You're here? I'm glad the bridge is noisy again.
저기 금. 저기도. 봤어?: Crack there. There too. See it?
Looking's fast. Going in comes after.
Where the one who walked the path ahead stopped — that's the gap.
Today's sortie: three walls. Five cracks.
How many seconds it took — got a bet on that with the counter. No winner yet.
The smoother the wall, the longer I look.
Bridge window frame — lifting a bit there. I'll fix it.
Scout, then me. I like that order.
Sorry I talk fast. I'll slow down for you.
Today I'm skipping gap-hunting. Just sitting here.
Saw you coming through the gap in the door first.
Sometimes having gaps is comfortable. This place is like that.
See it? Outside the window's smooth today. Not one crack.
Next sortie, I'll look at the wall you picked first.
When I look at a wall — top first or bottom first? Pick one.
거기. 매끈하면 숨긴 거야. 봤어?: There. Smooth means hiding something. See it?
You don't have to know. Looking's my job.
Everyone looks at the front. So it's tough there.
정찰 다녀온 애 발자국 끝나는 데 있지. 거기서 내가 시작해. 순서 바꿀: You know where the scout's footprints end? That's where I start. Swap the order?
Don't. Where she stops is where you start.
Yeah, not swapping. The two of us are one line.
It matters. Break the order and every wall looks the same.
If I go first, I don't know the way. I'd just stare at walls.
금 찾은 거 보고, 나 짧게밖에 못 해. 그래도 돼?: Reporting cracks — I can only do it short. That okay?
Keep it short. Everything's in your short words.
Write it up as a report.
One crack, one spot. That does it.
Write it? The wall gets fixed while I write.
틀린 쪽이 다음 출격 연료 채우기로 했어. 상대는 상상만 하는 애. 나: Loser fuels up for the next sortie. My opponent only imagines. No way I lose, right?
Who knows. Some places imagination reaches first.
Even if you lose, it's a few cans of fuel.
I'll fill the fuel for you.
Reaches first. …There are places like that. Not admitting it.
Few cans or not, I hate losing. I'll look faster.
Then it's not a bet. This one's ours.
수 세는 애 옆에서 기다리는 거, 나한텐 길어. 어떻게 버텨?: Waiting next to the counter takes forever for me. How do I hang on?
Spot one more in the meantime. Your eyes don't rest anyway.
One more. Nice. Not waiting — looking.
Holding back's my worst thing. I'll try anyway.
First? That's stealing the counter's part.
오늘은 금 하나 없는 걸 보고 싶어. 뭐 보면 좋을까?: Today I want to see something without a single crack. What's good to look at?
Let's look at the stars together. No cracks to find in stars.
Close your eyes and rest a bit.
Everything between the stars is a gap, though. …Still, I like it.
If I look at anything, cracks show up first again.
Closing them shows me more. Even the walls in my head.
Name one thing on this ship that looks the toughest. I want to look at it a long time.
This ship, with all of you on it.
This ship. Look as long as I want, no cracks. Nice.
Nothing in particular? Then you just haven't found it. I'll find it for you.
Isn't the vault the one thing I shouldn't be looking at? Haha.
Fixed. Spotted one more armor seam while I was at it.
Held 'em. Can't see a gap in our walls. Nice.
You're late. Looked at every wall while you were gone. Nothing left to see.
Rosaline bets one on alloy behind that door.
Right is good. Wrong is better.
Right before opening is the most exciting part.
Rosaline's guesses always run a little big.
Three doors today. Rosaline's got three guesses ready too.
다음 출격, 안에 뭐 있을지 같이 상상해 볼래?: Next sortie, want to imagine what's inside together?
Rosaline bets on parts. Your guess?
Yesterday's came out about half right. Half is a lot.
The friend who guesses by sound is calmer than Rosaline.
Every box in this room — Rosaline's already imagined what's inside.
Rosaline's taking the day off from imagining. Staying here.
No bets with you. Rosaline thinks she'd lose.
Turns out some things are nice without opening them.
Rosaline imagined one thing today. It's a secret.
Even if Rosaline's wrong, if you laugh, Rosaline wins.
Want to bet with Rosaline on what's behind the next door? Rosaline says fuel.
I'll bet on parts. Being wrong is fun too.
We'll know when we open it.
Okay, parts. Loser laughs out loud — deal.
If it's anything, Rosaline picks for you. Alloy.
"We'll know when we open it"? That's half the fun gone.
맞히기 채점은 회수량 장부 보는 애가 해 줘. 공정하지?: The one who keeps the haul ledger scores the guesses. Fair, right?
Numbers keep it fair. Your wrong days stay on record too.
Rosaline likes that it all stays. Wrong days are Rosaline's too.
We'll sort it out. She keeps a tight grip on that ledger.
If you score it, you'll say Rosaline got them all right.
로잘린은 열쇠 구멍 보면 안을 그려 봐. 지휘관도 그래?: When Rosaline sees a keyhole, Rosaline pictures the inside. Do you, Commander?
When you tell me about it, I can picture it.
Then Rosaline will paint it bigger and tell you.
If not really, Rosaline will lend you hers. Picture it big.
Don't plug it! No hole, no imagining.
Know why Rosaline tries to guess before opening? Wrong answers are okay.
Because opening ends it. The time before is the longest fun.
You could just open it fast.
Yep. Before it's open, it can be anything.
A little boredom, sure. But that's not all of it.
Open it fast and Rosaline's imagination can't keep up.
틀린 날엔 다들 웃어 주는데, 로잘린도 진짜 속상한 날이 있어. 그날은: Everyone laughs along on wrong days, but some days Rosaline is really upset. Will you notice on those days?
I'll notice. You'll be less chatty that day.
Caught. Quiet Rosaline is upset Rosaline.
Rosaline wishes you'd notice without being told. Let's practice.
Never wrong is no fun. That's not Rosaline.
When Rosaline imagines, the unit gets excited first. Seems the unit's more thrilled than Rosaline.
You two are one, so you get excited together.
Okay, not worrying. The unit's going to keep bouncing, though.
Hope so. The unit's imagination would be bigger than Rosaline's.
Want Rosaline to tell you one thing she imagined about you? No getting mad if it's wrong.
Tell me. I'll let you know what's wrong later.
Just one. You're smiling. Pretty often.
"No thanks"? Rosaline's imagining keeps going anyway.
직접 물으면 재미없는데. 하나만. 오늘 좋았어?: Asking straight out is no fun. Just one, then. Was today good?
Back! There was more inside than Rosaline imagined.
All fixed. Rosaline's unit is all shiny.
Held! Nobody got to see behind our door.
You came! Rosaline bet you'd come today.
A door remembers a hurried hand.
It is the door that decides when it opens.
Bridge door, you are diligent again today, my friend.
Being the name tacked onto the end of the roster, it still feels strange.
I heard the five children opening doors again today.
You are not startled to see me. My thanks.
Look at a door once before you knock, would you.
My preparations for the sortie are done. I shall go when a door calls.
The Commander's door opens and shuts with a gentle sound.
They call me a gatekeeper, but I do not guard. I wait.
The bridge window is a kind of door as well. It lets the outside in.
Being spoken to, I feel as though I have become a door myself.
Before the Commander, I keep nothing locked.
You there, my friend — when this one comes, open wide.
I never knew the work of waiting could be so warm.
I have long stood before doors, but this is the first place I have stepped inside.
문마다 성미가 다르다네. 오늘 문은 어떻게 대할 텐가?: Every door has its own temper. How shall you treat today's?
Like you always do. Talk to it first.
A hard shove should do it.
Just so. A door that has been greeted resists less.
"As long as it opens," hm. The door would be hurt to hear that.
Push a door and it pushes back. That is wrestling.
다섯이 앞에서 문을 열고, 나는 뒤에 선다네. 그 자리가 어떤가?: The five open the doors up front, and I stand behind. What do you make of that place?
It's where you can see everything. Where the five get stuck.
Leading from the front looks cooler.
Indeed. I keep in mind the doors that stop them.
It does not matter? That is easy on me. I prefer the back.
Looking fine belongs to the children up front. I shall not take it from them.
명단에 없던 이름이 이 배에 섞였네. 불편하진 않은가?: A name that was not on the roster has slipped aboard this ship. Does it trouble you?
Late, hm. Ho ho — you speak like a door.
No thought about it at all — that is the most welcome answer.
Even if you reprint it, I would like my name at the very end.
다섯이 각자 문을 열던 밤, 나는 아무도 안 건드린 문 앞에 있었네. 왜: The night the five each opened a door, I stood before the one no one had touched. Why there, do you suppose?
Because someone has to look at the door nobody looks at.
Maybe it was the closest one.
If that is how it looked, perhaps that is how it was. I do not know it all myself.
A gatekeeper who gets lost. What an amusing thought.
Whether it was close, I cannot say. Only that the door was quiet.
그 밤에 소리를 들은 아이가 하나 있었네. 나는 그 아이에게 무엇을 해: That night, one child heard the sound. What might I do for her?
Don't hide the sound of your footsteps.
I shall not hide it. I will let her ears find me.
Anything, hm. Then I shall start by pouring a cup of tea.
She opens doors better than I do. I shall stand beside her.
문 앞에 서면 기체가 문틀처럼 곧게 서네. 내가 먼저인지, 기체가 먼저인: When I stand before a door, my unit stands straight as a doorframe. Whether I came first or the unit did, I cannot tell.
It's just how you stand at a door. Your unit learned it too.
Learned, hm. We have stood together long enough for that.
Both, hm. That is the roundest answer of all.
Correction, you say. I could never let a doorframe hear that.
이 배에서 아직 인사를 못 한 문이 하나 있네. 어느 문인지 정해 주겠나: There is one door on this ship I have yet to greet. Would you choose which one?
My room's door. So it opens when you come.
Then I shall go greet it tonight. Two knocks, of course.
Any door? The doors will quarrel over who goes first.
Ho ho. That door is a busy one, so the greeting will be brief.
I have returned. Three doors accepted my greeting.
My unit stands straight again. My thanks.
Repelled. Our doors answered no one.
You were away a long while. The bridge door was waiting for the Commander too.
Nine for one door. Long day.
I'm back. The hold point was good.
I'm back. The door answered first.
I'm back. My ears still tingle.
See that? That wall's weak on the left.
Back. Next time I'll find four cracks.
I'm back! Got it wrong, and that was more fun.
왔어! 다음 판엔 뭐 걸까?: Back! What do we bet on next?
I've returned. I didn't hurry, and the door opened.
The door knew its moment again today.
I've returned. My hands are still cold.
Counted to five at the dock. Done.
Held. The door lasted to three.
I counted a long time. But you came.
Repairs done. I can put my weight in again.
The brace is straight. Thank you.
Maintenance done. I'll check the hold points first.
Held. The latch held to the end.
They withdrew. I still have strength left.
You're here. I kept your place open.
I waited. I saved my strength.
You're back. Jobs to hook up have piled up.
Repairs done. My ears can rest.
All done. The sound came back clear.
Held. The door never once cried.
They withdrew. The footsteps faded away.
We held. Not even a click.
You're here? I knew by your footsteps.
It was quiet a long time. Now it's nice.
I waited. All I heard was doors.
Repairs done. I know where it's weak.
Held. Didn't give them a single gap.
See that? Their armor was thin on the left.
We held. Next time I'll find their cracks.
You're here? The walls are as they were.
You're late. I found you a crack.
You came. Found something to look at.
수리 끝! 내기 하나 할래?: Repairs done! Wanna make a bet?
All done! I bet it'd be quick.
물러갔어! 다음 판은 뭐 걸까?: They withdrew! What's the next bet?
We held! Would've been funnier if I'd lost.
You came! Rosaline guessed right this time.
Took you long. I lost the bet.
You're here! Should've bet more on today.
All fixed. My hands are warm again.
The frame makes its proper sound again.
They withdrew. The door knew first.
We held. It wasn't time to open.
You're here. The tea's gone cold.
I waited. Doors always know the right time.
You're back. The bridge breathes again.
I'll watch the front. You watch the back.
Keep the voice low. That's how it carries all the way.
Not yet. I'll stand a little longer.
The armor plate's warm. Took a lot today.
You came. Front-line check. Not done yet.
No need to speak up. I hear it all.
The new ones keep coming up front. I told them not yet.
Saw the squad sheet. My spot hasn't changed.
Someone else counts my dents. I just look ahead.
I'd know your voice even through the radio.
Up front, I can't see behind. You watch it. That's enough.
Today I'll try talking longer. …No. Still can't.
I won't say not yet. Not to you.
Around you, my voice gets a little louder.
When I'm back, I look your way first. Words come after.
Even when I talk low, you catch all of it. I like that.
기함 급습이 오면 다들 나부터 노려. 알고 있지?: When a Flagship strike comes, they all aim for me first. You know that?
I know. That's why you're up front, and I've got your back.
…You've got my back. The front feels a little lighter.
I hold. Holding is my job.
Thin, and they go for someone else. Leave it.
작전 회의에서 한마디밖에 안 했어. 모자랐어?: I said one thing at the strategy meeting. Was it too little?
That one line silenced the room. It was enough.
If they heard it, that's enough. No need for more.
It was long. Halfway through I was just counting armor-plate sounds.
Slides… one page okay? I'll write one line.
A new one tried to stand in front of me. I only said not yet. Too short?
Short or not, with that voice they get it. Well done.
New ones are all like that.
그럼 한번 앞에 세워 보지 그랬어?: Why not let her stand up front once?
If she got it, good. I'll check again tomorrow.
They all do. I probably did too. Maybe.
Letting her stand there — not yet. Her armor's thin.
Noa counts even my armor dents. I've never counted them once.
You look ahead, Noa counts behind. You two are a set.
It's fine not knowing the numbers.
A set. Tell her that too.
Easier not to know. I just listen.
She says forgetting's fine. She'll start over from the top.
They say my voice is too low for the radio. Am I supposed to get louder?
No need. I'll turn up your channel.
…You'll turn it up. Then I'll keep talking like this.
I practiced. Lost my voice in three days.
My singing ends at the first note. That's as far as my voice goes.
They call me the reference point. But on days the reference wobbles, who do I look to?
Look at me. Even if things shake, I won't move from here.
…All right. I'll just turn my head your way.
There are. On those days I don't say a word.
You're not on the map. I don't look at it.
I always look ahead, so I don't really know what's behind. Show me someday, slowly?
When you're back, let's walk the hangar together. I'll show you one by one.
거울을 달아 줄까?: Want me to mount a mirror?
One by one. Then it'll be a long walk.
I know they're fine. I want to see their faces.
A mirror just shows my own face. I'm not curious about that.
Repairs done. I can stand up front again.
Blocked it all. Quiet back there.
Took a while. I kept the front.
One more mark today. Left shoulder.
No new plate for me. Lay it over the top.
A scratch is that day's memory. Too good to throw away.
My carving hand's gotten faster lately. Not a good thing.
The dock offered me a new plate again. I said no.
This mark? Last week's. Still stings.
Not hurt — learned. That's how I'll count it.
You can touch the plate. Bumpy, right?
I'm probably the only one who counts other people's dents too.
When you're watching, my hand shakes less as I carve. Feels less like a wound, more like a record.
I erased one of my first marks. That's over now.
Carved today's shallow. You fixed me up fast.
Could I carve one mark for a story about you?
Not where I got hurt — the days I came back. That's what I want to carve now.
The day they all fade won't come. That's okay.
With you around, there's less to carve. Funny, huh.
The maintenance crew wants to give me a new armor plate. Do I take it?
Let's go with whatever keeps all your marks. Layer over them.
Just keep the marks as photos.
Tell the crew that too. They listen to you.
Nice, sure. But smooth, I wouldn't recognize myself.
Photos are flat. Not seeing — touching. That's how I remember.
I always carve the same day. Let a day pass and my hand goes blurry.
So that's why you were in the dock so late. I'll leave the lights on.
새기는 도구를 바꿔 볼래?: Want to try a different carving tool?
Lights on would be nice. Today's is kind of deep.
Tomorrow brings tomorrow's mark. I can't fall behind.
Not the tool — the memory. Thanks anyway.
After sorties, everyone hides their scars. I'm the type who shows them.
You show them, so I can tell where it hurt.
보이면 겁나지 않아?: Doesn't it scare you, seeing them?
When someone notices, carving's less lonely.
It's different. I just never learned how to hide.
Not fear — a marker. So I get hurt less next time.
The day I erased my first mark, I thought I'd feel relieved. It felt kind of empty.
That mark was with you a long time.
If you erased it, that's that.
다시 새기면 되지 않아?: Can't you just carve it again?
It was there a long time. My hand hesitated forever before erasing it.
It's done. My head knows. My hand doesn't, that's all.
Carving it again would be a lie. That's over.
아야 자국은 내가 대신 세. 그 애는 앞만 보니까. 이상해?: I count Aya's dents for her. She only looks ahead. Weird?
Not weird. You fill in what the other lacks.
At least get paid for the counting.
Fill in. I like that. I'll count her share too.
Tell her to count and she just nods. That's it.
Already paid. She stands in front for me.
Every mark has a story. Could I tell you one someday?
I'd like to hear. Slowly, starting with the oldest.
The old ones are worn down. They have to be read slowly.
I'll make the time. I'm good at waiting.
재밌는 건 없어. 다 아팠던 거야. 그래도 들을래?: None are fun. They all hurt. Still want to hear?
Not much unmarked space left. I want to save what's left.
Save it. Until a day comes you really want to carve.
So what if it fills up.
거기 스티커라도 붙여 줄까?: Want a sticker for that spot?
I'll save it. A day to use it will come.
Fill up and there's nowhere for the next one. That scares me a little.
Stickers don't catch on my fingertips. If I can't feel it, it's no use.
Back. Got one more to carve.
Maintenance done. Told them not to touch the scratches.
You're here. A few more marks while you were gone.
…The new girl. …Her name, what was it.
…Wiping my armor. …You can sit beside me.
…Knowing names makes guarding easier. …So I memorize them.
…Not good at talking. …Thanks for listening anyway.
…Today I was the one breaking through. …My armor's edge is numb.
…I talk a little more now. …When I'm with you.
…At the front of the names I guard, I put you.
…Today, I looked back once. …Your voice was on the radio.
…Before the sortie. …Look at me, just once.
…두꺼운 장갑. …어디부터 뚫는지, 알아?: …Thick armor. …Know where to break through first?
The seams. That's what you always do.
…Go around, and the back's left open. …So I break through.
…The ones behind me. …I know all their names.
That's why everyone says it's easy being behind you.
…Black armor. …Picked it so I don't stand out.
Even if you don't stand out, everyone behind you is watching you.
밝은 색으로 칠해 줄까?: Want me to paint it something bright?
…Bright gets targeted. …If it were just me, maybe.
…Memorizing names. …Sometimes I mix them up. …Similar ones.
Then memorize them with faces. I'll look with you.
…지친 날엔. …뒤에 서도 돼?: …On tired days. …Can I stand at the back?
You can. That day, I'll call your name.
…The front. …Someone else, just for a day.
…Someday. …I wish someone would remember my name, too.
I already have. Io. I won't forget.
목소리를 녹음해서 틀어 줄까?: Want me to record my voice and play it for you?
…Recordings, always the same sound. …People, different every time.
…Not just footsteps. …I want to know you by voice, too. …Say anything.
Then I'll tell you one thing every day.
I don't have much to say, though.
편지로 써 줄까?: Want me to write it in a letter?
…Even if there's nothing. …"Nothing" is a voice, too.
먼저 닿는 게 제일 재밌어!: Getting there first is the best part!
수리 도크 침대, 이제 내 몸에 맞아!: The repair dock bed fits me perfectly now!
다들 늦어! 기다리다 졸겠네!: Everyone's so slow! I'll fall asleep waiting!
왔어? 나 오늘은 도크 안 갔다!: You're here? I didn't go to the dock today!
리벳 반장이 또 한숨 쉬더라! 내가 뭘 했다고!: Chief Rivet sighed at me again! What'd I even do!
솔직히 도크 가는 거 좀 미안해. 아주 조금!: Honestly, I feel kinda bad about the dock trips. Just a tiny bit!
들이받기 전에 네 목소리 들으면 덜 떨려! 진짜야!: Hearing your voice before I ram, I shake less! For real!
Everyone thinks I'm fearless. Everyone but you.
오늘은 반장한테 칭찬받았어! 긁힌 데 하나뿐이래!: The chief praised me today! Only one scratch, she said!
들이받고 나서 무전 켜면 네 목소리가 있지. 그게 좋아!: After I ram, I switch on the radio and your voice is there. Love that!
나 사실 조용한 것도 좋아해. 너랑일 때만!: Truth is, I like quiet too. Only with you!
다음엔 도크 말고 너한테 먼저 올게!: Next time I'll come to you first, not the dock!
방어형이라 불러도 돼. 너만은!: You can call me defensive type. Only you!
편성표에 또 방어형이래! 그 칸 지워 줄 수 있어?: The squad sheet says defensive type again! Can you erase that box?
I'll erase it. Your box will say "very front."
그럼 공격형으로 바꿔 볼래?: Want to switch it to attack type, then?
맨 앞! 그게 딱 나야!: The very front! That's totally me!
이름일 뿐이면 바꿔도 되잖아! 응?: If it's just a label, you can change it! Right?
공격형은 또 좀 다른데… 아무튼 방어형만 빼면 돼!: Attack type's kinda different too… Anyway, just drop defensive!
도크 단골이라고 다들 놀려! 나 그렇게 자주 가?: Everyone teases me for being a dock regular! Do I really go that often?
You do. Because you're the first to hit.
Just get hurt a bit less.
도크 벽에 네 포스터라도 붙일까?: How about your poster on the dock wall?
먼저 부딪히는 값이야! 하나도 안 아까워!: That's the price of hitting first! Totally worth it!
덜 다치면 덜 빨라! 그건 싫어!: Get hurt less, go slower! No thanks!
포스터는 반장이 바로 뗄걸! 하하!: The chief would rip a poster right down! Haha!
다들 출발이 너무 느려! 신호 좀 빨리 줘!: Everyone's way too slow to launch! Give the signal faster!
You get yours one beat early. In exchange, look back once.
신호 없이 먼저 가 보는 건?: What about going ahead without a signal?
You can get ready on the way! …Can't you?
그건 진짜 혼나! 신호는 꼭 줘!: I'd get in so much trouble! Always give the signal!
리벳 반장은 나만 오면 고장 났냐고 물어. 걱정하는 거 맞지?: Chief Rivet asks if I'm broken every time I show up. She's worried, right?
Right. She knows your frame's sound better than anyone.
She asks because it's her job.
Ask her to check if it's really broken.
소리로 안다니! 그럼 나 숨길 게 없네!: She knows by sound! Then I've got nothing to hide!
일이라도 그 말투는 걱정이야! 내가 알아!: Job or not, that tone is worry! I can tell!
봐 달라고 하면 하루 종일 붙잡혀! 싫어!: If I ask, she'll keep me all day! No way!
들이받기 직전엔 사실 무서워. 다들한텐 비밀이야!: Right before I ram, I'm actually scared. Secret from everyone!
You go first even scared. That's why everyone follows.
눈 감고 들이받으면 덜 무섭지 않아?: Wouldn't it be less scary with your eyes shut?
그런가! 그럼 무서운 채로 갈래!: Is that it! Then I'll go scared!
있지! 근데 말하고 나니까 좀 시원하다!: I can! But saying it out loud feels kinda good!
눈 감으면 어디 박는지 모르잖아! 더 무서워!: Eyes shut, I won't know what I'm hitting! Way scarier!
가끔은 아무 데도 안 들이받는 날이 있으면 좋겠어. 이상한 소리지?: Sometimes I wish there were days I didn't ram anything. Weird thing to say, right?
Not weird. On those days, let's walk slowly together.
천천히! 그건 진짜 어려운데… 한번 해 볼래!: Slowly! That's really hard… but I'll try!
오겠지? 오면 제일 먼저 알려 줄게!: They will? I'll tell you first when one does!
베개! 그건 들이받아도 아무도 안 다치네!: A pillow! Nobody gets hurt ramming that!
나 빨리 닿는 거 말고 잘하는 게 있을까? 하나만 찾아 줘!: Am I good at anything besides getting there fast? Find me just one!
When you laugh, the mood in the dock changes. That's a talent too.
도크 분위기! 그럼 앞으로 더 크게 웃을게!: The dock mood! Then I'll laugh even louder from now on!
편성표는 싫어! 방어형 칸이 자꾸 보이잖아!: No squad sheets! I keep seeing that defensive-type box!
다녀왔어! 오늘도 내가 제일 먼저 닿았어!: Back! I got there first again today!
도크 졸업! 오늘은 빨랐지?: Graduated from the dock! Fast today, right?
막았어! 막는 것도 들이받는 거야!: Blocked it! Blocking is ramming too!
늦었잖아! 나 혼자 나갈 뻔했어!: You're late! I almost went out alone!
What shakes is always the quiet side.
그늘이 편해. 왜 다들 밝은 데로만 가?: Shade is comfortable. Why does everyone only go toward the light?
When I hear healing behind me, I feel safe. Why, I don't know.
내 차례는 조금 뒤야. 그게 왜 늦은 거야?: My turn's a little later. Why does that count as late?
You came? I'm here, behind the pillar.
앞에 안 나간다고 뭐라 하던데, 왜 그래야 해?: They nag me for not going up front. Why would I?
Today's defense line was thin on the left. From the shade, you can see it all.
Everyone looks ahead. So I look to the side.
The shade you don't watch, I'll watch. There, I'm sure of myself.
히카리랑 짝이면 마음이 놓여. 이상하지?: Paired with Hikari, I feel at ease. Weird, isn't it?
I know you go quiet sometimes. Me too.
It's always your voice that tells me when to step out.
Next to you, the shade gets wider. Why is that?
I don't usually speak first. With you, I do.
On shaky days, call me. I'll come right away.
앞에 안 나서는 나를, 왜 너는 믿어?: Why do you trust me, when I don't step up front?
오늘 왼쪽 끝에 있었어. 왜 거기였는지 알아?: Today I was at the far left. Know why there?
Everyone was watching the right. You took the empty side.
Guess that spot was left over.
You saw. That's where it shakes first.
No spot's left over. I chose it.
Not because I like it. …I like it a little.
기다리는 동안 내가 뭘 하는 것 같아?: What do you think I do while I wait?
Checking where everyone is, one by one.
I thought you were dozing off.
Checking, yes. To be exact, I'm looking for gaps.
Rest and I'll miss it. Resting's for after we're back.
If I doze, someone behind me always wakes me.
With a healer frame beside me, I last longer. Guess the waiting types get along.
You both wait for the moment others missed.
You two make a good pair.
회복은 빨리빨리 하는 거 아니야?: Isn't healing supposed to be quick?
The missed moment… yes. I stand in that gap.
We do. I still don't know why.
빨리하면 틈이 생겨. 왜 서둘러?: Rush it and gaps open. Why hurry?
히카리가 뒤에 있으면 나는 한 걸음도 안 비켜. 왜인지 알아?: With Hikari behind me, I don't step aside even once. Know why?
If you move, she gets hurt. You see that first.
Seeing first is my job. Not stepping aside is my heart.
Not just because we're partners. I like her voice.
Scared? Of her? I can't picture it.
그늘에서 기다리다 보면 가끔 너무 조용해. 그럴 때 무전 한 번만 해 줄: Waiting in the shade, it gets too quiet sometimes. Then, would you radio me once?
I will. I'll leave it on even with nothing to say.
음악 틀어 줄까?: Want me to play some music?
Just leaving it on is enough. I like the static.
I don't know when I need it. In the shade, everything's quiet.
Music pulls my ears to it. Then I'd miss things.
Will a day come when I want to stand in the middle? The shade is comfortable. I don't know myself.
Stand when you want to. Then I'll watch your back.
무대 조명이라도 달아 줄까?: Want me to rig up a stage light?
If you're watching… once might be okay.
안 어울려도 한 번은 궁금하잖아. 왜 안 돼?: Even if it doesn't suit me, I'd be curious once. Why not?
No lights. It doesn't need to be that bright.
Some days I wait and never go out at all. Those are the best days.
The days you didn't go out were all safe days.
So it was a quiet day.
You noticed. On those days, the shade's a little warm.
It's not idle. I was watching to the end.
That's not mine to decide. The side that shakes decides.
Back. I watched it all from the shade — nothing shook.
Repairs done. Going back to the shade.
I saw a gap. Cut it off there.
You're back. I watched everything while you were away.
Fortresses don't move. Behind five shields is my place.
The legend walks ahead. I walk behind.
I am not breached. That is all.
Words, I keep short. A shield stands long.
Commander. This ship's shields are thick. A good ship.
The rumors arrived before I did. Pay them no mind.
I watch the backs of the five. That is today's work.
I joined late. I will stand that much longer.
You look at me before the rumors. That is rare.
I heard the five laughing. Not bad.
Old records weigh heavy at times. Today they weigh a little.
Your orders are short. I like that.
Call me, not the legend. For you, that is right.
I will stay on this ship. I will tell the five myself.
If I were to choose one thing to keep at my back, it is you.
Today I wish to speak at length. Hear me.
Have you heard the rumor that I cannot be breached? Do you believe it?
I don't know about rumors. I saw you hold today.
한 번쯤 뚫려 봐도 재밌지 않아?: Wouldn't it be fun to get breached just once?
You believe what you saw. That is right.
Others' words are wind. They pass.
If it is a jest, I will take it. A shield does not laugh, though.
Behind the five shields is my place. Are you sorry it is not the front?
No. With the back secure, the five can look ahead.
The very front would suit you better.
The five look ahead. Then it is enough.
If it does not matter, I will decide. The back.
I do not stand by what suits me. I stand by use.
I came late. The five did not treat me as a stranger.
Without knowing it, they were all waiting for you.
선물이라도 들고 왔어?: Did you bring gifts or something?
Waited. I will take that word with weight.
Kindness is this ship's armor, then.
No gifts. I gave them my back instead.
I once searched where the legend came from. It was another ship's record.
Tell me about that ship when you want to. I'll listen.
Old records are all like that.
그 기록, 복사해서 걸어 둘까?: Want me to copy that record and hang it up?
When I want to. I will remember those words.
They are. Still, that one volume is different.
Do not hang it. Let a ship that has passed, pass.
After the five are asleep, I make one more round. Will you walk with me?
Let's walk together. I'll match your pace.
You can rest if you're tired.
You could just use a patrol drone.
Do not match me. I will slow down.
Rest comes after the round, too.
A machine does not look at sleeping faces.
At times I picture the day I lay down my shield. Do not laugh.
I won't. I hope you'll still be on this ship that day.
I will be. Even without a shield.
Far. That is why I said it now.
Light, yes. But my hands would feel empty.
Hearing them train, I want to call the cadence. Meddling, I suppose.
It's not meddling. Call it — they'll love it.
If you want to, do it.
They will love it. Then I will keep it short. One, two.
I want to. That is why I asked you.
Clapping is praise. A cadence is a stride.
I said I'd come back. All behind me are safe.
Repairs complete. I will stand again.
Blocked. This ship is not breached.
You are late. The ship is safe.
Front line squared away. Still have my voice.
Back. I kept my voice low and they all heard.
Back. One more on the right arm.
Back. Small scratch this time. I'll still carve it.
Back. One more line on the plate.
왔다! 오늘도 일등으로 닿았어!: Back! First to make contact again today!
다녀왔어! 방패 들고 뛰니까 재밌더라!: I'm back! Running with the shield was fun!
도착! 다음엔 더 빨리 닿을 거야!: Here! Next time I'll make contact even faster!
Back. I picked only the quiet side.
Back. One spot nearly wobbled. I held it.
I have returned. The shield is still warm.
All five shields stood. So did I.
Returned. The one who walked ahead is safe too.
Fixed. Heading back to the front line.
Repairs done. Voice is fine too.
All done. Don't worry about the rear.
We held. I kept my voice low and they all followed.
They withdrew. Everyone's safe, rear included.
You're here. I didn't leave the front empty.
I waited. You take the rear.
Been a while. I saved my voice.
Fixed. Left the marks as they are.
Repairs done. Turned down a new plate.
All done. The scratches are mine.
Didn't break through. More to carve.
We held. Deep scratch this time. Good.
You're back. Let me show you the plate.
You were gone long. Too many marks to count.
You're here? I carved one thing.
수리 끝! 다시 들이받을 수 있어!: Repairs done! Ready to charge again!
고쳤다! 방어형 아니라니까!: Fixed! I said I'm not the defensive type!
도크 끝! 다음엔 더 빨리 닿을 거야!: Out of the dock! Next time I'll hit even faster!
들이받아서 막았어! 재밌었어!: Blocked them by charging! That was fun!
지켰어! 이것도 공격이야!: We held! This counts as attacking too!
왔다! 심심해서 죽는 줄!: Finally! I nearly died of boredom!
늦었어! 먼저 나갈 뻔했다니까!: You're late! I almost went out without you!
Fixed. Heading back to the shade.
Repairs done. Quiet places are comfortable.
All done. I've marked where it'll wobble.
Held. The quiet side wobbled first.
Cut them off. I could see it all from the shade.
We held. I plugged the empty spot.
You're here. The shadows grew long.
You were gone long. I was watching it all.
Repairs complete. I take up the shield again.
Maintenance complete. I will walk behind.
They withdrew. The fortress did not move.
We held. The one ahead is safe too.
You have come. I never set down the shield.
I waited. The ship is as it was.
You have returned. All five stand.
Three crates had loose straps. Tied them.
Found a name tag. Just a code on it.
One hangar light's out. Reported it.
Know the Scrapworks route by heart. Could fly it eyes closed.
Your cargo too. Give. Sort together.
First time I stood in the hangar, it was quiet. Now it's loud. I like it.
Back, then the door. You there? Check.
Talked a bit today. Three words.
We're here. ...Wanted to say it once more.
Hearing your voice makes the sorting go faster.
Better now than the days I stood alone.
화물칸 정리, 아무도 안 시켰어. 해도 돼?: Sorting the cargo hold. Nobody told me to. Is it okay?
Please do. In any section you've touched, I can see where everything is.
Do it if you want to.
정리 담당을 따로 둘까?: Want me to put someone else on sorting?
Can see it all, you said. Left section tomorrow too.
I want to. So I do.
If someone else does it, what do I do? I'll do it.
폐공장 길, 오늘도 같았어. 지루해 보여?: Scrapworks route was the same again today. Look boring?
Coming back safe on the same route every time. Not everyone can do that.
새 출격지로 바꿔 줄까?: Want me to switch you to a new sortie site?
A little. Me too, a little.
I'll go even if you switch. Drop by the Scrapworks sometimes.
돌아오면 「다 왔어」만 해. 더 길게 말해야 돼?: When I get back I only say "We're here." Should I say more?
That one line says it all. Even that you're safe.
Says it all, you said. ...We're here.
This is what's comfortable. Sticking with it.
Reports. Letters, I can write long.
The day I stood alone in the hangar, I wasn't scared. They say everyone else would've been.
Even that day you went looking for something to do first. No room to be scared.
That was a long time ago.
The hangar lights must've been bright.
Found it. One crate. That was my first sorting.
It was dark. Still wasn't scared.
My partner on my first escort squad talked a lot. I only listened. Was that okay.
It was fine, I'm sure. A partner who listens is the most reassuring kind.
편성을 바꿔 줄까?: Want me to change the squad?
Next time. A word or so.
Not changing it. I like that partner.
Not cargo. I want to keep something of yours. Anything.
Then this. Put it at the very back of your cargo hold.
Nothing in particular to hand over, though.
Very back. That's where it shakes least.
It's fine if there's nothing. I'll keep the spot empty.
The name tag. I keep touching the worn-off spot with my fingertips. Don't know why.
Maybe touching it is a kind of sorting too. Just like you.
새 명찰을 하나 만들어 줄까?: Want me to make you a new name tag?
Sorting. ...Will it end once I've touched all of it.
Bored hands stack crates. This is a different hand.
A new one wouldn't say Aster. I'll keep this one.
Cargo hold didn't open. Blocked it all.
You're back. ...It was quiet a long time.
Today's haul, matched to the gram.
One more line in the ledger. Nice and clean.
When the load leans to one side, my back knows first.
Seven grams short. Where'd it leak?
왼쪽 칸이 삼 그램 무거워. 옮겨도 돼?: The left bay is three grams heavy. Mind if I move it?
Will you look over the ledger? There shouldn't be a single wrong line.
I hate a shifting load. Mine doesn't shift.
Everyone treats me like a senior because I've flown so long. The numbers get counted the same.
I made a new column in the ledger. What it's for, I don't know yet.
The loads you hand me weigh exactly right. Funny, that.
Today I want to close the ledger and talk about something else.
Fly long enough and the empty columns weigh more than the cargo.
I was counting your footsteps on the way here.
There's room left in the ledger, but the pen won't move. Because you're here.
Something I can't count showed up. I don't mind it.
You can't be weighed in grams. So I look at you often.
회수량을 그램까지 세는 거, 쓸데없어 보여?: Counting the haul down to the gram. Does it look pointless?
Matching to the gram is why your loads have never shifted once.
저울을 새로 사 줄까?: Want me to get you a new scale?
Never shifted, right. I'll keep it that way.
"Close enough" spills someday. Better that I count.
My back is more accurate than a scale. Thanks, though.
When I say I feel the cargo's weight balance with my body, everyone laughs.
Nothing to laugh at. Your unit is as good as your back.
They probably think it's a joke.
My back, huh. That's why I know first when the load tilts.
It's not a joke. Next time I'll show them in weight.
Sensors are slow. I know first.
장부 맞추다 보면 밤이 새. 같이 검산해 줄래?: Balancing the ledger keeps me up all night. Will you double-check it with me?
You read them out. I feel like just listening would check it.
A calculator would finish it in no time.
Just listen. That's the best double-check.
By tomorrow the numbers grow again. I'll do it today.
A calculator can't see a wrong line. I can.
캐리어 중에 내가 가장 오래 날았대. 오래 날면 뭐가 남는 것 같아?: They say I've flown the longest of all the Carriers. What do you think is left after flying that long?
Steady hands. Your loads are the proof.
비행 기록 패를 만들어 줄까?: Want me to make you a flight-record plaque?
Hands, huh. That's not an item in the ledger.
Wish fatigue could be counted too.
Plaques just gather dust once they're hung.
There's a column in my ledger I can't fill with numbers. Should I erase it?
Keep it. Even if numbers can't fill it, you're still counting something there.
Erase it if you're not using it.
Fewer columns would make the ledger lighter.
I'll keep it. Just keep it covered.
It's not unused. It's just not usable yet.
Getting lighter scares me. I won't do that.
내 장부는 숫자뿐인데, 너는 매일 뭘 세면서 지내?: My ledger is all numbers. What do you count every day?
The sound of your ledger pages turning. That's my daily clock.
A clock, huh. Then I'll turn the pages slowly today.
Nothing in particular? Then I'll tack your day onto the end of my ledger.
Too many stars. The ledger would run out.
A load that never shifts is my pride. But could I let it shift just once?
Go ahead and shift. If it spills, we'll pick it up together.
짐을 끈으로 더 묶어 줄까?: Want me to strap the load down tighter?
If we're picking it up together... I'll tie one bay a little looser.
Right. I know that, but sometimes my back itches.
Any tighter and I'd suffocate. Not the load. Me.
Back. Ledger and cargo weight, an exact match.
Repairs done. Center of gravity, right where it belongs.
Not one gram lost. Cargo hold's safe.
A lot of days went by. I logged every one in the ledger, though.
One lap when the sun sets. That's a promise, you know.
The farther you go, the longer the sunset lasts. Not scary at all.
Today's sky is more violet than orange.
I love the twilight. Everything goes soft.
Did you see the sunset earlier? I circled once and came back.
The farther the sortie site, the wider the sky. At dusk, it has no edge.
My lookout spot? I don't tell just anyone, you know.
When the way home falls at dusk, I come back slow on purpose.
Everyone's found my lookout spot. Still, a sunset shared is nice too.
Today's circle went half a lap extra. The colors were too good to waste.
Thanks for waiting through my dusk circles, everyone.
I don't photograph sunsets. I keep them in my eyes only.
Today's sunset, I wanted to show you first. It was violet, you know.
선회할 때 네 쪽 창을 한 번 지나가. 알았어?: When I circle, I pass your window once. Did you notice?
Going far is fine because this is where I come back to.
When the twilight comes, you're the first thing I think of.
노을 지면 한 바퀴 도는 거, 편성 시간 잡아먹지?: Circling once at every sunset eats into squad time, doesn't it?
That one lap is what completes your way home.
Take a photo instead of circling.
Complete. Without it, it's only half, you know.
Even a few seconds changes the whole sky.
A photo can't hold all that color.
Everyone says flying far is scary. For me it's thrilling.
Probably because the sky gets wider the farther you go.
Far places burn more fuel, though.
A widening sky. That sounds like me.
If we're different, I'll be thrilled enough for the scared ones too.
I'll go easy on fuel. Can't go easy on the sky, though.
하늘 색 이름, 내가 스무 개쯤 지어 놨어. 하나 들어 볼래?: I've named about twenty sky colors. Want to hear one?
들려줘. 오늘 하늘엔 어느 게 맞아?: Tell me. Which one fits today's sky?
You could just call them by color-chart numbers.
Today's is "orange before it cools." Just named it.
Similar, but different. It changes every minute, you know.
I don't want to memorize numbers. That's rude to the sky.
노을을 좋아하게 된 날은 생각이 안 나. 이상하지?: I can't remember the day I started loving sunsets. Strange, right?
Sometimes the things you love come without a date.
Doesn't matter if you can't remember.
Dig through the archive and it'll turn up.
Without a date. That's exactly how sunsets come, you know.
It doesn't matter. The sun will set again today anyway.
Would there be a sunset in the records? Tell me if you find one.
I showed my lookout spot to just one person, and in two days everyone knew. Funny, huh.
Means it was that good. Good enough to brag about.
Bragging. Hearing it that way makes me happy too.
Fast, yeah. Faster than the sun goes down.
A new spot? That angle only exists there.
선회할 때 무전을 잠깐 꺼 둬. 하늘 소리만 듣고 싶어서. 혼날 일이야?: When I circle, I switch off the radio for a bit. I just want to hear the sky. Will I get in trouble?
For one lap, it's fine. Switch it back on after.
I thought the radio was broken.
I'll switch it on right after. First words go to you.
If you didn't know, keep it a secret. Just between the sunset and me.
It's not broken. Just one minute alone with the sky.
노을이 오래오래 안 끝나는 데가 있으면 좋겠어. 어딘가 있을 것 같지 않: I wish there were somewhere the sunset never ends. Don't you think there's a place like that somewhere?
If there is, you'll find it first.
No night there, then. Sounds tiring.
If I find it first, you get to name it.
There will be. If not, I'll just circle a long time.
Even tired, I'd love it. I'll watch half asleep.
Back. Circled once on the way.
Repairs all done. Finished before the sunset.
Held them off. The sky's still the same color.
You came. I watched the sunset alone a few times.
Heard? Oh, wait. I'm not supposed to tell that one yet.
정비 도크 소식, 따끈한 거 있는데!: Got some hot news from the Repair Dock!
Quick hands, quicker mouth. That's me.
누가 승급했대. 누군지는 비밀!: Word is someone got promoted. Who? Secret!
있잖아, 오늘 격납고에서 제일 웃긴 일 알려 줄까?: Hey, want to hear the funniest thing in the hangar today?
격납고 소식 세 개 있는데, 뭐부터 들을래?: Got three pieces of hangar news. Which first?
Went hanging out at the dock. Their coffee is seriously awful.
빨리 말하다 혀 깨물었어. 웃지 마!: Bit my tongue talking too fast. Don't laugh!
Today, no news. I'll talk about me. Briefly.
There's stuff I know and still don't tell. Really.
I don't pass your stories on to anyone. That's a promise.
Of all the hangar news, yours is what I wait for most.
It bugs me that your news is the one thing I hear late.
Didn't hear a single rumor today. I was with you.
내 얘기 들을 사람, 너 하나면 돼. 이건 소문 내지 마!: Someone to hear my stories? You're enough. Don't spread this one, okay!
When the fast-talker goes quiet, you know what's up, right? It's 'cause I'm happy.
격납고 소식 내가 제일 먼저 아는 거, 시끄러워?: Me knowing hangar news first. Is it noisy?
Thanks to you I'm first to know who got hurt. It's a welcome noise.
방송 담당 해 볼래?: Want to try being the announcer?
고마운 소리래! 이건 소문 내도 되지?: A welcome noise, I heard! I can spread this one, right?
Sometimes means I'm tolerable, right? Great.
Announcing? Hand me a mic and I won't stop.
도크랑 친해서 수리 순서 당겨 온다는 소문, 들었지?: The rumor that I'm tight with the dock and get repairs moved up. You heard it, right?
Whatever the rumor, it's nice to see you getting along with the dock crew.
Nice to see, I heard! Gotta go brag at the dock.
사실이면 벌써 내가 떠들고 다녔겠지?: If it were true, I'd already be shouting it everywhere, right?
네 건 안 돼. 순서는 순서거든?: Not yours. Order is order, you know?
I'm the fastest at loading cargo. But everyone only remembers my fast mouth.
I know about the fast hands too. Your cargo's always loaded first.
빨리 실으면 흔들리지 않아?: Doesn't loading that fast make it shift?
You saw! Spread that one around for me.
Fair. But give the hands some credit too.
It doesn't shift. Fast and sloppy aren't the same thing.
누가 다친 걸 알고도 말 안 한 날이 있어. 소식통 실격일까?: There was a day I knew someone got hurt and didn't say. Does that disqualify me as the news source?
You were waiting for her to say it herself. That's part of the news source's job too.
The list of the injured is in the infirmary.
A news source who waits, huh. I'll remember that one too.
Not just once. There were a few more.
A list doesn't show the hurting faces, though.
격납고에서 나만큼 빨리 웃는 애가 하나 있어. 분하지 않아?: There's one girl in the hangar who laughs as fast as I do. Isn't that annoying?
When you two laugh together, half the hangar lights up.
웃는 것도 순서가 있어?: Is there an order for laughing too?
Hold a joke contest or something.
Half? With two of us it should light up all the way. I'll laugh more.
There is! News or laughs, I'm first.
If we held a contest, she'd win. Not spreading that one.
다들 남 얘기는 나한테 물으면서 내 얘기는 안 물어. 지휘관은 뭐가 궁금: Everyone asks me about other people, but nobody asks about me. What do you want to know, Commander?
What your face looks like after you've told everyone else's stories.
The five pieces of news you heard today.
My face? That's... I've never seen it either.
Nothing! Then I'll chatter beside you till something comes up.
Five, here goes. One, two... no, wait, that's not it.
I talk fast because it feels like if I stop, the next part won't come.
I'll wait even if it breaks off. Take your time.
Record it and it won't break off.
천천히… 해 볼게. 지금 이것도 빨랐지?: Slowly... I'll try. Was that fast just now too?
Fast, yep! But today I even said why.
A recording wouldn't notice if it broke off. That's scarier.
I'm back! Got three pieces of news from the way here.
Repairs done! Got a story from the dock too.
막았대! 아니, 내가 막았어!: Word is we held! No wait, I held!
어디 갔었어? 소식 잔뜩 밀렸다고!: Where'd you go? The news is piling up!
It's fine. Catch your breath first.
The newcomers trailing after me again today. Cute, aren't they.
One breath, then let's head out.
While waiting, quietly staying beside someone is best.
A newcomer's hands were shaking, so I swapped her gloves. That was enough.
The more urgent it is, the lower your voice. That's the trick.
Smooth route today. The newcomers will sleep well tonight.
I was beside a girl who got hurt. Until she fell asleep.
A newcomer led for the first time today. Watching from behind, I was the nervous one.
Lean on me sometimes too. I'll be the big sister.
The one in command gets tired too. Big sister knows.
I'm glad I don't have to stay calm in front of you.
When I get back, I look for your face first. If you look okay, big sister can relax too.
About the long road I was out on, I'll tell you someday. Not today.
Could I lean on you today? Just for a bit.
The newcomers keep following only me. There are plenty of other big sisters.
They say their hands stop shaking when they're beside you.
There's a phase for following someone around.
신입 교육반을 따로 열까?: Want me to set up a separate class for newcomers?
They stop? I'm glad. I'll walk with them again today.
If it's a phase, it'll pass. It's fine — missing it is big sister's job.
Even with a class, they'd end up sitting next to me.
They say everyone's calm when I'm in the squad. I just fly normally.
Flying normally is the hardest thing. Everyone watches you and copies it.
If they copy me, I'd better fly even more normally.
My skill's average. I know that well.
Someone else is good at leading. I'm comfortable at the back.
The more urgent the radio call, the lower I keep my voice. That's how everyone hears.
When your voice comes through, the other end of the radio goes quiet.
크게 말해야 들리지 않아?: Don't you have to speak loud to be heard?
I'll turn up your radio volume.
If it went quiet, good. Everyone got their breath back.
Loud makes even the newcomers rush along with it. So I go low.
Leave the volume as it is. A low voice carries farther.
Staying a long time beside a hurt girl. It's not like I'm doing anything for her.
When they wake up and yours is the first face they see, they feel safe.
You could just leave them to the infirmary.
If they feel safe... I'll stay late again today.
Even when I leave them there, my feet carry me back.
A snack. They do say they're hungry when they wake up.
옛날 길 얘기, 안 해서 미안해. 궁금하지?: Sorry I never talk about the old road. You're curious, right?
Curious, but I won't ask. You being here now comes first.
Being here comes first. Thank you, truly.
Only a little, then I'm relieved. That road's story can wait — slowly, later.
Go ahead and ask. They'll all just say "big sister."
지휘관은 지칠 때 누구한테 기대?: Commander, who do you lean on when you're tired?
Lately my steps keep heading your way.
There's no one I lean on.
Then I'll be wherever your steps land.
If there's no one, big sister will come to your side first. Slowly.
A bed's nice too. I'll tuck the blanket in for you.
Sometimes I wish someone would stay beside me for a long time too. Is that greedy?
It's not greedy. Today I'll stay a long time.
A long time... then I'll bring out one more cup of tea.
Everyone does? What a relief. I thought big sister was the only greedy one.
A newcomer? They'd fall asleep first.
We held. No one's hurt, so don't worry.
You're back. Were you all right? Take your time telling me.
The wind says this way. I'll follow.
Light, light. The cargo and me both.
Where'd I come from? Hmm, somewhere over that way.
With all five together, the hangar air felt light. Floaty.
The wind blew right. So I drifted a little right too.
Keep the cargo straps loose. Cargo needs room to breathe too.
Floated out and back. Cargo's all there.
There's one girl who listens to me without laughing. You're that kind too.
Not being in the records doesn't weigh much on me.
If you call, I'll ride the wind and fly to you first.
The hangar wind is always weak. So here I walk slowly.
The way to you, I know without asking anyone.
I'll stay here today. Taking a break from drifting.
My heart feels light today. Maybe because I'm beside you.
Even when I act playful, being here is for real.
내 짐이 안 없어지는 건 바람이 길을 알려 줘서야. 믿어?: My cargo never goes missing because the wind shows me the way. Believe it?
I believe it. Your cargo always shows it.
항법 장치를 바람이라고 부르는 거지?: You're calling your nav system "the wind," right?
Shows it, you say. The route will get a big head hearing that.
Luck rides in on the wind too. Just take it lightly.
No device installed. It's really the wind. Heh.
기록 없이 들어온 기체래, 나. 신경 쓰여?: They say I'm a unit that came in with no records. Does that bother you?
You being here right now is more certain than any record.
Guess I'd better lock the hangar door.
Certain, you say. Makes me want to stop for a moment.
Not much? Good. Not much for me either.
Even locked, there are gaps. I'm good at slipping through those.
I like traveling light. When it's heavy, I can't see the way.
So that's why your cargo always looks light. Even though you carry the same.
Heavy or not, cargo gets loaded.
짐을 줄여 줄까?: Want me to lighten your load?
It only looks that way. There's a way to share the weight.
I'll load it. Flying light while carrying it is my knack.
Don't cut it. I'll be the one acting light.
When I talk about the wind, everyone laughs. But there's exactly one girl who doesn't.
Because someone doesn't laugh, your story gets to keep going.
Try talking about an anemometer instead of the wind.
Keep going. In front of her, I talk at length.
Laugh all you want. I don't sulk.
An anemometer doesn't know direction. The wind does.
You know the girl who circles once at sunset? Flying on her tail, the air's soft.
Flying on her tail without a word. She probably knows.
뒤에 붙으면 위험하지 않아?: Isn't it dangerous flying right behind her?
Circling together must burn more fuel.
She knows and pretends not to. I like that.
My body measures the gap on its own. We won't collide.
A bit more. But I rode the wind that much farther.
There was a day the wind told me nothing. That day, I picked the way myself.
You made it back fine on the way you picked. Without losing a single piece of cargo.
Even the wind must take days off.
On days like that, stay in the hangar.
The way I picked. Saying it out loud, I feel kinda proud.
If it was a day off, maybe I should've rested with it.
If I stay in the hangar, the wind can't find me.
Never losing a thing is heavy sometimes. Is there anything I can let go of?
You can let go. What slips away, I'll remember with you.
Empty the cargo hold and you'll be lighter.
If you'll remember it with me, maybe I'll let one go.
It's good, sure. But drifting always leaves something behind.
Emptying is easy. The heart doesn't empty.
Light again. Thanks for fixing me.
Rode the wind. Nothing got taken.
The wind told me first. That you were coming.
Back. Haul matched to the decimal.
Back. One more line in the ledger.
Back. Weight difference zero. Feels good.
Back. The sunset ran long today.
Back. One lap — that's a promise.
Back. The far-off sunset was prettier.
Back! Today's news is still hot.
다녀왔어. 이건 비밀인데, 들을래?: Back. This one's a secret — wanna hear?
Here! Heard something fun on the way.
Back. The new girls are all fine too.
Back. Catch your breath — let's rest now.
Back. The wind showed me the way.
Took a while. I tidied up.
You came. Cargo's as it was.
Repairs done. Logged it in the ledger.
We held. Not a gram went out.
They withdrew. Zero loss — I'll log it.
You're here? The ledger's backed up.
You were gone long. I logged every date.
You came. The weights haven't changed.
Fixed. I can go watch the sunset.
Repairs done. I'll take a lap.
All done. The sky's still bright.
We held. The sky's the same color.
물러갔어. 이제 한 바퀴 돌아도 되지?: They withdrew. Can I take a lap now?
왔구나. 같이 노을 볼래?: You're back. Watch the sunset with me?
Took you long. The sun set three times.
I waited. Circling alone is boring.
Fixed! Heard one more bit of dock gossip.
수리 끝! 이건 비밀인데…: Repairs done! This is a secret, but…
다 됐어! 정비반 얘기 들을래?: All done! Wanna hear the crew's gossip?
지켰대! 아니, 우리가 지켰어!: They say we held! No, we did hold!
You're here! I've got a mountain to tell you.
어디 갔었어? 소식 식겠다!: Where were you? The news is going cold!
You came! You're the first I'll tell.
고쳤어. 이제 아프지 않지?: Fixed. It doesn't hurt now, right?
Repairs done. Let's catch our breath and go.
All healed. I'll go check on the new girls too.
We held. I'll look after the ones who got scared.
왔구나. 많이 바빴지?: You're back. You were busy, huh?
I waited. It's okay, take your time.
Been a while. Everyone missed you.
Fixed. Good for riding the wind.
Held. The wind was on our side.
We held. Didn't lose a thing.
They withdrew. The wind changed direction.
You're back. The wind got warmer.
You were gone long. The wind was bored.
You came. I knew by the smell of the wind.
A good day, defined? One where fewer get hurt.
When the math is quiet, so is the judgment.
Units due back — I'll count them once more.
Everyone's in. Today's report is short.
An empty damage column means nothing to read. That's good.
A squad roster is numbers. Numbers are calm. I like that.
On days my frame feels heavy, my words get short. Today is one.
My report handwriting's gotten a little rounder lately, apparently. Someone said so.
There's someone I want to ask whether my call was right. You.
I came to report, but words come out before the numbers.
When the gauge needle wavers, I look your way. Then it stops.
Defining things is my job. You don't fit a definition.
The hull is warm. Only when you're on the Bridge.
Can I come even with nothing to report? Today is that kind of day.
I drew a place for you into my blueprints. The dimensions are classified.
계기판 바늘은 표정이 없어서 읽기 쉬워. 사람 얼굴은 어려워. 내 얼굴은: A gauge needle has no expression, so it's easy to read. Faces are hard. What about mine — can you read it?
Easier than a needle. Your lips move when you count.
My lips move. That's a scale no gauge has.
"I don't know" is an honest answer too. I can't read my own face either.
Practice, and I'd end up like a needle. I'll pass.
손상 보고가 한 줄뿐인 날은 쓸 게 없어. 그런 날 보고서, 심심해 보여: On days the damage report is one line, there's nothing to write. Do those reports look dull?
One line is plenty. It's the long days that are scary.
They're easy to read. I like them.
Write a bit more next time.
I'll cut down the scary days. That's my job.
I write them to be easy. Glad they read well.
For a long one, someone has to get hurt. I'll keep it short.
다른 애 기체에 긁힌 자국을 보면 내 장갑이 근질거려. 이상해?: When I see scratches on another girl's frame, my armor itches. Is that strange?
You fly together, so you feel together. Not strange at all.
Just send it in for repair.
Feeling together. Then keeping them from getting hurt is together too.
I'll send it in. Though itching isn't on the repair list.
Hands can't reach armor. I'll take the thought.
다른 기함들 설계도가 내 걸 보고 복원됐대. 무거운 일일까?: They say the other flagships' blueprints were restored from mine. Is that a heavy thing?
Your lines held the others up. Heavy, but a good kind of weight.
You should at least get a design fee.
Held them up. Defined that way, it got lighter.
In the past. Right. The girls coming in now matter more.
If I'm owed anything, I'll take it as everyone coming back safe.
귀환하는 기체를 세다가 하나가 늦으면 숫자가 거기서 멈춰. 그 사이에 나: When I'm counting returning units and one is late, the number stops there. What do I do in the meantime?
Call out to me as far as you've counted. We'll wait for the rest together.
Leave the counting to the instruments.
Call out what I've counted. The stalled number will weigh less.
They'll come. I'll hold on to those words while I wait.
Instruments only count. They can't wait.
지휘를 내려놓은 나는 뭐라고 정의하면 될까?: Me, with command set down — how would you define that?
Definitions can wait. For now, just stay beside me.
A definition put off till later. That's a first for me.
A flagship on break. Even that smells of work.
More classes, more math. No, thanks.
내가 판단을 틀리는 날이 오면, 넌 먼저 뭘 물어볼 거야?: If the day comes when I get a call wrong, what will you ask first?
Whether everyone made it back. The call comes after.
보고서가 몇 장인지?: How many pages the report is?
Whether everyone's back, first. Same order as mine.
I won't factor "won't get it wrong" into the math. Thanks, though.
As for pages — the fewer, the better the day.
All units back. I'll keep the report short.
My armor's quiet again. Repairs done.
We held. I'll count the numbers later.
You're here. I won't count the time I waited.
Half the noise scattered. The other half stayed.
I like days when even a quiet voice gets through.
I just left one signal on, that's all.
About half of today's jamming scattered. Everyone just held through the rest.
I'll keep comms on. Call and I'll hear you right away.
Noisy zones? I just get a little louder.
My antenna tip feels hoarse. Guess I shouted a lot today.
In zones with lots of jamming, everyone looks for me. I kind of like that.
Your voice comes through clear even in the noise. Funny, huh.
There's someone I want to measure by something other than signal strength.
Can we talk with comms off? I don't want this one on record.
Not talking loud — I'm practicing talking soft. For you.
I put one channel of yours on my frequency. That's all.
My signal today — not far. Just to here.
Even when I call softly, you turn around. I like that.
교란이 절반은 남잖아. 그걸로 모자라다고 느껴?: Half the jamming still gets through. Does that feel like not enough?
You cut half, so everyone can hold through the rest.
Everyone holds, huh. Hearing that makes my voice get a little louder.
Half is half. Yeah — I just do exactly that much.
Earplugs would block me out too. That's a problem.
My voice is too loud when I open comms, right? Everyone says it hurts their ears.
In the noise, that's the volume it takes. The way comes before ears.
Try turning it down a little.
The way before ears. That's just what I wanted to say.
I'll turn it down. Just on days without noise.
I can't sing. My pitch won't lock on like a frequency.
출격 전에 주파수를 몇 번이고 다시 맞추는 거, 답답해 보여?: Me re-tuning the frequency over and over before a sortie — does that look tedious?
Every extra tune means everyone gets less lost.
Let's switch everyone to one channel.
Less lost, huh. Then I'll tune once more.
I'll handle it my way. It's how I've always done it.
One channel, and all the noise piles onto that one. That's trouble.
재머 애들이 비결을 묻길래 목청 덕이라고 했어. 너무 대충 답했나?: The Jammer girls asked my secret, so I said it's just my big voice. Too lazy an answer?
That's not lazy — that is the real secret. Nothing to hide.
Warm tea is supposed to be good for the voice.
Nothing to hide — I like that.
Explaining gets long. Long means noise creeps in.
Tea won't reach my antenna. It'll warm me inside, though.
시끄러운 구역에선 다들 내 채널부터 찾아. 함교에서 듣는 쪽은 어때?: In noisy zones, everyone finds my channel first. How is it listening from the Bridge?
I open your channel first too. It's the clearest.
They all sound about the same.
The clearest, huh. My signal's going to get stronger for no reason today.
About the same, huh. Then I'll just have to get a bit clearer.
Soundproofing, huh. My voice'll get over that wall too.
크게 외치는 건 쉬운데, 진짜 하고 싶은 말은 잘 안 나와. 어떻게 하면: Shouting is easy, but what I really want to say won't come out. What do I do?
Say it softly. I'm listening on that frequency too.
Softly. Then I won't shout this time.
I'm afraid writing gets erased. I'll try anyway.
That's my work voice. This is different.
모함이 제일 조용해지는 때를 찾는 중이야. 같이 찾아 줄래?: I'm looking for when the Mothership gets the quietest. Will you look with me?
After everyone's back and maintenance is done. That's the stillest time.
그런 때가 있긴 해?: Is there even such a time?
After maintenance. I'll save my voice for then.
There is. It's just so brief it's easy to miss.
Shut the engines off and everyone jumps. Me too.
Everyone's in. Signal stayed clear to the end.
Antenna's clear again. I can hear fine now.
The raid's passed. Just thanks to the facilities holding.
Oh, got you. Haven't caught your signal in a while.
I carry the heavy stuff, so it's fine.
Three Hangar slots. Don't call it cramped.
The front line's mine, so move.
The others are fine again today. Because I was up front.
Didn't scrape the wall coming into the Hangar. Really.
My frame's heavy, right? That's how solid it is.
Ready to sortie. I checked the others' gear too.
Standing in front doesn't scare me. Just between us — it scares me a little.
Looking after the others, I keep putting off my own maintenance. Look after me a bit, would you?
Thick armor, so they figure my heart's thick too.
The very front, I'm used to. An empty space at my back is what feels strange.
With you I don't have to play big sister. It's easy.
A three-slot frame gets small in front of you. Weird, huh.
다른 애들 다 재우고 왔어. 이제 좀 쉬어도 되지?: Put all the others to bed. I can rest a little now, right?
Let's carry the heavy stuff together. Just this once, I'll try saying that.
I take up three whole slots, so the Hangar's cramped, right? I'm asking because I feel bad.
Those three slots are why the other slots are safe.
The other slots are safe, huh. Then I'll take mine proudly.
Expanding it'd be great. The others' slots first.
Frames don't get lighter with practice. You're funny.
출격하면 저쪽 기함이 꼭 나부터 노려. 이게 좋은 걸까?: When I sortie, their flagship always goes for me first. Is that a good thing?
With you up front, everyone gets hurt less. In return, I'll do the worrying about you.
You do the worrying, I take the hits. Not bad.
I know it can't be helped. That's why I'm the one who stands there.
Popular, huh. That kind of popularity, I'm not handing to the others.
출격 전에 다들 장비를 내가 한 번씩 봐. 참견 같아?: Before a sortie, I check everyone's gear once. Does that seem nosy?
Not nosy. After you check, everyone's face relaxes.
Their faces relax, huh. Honestly, that's what I check for.
