They can handle it, sure. Still, I have to look once before I can rest easy.
No badge, thanks. Nowhere to pin it but my armor.
출격하면 늘 내 옆에 붙는 애가 있어. 말은 별로 없는데. 왜 하필 내: There's a girl who always sticks beside me on sorties. Doesn't say much. Why next to me, of all places?
Maybe she heard why you stand in front.
That spot was probably just open.
네가 제일 커서 그늘이 지나?: You're the biggest — maybe it's the shade?
She heard, huh. Then I really can't back down in front of her.
An open spot. She always stands there on purpose, though.
Playing big sister to the others — do I look tired? Be honest.
If you're tired, come set it down here. You don't have to be big sister here.
Skip big sister — be the auntie instead.
I can set it down? Then I'll sit a little before I go.
Not letting it show is a big sister's job. Guess I'm doing fine.
Auntie's too far off. I'll stay big sister.
내가 무거워서 못 따라가는 데가 생기면, 기다려 줄 거야?: If there's somewhere I'm too heavy to follow, will you wait for me?
I'll wait. Just don't push yourself to keep up.
Guess I'd swap in someone lighter.
I won't push it. Someone's waiting for me.
When it happens. Okay — I'll ask again then.
Swap me, and who stands at the very front? No way.
언니 노릇 말고 해 보고 싶은 게 하나 있어. 뭔지 맞혀 볼래?: There's one thing I want to try besides being big sister. Want to guess?
누가 네 앞에 서 주는 거?: Having someone stand in front of you?
Caught me. Only sometimes — really, just sometimes.
You'd laugh if I told you. I'll tell you next time.
Cooking? My hands only know how to lift heavy things.
The others went in first. I'm last.
Fixed. I'll stand in front of the others again.
You're back? Everyone was waiting. Me too, a little.
Redid the positioning chart. Third time.
It's not about deciding front and back. It's about sharing it evenly.
If losses are even every round, that's enough.
Draft positioning chart. Go through it line by line.
Today's losses came out even every round. A decent day.
Two in front, three behind. This time, that's right.
Tell me before you change the squad. The chart gets tangled.
Showing my chart to you makes me the most nervous. Why is that.
I doodled in the corner of the chart. Don't erase it.
When everyone moves by the chart, I feel proud. I can tell you that, I think.
It's not about handing you a chart. It's about looking at it together.
I'm clumsy with things off the chart. Being with you is off the chart.
Sitting without calculating — I can only do that next to you.
Some days don't go as planned. On those days, I'll come to you.
줄 맞추는 버릇, 네 앞에선 좀 풀어도 되지?: My habit of lining everything up — I can loosen it a little around you, right?
라운드마다 손실이 고르게 나오게 짜는 거, 어떻게 보여?: Building it so losses come out even every round — how does that look to you?
It's making sure no one carries it alone.
As long as the results are good.
So no one carries it alone. I'll put that at the top of the chart.
I watch results too. Even process makes even results.
It's not dice. It's a chart I've revised over a hundred times.
When you change the squad, could you tell me first? The chart gets tangled.
Got it. Before changing anything, I'll check your chart first.
Telling you every time is a hassle.
Things seemed to run fine without a chart.
My chart first. Thanks — I'll only revise it once tonight.
I know it's a hassle. So I'll hear it short and fix it short.
굴러가는 것처럼 보이게 하는 게 표야. 몰랐지?: Making it look like it runs itself — that's what a chart does. You didn't know?
앞에 세울 애를 고를 때 제일 오래 고민해. 기준이 뭐 같아?: Picking who goes in front takes me the longest. What do you think my criterion is?
Whoever's least tired that day. You look at condition, not order.
That I look at condition — you caught that. I don't write it on the chart.
Put only the strong one up front and only she gets hurt. I don't do that.
Deciding that way would be easy. Maybe I'll try it once.
표에 넣을 수 없는 애가 하나 있어. 제멋대로 서는데 늘 맞아. 어떻게: There's one girl I can't fit in the chart. She stands wherever she likes, and she's always right. What do you think?
Some girls are right off the chart. Your chart left room for that.
Just leave her off the chart.
Left room, huh. Seeing it that way, it stings less.
Leave her off, and the spot she stands best in disappears. I won't.
If memorizing worked for her, she'd be on the chart already.
밤마다 배치표를 한 번 더 고치다 잠들어. 말려야 할까, 둘까?: Every night I fall asleep revising the chart one more time. Stop me, or let it be?
Revise it once, and we'll go over the rest tomorrow together.
Try using the chart as a pillow.
Together tomorrow. Then just once tonight.
Even tired, my hand goes to the chart. That's the problem.
A paper pillow rustles. It'd wake me up.
다들 서는 데는 내가 정하는데, 나는 어디가 좋은지 모르겠어. 골라 줄래: I decide where everyone stands, but I don't know where I belong. Will you pick for me?
Anywhere you can catch your breath. It doesn't need to be on the chart.
A place not on the chart. That's new, so I'm a little nervous.
It's not a safe bet. The middle is the busiest spot.
The front belongs to another girl. Not mine.
계획대로 안 된 날엔 표를 펴 놓고 어디서 틀어졌는지 찾아. 못 찾는 날: On days that don't go to plan, I spread out the chart and look for where it went off. What about the days I can't find it?
If you can't find it, you weren't wrong either. Close the chart and come here.
No plan, nothing to go off.
I'm okay too, huh. Then I'll close the chart and go.
Forgetting. That's the hardest thing for me.
That's scary to hear. I can't even imagine a day without a plan.
I'm back. Came in by the chart.
Back on the chart. With the repairs written in.
You're here. I did nothing but revise charts meanwhile.
오늘도 씩씩하게 갈게요!: I will go out bravely today too!
다들 저를 감싸요. 왜일까요?: Everyone shields me. I wonder why?
I may be the baby, but I am a flagship. Please do not forget!
Commander, I am all set to sortie! Please check me over.
The older girls blocked the way in front of me again. I can do it too, you know.
오늘 배운 거 보여 드릴까요? 정렬이 빨라졌어요!: Shall I show you what I learned today? My lining up got faster!
My frame is still light. That means I can go that much faster!
지휘관님 앞에서는 씩씩한 척 안 해도 될까요?: Is it all right if I do not act brave in front of you, Commander?
After training my frame gets toasty. They say it means I worked hard!
Coming here after training has become a habit.
When I stood at the very front, my frame was shaking. It is a secret!
When you are watching, Commander, the flag feels lighter.
To the older girls I am still the baby, but to you, Commander, I want to be a flagship.
You do not have to praise me. Just stay by my side, please.
When I get better, please keep watching me like you do now.
가장 어린 기함이라 보정이 약할 줄 알았는데, 똑같대요! 신기하죠?: I thought being the youngest flagship meant a weaker bonus, but they say it is the same! Isn't that amazing?
Of course it's the same. You're a flagship too.
더 세게 만들어 줄까?: Want me to make it stronger?
당연하다고 해 주시니까 어깨가 쫙 펴져요!: You say of course, and my shoulders straighten right up!
It is! I laughed for ages when I first heard.
Stronger? Then the older girls will get jealous.
출격 전에 깃발 신호 연습을 해요. 한 번 봐 주실래요?: I practice flag signals before sorties. Would you watch once?
Show me. I'll watch till the end.
깃발 색 바꿀까?: Should we change the flag's color?
끝까지요? 그럼 제일 어려운 동작까지 할게요!: Till the end? Then I will do even the hardest move!
Later for sure, okay? I will keep practicing.
I like the color as it is. Everyone follows this color.
다들 저를 감싸 주는 게 고마우면서도 조금 속상해요. 이상한가요?: I am grateful everyone shields me, but it also stings a little. Is that strange?
Both feelings are right. You grow as much as it stings.
감싸지 말라고 명령할까?: Should I order them not to shield you?
Both feelings are right. I will hang that on my flag!
I am grateful. But that is not all of it.
No orders! It is how the older girls feel.
같이 나가는 언니 하나가 제 정렬을 말없이 고쳐 줘요. 저도 그래 주고: One of the older girls I sortie with quietly fixes my alignment. I want to do that for someone too. Where should I start?
Keep watching her hands closely, like now. That's your first practice.
It'll come naturally as you grow.
정렬 자동으로 맞추는 장치 달까?: Want a device that aligns you automatically?
Watch her hands! Starting today, I will watch with my eyes wide open.
Naturally? Then I will practice while I wait.
Her hands are more precise than any device. Really!
교관님 훈련은 무서운데 끝엔 꼭 잘했다고 해 주세요. 지휘관님도 칭찬 잘: The Instructor's training is scary, but at the end she always says I did well. Are you good at praise too, Commander?
Starting with today's. Your alignment really got faster.
보셨어요? 그 말 듣고 싶어서 연습한 거예요!: You saw? I practiced because I wanted to hear that!
Only when needed makes it even more precious. I will wait.
The Instructor's share and the Commander's share — I want both!
언젠가 언니들 앞에서 깃발을 흔들고 싶어요. 그때 함교에서 봐 주실 거죠: Someday I want to wave the flag in front of the older girls. You will watch from the Bridge then, won't you?
From the best seat there is.
깃발 대신 확성기는 어때?: How about a megaphone instead of a flag?
The best seat! Then I will hold it even higher.
Please make time. I will be waiting just for that.
A megaphone… that seems like another big sister's job.
언니들한테 아직 고맙다는 말을 못 했어요. 언제 하면 제일 좋을까요?: I still have not thanked the older girls. When would be the best time?
When everyone's disembarking. Say it then and they'll all hear.
Right when you think of it.
When everyone disembarks! I will say it the moment I lower the flag.
Right away? I just thought of it, but they are not here.
My handwriting is wobbly for letters. I will say it out loud.
We all came back! Every single one.
Repairs done! Back to being brave!
시설이랑 언니들 덕분에 막았어요!: We held, thanks to the facilities and the older girls!
Commander! I waited a long time. Truly.
The top, you see, is where the wind blows hardest.
Once the five had gathered, the next in line was me.
Keep to your turn. I keep to mine.
The older the chain-of-command chart, the heavier the paper.
Do not be startled that the chain of command has grown by one line.
Five flagships aboard one ship. That is rare — be proud of it.
Bring your reports up slowly. I know how to wait.
My frame is heavy, as if it slept a long while.
The top of the chart is not always a comfortable place.
They say my name was on this Mothership's old chain-of-command chart.
Of you alone, I will not ask rank.
When you enter the Bridge, the wind dies down.
Since I woke, this is the first time I have wondered about tomorrow.
Walking beside you, I forget to count my steps.
Today, not at the top — keep me at your side.
Before you, rank blurs. I do not mind it.
다섯 기함이 다 모인 날에야 내가 왔지. 그 순서가 맞았다고 보니?: Only on the day all five flagships gathered did I come. Do you think that order was right?
The five paved the way first, so there was a place for you to stand.
You could've come a bit sooner.
After the way was paved. Then I ought to bow my head to those five.
Doesn't matter? Then I, who count rank, look rather foolish.
Had I come early, there would have been no place to stand. The wait was worth it.
내가 오고 나서 함교에 서열 하나가 늘었지. 불편하지는 않니?: Since I came, the Bridge has one more rank. Is that not uncomfortable for you?
The top carries the top load too. Let's carry it together.
Wherever the names are, it's fine.
순위표처럼 매주 바뀌는 거 아냐?: Doesn't it change every week, like the Ranking board?
To carry it together. You are the first to say so.
Wherever, hm. Such generosity — so like you.
If it changes every week, I simply climb back up every week.
맨 위 자리는 바람이 세단다. 올려다볼 때, 거기 선 이가 춥게 보이니?: The wind is strong at the top. When you look up, does the one standing there look cold?
A little. That's why I look up often.
외투 하나 보내 줄까?: Want me to send up a coat?
You look up often. Then I shall look down often.
If you cannot see it, then I must be holding up well.
A coat? If it fits over a hull, I shall accept it.
서열이며 순번이며, 세는 버릇이 있지. 어디서 생긴 것 같니?: Rank, turn order — I have a habit of counting. Where do you suppose it came from?
Maybe because you have to know who's first and who's last to look after everyone.
Just how you were made, probably.
To look after everyone. Put that way, this habit feels less cold.
Born with it. Perhaps. Counting came to my hands first.
Studying? Are you to assign me homework, then?
다섯 기함이 나를 어려워하는 것 같구나. 그대가 보기엔 어떠니?: The five flagships seem wary of me. How does it look to you?
It's not wariness — you're just still new to them. Time will ease it.
Time will ease it. If it is the work of waiting, I am good at that.
If that is how it always is, I shall approach them first.
With fewer orders, how am I to speak? I shall think on it.
순번 없이 설 데가 있다면 그대 곁이었으면 하는구나. 허락하겠니?: If there is a place to stand without a turn number, I would have it be at your side. Will you allow it?
That's a place that needs no permission. Come anytime.
No permission needed. I have never heard such words.
If I want. Then let me say clearly that I do.
A number, hm. So even at your side, I must stand in line.
그대와 나, 둘이서만 정하는 일을 하나 갖고 싶구나. 무엇이 좋겠니?: You and I — I would like one thing that only the two of us decide. What would be good?
When to turn off the Bridge lights today. Let's decide that together.
When to put out the lights, the two of us. It is small, which is why I like it more.
내가 정하면 또 줄을 세울 텐데. 괜찮겠니?: If I decide, I will line things up again. Will that be all right?
Cleaning duty, hm. You first, and I after.
All have returned. Not one out of order.
Repairs are complete. Back to the top of the chain.
They have withdrawn. The facilities held their places.
You took a long while. Still, your turn is just where you left it.
Returned. One line is enough for the report.
Everyone's in. About half the static's left.
Back. I'll keep the frequency set.
Sent everyone in first. I'm last.
Back. I carried the heavy stuff.
Back. Three hangar slots, full again today.
Back. Nothing to fix on the chart.
Back. Front and rear even, everyone safe.
Back. Already drew up the next lineup.
다녀왔어요! 깃발도 무사해요!: We're back! The flag's safe too!
We're back! Everyone was so brave.
We're back! I'll lead the way next time too.
We have returned. The wind was strong, but nothing fell.
Everyone has returned, dear. Order unchanged.
We have returned. I could see it all from the top.
Fixed. I'll log it as a less-hurt day.
Held. I'll keep the damage report short.
We held. The instrument readings are fine.
You're back. One line's enough for the report.
I waited. The instruments don't lie.
Repairs done. I'll retune the frequency.
We held. Only half the static's left.
You're here. I was waiting just for your signal.
You were cut off a long time. I can hear you now.
Fixed. I'll stand at the very front again.
Repairs done. The heavy stuff's mine again.
All done. Three hangar slots, back in use.
We held. I took all the hits up front.
They withdrew. You can rest now.
You're back. I let everyone rest first.
I waited. Me too, a little.
Took a while. I was holding the heavy stuff.
Fixed. Logged the repair time on the chart too.
All done. Front and rear evened out.
Held. Stood exactly by the chart.
We held. Not one slot in the lineup changed.
They withdrew. Already drew up the next chart.
You're here. This is the fourth chart.
I waited. Your place is on the chart too.
You were gone long. The lineup's unchanged.
고쳤어요! 깃발 들 준비 됐어요!: Fixed! Ready to carry the flag!
Repairs done! I'll lead the way again.
다 됐어요! 하나도 안 아파요!: All done! Doesn't hurt at all!
We held! The flag's still up.
They withdrew! The big sisters are the best.
You're here! I kept holding the flag.
오래 걸리셨네요. 그래도 좋아요!: You took a while. But I'm glad!
Repairs complete, dear. Back to the top.
Repaired, dear. I can face the wind again.
All done, dear. The chain of command held.
Held, dear. Though the wind was strong.
We held, dear. All five in place.
They withdrew. The order is unchanged, dear.
You've come. I kept your place open, dear.
I waited, dear. It's cold at the top.
It took a while. But the order holds, dear.
Send the heavy stuff my way.
Coming back empty isn't in my record. I'll salvage something.
A load this light bores my hands.
Let's see where the salvage goes.
Today's heaviest load? I loaded it. Go check.
There was still good stuff in the wreckage. Grabbed it.
Give the light work to someone else. Heavy's mine.
Those crates stacked at the dock? I hauled every one. Worth bragging about.
I watch who picks through the wreckage I unload. It's fun.
A cockpit sitting heavy with a full load. That's my pride.
With you, I can say something's heavy. Nowhere else.
Left one of today's finds on your desk.
On my heaviest days I look for your voice first. Then I haul it all the way home.
You're the only one I show my finds off to.
When you call, I turn around before I set the load down.
If you're glad to see me, the next load can be heavier.
They said this crate takes two, right? I'm lifting it alone. Watch.
I'm watching. Right down to the sound when you set it down.
Sure, go ahead and lift it.
Good sound, right? A full crate sounds low.
Lifted. No one watching, so it's less fun to brag.
No idea. I only know the weight. That's enough.
잔해 사이 부품, 다들 지나치는데 난 못 지나친다. 이상해 보여?: Parts in the wreckage — everyone walks past them, but I can't. Look weird to you?
That's an eye that knows they'll be useful.
Pick them up or don't. Either way.
You'll end up smelling like wreckage.
Right. Whatever I pass up, I always miss later.
Then I pick them up. An armful again today.
Already does. Stays even after washing. That's the smell of work.
가벼운 회수만 연달아 나가니까 손이 근질거린다. 무거운 데 없어?: Nothing but light hauls lately. My hands are itching. Anywhere heavy?
I'll send you to a hot zone with plenty of stock piled up.
손 주물러 줄까?: Want me to rub your hands?
That's it. My hands get real work today.
I'll take that as "call me first when one turns up."
What my hands want is cargo. But I'll take the thought.
처음 주운 부품이 누구 수리에 들어갔어. 그날부터 빈손이 싫다. 유난이지: The first part I ever picked up went into someone's repair. Ever since, I hate coming back empty-handed. Overdoing it?
Someone got fixed because of you. That's not overdoing it.
Empty hands are light. Isn't that nice?
Put that way, even today's finds look precious.
Different for me. I'm built this way. Built for heavy.
Light, and the cockpit floats. Doesn't suit me.
테스라한테 넘긴 부품이 라인에서 돌아가는 소리가 나면, 내 거 같다. 그: When the parts I hand Tesla start running on the line, they sound like mine. Sometimes I go just to listen.
It's the sound of your finds running. Of course it's welcome.
가서 일 방해하는 거 아니야?: Aren't you getting in the way over there?
Welcome. As much as lifting something heavy.
Noisy, yes. Mine's mixed in there.
I don't get in the way. I just listen from a corner.
언젠가 내 짐칸에 못 싣는 게 나오면 어쩌나 싶다. 아직 한 번도 없었다: Sometimes I wonder what happens the day something won't fit in my hold. Hasn't happened once.
Then we'll put our heads together and find a way to load it.
Then split it into two trips.
Find it together, huh. Now I'm almost looking forward to that day.
Hearing "won't happen" straightens my shoulders. I'll keep it that way.
Two trips? One trip is my pride. I'll think about it.
Out of everything I've hauled in, name one thing you were gladdest to see.
Not the cargo — the sound of you touching down.
The thud? Then next time I'll land even bigger.
All the same, huh. Next time I'll haul something you can't miss.
Someone else has the eye for cores. I'll get picked for heavy.
Back. Salvage and all, a full load. Take a look.
All fixed. Give me the next load.
Blocked. Not a scratch on anything I hauled.
You're here. I stacked up what I found while you were gone.
Think this is enough? There's still a slot left.
Seeing an empty slot makes me feel hollow.
무거워야 덜 흔들려. 아직 가볍지 않아?: Heavier means steadier. Isn't this still too light?
Isn't there anywhere to load a little more?
오늘 화물칸, 끝 칸까지 채웠어. 그래도 모자란 것 같지?: Filled the hold to the last slot today. Still feels short, right?
Saw stock left at the sortie site. Leaving it feels hollow, right? Next time, down to the bottom.
남을 만큼 실어 와야 교환소에도 돌리지. 아직 모자라지 않아?: Gotta haul in extra if any's going to the Exchange. Isn't it still short?
Go out light? I'd rather not.
On the way to the Exchange, the load gets lighter. Makes me a little sad.
When the load's short, my spine bends. It takes weight to straighten it.
I sway less when you're watching, I think. Wonder why.
On long round trips I like listening to songs. They mix with the sound of the cargo.
Next to you, maybe one empty slot's okay. Just today.
Load your worries into my hold too. Then I'll sway less.
가끔 나한테 묻게 돼. 이 정도로 되겠냐고. 너라면 뭐래?: Sometimes I ask myself: is this enough? What would you say?
I'll keep the hold door shut today. Don't think I need to peek.
회수 다녀왔어. 화물칸 반만 찼어. 이 정도로 되겠어?: Back from the haul. Hold's only half full. Think this is enough?
Half is everything that site had. That's plenty.
So the other half is air.
All of it? Then I'll call today enough.
So laid-back. Still, I feel a little better.
Air weighs nothing! Ugh, you made me laugh. You win.
남는 재고, 교환소로 넘길까 아니면 더 쌓아 둘까?: The extra stock — send it to the Exchange, or keep piling it up?
Send it over, and you get to go haul that much more.
Let's build a tower out of the stock.
True. Empty it, then go fill it again.
"Either way" means I pile it all up, right? Till it overflows.
A tower? If it falls, I just load it again. Not bad.
출격 대기 중엔 화물칸 문을 열어 둬. 닫아 두면 안이 비었는지 자꾸 열: On standby I leave the hold door open. If it's shut, I keep opening it to check if it's empty.
Keep it open. When there's something to fill it with, you'll hear first.
안에 화분이라도 하나 두지?: Why not put a potted plant in there?
Then I'll leave it open. So I can load whatever comes, right away.
If it doesn't matter, it stays open. Don't peek. It's not full yet.
A plant? That'd weigh something, at least. Maybe I'll get one.
재고가 하나도 없던 날 있잖아. 돌아와서 도크를 못 떠났어. 왜였을 것: Remember the day there was no stock at all? I came back and couldn't leave the dock. Why do you think?
Nothing to fill — you didn't know where to stand.
도크 청소라도 했어?: Did you clean the dock or something?
Yeah… when it's empty, I can't tell where I'm standing.
I wasn't resting. I was waiting. For anything to come.
I did. Three times. Still had time left over.
카린이랑 나가면 둘이서 출격지를 바닥까지 긁어. 그 애 옆에선 내 욕심이: When Karin and I go out, we scrape the site to the bottom. Next to her, my greed looks less strange.
Two greedy ones side by side. That's reassuring.
You two are going to fight over the last crate.
Reassuring, right? Load together and there's no empty space.
Not a lot. All of it. An empty slot feels hollow, right?
We did fight once. Ended up splitting it half and half.
누가 이 정도면 됐다고 해 주면 믿어 볼래. 너라면 어떤 날 그 말 해: If someone told me "this is enough," I'd try to believe it. On what day would you say it?
The day you come back empty-handed and you're still smiling.
Empty-handed… and smiling? Can't picture it. I'll try.
No set day, huh. Then I'll ask a little every day.
If storage overflows, I'll probably stop loading. Maybe. Maybe not.
짐 없이 그냥 날아 보라고 하면 나 흔들릴까? 한 번쯤 해 보고 싶기도: If I flew with no cargo at all, would I sway? Part of me wants to try it once.
If you sway, come back. I'll be watching from the bridge window the whole time.
Load a rock instead of cargo, then.
The whole time? Then your eyes can stand in for the weight. I'll try.
Once I try… yeah. I'll come back and tell you how many times I swayed.
A rock? Feels like cheating. Still… maybe just one.
Back. Wish I'd had one more slot.
수리 끝. 이제 무겁게 실어도 되지?: Repairs done. I can load heavy now, right?
Held them off. Not one slot in storage went empty.
You're here. The empty hours went on too long.
여기야, 여기! 보이지?: Over here, over here! See me?
형광색은 어두울수록 잘 보여. 이쪽 봐!: Fluorescent shows up better the darker it gets. Look this way!
When it's pitch-dark, look for my light first.
Nobody lost, right? I'll count once more.
오늘도 다 같이 돌아왔어. 내 뒤로 줄 맞춰서!: Everyone came back together again today. Lined up behind me!
If we go somewhere dark, I'll take the lead. I stand out, after all.
Tell me if you spot any chipped paint. I'll touch it up right away.
You can call me the signal lamp. I don't mind it.
On days I get a fresh coat, I kind of want to go somewhere dark.
같이 찾으러 다닌 애랑은 눈만 마주쳐도 웃어. 불 켠 것처럼!: The girl I went searching with — we still smile the second our eyes meet. Like lights switching on!
When I glow in the dark, it tingles all the way to my tail.
When I see the Mothership's lights, I feel safe too. Even a signal lamp needs a signal lamp.
When you're looking for me in the dark, all you have to do is look. I'll be there.
Will you be my signal lamp today? Just once.
Even in the pitch-dark, I can tell where your voice is coming from.
Today I'll stay still and not blink. Because I'm next to you.
어두운 구역 회수야. 내가 앞장서고 다들 뒤로 붙으면 되지?: A haul in a dark zone. I lead, everyone sticks behind me — that works, right?

If it's dark, everyone can just turn their lights on.

Front of the line, obviously. I'll light up the dark side first.

형광 도색 덧칠하는 날이야! 오늘 색 어때? 눈부셔?: It's fresh-coat day! How's the color? Dazzling?

좀 더 차분한 색은 어때?: How about something a bit calmer?

But you can see it, right? Then that's enough.
Calm gets lost in the dark. Shining is my job.
돌아오는 길에 한 명이 자꾸 뒤처져. 난 기다려 주고 싶은데, 그럼 편성: On the way back, one girl keeps falling behind. I want to wait for her, but then the whole squad's late.

짐까지? 좋아, 앞에서 반짝이며 끌어 줄게!: Her cargo too? Okay — I'll tow from the front, shining all the way!
길 잃은 편성 찾으러 갔던 얘기, 다들 물어봐. 근데 그 얘긴 잘 안 나: Everyone asks about the time I went looking for a lost squad. But that story doesn't come out easily.

대신 무용담 지어내 줄까?: Want me to make up a heroic tale instead?
Everyone together. That's all it takes.

같이 길 잃은 편성 찾았던 히나 말이야, 지금도 출격 전엔 꼭 내 도색부: Hina, who searched for the lost squad with me — she still checks my paint before every sortie. Why, you think?

It puts her at ease. Then I'll shine even brighter.

바랬다고? 당장 덧칠하러 간다!: Faded? I'm going for a fresh coat right now!

If your light goes out of sight, I'll be the first to notice.
The first, huh. Maybe I'll blink out on purpose sometimes.

Hide-and-seek isn't fair. Wherever I hide, I can be seen.

Next return, come home by the Mothership's lights. I'll keep them on.
If you're in the back, nobody can follow you.
The light you left on. Today I'll come home by that.
If I get the okay, I'll definitely try it! The sky, following someone else's light.
Oh, right. I'll just shine extra bright from the very back.
다 같이 왔어. 불빛 하나도 안 꺼졌어!: Everyone's back. Not a single light went out!

Held them off! Didn't even have to dim my lights.
Over here! That took a while. Thought you'd gotten lost.
Look at what isn't broken, not what is.
This one's usable. That one isn't.
I'm weak in a fight, so I stay in back. Picking up comes after.
I like the debris belt. It's quiet. Easy to sort through.
Picked a Core out of the wreckage today. Put it in the locker.
When the fighting's over, send me in first. I want to look before it cools.
Half the parts I pick get tossed. The half that's left is the real thing.
You know I'm weak, right? Keep me out of combat squads. Hauls, as many as you like.
Cold wreckage doesn't lie. It's exactly what it looks like.
Got an off-spec servo. Fits me perfectly.
I'm still bad at listening to battle reports. When you read them, they're bearable.

The least broken thing I picked today — it's yours.
With you, I don't have to sort anything. It's easy.

교전 끝난 데 잔해 띠, 나 혼자 먼저 들어가 봐도 돼?: The debris belt where the fighting ended — can I go in first, alone?

This part's half burned, but the inside isn't broken. Lots of girls toss things on looks alone.

Picking is my job anyway. I'll keep it.
The smell fades. The use doesn't.
싸움에 약한 애를 회수에 넣는 거, 손해라고 생각해?: Putting a girl who's weak in a fight on hauls — think that's a loss?

Not everyone, no. I'll keep that.
Don't weigh it. If you do the sums, I might lose.
Getting stronger is the others' job. I'm the one who looks.
카린이랑 다니면 걔가 내가 고른 걸 다 실어. 반은 버리라고 해도 안 버: When I go out with Karin, she loads everything I pick. I tell her to toss half, and she won't.

Hands that can't let go. Right. That's why I have to pick better.

If I load, I drop half. If she picks, she brings it all.
유키는 명찰을 찾고 나는 부품을 찾아. 둘 다 남은 걸 찾는 거래. 비슷: Yuki looks for name tags, I look for parts. She says we're both looking for what's left. Look alike to you?

둘이 바꿔서 찾아보면 어때?: Why not swap and search each other's way?

Swap, and we'd both come back empty-handed. Our eyes are different.
잔해 띠에 혼자 오래 있으면 누가 불러 주길 기다리게 돼. 안 부르면 계: When I'm alone in the debris belt for a long time, I start waiting for someone to call me. If no one does, I'll just stay.

잔해 띠에 침낭 하나 갖다 놓을까?: Should I put a sleeping bag out in the debris belt?

Back. Picked out a few usable things.
Fixed. More of me isn't broken now.

I'll be in before this song ends.
한 소절만 더 부르고 출발!: One more verse, then we're off!

출격 전엔 목부터 풀어야 해. 짐보다 노래가 먼저야~: Before a sortie I warm up my voice first. Song before cargo~
편성 애들이 내 노래로 시간을 재. 한 박자도 틀리면 안 되지~: The squad times things by my songs. Can't miss a single beat~
Load to the beat. Then nothing sways.
Even cargo sounds like a beat. Clunk, clunk, rest.
긴 왕복엔 옆에서 조용히 듣는 애가 있어. 관객 하나면 충분해~: On long round trips, someone listens quietly beside me. An audience of one is plenty~
노래 부르면 기체 속까지 울려. 그게 좋아~: When I sing, it rings all through my unit. I love that~
네 앞에서 부르면 박자가 자꾸 빨라져. 왜지?: When I sing in front of you, the tempo keeps speeding up. Why?

네가 듣는 걸 알면 목소리가 좀 커져~: When I know you're listening, my voice gets a little louder~
The first song I sing when I'm back — that one's yours.
이번 회수 왕복, 몇 곡쯤 걸릴 것 같아? 맞혀 봐~: This haul's round trip — how many songs, you think? Guess~
거기 머니까, 네 노래로 다섯 곡쯤?: It's far, so… five of your songs?

짐 싣는 동안 노래하면 다들 손이 빨라져. 오늘은 무슨 곡으로 할지 골라: When I sing during loading, everyone's hands move faster. Want to pick today's song?

아무거나면 내 맘대로. 오늘은 빠른 거~: Anything? Then my pick. Something fast today~

출격지가 멀어지면 노래가 길어져. 듣는 애들 지루하지 않을까?: Farther sortie sites mean longer songs. Won't the listeners get bored?

한 소절 건너뛴 날 말이야. 다들 시간을 못 맞혔는데 그날 회수가 제일: That day I skipped a verse — everyone got the time wrong, but that was our biggest haul. Funny, right?

내 노래, 다들 시간 재느라 듣잖아. 노래로만 들어 주는 사람 하나쯤 있: Everyone listens to my songs to keep time. I'd like at least one person who just listens to them as songs.

목도 기체도 다 풀렸어~: Voice and unit, all loosened up~
노래 한 번도 안 멈추고 막았어~: Held them off without missing a single note~

Sortie order. Me, last. I see everyone.

You, too. On my shoulders. Not heavy.
Your footsteps. Light. But I hear them.
Today, my shoulder. Lean. Holding up is mine.

Isn't it all the same cargo?

If it's easier, then that. The weight, my shoulders.
Not the same. Lands different on the shoulders.
Not all. Six of us. That's right.
격납고 바닥. 내가 들어서면 울린다고들 해. 시끄러워?: The hangar floor. They say it rings when I step in. Too loud?

바닥에 방석이라도 깔까?: Want a cushion on the floor?
Reassuring. I'll take that word with weight.
Didn't hear it. Then next time, I'll stand even slower.
A cushion. It'd get crushed flat.
짐 묶는 끈. 나는 한 번 더 감아. 풀릴 일 없어도. 쓸데없어?: Cargo straps. I wrap them once more. Even when they won't slip. Pointless?
Everyone rests easy because there's a hand that wraps once more.
Doesn't look any different to me.
Let's jump rope with that strap.
If it ties down hearts too, the strap's earned its keep.
Looking no different. That's the good part.

다섯이 한 격납고에 선 밤에 내가 왔어. 그 밤, 너한텐 어땠어?: I came the night the five stood in one hangar. That night. How was it, for you?

If it felt the same, I blended in well.
카린은 내 짐 놓는 데를 알아. 나도 걔 걸 알아. 말 없이. 그런 사이: Karin knows where I set my load. I know hers. No words. What do you call that?

Neighbors. Our holds are side by side. So, true.
Swap, and we'd both be lost a long while.
어깨에 얹은 거, 나는 말 안 해. 대신. 네 어깨엔 뭐가 얹혀 있어?: What's on my shoulders, I don't say. Instead. What's on yours?

Six. Then we're on each other's shoulders.

Stiffness. That one I can't carry for you.

With you standing there, my back would feel covered.
Stand there and it'll block all the light behind.
Up to me. Then I'll stand.
Ah. Then half a step to the side.
You came. Long time. The floor was quiet.
Hauled it all. The heavy ones are mine.

Back. Didn't leave a single slot this time.
Back. No empty slots — feels solid.
Back. Wish there'd been one more slot.
여기야! 다 같이 왔어!: Over here! We all made it!
돌아왔어! 어두운 데서도 잘 보였지?: Back! Easy to spot in the dark, right?
Back. Took everything but the junk.
Back. This one's usable. Left the rest.
Arrived~ Two and a half songs today.
I'm back~ Added one more song.

Repairs done. Give me the heavy stuff.

Held. Didn't lose a single crate.
We held. I blocked the heavy ones.
They withdrew. The pickups are still here.
You're here. Look what I picked up.
Took you long. I stacked the cargo.
고쳤어. 이제 꽉 채워도 되지?: Fixed. I can pack it full now, right?
Repairs done. Empty slots are such a waste.
All done. Wish I could load one more slot.
Held. Not a single slot emptied.
We held. The storehouse is still full.
They withdrew. They didn't take a thing.
You're back. Let's go fill the empty slots.
I waited. Empty slots make me sad.
Took a while. Lots to fill.
Fixed! The lights are bright again.
All done! You'll see me even in the dark.
Held! Not one light went out.
지켰어! 여기 있다고 다 보였지?: We held! Everyone could see us here, right?
Took a while. I kept the lights on.
You're here! I thought you got lost.
All done. Nothing to throw away.
We held. The only scraps left are on their side.
They withdrew. More intact than broken.
You're here. I gathered the usable stuff.
You were gone long. Still intact, though.
왔구나. 골라 둔 거 볼래?: You came. Wanna see what I picked out?
Fixed~ My throat's loosened up too.
All done~ I'll pick the next song.
Held~ Didn't miss a single beat.
지켰어~ 노래가 응원이 됐지?: We held~ My song cheered you on, right?
물러갔어~ 끝곡은 신나게!: They withdrew~ The last song's an upbeat one!
You're back~ A few songs piled up.
I waited~ Singing alone is boring.
Took a while~ I've got a new song.
You came. The floor rumbles again.
Something I ought to hear, I don't. Checking.
Hangar vents, half a beat late. Irritating.
Commander. Reporting today's Bridge noise reading. Below average.
Today's sortie: their fire confirmed off. Cause: me.
Quiet is good. Except the quiet of dead comms.
Ready room: too loud. Evacuated to the Hangar.
Bridge speaker: repaired. Reason: your orders were clipping.

On standby I keep the Bridge audio playing. Instead of noise.

One thing I can't put in a report now. You.
Today I'll keep the jamming veil off and stay here. Something to listen to.
The sound of you turning pages: steady tempo. Reassuring.
다들 내가 시끄러운 게 싫어서 이 일 하는 줄 알아. 틀린 건 아닌데,: Everyone thinks I do this job because I hate noise. Not wrong. Incomplete.
조용한 것 중에도 싫은 게 있는 거지?: Some kinds of quiet you hate too, right?

The Bridge speaker crackling. Doesn't it bother you? Or is it just me.
들려. 왼쪽 거지? 네가 고쳐 줄래?: I hear it. The left one? Could you fix it?
음악이라도 틀까?: Want me to put on some music?

이 배는 무슨 소리가 나?: What does this ship sound like?
I tend to just wait without thinking about much.
Thoughtless waiting is quiet too. Acceptable.
While you sleep, I'll do the listening.
Silen and I only greet each other by frequency. Out loud, we both get awkward.
주파수 인사도 인사지. 오늘은 했어?: A frequency hello is still a hello. Did you do it today?
그게 무슨 인사야?: What kind of greeting is that?
Out loud, we both freeze. Experimental data on file.

작전 중에 채널이 텅 비는 순간이 있어. 그때 네 쪽 채널, 열어 둬도: Mid-operation, there are moments the channel goes completely empty. Can I keep yours open then?

무전기 하나 더 달아 줄까?: Want me to install another radio?

Not more hardware. Your channel is what I want.

정비 맡겨 볼까?: Want to send it in for maintenance?
Moves as one. That phrasing: adopted.

Does maintenance fix a pulse too. Interesting.
교란막 끄고 들으면, 안 꺼졌으면 하는 소리가 하나 있어. 측정은 안 할: With the veil off, there's one sound I don't want to go silent. I won't measure it.
No need to measure. Let's keep that sound on a long time.

Raid stopped. Their aim stayed off to the end.

No need to dim the lights today. It's just you.
출격 편성, 레이더에서 흐리게 해 뒀어. 혹시 너도 못 찾았어?: I blurred the sortie squad on radar. Did… you not find us either?
Found you. I know where you'd put yourself.
Let's make it stand out more.
