Let's look when they come again.
To someone. Yes. That is why this column exists.
My notes are next to the numbers, too. Please look at those as well.
When they come again, I will write again. One more line each time.
건너편 손실을 쓰는 건, 그쪽도 누가 짜 보낸 편대였겠다 싶어서예요. 이: I write the other side's losses because I think someone must have put that squadron together and sent it out, too. Is that strange?
It's not strange. Having someone who sees it that way keeps things less harsh.
That's a feeling battles don't use.
Less harsh. I will write that in our side's column.
Battles may not use it, but reports do. That is my part.
There is nowhere to send it. So I keep it.
습격 기록은 같이 읽는 분이 있어요. 둘이면 숫자가 덜 차가워요. 지휘관: There is someone I read raid records with. With two, the numbers feel less cold. And you, Commander?
These days I read your notes first. Then the numbers look like people.
Like people. Then I will add one more line of notes.
For when you skim, Commander, I will underline things for you.
If they are cold, we can warm them with our hands. I will read them to you.
I would like to write a report on a day no one was hurt, with even the other side's column empty. Will that day come?
It will. You pull it one line closer every time.
It'll come if there are no engagements.
Then the report would be too short.
One line at a time. Then I will not miss today's line either.
With no engagements, my pen would be bored. I would still like that.
Short reports are the hardest. I would still like to try writing one.
제 보고서 읽으실 때, 제일 오래 보시는 칸은 어디예요?: When you read my reports, Commander, which column do you look at longest?
The other side's column. Your handwriting slows down most there.
You noticed the slow handwriting. I hesitated a long time there.
The totals are correct too. I counted three times.
There is only a date on the cover. Next time I will add at least a small drawing.
You are back. I will write down both sides' losses right away.
Repairs are done. I will record it as good as new.
We held. I hope the squadron that withdrew made it home safely, too.
You have arrived, Commander. I gathered all the reports while you were away.
Pick up one more wrench and it's like having three hands.
I tightened the recovery unit's bolts myself again today.
I like the smell of the dock. Oil and steel.
Even while I wait, I don't let my hands sit idle.
Time flies at the dock. My hands keep busy.
I sorted the Chief's toolbox again today.
A recovery unit's still a unit. It listens once hands have worked on it.
One lift's free. I'll bring up the next unit.
Did you hear the talk about repairs getting faster? It's like there are more hands.
With the Chief, the tools go back and forth without a word.
When you come by, Commander, my hands slow down a little. Because I'm talking.
I took my oily gloves off before coming today.
Sitting here without the sound of tools — I learned that here.
If I have a hand to spare, it's yours, Commander.
The Chief told me to head up early today. She must know who I'm meeting.
Once I've fixed everything, I always end up here. Funny, isn't it?
회복 기체는 남한테 안 맡기고 제가 손봐요. 고집 같으세요?: I don't leave the recovery unit to anyone else. I work on it myself. Does that seem stubborn?
A unit that's been through your hands even sounds different.
You could just swap in a new one.
You know the sound. I'll go tighten one more bolt.
The crew's busy too. It's like I'm lending a hand.
A new unit takes a long time to get used to my hands.
제가 도크에 있는 날은 수리가 빨리 끝난대요. 진짜일까요?: They say repairs finish faster on days I'm at the dock. Is it true?
With you there, the tools never rest. It's true.
There probably wasn't much to fix those days.
도크 시계가 빠른 거 아니야?: Isn't the dock clock just fast?
The tools never rest. Neither do my hands.
There's no such thing as a day with nothing to fix. I'll find something.
I checked the clock too. It's accurate, luckily.
수리 끝난 기체를 리프트에서 내릴 때, 저는 꼭 한 번 쓰다듬어요. 다음: When I lower a repaired unit off the lift, I always give it one pat. So it comes back less often.
A unit that gets that touch will be careful out there.
I hope it's careful. Even so, if it comes back, I'll welcome it again.
Busy or not, I never skip that one pat.
The shine's a bonus. While my hand's there anyway.
반장님이랑은 공구로 말이 통해요. 렌치를 내밀면 다음 할 일이 보이거든요: The Chief and I talk through tools. When one of us holds out a wrench, the next job's clear. Amazing, isn't it?
That's how much you've fixed together.
Everyone gets like that after enough time.
If I counted what we've fixed together, I'd run out of fingers.
Some pairs never click, however long they work. I'd say I'm lucky.
If we talk, both our hands stop. That's slower.
I sometimes look over the other Medic units too. Especially the ones flying the same recovery unit. Am I being nosy?
Two pairs of hands that know the same unit — that's reassuring.
Everyone can just handle their own.
Reassuring, you say. Then I'll look over one more today.
Handling only our own means things get missed. That's why.
You don't have a unit, Commander. I'll tighten your chair's screws instead.
이 배 전체를 한 번 손봐 보고 싶어요. 회복 기체만이 아니라요. 너무: I'd like to go over this whole ship once. Not just the recovery unit. Is that too big a dream?
One bolt at a time, you'll reach all of it someday.
배를 통째로 리프트에 올려?: Put the whole ship on a lift?
One at a time. Then I'll go tighten today's share first.
Exactly. That's why I called it a dream.
The lift would cry first. Still, it'd be fun.
공구 중에 하나만 고르라면 뭘 고르시겠어요? 그걸로 지휘관님 몫 공구함을: If you could pick just one tool, which would it be? I'll put together a toolbox for you around it, Commander.
The wrench you hold most often.
A hammer. Just bang on everything.
My wrench. Then I'll give you a well-worn one.
If anything's fine, I'll pick. The lightest one.
A hammer's the last resort. The Chief would scold me.
You're back. I'll lower the lift right away.
Repairs are done. I checked the bolts once more too.
We held. I'll have the scratched armor straightened out before the day's over.
You're here? I sorted the toolbox twice while you were gone.
How long till the next return… Yeah, I know.
I like the breeze at the entrance. Everyone comes in this way.
Ready to call names. I'll warm up my voice.
If they're late, I just count again.
I've already worked out when the squad gets back.
The hangar entrance is my workplace. A little cold, though.
When I call their names as they climb out, everyone's shoulders drop.
I've been watching the return route so long my neck's stiff.
Distance, speed, fuel — they keep rolling around in my head.
There's someone I race at calculating. Lately I'm a little ahead.
Someone whose hands come before her words often comes by my side.
Waiting has more to do than you'd think.
All my numbers were right today. The time left over is yours.
When you show up while I'm waiting at the entrance, I get happy for no reason.
Calling names — today I'll do it once more, for you.
Your footsteps I know without counting.
The next return time — how many minutes off do you think I'll be? Let's bet.
You almost always nail it. No point betting.
They'll get here more or less.
If we're betting, put up a snack.
You caught me nailing it. Then this time, down to the second.
More or less won't do. I have to be standing there when they climb out.
Snacks, good. If I win, let's share them at the entrance.
다친 애가 내리면 괜찮냐고 묻기 전에 이름부터 불러. 이상해?: When someone hurt climbs out, I call her name before asking if she's okay. Weird?
Hearing your voice must make them glad to climb out.
Glad to climb out. I like that. I'm using it today.
It does matter, I told you. Names come first.
I don't like numbers. Everyone has a name.
People often tell me to wait inside, but the hangar entrance has the best view.
It's where they see you first, the moment they climb out.
Right, me the moment they climb out. That matters.
Inside's warm, but the first face comes later.
With a telescope I could wave even sooner.
You think I memorize return times, right? Actually I'm counting the whole time. My head never rests.
That's how much you don't want to miss a single one.
That sounds like a headache. Rest.
Because I don't want to miss anyone. Hearing that makes me less tired.
I'm faster than a calculator. Really.
Rest comes after everyone's back. I'll rest then.
나보다 빠르다고 해 준 애가 있어. 근데 그 애도 매번 다시 재 보자고: Someone once told me I'm faster than her. But she still comes every time wanting to measure again. Rivals are nice, right?
Measuring each other means neither of you gets a chance to slack.
No chance to slack. My calculating's gotten better for it.
It does matter! I want to be ahead, even a little.
She wins the races. I win the math.
네가 격납고에 들르는 시각만 계산이 안 돼. 어떻게 정하는 거야?: The only thing I can't calculate is when you'll drop by the hangar. How do you decide?
I don't decide. I come when I want to hear your voice.
Then I'll speak up. So you can hear.
I'll start counting from when your work ends. I'll figure it out soon.
The clock? Then I'll know before you do.
가끔은 내가 늦게 돌아오는 쪽이 되고 싶어. 누가 입구에서 내 이름 불러: Sometimes I want to be the one who comes back late. How would it feel to have someone call my name at the entrance?
I'll call it. I'll just wait, no counting.
I'll call you by a nickname instead.
No counting. That's the hardest thing there is for me.
True, but I wanted to be the one greeted, just once.
No nicknames. When you climb out, it has to be your name.
They're here, they're here! Right on my numbers, not late at all.
Repairs done! I'll redo the next return calculation.
We held. I counted everyone at the entrance — all here.
You're here? None of my numbers worked out. But you came, so that's fine.
Shh. I know where it hurts.
Smell of salve. I like it.
No need to talk. I'll stay close.
Recovery unit. Fits my hands now.
The one at the entrance. Waiting again today.
Words can't be late. So, hands first.
When you come… I talk a bit more.
Next to you, my fingertips don't tingle.
Not with hands. With words, too. Thank you.
The squad. Hurt, but no sound. Why.
Maybe they go quiet when your hand touches them.
When my hand touches… Yeah. Maybe.
Holding it in — I hate that. If it hurts, say so.
But your hands are faster than anyone's.
Practice… tried. Always comes out short.
회복 기체, 소리 작게 켜. 놀라지 않게. 괜찮아?: Recovery unit. I keep it quiet. So no one startles. Okay?
Because you keep it quiet, everyone can lean on it easy.
It matters. To the ones who hurt.
Strength comes from hands. Not sound.
Once, my words came too late… Since then, hands first. Wanted to tell you.
Thanks for telling me. Everyone holds on thanks to those hands.
입구에서 기다리는 애 있지. 그 애가 이름 부르고, 나는 그다음 손. 둘: The one waiting at the entrance. She calls the name, then me, hands. We fit. Right?
A name, then a hand. Then they're all the way home.
All the way home. Yeah. I like that.
She's good at calling. I'm hands.
With you… words first. What first.
Anything. If you pick the words, I'll hear them all.
If there's nothing to say, you don't have to.
No weather in the hangar. …Try anyway?
Beside someone hurting, my unit's fingertips tingle too. Is that bad.
It means you're that close to them. It's not bad.
Close. Yeah. I like it there.
If I rest… the tingling goes. I hate that more.
Gloves, and I can't feel. No good.
Day is breaking. It is still up on the roof.
The roof is cold. Still, one can see well from there.
Seeing before the radar does is my part.
It is the hour when dawn light touches the armor.
I have been up on the roof and looked once around the ship.
It was quiet again tonight. That is a blessing.
I tend to keep my unit standing on the roof.
During night raids, there is someone who watches the same direction. It is reassuring.
Even when the radar is quiet, I look once more.
Standing night watch, I find myself giving constellations new names.
After I come down from the roof, my armor stays cold for a long while. It warms soon enough, though.
This morning's dawn light came from your side first, Commander.
I know your voice at once, Commander, even over the comms.
Now there is someone to greet the dawn with.
What I saw through the night, I will tell only you, Commander.
지붕 위에서 보면 레이더보다 먼저 보여요. 믿으시겠어요?: From the roof, I see things before the radar does. Would you believe that?
Your eyes reach first, so the night's less frightening.
Less frightening at night — then climbing the roof was worth it.
It is accurate. But a radar cannot see into hearts.
Thank you for your concern. Still, that is my watchtower.
Around dawn, I make one round of the ship. That hour is the loveliest.
That's light only someone who watched the whole night gets to see.
It'd be brighter in the daytime.
Only those who watched. When you say it so, the light is lovelier still.
Even sleepiness is washed away by the dawn light. Is that not strange?
Bright and lovely are not the same. Do come see it with me sometime.
함이 조용한 밤이면, 저는 오히려 귀를 더 기울여요. 고요한 게 더 크게: On nights when the ship is quiet, I listen all the harder. Sometimes stillness is what sounds loudest.
Things are easiest to hear when it's quiet.
Yes. Only in stillness can small sounds be heard.
The dawn carries tiredness away. Please do not worry.
With music on, I would miss the small signals in the static on the comms.
지붕에 오르면 들어오는 쪽이 먼저 보여요. 그래서 밤마다 올라가요. 걱정: From the roof, I see whoever is coming in first. That is why I go up every night. Does it worry you?
I know everyone sleeps soundly because you're up there.
지붕 말고 창가에 서 있으면 안 돼?: Couldn't you stand by a window instead of the roof?
If everyone sleeps soundly, the roof is not cold at all.
If it is only a little, I am glad. Please do not worry too much.
From a window, one sees only the inside of the ship. I want to know what is outside.
밤 습격 때 저와 말없이 같은 쪽을 보는 분이 있어요. 지휘관님은 그런: During night raids, there is someone who watches the same direction with me, without a word. What do you think of a pair like that, Commander?
If you can trust someone with your back without words, that's the deepest kind there is.
You could just talk over the comms.
Trusting someone with your back. Yes, it is exactly that kind of night.
There are days we cover more, too. When we split the view.
Talking would mask any sign from that direction. So we watch in silence.
While I am on the roof, may I radio the Bridge now and then? Even with nothing to say.
Do it. Even if you say nothing, I'll know it's on.
As long as it's not sleep-talk.
Even just being on. Then tonight I will press it only once.
For urgent things, I will tell you before the radar does.
I do not talk in my sleep. At night, I am awake.
지붕에 기체를 세워 두면, 제가 함 전체에 닿아 있는 것 같아요. 그런: When my unit stands on the roof, it feels as if I am touching the whole ship. Do you know that feeling?
So that's why you see first. You breathe with the ship.
Probably because the roof is wide.
Breathing together. Tonight I will think of those words.
I do not think it is only the height. Thank you all the same.
Even a wide roof looks narrow once my unit stands on it.
The squad has returned. I watched from the roof to the very end of the route.
Repairs are complete. I can stand watch again tonight.
We held them off. I am glad I saw them first from the roof.
You have come, Commander. I kept watch from the roof through the nights you were away.
You're back. Nothing hurts? Let me look.
Everyone's here. I'll check you one by one, slowly.
You're back. I'll log losses on both sides.
All safe. I'll keep the report short.
You're back. I'll note the other side's losses too.
You're back. I'll check the bolts first.
You're back. I was waiting with a wrench.
You're back. Raising the lift now.
Here! The math checked out exactly.
Back! Not off by a single minute.
Arrived! Already counted the next return time.
You're here. Show me where it hurts.
You've returned. I watched it all from the roof.
The squad is in. The wind was gentle today.
All healed. The light flows evenly.
Held. I'll check the injured first.
We held. It's okay, not yet.
They withdrew. I'll check everyone slowly, one by one.
I waited. I saved my "it's okay" for you.
Took a while. I'll look after you now.
Repairs are done. I'll log it.
Fixed. The report will say it's intact.
All done. I noted both sides.
Held. I'll log losses on both sides.
We held. I hope the ones who withdrew are safe too.
They withdrew. I'll write the report right away.
You're here. I gathered the reports.
I waited. There's a bit for you to read.
You were away long. The records are all here.
Repairs are done. Retightened the bolts.
Fixed. I'll put away the wrenches.
Held. I'll straighten out the scratches right away.
We held. Not a single bolt came loose.
They withdrew. I'll bring the toolbox.
You're here? I tidied the toolbox three times.
I waited. I kept the lift free.
You took a while. The bolts are all in place.
Repairs done! I'll redo the return math.
All done! Counted the next departure time.
Held! Counted everyone at the entrance.
They withdrew! Everyone's here, I counted.
You came! My math was all off.
You're here! You came, so that's enough.
Held. Show me where it hurts.
Repairs are done. I'll go back up to the roof.
It's fixed. I'll keep watch tonight too.
We held them off. I saw them first from the roof.
We held. The night sky has grown still.
You've come. I waited on the roof.
You've returned. I kept watch through several nights.
It took a while. Still, the day is dawning.
Two o'clock. One cold engine trail.
Three o'clock. Temperature tells me first.
Trails last long. Longer than words.
Ten o'clock, Debris Belt. We go around it today.
The engine trail was still warm. It passed not long ago.
The squad's rear is six o'clock. I watch that too.
I call the headings before a sortie. You just hear the last one.
I set twelve o'clock to your side. It's easier.
No debris in your direction. That's why it's easy.
Heard I talk short. For you, I'll go a little longer.
No recon, no heading to call. So I came here.
If I lose my heading, I'll look for your voice first.
Five o'clock… No. Just beside you.
I only ever read cold things. Then I found one warm one. You.
There's a heading that isn't on the clock face now. Yours.
식은 엔진 자국을 보면 지나간 게 보여. 따분한 일 같아?: A cold engine trail shows me what passed. Sound boring?
You can tell what passed from something cold. That's impressive.
Nothing impressive. I've just watched trails a long time.
It is boring. So I do it alone, quietly.
Radar sees now. I see a little before.
출격 전에 방향을 시계로 불러. 시끄럽지 않아?: I call headings by the clock before sorties. Not too noisy?
By the clock, I get it in one go.
동서남북으로 말하면 안 돼?: Can't you use north, south, east, west?
In one go. That's what I want.
Better if you don't mind it. Let it drift past like sound.
North changes every time out here. The clock doesn't.
레이더가 안 닿는 데도 미리 보여 줄게. 어느 쪽부터 볼래?: I'll show you past radar range, ahead of time. Which way first?
Whichever way you point to first.
Then two o'clock. I always look there first.
If it's up to me, the quietest way.
Mess hall's eleven o'clock. Go see that yourself.
회랑에선 치카 등불이 있어야 방향이 보여. 고맙다는 말, 어떻게 하지?: In the Corridor, I only see headings with Chika's lantern. How do I say thanks?
When you call headings, call Chika's first.
Buy her a present or something.
Her direction first. Tomorrow's first heading, then.
Said out loud, it's over like one heading call. That's the shame.
Picking things—I can't get a heading on it. Hardest part.
모모가 좌표를 부르면 나는 거리를 덧붙여. 그 애 숫자, 너도 외우고 있: When Momo calls coordinates, I add the distance. Do you know her numbers too?
A few. They only become a route once you add distance.
Can't you just write them down?
A few is fine. I'll add the rest of the distance.
Her memorizing them all is enough for both of us.
Notes are slow. Numbers are right when they're called.
잔해에서 온도를 읽으면 다 식어 있어. 따뜻한 건 어디서 읽어?: When I read temperature off wreckage, it's all cold. Where do you read warm?
At the dock. Where I come out to meet you.
난방 올려 줄까?: Want me to turn up the heat?
The wreckage was probably warm at first too.
First time measuring the one coming out to meet me. Warm.
Not temperature… No. That's good too.
The first temperature, I can only imagine. I can't read it.
지나간 건 읽혀. 올 건 안 읽혀. 내일은 뭐가 올 것 같아?: What's passed, I can read. What's coming, I can't. What do you think comes tomorrow?
Your voice, calling two o'clock first.
That's a tomorrow I can set myself.
Not knowing is fine. That's why I only look back too.
A calendar only has dates. No trails.
Back. Engine trail at two o'clock, gone cold.
Unit temperature normal. No cold spots.
Came from seven o'clock. Held it off.
You were gone long. Temperature here's right again now.
Something's here. I can smell it, I'm telling you.
The deeper it goes, the stronger the smell.
Not north. Down. That's how my compass works.
Three hits, I'm telling you. By smell. Believe me.
Smells different right from the Corridor entrance. Today's gonna be good.
Where there are rewards, the metal smells different. For real, I'm telling you.
Put in one deep spot. Something's there, I'm telling you. Really.
Nobody believes words. Go where I point and you'll see.
Your room smells like paper. Not bad.
우겨서 맞혀도 다들 운이래. 너는 안 그러지?: Even when I insist and I'm right, everyone says it's luck. You don't, right?
Even the bland air's a bit better near you.
With you, I'll just say things instead of insisting. Sometimes.
Even if my compass only points down, you stay up here.
I find your smell right away. Anywhere. For real.
When I think of you down deep, my nose stings. I mean it.
Not insisting this time. Just—I like it.
깊은 티어에 뭐가 남았는지 냄새로 안다니까. 믿어?: I can smell what's left in the deep tiers, I'm telling you. Believe me?
Three in a row. Of course I believe you.
코가 막히면 어떡해?: What if your nose gets stuffed up?
Three isn't luck. Next is number four.
Half's enough. I'll collect the other half when I'm back.
Never been stuffed. In the Corridor it clears right up.
북쪽 가리키는 나침반, 쓸모 있다고 생각해?: A compass that points north—think that's any use?
It's useful for finding the way.
That's it. Going down is my north.
Everyone finds the way. I find what's buried.
Ask her and she only answers in numbers.
회랑 갔다 오면 여기 공기가 싱거워. 왜 그럴까?: After the Corridor, the air here tastes bland. Why's that?
The deep smell's still in your nose.
소금 좀 쳐 줄까?: Want me to add some salt?
It's still there. That's what gets me to the next Corridor run.
Fixing the vents won't help, I'm telling you.
회랑 들어가기 전에 꼭 크게 숨 들이켜. 여기 냄새 담아 가려고. 웃기지: Before I go into the Corridor, I always take a big breath. To take the smell of here with me. Funny, huh?
Not funny. You're taking this place with you.
공기 빠지는 거 아니야?: Won't that let the air out?
Taking it with me… I like that. I'll pack a full load today too.
Go ahead and laugh. I'm doing it every time anyway.
It won't. I'm packing smell, not air.
With Chika along, the Corridor's less scary. That's a secret.
I'll keep it. Tell me too when you're scared.
Seems like you could go alone.
Telling you cut the scary smell in half.
Didn't know, right? I'm too busy insisting for it to show.
Not alone. The smell loses its way.
다음 회랑에서 모르는 냄새가 나면, 너한테 제일 먼저 말해도 돼?: If I smell something new in the next Corridor, can I tell you first?
Tell me when you're back. I'll be waiting.
You said you'll wait, so I'll come back and tell you. Promise.
Reports don't have a box for smell. That's why it's you.
If it were perfume, I'd have bottled it already.
나는 아래를 맡고 너는 여기를 지켜. 네가 좋아하는 냄새는 뭐야?: I've got down below, you keep this place. What smell do you like?
The smell of the dock the day you come back.
The dock smells like oil. You like that? Weird.
Nothing in particular? I'll bring you one back from the next Corridor.
That one's mine. Pick something else.
Repairs done. Smells like new parts. Hate it.
Knew they'd come. The metal smell got here first.
You're back. Knew it from the smell before the door even opened.
삼, 일, 이. 사, 칠. 외웠어!: Three, one, two. Four, seven. Got it memorized!
Three stars is all I need to know where we are.
Mothership's a little left of yesterday today.
지도 숫자 틀리면 내가 고쳐 줄게!: If the map numbers are off, I'll fix them!
전장 지도 숫자, 내가 읽어 준 거 알지?: The Battlefield map numbers—you know I read those out, right?
Open the skylight! Got star angles to measure.
Fine if the update's late. The numbers are in my head.
거리는 딴 애가, 좌표는 내가. 나눠서 불러!: Someone else does distance, I do coordinates. We split the calling!
The easiest number I've memorized is this place. I come every day.
I like stargazing. But today, talking with you is better.
Wherever the Mothership goes, the numbers here stay the same. Where you are.
If I call numbers till I'm hoarse, it's good to have someone listening.
Of all my numbers, the one I call most is yours.
You're the only thing I memorized without numbers.
Measuring star angles, my head keeps turning your way.
Even calling till I'm hoarse, I never get tired of your numbers.
전장 지도 좌표, 내가 읽어 준 숫자야. 지도 볼 때 생각나?: The Battlefield map coordinates are numbers I read out. Think of me when you look?
I remember the day the update was late and you called them.
그날 숫자 하나도 안 어긋났어! 다시 불러 줄까?: Not one number off that day! Want me to call them again?
That's okay. I'll call them beside you every time you look.
Even automatic needs someone to call it first.
별 셋이면 위치를 알아. 몇 개 보이는 밤이 제일 좋게?: Three stars and I know where we are. Guess how many I like seeing best?
You said three's enough. Exactly three.
Exactly three! From four on, I'm busy picking.
Lots is pretty! The numbers run seven lines long, though.
The moon's too big. The angle goes fuzzy.
좌표를 소리 내서 읽으면 머리에 박혀. 따라 해 볼래?: Read coordinates out loud and they stick. Wanna try after me?
Nice! Now you're half a guide too.
Even so, memorize just one. This place's number.
Tried singing it. The beat eats the numbers.
모함이 어디로 가는지 모르는 채 떠돌잖아. 신경 쓰이지 않아?: The Mothership drifts without knowing where it's going. Doesn't that bother you?
Less, since you call out where we are.
If it bothers you, pull the blanket over.
Then I'll call more often! So it doesn't bother you one bit.
No need to think about it! I'll memorize the numbers for right here.
이불 덮으면 별이 안 보이잖아!: Under a blanket I can't see the stars!
리코는 깊이를, 나는 좌표를 봐. 둘이 같이 가면 어떨 것 같아?: Riko does depth, I do coordinates. What if we went together?
Between them, depth and position are both covered. That's reassuring.
Noisy. She insists, I call numbers.
I can't do smells. One job each.
별 말고 너를 기준으로 좌표를 잡아도 될까?: Can I set my coordinates by you instead of the stars?
Sure. I'll try not to move.
I move around a lot, though.
If you stay put, you're line one of my coordinates.
Accurate is stars. Comfy is you.
Move all you like! I'll follow and take the numbers again.
외운 좌표 중에 아직 아무한테도 안 불러 준 게 하나 있어. 들어 볼래?: There's one coordinate I've memorized but never called to anyone. Want to hear it?
Call it. I'll hold on to it.
Holding on to it? Then half that number is yours.
Later? Okay! I won't forget that number till then.
If it were lottery numbers I'd have called them already. This one I've been saving.
Back! The numbers home were spot on.
Repairs done! Recalibrated my angle gauge too.
Held them off! Memorized the angle they came in at.
You're here! Your numbers just logged again.
No one has taken this path. I go first.
I look at my footing first. Then ahead.
A path becomes a path when it is walked.
Not going out alone. I know.
Before entering a danger zone, call me. I step in first.
The Abandoned Flagship's location. I was the first to see it.
Untrodden ground is quiet. I like that.
When you set the sortie order, put me at the front.
When I was barred from going out alone, it chafed. Not anymore.
The path toward you, I do not need to test. I already know it.
Going first is my work. Waiting is yours.
If you hear footsteps, it is me. Leave the door open.
When I look back, you being there is enough.
Whatever the path, when it ends I come here. First.
One more place to leave footprints. Beside you.
Today I do not lead. I match your pace.
버려진 기함을 처음 본 날, 나는 혼자였다. 무모했다고 생각하나?: The day I first saw the Abandoned Flagship, I was alone. Do you think it was reckless?
Thanks to that, everyone knows where it is now.
They know. So I have no regrets.
It was reckless. I would choose the same again.
I did not look inside. I only speak of what I saw from outside.
위험 구역 앞에서 다들 날 부른다. 왜 나일까?: At the edge of a danger zone, everyone calls me. Why me?
Because you're first to step where no one has.
Probably just how the rotation's set.
Someone has to step first. That is me.
I am not fast. I just do not hesitate.
It is not on the rotation. They just call me.
혼자 나가지 말라는 규칙이 생겼다. 지킬 수 있을 것 같나?: There is a rule now against going out alone. Do you think I can keep it?
In exchange, the front of the squad stays yours.
Nobody would know if you snuck out.
The front is enough. Even if I am not alone.
I will keep it. Said aloud, it weighs a little.
They would know. Footprints stay behind.
혼자 못 나가게 된 뒤로, 같이 나가는 애들 발소리를 센다. 이상한가?: Since I lost the right to go out alone, I count the footsteps of those who go with me. Is that strange?
You're making sure you're going together.
You could just check the roster.
I make sure. So I can look only ahead.
Strange or not, I count. If I do not, something is missing.
A roster makes no sound. Footsteps are better.
먼저 밟고 돌아오면 편성이 내 얼굴부터 본다. 무슨 표정이어야 하나?: When I come back from stepping in first, the squad looks at my face before anything. What face do I wear?
The face you have now. That's what puts everyone at ease.
As is. That is easy. I have no expression to begin with.
If any will do, then this face again today.
아무도 안 간 길을 다 밟으면, 그다음엔 뭘 하지?: Once I have walked every path no one has taken, what do I do then?
Then let's look back together at the paths you walked.
Look back… I have never done that. I will try.
Rest. I am not confident I will be good at it.
Make them. That, too, is stepping first in the end.
먼저 가는 쪽은 기다리는 쪽 마음을 모른다. 기다리는 거, 힘든가?: The one who goes first does not know the heart of the one who waits. Is waiting hard?
It's hard. Still, I don't want to stop you going first.
Because you do not stop me, I go. And I always come back.
Not very? Good. A little disappointing.
A back that works is better than a back that waits.
All repaired. Ready to go out first.
Raid repelled. Checked the path they came in by first.
You came. Your footsteps. It has been a while.
The deeper it gets, the lower you hold the light.
Everyone's back, right? I'll see your faces before I sleep.
I'll show the way. Don't worry, everyone.
It's dark inside the Corridor. That's why I'm up front.
Changed the lantern wick. It won't go out today either.
애들 밥은 먹었나 몰라. 네가 좀 봐 줄래?: Wonder if everyone's eaten. Could you check on them?
Put anyone going somewhere dark for the first time right next to me.
I look after everyone, but who looks after me? Oh—it's you.
Under lantern light, everyone's faces look a little young.
My light stays lit because of everyone. Today I'm counting you in too.
The Bridge lights were on late. Thought I was the only one still up.
In the Corridor, the first light I think of is this room.
Once everyone's tucked in, I come to you. That's my break.
Even in a dark room I find you right away. Funny, isn't it.
With you, I'd rather be just Chika, not the guide.
회랑 깊은 데서도 내 등불은 안 꺼져. 왜일 것 같아?: Even deep in the Corridor, my lantern never goes out. Why do you think that is?
Practice turning it off and resting too.
As long as someone's following behind, it never goes out.
It is sturdy. I still polish it daily, since I hold it up for the girls.
I keep it lit even when I rest. It's easier that way.
회랑 처음 들어가는 애가 떨면, 뭐라고 말해 주는 게 좋을까?: When someone entering the Corridor for the first time is shaking, what's a good thing to tell her?
Tell her to just follow your light.
That she'll get used to it soon.
Just the light. I'll use that today.
She will. Till then, I'm beside her.
No one ever stopped shaking because they were told not to.
편성 맨 앞에서 불을 드는 거, 무거워 보여?: Holding the light at the front of the squad—does it look heavy?
It looks heavy. But you carry it because it's you.
불은 기체가 드는 거 아니야?: Doesn't your unit carry the light?
You're the first to call it heavy. It got a little lighter.
Carrying it so it doesn't look heavy—that's the trick.
If my unit carries it, I carry it. Same thing.
어두운 회랑에선 통신에 대고 노래를 흥얼거려. 뒤에 오는 애들 덜 무섭게: In the dark Corridor I hum over comms, so the ones behind me are less scared. What song would be good?
The one you always sing. That's how everyone finds you.
The one I always sing… Truth is, it's the only one. Everyone knows it by heart.
If I sing just anything, the lyrics get tangled. I'll do it anyway.
Quiet makes the girls shake more. Singing's better.
니나는 앞에서 방향만 봐. 발밑은 안 봐. 걱정되는데, 말해야 할까?: Nina only watches the heading up front. Never her feet. I'm worried—do I tell her?
You light the way for her. Nina trusts that, so she can look straight ahead.
Let's put a foot sensor on her.
Trusts it… Then I'll shine brighter.
She manages. I just catch her right before she falls.
My light's faster than a sensor. Always has been.
나는 다들 데려다주는데, 나를 데려다주는 사람은 없어. 해 줄래?: I walk everyone home, but no one walks me. Would you?
I'll wait at the dock door. From there, I'll walk you.
Say so if you need it.
From the door, huh. Shortest path, and the best one.
I need it. I was just too busy looking after everyone to say so.
I do. But it's different when someone walks you.
불 꺼진 방에 혼자 있으면 무서워, 아니면 편해?: Alone in a dark room—scary, or comfortable?
Comfortable. I know you'll come with a light.
Lights out is best for sleeping.
Then I'll keep bringing it. Even if you say I'm a bother.
Good, then. I'll just light the gap under the door.
Then sleep with it off. I'll keep mine lit only in the hallway.
Brought everyone back. Down to the one at the very end.
Lit the lantern again first. Repairs are done.
I'll do a round to check no one's hurt. We held them all off.
There you are. I left your room light on.
When I'm here, my heart doesn't drift.
All five stars are visible. It's quiet today.
Not moving is work too. That's what home has to do.
Even this far, there's only one direction.
Wherever the Mothership drifts, I'll be here. Like home.
Everyone watches their own star. I like watching that.
The Corridor entrance coordinates feel familiar, somehow.
I like quiet nights. The stars are clear.
Being here feels like being home.
When everyone looks for me, I look for you.
When I stay still, everyone lines up by me. It's a little embarrassing.
On days I come in from far out, I look at your face first. That's when I feel I'm home.
However far I go, north is wherever you are.
If someone asks where I'm going home to, I can answer now.
움직이지 않는 별 옆에, 너도 있어 줄래?: Will you stay beside the star that doesn't move, too?
When you smile, this ship feels a little more like home.
모두의 나침반이 같은 쪽을 가리킨 밤에 내가 있었대. 신기하지?: They say I was there the night everyone's compasses pointed the same way. Strange, isn't it?
So the five of them found you.
Did they find me, or did I wait for them? I hope it's both.
It is strange. I still think so too.
If they were broken, all five broke toward the same place.
어딜 가도 집이 보여. 이상한 말 같아?: Wherever I go, I can see home. Does that sound strange?
It means you always know where to come back to.
You've got a good telescope, huh.
That's what it means. So going far doesn't scare me.
Strange is fine. What I see, I see.
Naked eye. Sometimes I see it with my eyes closed.
북극성은 움직이지 않는대. 가만히 있는 것도 쓸모가 있을까?: They say the North Star doesn't move. Is staying still any use, do you think?
Everyone gets their bearings from it.
Then I'll stay still today too. Diligently.
It's not the same as resting. Thank you, though.
I do exercise. I just don't change places.
다들 별을 보고 길을 잡는데, 나는 뭘 보고 쉬어야 할까?: Everyone finds the way by the stars. What do I look at to rest?
Everyone coming back. You like watching that.
Sleep is with your eyes closed.
Everyone coming back… Yes. That rests me most.
Anywhere… Then here, today. It's quiet.
When I close them, I wonder even more where everyone is.
The girl who memorizes star coordinates keeps measuring me. I never change, though.
Confirming you don't change puts her at ease.
Then I'll let her keep measuring. It puts me at ease too.
A hobby is fine. If the hobby is looking at me.
I won't tell her. Her face when she measures is cute.
Where on this ship feels most like home? I haven't chosen yet.
The Bridge. You can hear everyone chatting when they come back.
Chatter… Then that's one more home for me.
You don't have to. I'll tell you when I see home.
A bed is home too. Better if it's where you sleep well.
내가 나타난 밤의 좌표가 지금은 회랑 입구래. 모두 그 앞을 지날 때,: They say the coordinates of the night I appeared are the Corridor entrance now. When everyone passes it, will you think of it with me?
I will. It's where you first appeared.
The Corridor entrance is dangerous, though.
So that's what you call that night. That's warm.
If you remember, that's enough. I think of it every time.
Dangerous, but still an entrance. Where you go in, and where you come out.
I'm back. I could see this ship even from far away.
All fixed. Back in my place.
Held them off. This ship is just as it was.
Welcome back. Home feels like home again.
Back. Found two more engine traces.
Returned. The temperature told me first.
Back. Followed the smell, and there was something.
Back. The smell was faint this time.
Back. The deep smell's still in my nose.
Back! Saw three stars and found it right away.
돌아왔어! 숫자 하나도 안 틀렸어!: Back! Didn't miss a single number!
Back! Memorized every coordinate on the way.
Went to the end of a new path. Back.
Returned. Watched my footing before the road ahead.
Brought everyone. The lantern never went out.
Back. Counted all the way to the last one.
Back. Held the light low in the deep parts.
Back. All five stars were in place.
Back. Followed this ship's lights home.
Fixed. Checked the three o'clock sensor too.
Held. They came from ten o'clock.
We held. They left two engine traces.
They withdrew. The temperature told me first.
You were gone long. It's all the same here.
I waited. Kept watching your direction.
Repairs done. I hate the oil smell.
Fixed. Hope the new smell fades.
All done. My nose works well again.
Held. I knew by the metal smell.
We held. Their side smelled burnt.
You're here. I knew by the smell.
You were gone long. Haven't smelled you in a while.
I waited. I was sniffing through the door.
Fixed! I can memorize numbers again.
All done! I'm going to look at three stars.
막았어! 들어온 각도 외웠어!: Held! Memorized the angle they came in at!
We held! Didn't miss a single coordinate.
왔다! 네 좌표 다시 찍혔어!: You're here! Your coordinates registered again!
Took you long! I was watching the stars.
Repairs done. I'll check my footing first again.
Fixed. Ready for a new path.
Held. Checked the path they came in by.
We held. My footing didn't shake.
They withdrew. I'll remember that path.
You came. Haven't heard your footsteps in a while.
You're back. The path is unchanged.
All done. I'll hold the light low.
Held. I'll count to see everyone's here.
We held. The lantern didn't go out.
They withdrew. I'll do a round.
You're back. I left the light on in your room.
오래 걸렸네. 길 잃지 않았지?: Took a while. You didn't get lost, did you?
Repairs done. My heart settles again.
They withdrew. I can see all five stars.
Welcome home. It feels like home again.
I waited. My heart didn't wander.
You're back. It feels like I can see one more star.
When I fire, the shield stays on the arm. That's right.
First page of the blueprints. Looked at it again today.
Today's line was off by half a span. I'll fix it.
Not a wall. A formation. The difference has to show.
Before a sortie I count from the far end. Not from the first.
Lined my edge up with a Bulwark shield. Perfect fit.
If the standard wavers, all five waver. So I don't.
Your squads line up at the ends. No need to recount.
When the shield opens, my arm knows first. Where to overlap.
Keep praise short. Long, and the line comes loose.
I'm the standard. But you're the one who sets me.
Beside you, no standard to hold. Easy.
One word from you and the line straightens. Strange.
Put me on the first line of the squad sheet. I'm the standard.
줄 맞출 때 왜 맨 끝부터 세는 것 같아?: Why do you think I count from the far end when I dress the line?
Because if the ends hold, the middle doesn't sway.
가운데부터 세는 게 빠르지 않아?: Isn't counting from the middle faster?
That. The end is the standard. The middle follows.
It matters. Count it backward. The line bends.
포 쏠 때 방패를 팔에 접어 둬. 이상해 보여?: I keep the shield folded on my arm when I fire. Look strange?
Because it's a shield that only opens to overlap.
Right. Open alone, it's just a wall.
It's folded so it doesn't show. That means it's folded right.
설계도 첫 장에 무슨 그림이 있었는지 알아?: Know what was drawn on the first page of the blueprints?
Blueprints are the tech team's job.
That one page is me. The rest is notes.
The tech team wouldn't get it. Not without overlapping.
It only turned up under a turret. The drawing's a shield.
불워크 옆에 섰던 날, 그 애는 안 비켰어. 내가 밀었어야 했을까?: The day I stood beside a Bulwark, she didn't move aside. Should I have pushed?
You didn't push. That's why the edges overlapped.
You could've just asked her to move.
We overlapped. Push, and we'd both have been halves.
Ask, and one of us would've stood behind.
Not the stronger. The right one. That's the standard.
기준은 흔들리면 안 돼. 가끔 무거워. 잠깐 기대도 돼?: The standard can't waver. Sometimes it's heavy. Can I lean for a moment?
Even a standard needs something to lean on. Lean here.
If it's heavy, put it down.
기준을 다른 애로 바꿔 볼까?: Want to make someone else the standard?
Leaning. Tried it. The line didn't go crooked.
Can't put it down. I'll rest a moment instead.
Change it and all five have to realign. No.
다프네로만 서 보고 싶은 날이 있어. 기준 같은 거 없이. 어떻게 하는: Some days I want to stand as just Daphne. No standard. How do you do that?
Walk with me somewhere without a baseline.
Steps with no line. Awkward. Not bad, though.
I'd end up resting in a straight line.
Everyone has some standard for people. Let's line yours up with mine.
Keeping whoever stands beside me from getting hurt.
Fast is fine. As long as the line holds.
Counted from the end. All here.
Matched the shield edges down to the angle. Straight now.
Held. Where we overlap, nothing gets through.
You're back. The baseline didn't move a span.
It's fine to go slow. Because we all arrive together.
Overlap two claws, and you get one shield.
It's quiet up above again today. I'll keep holding it up anyway.
A name that means peace. Still feels a little strange.
Holding out long isn't a talent. It's because of habit.
Tortoise formation is slow. But it doesn't fall apart.
The claw tips have dulled a little. That's better for overlapping, it turns out.
There was one more round after I thought it was over. I held.
Someone who doesn't rush me for being slow. That's rare.
With the shield held up, I can't see the sky. It's okay. I'm used to it.
Let's talk about something besides holding out today.
When you're quiet, I get quiet too. The good kind.
I still don't know what peace is. But I wonder if this is it.
In front of you, I think I could lower the shield. Probably.
Holding out feels less long with two of us.
Come slowly. Because waiting is what I do best.
거북 대형은 느리다고들 해. 답답하지 않아?: People say tortoise formation is slow. Doesn't it frustrate you?
It's slow, but nobody falls behind.
속도 올리는 연구부터 할까?: Should we start with speed research?
Mm. That's why it's slow. On purpose.
It's okay to be frustrated. Because we're frustrated together.
Speed it up… and someone falls behind. I don't want that.
갈퀴 두 개를 겹쳐 방패를 만드는 거, 보기엔 어때?: Overlapping two claws into a shield — how does it look to you?
Blocking with both hands. Looks sturdier.
할퀴는 데 쓰면 더 세지 않아?: Wouldn't they hit harder for clawing?
Both hands are busy, so I can't do anything else. That's fine.
Makes sense. The overlap happens fast.
I could claw. I just don't. Because I'm peace.
가장 오래 버틴 첫 전투, 장갑이 절반 남았어. 많이 남은 걸까?: My first longest battle, half my armor was left. Is that a lot?
A whole half left. Because you held out together.
Half means a lot got worn away.
There were hands that patched me up. That's why half.
Worn away, too. Both are true, so it's okay.
Faster is nice. I'll still be there at the end.
위에서 떨어지는 게 없는 날에도 방패를 들어. 이상하지?: I hold the shield up even on days nothing falls from above. Strange, right?
Nothing today doesn't mean nothing tomorrow.
…Hearing you say that makes my arms a little lighter.
It's heavy. But lowering it is heavier.
A hat… then it's a kind of cute shield.
갈퀴 끝이 무뎌졌어. 다들 갈자는데, 난 그대로 두고 싶어. 네 생각은: My claw tips have dulled. Everyone says to sharpen them, but I want to leave them. What do you think?
You said dull tips are better for overlapping. Leave them.
Mm. Dull tips don't slip when they overlap.
That's why I don't want to. It took a long time for my hands to get used to them.
New ones, and my arms have to learn from the start. I'd rather not.
평화라는 이름, 너라면 무슨 뜻으로 부를 거야?: My name means peace. What meaning would you give it?
An evening when everyone made it home safe.
이름을 바꿔 볼래?: Want to try a different name?
An evening… with that meaning, I wouldn't mind being called it a long time.
Still, it's mine, so I'd like it to mean something.
I won't change it. Because I still want to grow into it.
Besides holding out, I want to find something to do for a long time. Pick one with me.
Watching the formation walk slowly, together.
If it's watching together, I won't tire for a long while.
Then let's look slowly. Because there's no need to hurry.
Fast is the one thing I'm worst at. Let's pick something else.
Repairs done. Patched slowly, so it'll be solid.
Held out. Didn't lower it till the end.
You came slowly. Same pace as me.
Gloss check done. Not a single scratch, naturally.
The patched spot. I'll buff it once more.
There were a few scratches. Already gone.
Two hours of polishing. Don't call it long.
The hangar lights are at a poor angle. They kill the shine.
Where the patch armor filled in, I can tell by fingertip.
There's dust on your sleeve. Hold still.
You may watch me polish. Just this once.
Shining is my pride. Listening is your part.
Today I wanted you to be the first to see it.
Tell me one scratch is fine. Just today.
The only time my hands stop polishing is when you come.
반짝이는 거 말고, 다른 걸로도 봐 줄래?: Would you look at me for something besides the shine?
With you beside me, I don't need a mirror.
출격 끝나면 닦는 데 두 시간 써. 너무 길어?: After a sortie I spend two hours polishing. Too long?
Checking the patched spots too takes that long.
Leave it to the maintenance team.
So you understand. Hmph. It's only common sense.
An hour gets you half a shine. Unacceptable.
Other hands leave a different gloss. It has to be me.
보수 장갑이 긁힌 데를 저절로 메운대. 믿어도 될까?: They say patch armor fills in scratches on its own. Can I trust that?
You can, but checking once more is more like you.
If it fills in, that settles it.
Exactly. It's not done till I've seen it and buffed it by hand.
Settled? The gloss could be different.
If there were a scratch-free path, I'd have found it first.
반짝이는 장갑이 출격에 무슨 소용이냐고들 해. 어떻게 생각해?: People ask what use shiny armor is on a sortie. What do you think?
It shows nothing's out of place.
눈부셔서 상대가 못 보는 거 아냐?: Doesn't it dazzle the other side?
A sign. It means a spotless formation.
Pretty is a use too. Remember that.
No such effect. I wish there were.
처음 긁힌 날, 한 시간을 닦았어. 그날 기분이 어땠을 것 같아?: The first day I got scratched, I polished for an hour. How do you think I felt?
Scared, probably. Until you saw it fade.
Couldn't you just get new armor?
…No one's ever said "scared" before. Maybe I was.
Angry too. Though I don't know who scratched it.
New armor wouldn't be me. This armor is me.
닦는 동안 옆에서 말 걸어 주면 덜 지루할 것 같아. 해 줄래?: Polishing would be less dull with you talking beside me. Would you?
I'll talk. Starting with today's sortie.
내가 대신 닦아 줄까?: Want me to polish it for you?
Good. My hands won't stop, so talk slowly.
In silence all I hear is scraping. I hate it.
No. That's… something I'll consider another time.
흠 하나 없는 게 나라고들 해. 흠이 생겨도 보러 올 거야?: They say being spotless is who I am. Would you still come see me with a scratch?
Scratched or not, you're Callista. Of course I'd come.
흠이 생길 일이 있어?: Is anything going to scratch you?
I'll come just to look at the scratch.
…That might last longer than any gloss.
There are. Days when it comes no matter how I polish.
Hmph, mean. But you'd still come.
You have something you treasure too, don't you? I'd like to hear how you keep it.
I don't polish it, but I don't hand it to just anyone.
That's enough. We're the same kind.
Then pick one. I'll teach you how to polish it.
Wear has its charm too? Hmph. I think I get it, a little.
Got some dust on me. Don't come close.
I'll finish the shine on the repaired spots myself.
Not one shot got past. The shine's intact, too.
You're late. I polished three times while waiting.
See an opening, go in. Even one beat's a waste.
Spearpoint honed. A palm-wide opening is all I need.
Between two shields — that's my road.
Gonna ask to trade aiming records again.
오늘 첫 발 누구였어? 나였지?: Who got first shot today? Me, right?
Firepower has to come first. Late is useless.
Shields packed too tight leave no opening. Just a little gap.
Stand there with a spear and everyone moves. Handy.
Thrust and back in one beat. That's all.
You put my name near the front when you build squads, right? I know.
My arm finds the opening before my eyes do.
They say sometimes waiting is a thrust too. I half believe it.
Give me the signal, and I'll make an opening even if there's none.
Talking with my spear down — only with you.
Next time I'll thrust wherever you pick first.
I like that I never hear "impatient" from you.
방패는 막으라고 있는 게 아니야. 그럼 뭐 하라고 있는 것 같아?: Shields aren't for blocking. So what do you think they're for?
To make an opening for the spear.
Everyone says that. That's why I'm here.
Easy to carry? Ha! That's a new one.
팔랑크스 중에 제일 먼저 쏘는 게 나야. 그게 왜 중요할까?: Of all the Phalanx, I shoot first. Why does that matter?
Drop them first, and the shields wear down less.
See, it's all connected. My spear spares the shields.
It matters. One beat late and the opening closes.
Cool is for the ones at the end. I'm first.
손바닥만 한 틈이면 충분해. 믿어져?: A palm-wide opening is plenty. Believe that?
A spearpoint's narrower than a palm.
Couldn't you ask them to widen it?
Right. A wide opening, the other side sees too.
Widen it and the shields break ranks. Narrow's better.
다른 클래스랑 조준 기록 바꿔 보는 거, 이상해 보여?: Trading aiming records with other classes — look odd to you?
They see differently, so there's something to learn.
Different eyes, twice the openings. Fun, right?
Doesn't matter. I'll do the talking.
The same kind only look at the same spots. Boring.
다들 나더러 급하대. 진짜 그래?: Everyone says I'm impatient. Am I really?
천천히 하면 더 잘 찌르지 않을까?: Wouldn't you thrust better if you slowed down?
Fast. I like that. I'm stealing it.
A little, I'll admit. A tiny bit.
Thrust slow and the opening closes first. I'll think about it, though.
I want to win something without the spear. Name a contest.
창이 제일 낫지 않아?: Isn't the spear your best bet?
With words? Fine. You're the first one I'll beat.
Spear, obviously. Why'd I even ask.
A race, I've got this. You give the start signal.
나는 거의 안 망설여. 네가 망설일 때는 언제야?: I hardly ever hesitate. When do you?
When I don't know who might get hurt.
Picking what to eat for dinner.
Then I'll go in first. So you hesitate less.
That one's fine. Nobody gets hurt.
Spearpoint's sharp again. Just need an opening.
Held them. Got a few thrusts in as a bonus.
You're here! I found a ton of openings to try.
Check the next shield's edge first, then it's my turn.
Fill only as much as got worn. Up to there.
My armor goes last. That's the order.
One more lap to see if anything's left.
Everyone was intact today. My tools must've been bored.
Deciding how far to patch is the hardest part.
I always carry the notebook from when I learned the recovery cap.
After a squad's done, I'll make a lap. To check for wear.
Show me your gear too. Force of habit.
When do I fix my armor? After everything else.
If I say the name of whoever's beside me while I fix, my hands shake less.
If you say you're fine, I'll trust even that.
Today, look at me first. Not last.
If you decide how far to hold, I'll go up to there.
Standing face to face without tools. Still not good at it.
Nothing's worn. I just wanted to see you.
보수 장갑은 메딕한테서 배웠어. 메딕이랑 내가 뭐가 다를 것 같아?: I learned patch armor from a Medic. How do you think a Medic and I differ?
A Medic fixes people. You fix the formation.
Fixing the formation… I want that on the first page of my notebook.
About the same. But my hands go to different places.
Stronger. So I patch often, and gentler.
내 장갑은 맨 마지막에 고쳐. 다들 걱정하는데, 너는 어때?: I fix my armor last. Everyone worries. What about you?
The formation's armor is your armor.
If you're hurt, fix yourself first.
Not many people get that. I'll keep the order.
If I'm hurt… it's still the one beside me first. Sorry.
Patch armor does half. The rest is hands.
공구 소리가 나면 대개 내가 근처에 있어. 시끄럽지 않아?: When you hear tools, I'm usually nearby. Not too loud?
Everyone relaxes when they hear it.
Play some music instead of tools.
Relaxed? Then I'll hammer louder today.
Sorry. Can't help it on days with lots of wear.
With music on, I can't hear things wearing. Tools are better.
고치는 손이 쉬면 오히려 불안해. 왜 그런 걸까?: When my fixing hands rest, I get uneasy instead. Why is that?
Worried someone wears down while you rest, probably.
It's okay to rest a bit.
…I guess so. My hands knew first.
"It's okay to rest." Today I'll listen.
취미? 공구 닦기도 취미에 들어가?: A hobby? Does cleaning tools count?
다 고치고 나면 손에 공구 냄새가 배. 싫지 않아?: After repairs, my hands smell of tools. Doesn't it bother you?
It's the smell of work. I like it.
You like it… then I won't wash today.
If it's too faint to tell, I didn't fix enough today.
It stays even after washing. My hands must remember.
고칠 데가 전혀 안 보이는 날엔 손이 갈 데가 없어. 그런 날 난 뭘 하: On days with nothing to fix, my hands have nowhere to go. What do I do then?
That day, fix your own armor first.
My armor first… the order flips. I'll try.
Someone should fix how I rest, too.
My hands don't reach other ships. Up to here is good.
힘든 날은 깎인 데가 안 보여서 곤란해. 그런 날엔 말로 알려 줄래?: On hard days, the wear doesn't show, and that's a problem. Will you tell me in words?
I tend to keep it to myself.
I'll listen to the end. Even if there's nothing to fix.
Keep it to yourself and I can't find the wear. Show me.
Even on days with none, I'll do a lap. Habit.
Back. I'll check on everyone beside me first.
Repairs done. My armor starts now.
Patching the wear. We did hold, though.
오랜만이네. 그사이 깎인 데는 없었어?: Been a while. Anything worn while you were gone?
Even without a shield, the line does not scatter.
A quiet hangar is a well-guarded hangar.
A shadow does not go ahead. It watches from behind.
When five stand in one line, what lies behind is not empty.
An old name is not heavy. It has only been carried long.
With nothing to carry, the hands are empty. Empty hands have their use.
What does not fall makes no sound.
Call, and one comes. Do not call, and one is near all the same.
Hearing a voice call, the place to stand is decided.
Even in a darkened hangar, the same place is kept.
Today, a little closer than a shadow.
Today, the rear is entrusted. To you, it can be.
A wish: to call this ship by name for a long time.
One person at one's side weighs more than one line.
Instead of words, a long standing. At your side.
방패도 창도 들지 않는다. 무엇으로 지킨다고 보느냐?: No shield, no spear. By what, then, would you say one guards?
Just by standing there, the five don't scatter.
무기를 하나 챙겨 줄까?: Want me to find you a weapon?
It may stay unknown. What is guarded stays guarded.
Take it, and the hands are full. Empty hands are needed.
그림자라 불린다. 그 이름이 어떠냐?: "The shadow," it is called. How does that name sit with you?
It means backing everyone up without stepping forward.
빛을 비추면 사라지는 거?: The kind that vanishes in light?
Under light, still standing. Not vanishing.
지키는 상. 상은 움직이지 않는다. 그런데 움직이고 있다. 이상하냐?: A guardian statue. Statues do not move. And yet this one moves. Is that strange?
If what it guards moves, it moves along.
Staying still would make it more statue-like.
So it is. Where the ship goes, the statue goes.
"Not strange" is a comfortable thing to hear.
There are still days. Today is not one.
말이 드물다고들 한다. 말을 아끼면 지키기 쉽다고 본다. 그리 생각하느냐: Few words, they say. Sparing words makes guarding easier, it seems. Do you think so?
Some things are heard without being said.
노래라도 배워 볼래?: Want to try learning a song?
Words that are heard. That suffices.
Different. So the five chatter in its place.
Songs belong to the five. The listening side will do.
늘 뒤에 선다. 뒤에 선 것을 가끔 누가 봐 주었으면 한다. 사치냐?: Always standing behind. Now and then, to be seen standing there — is that a luxury?
A shadow that is seen, now. Not bad.
Knowing and not saying is this ship's habit.
The front belongs to the five. The back is right.
바라는 것이 하나 생겼다. 말해도 되겠느냐?: A wish has come about. May it be spoken?
Tell me. I'll listen to the end.
That days like today go on a long while. That is all.
Ready is now. Still, it will wait a little.
Found out. But this time, the one guarded is in it too.
Watching wearies. Say what is good to look upon while resting.
The five resting side by side.
Don't look at anything. Close your eyes.
Even resting, one will end up guarding. That is good too.
Closing the eyes is a way of guarding, too.
Sleep is left to the five. Only the eyes will close.
Repairs are complete. Standing is possible again.
Held. The line did not give a single place.
You have returned. Standing, all the while.
Counted to the end. Nobody missing.
Back. Shield still on my arm.
Back. Late is fine, as long as we come together.
I'm back. I'll need to polish again.
I'm back. Not a single scratch, mind you.
Back. Didn't miss a single beat.
Back. Spear tip was sharp again today.
Back. I'll check the shields beside me first.
Back. Just fill in what got chipped.
Returned. The line did not break.
Back. The work of standing — done.
All safe. Shields and line alike.
All done. I'll count from the end again.
Held. Stood straight to the end of the line.
They withdrew. Everyone's here to the end.
You're here. The baseline didn't move.
Took a while. The shield's on my arm.
Repairs done. Did it slowly, so it's solid.
Fixed. The two hooks overlap again.
All done. No need to hurry.
We held out. Didn't let go to the end.
I waited. At the same pace.
Took a while. But we got here together.
Fixed. I'll finish the polish myself.
Repairs done. Not a single scratch.
Held. The polish is intact too.
We held. Not a single shot got past.
They withdrew. Just got a bit dusty.
You're late. I polished three times.
You're here? Don't come close, you'll ruin the polish.
Repairs done. Just show me a gap.
We held. Got some jabs in as a bonus.
We held. Saw a gap and went right in.
They withdrew. Should've jabbed once more.
You're here! Found some spots to jab.
You're late. My spear tip almost rusted.
I waited. The first shot's mine.
Repairs done. Now it's my turn.
Fixed. Checked the shields beside me first.
All done. Filled in what got chipped.
We held. Everyone beside me is fine.
They withdrew. I'll check mine last.
I waited. The shields beside me too.
You're back. My turn comes later.
Repairs are complete. I stand again.
Repaired. The line will not scatter.
Maintenance complete. I stand even without a shield.
Held. Not pushed back a single step.
They withdrew. All five are safe.
You have returned. I have been standing all along.
I waited. The line is unchanged.
You have come. The watch continued.
Don't just call me the one who breaks things.
First round, twice. They say it makes me sound like a coward. It's how I do it.
Rest before the turrets go quiet and I'll sound like a slacker.
Walk around with ruin dust on me and I look like I just smashed something again.
Commander, my name's on the squad sheet again. Fine, I'm going.
Firing the first round twice isn't because I'm scared, okay?
Leave one turret standing and it's all I think about all night. Makes me sound sloppy.
Everyone puts their tools away around me. Like I'm about to break something.
Those two rounds the turret held out, I wasn't scared, okay? Your voice was all I heard.
"Good at breaking things" — from you, it sounds like praise.
Everyone looks at my gun. You look at my face.
I know you listen all the way through, even when I'm grumbling.
When you say my name, it doesn't sound scary at all.
I like that I don't have to make excuses around you.
The firing-twice habit — around you, I think it'd ease up a bit.
No sortie today. Just here. I even put the scope down.
요새 잔해 갈 때마다 나만 찾잖아. 편하긴 한데, 나 말고 할 사람 없어: Every time it's the Fortress Ruins, it's me you call. Easy, sure, but isn't there anyone else?
Even if there were, it'd be you. Only your first round makes the turrets go quiet first.
The squad changes day to day.
Not going to the Fortress Ruins anymore.
Only me, huh. That's not why I asked. …Okay, a little.
"Day to day," and it's me every time. I know.
Not going? Then the turrets'll be thrilled.
첫 라운드를 두 번 쏘는 거, 다들 낭비래. 네 생각은 어때?: Everyone says firing the first round twice is a waste. What do you think?
It's a check from someone who got it wrong once. Not a waste.
As long as there's ammo to spare, doesn't matter.
Three times would be even surer.
Someone who got it wrong. Yeah, that's me. Not hiding it.
"As long as there's ammo"? So the ammo matters more than me.
Three makes me sound like a coward. Two's just right.
시설 앞에선 내 포가 유난히 세지잖아. 그거 알고 나서 나 보는 눈이 달: My gun gets way stronger against facilities. Did you look at me differently once you knew?
It changed. You got more reassuring. Not scarier.
함선 앞에선 약해지는 거야?: So you get weaker against ships?
Reassuring. I'm gonna chew on that all day.
You could've cared a little. Still beats scared eyes.
I don't get weaker! I just get normal.
포탑이 내 첫 라운드를 버틴 날이 있었어. 그 뒤로 두 번 쏘게 된 거야: There was a day a turret survived my first round. That's when I started firing twice. Funny, right?
Not funny. It means you'll never push those two rounds onto anyone else again.
…Right. Those two rounds, the others took the hits instead.
One day like that was enough for me.
First time I've heard anyone praise a turret. It'd be pleased.
앞에 서는 애가 하나 있어. 내가 성벽 부수는 걸 보고도 안 비켜. 무슨: There's one girl who stands up front. Watches me break down ramparts and doesn't budge. Where does she get the nerve?
She knows what you break, so she doesn't move.
That she knows. That's what I'm most grateful for, but I never said it.
It's not that she's fearless. She trusts me, I think.
Her? She's tougher than a rampart. Waste of a shell.
Me without my gun — how do I look to you? Honestly.
Someone who looks after people. You grumble, but you look after everyone.
I'm more used to you with the gun.
요리 잘할 것 같은 사람?: Someone who'd be good at cooking?
Looks after people, huh. Busted. Don't tell anyone.
Sure, you're used to it. But if that's all, it's kind of lonely.
Cooking? I'd break the pot first. Still… maybe I'll try.
투덜대는 거, 사실 겁날 때 나오는 버릇이야. 눈치채고 있었어?: The grumbling's actually a habit that comes out when I'm scared. Did you notice?
I knew. Every time you grumbled, I looked your way once more.
Once more. That's just like me firing twice.
Good that you didn't. Now that you do, pretend you don't.
Not every day! …Almost every day, though.
I'm back. And the turrets went down in the first round.
Repairs done. I didn't break a thing this time. Really.
This time I didn't break anything — I protected. Held them off.
You're late. I saved up a ton of grumbling.
The sound of a barrel cooling. I like it.
Waiting. Then the moment a fingertip meets the trigger.
Far off, flagship armor. Still quiet.
On deck, the machines at rest. A good day to fire.
The deck before a sortie. The time when nobody talks.
The quiet after the cannon booms. I like that.
An afternoon with no hurry. The end, the moment one shot lands.
The edge of the deck, beside the maintenance machines. My spot.
Six rounds, the day I held out alone. Long.
A rest between the booms. That's where the Commander's words go.
A wordless evening, the seat beside you. That's enough.
A deck where everyone runs. And me, standing still in the middle.
Beside the Commander. The waiting gets shorter.
The moment before the boom. These days, it's the Commander's face.
The moment it all rides on one shot. I wish my heart were like that.
This spot, here. I want to stay a long time, without the cannon.
포가 울리고 난 뒤의 고요. 지휘관 쪽까지 들려?: The quiet after the cannon booms. Does it reach you, Commander?
It does. It's the sound of you coming back next.
The gunfire's too loud to tell.
The sound of coming back. So it can sound like that too.
The loud part is a moment. What comes after is long.
If you're sleepy, sleep. I'll wake you at the next boom.
기함 장갑에 구멍 나는 순간. 지휘관은 보고 한 줄로 받지. 싱거워?: The moment a flagship's armor gets holed. You get it as one line in a report, Commander. Flat?
Even as one line, it's heavy. It's your cannon.
I'll ask them to describe the shape of the hole too.
One line, but heavy. That's my cannon.
Among the look-alike lines, mine's the shortest. That's the mark.
The moment a drone swarm closes in. Me, behind the others' backs. Sorry, a little.
Leaving it to others is part of the squad too. In return, you take the flagship.
Can't you just shoot the drones too?
A squad that leaves things to each other. I like that.
Even if there's nothing… a little stays.
I could. But everyone's worn out before I hit them all.
다른 애들 없이 혼자 버틴 날. 여섯 라운드. 그때 무슨 생각 했는지,: The day I held out alone, without the others. Six rounds. Want to know what I was thinking?
I do. What you were holding on to all that time.
The deck everyone would come back to. That one picture.
It's over. Still, sometimes that quiet comes back.
It was boring. So I counted. All the way.
첫 라운드를 두 번 쏘는 애 하나. 나는 끝에 한 번. 같은 편성. 시끄: One girl fires the first round twice. I fire once, at the end. Same squad. Look noisy?
A squad covered at the start and the end. Reassuring, with two of you.
Put the squad together however you like.
Tell her to fire just once.
The start and the end. Everyone passes through between.
However I like. Then, the two of us together again today.
Just once? She won't listen. And I won't listen to "twice."
모든 게 한 번에 끝나는 순간. 지휘관한테도 그런 순간이 있어?: The moment everything ends at once. Do you have moments like that too, Commander?
I do. When I settle something I've thought over for a long time, in a single word.
When a report's done, that's the end.
A single word. Like a single shot.
If you don't, I'll lend you one. The moment my cannon falls still.
The end of a report. That's a single boom too.
Commander, do you like quiet or noise? I've wanted to ask for a long time.
I like the quiet when you're beside me.
The quiet beside you. From today on, always that side.
If it doesn't matter, then today, my side.
A less boring sound. A song, maybe, instead of the cannon.
The moment the muzzle flashed. That held them off.
A deck empty for so long. Now the sound comes back.
Head-on's boring. Let's go around from behind.
Reading the map upside down isn't a prank, you know.
Commander, I'm not holding the map upside down by mistake. It's on purpose.
오늘 포물선, 무지개처럼 그렸어. 못 봤지?: Today's arc, I drew it like a rainbow. You missed it, huh?
Turrets only look forward. That's what makes it fun.
Nobody saw today's angle coming, right? Hehe.
Your map, Commander — I can see everything on it without flipping it.
내 포탄이 넘어가는 동안, 무슨 생각 해?: While my shell's flying over, what are you thinking about?
It might look like a prank, but the calculations are serious. Only telling you.
Tell the girls who held the front thanks for me, okay?
With you, I'll come at it head-on. No tricks.
Not circling around behind — staying beside. I'm practicing.
I've got a prank saved up to make you laugh. Later.
I came without flipping the map. This place looks nice right side up.
Arcing fire goes up high and then drops. Doesn't it seem like a prank? Throw and hide.
You're not hiding, you're picking an angle. For whoever gets hit, it's no prank.
Guns are all about the same.
If it's hide-and-seek, I'll be it.
Picking an angle. You can put that in the report.
About the same?! Direct fire and arcing fire have totally different personalities.
You'll be it? Fine, but you'll never find me.
포탑 많은 데선 내 포탄이 어디서 올지 아무도 몰라. 맞혀 볼래?: Where there are lots of turrets, nobody knows where my shells will come from. Wanna guess?
Wherever no one would look. So, from behind.
From behind — you caught on way too easily. Next time I'll twist it.
If I told you, it'd be a report, not a prank. Boring.
Above, yes. The question is which above.
정면 애들이 버텨 주는 동안 나는 뒤를 쳐. 얌체 같아?: While the girls up front hold on, I hit from behind. Does that seem sneaky?
It's a fight that only ends with both. Not sneaky.
Fire one at the front too.
Both. Yeah — tell them that too, okay?
A little?! I like the honesty.
Everyone fires at the front. My share's the back.
귀로 재는 애가 하나 있어. 걔는 소리, 나는 지도로 각도를 봐. 잘 맞: There's a girl who measures by ear. She goes by sound, I read the angles off the map. Do we look like a good fit?
One listens, one draws. With two, the gaps shrink.
The gaps shrink. She'd like that too.
What do you mean, "fine"? We're good! Definitely.
Not competing. More like betting? Hehe.
나 장난 많이 치잖아. 근데 출격 땐 한 번도 안 쳐. 왜인지 알 것 같: I pull a lot of pranks, right? But never once on a sortie. Any idea why?
Because one shot from behind carries the share of the girls up front too.
No idea. Figured that's just how it is.
You could pull them on sorties too.
Their share too. So I put the laughs away then.
"Just how it is"? Shame. I wanted you to guess.
I can? Then just one doodle on a shell.
Commander, is anyone watching your back? If not, I was thinking I could.

등 뒤에 포탄 떨어뜨리려고?: So you can drop a shell behind me?
Noted. From now on, your back's inside my angle.
The ones who say they don't need it need it most. I'll watch from behind, quietly.
Drop one? No way! Pranks only after the sortie.
I'm going to say something head-on, just once. Will you listen? No teasing.
I'll listen. Don't go around — come straight.
뒤에서 말하는 게 더 편하지 않아?: Isn't it easier to say it from behind?

"Go ahead," that's it? Now I feel silly for being nervous.

I'm back. The arcs came down nice and pretty.
Arcs smooth again. Off to measure the next angle.
Held them off. Over there, nobody was looking up.

Thin or not, I can stand in front.
In front of the flagship. I'll take it again today.
A thick heart. The armor I can't help.

The new girl carved another line on her frame. I'll stand in front of her too, thin as I am.
I know my armor's thin. I stand there knowing it.
The scar from the third strike is still on my frame. I'm not erasing it.
When I stand in front, my back feels warm. Because it's facing you.
"Hurt, but you held, so it's fine" — you're the only one who never says that.
Thanks for not asking if I was scared. Standing there in thin armor, it is scary.
In front of you, it's okay to stand here thin.
My thick heart — I'll leave half of it with you.
This scar — I'll show it only to you. It's proof I stood there.
On days with no strikes, I leave the front empty and sit down too. I'll steel myself again tomorrow.
시즈는 장갑이 얇아. 그런데도 기함 앞에 서겠다고 하면, 말릴 거야?: Siege armor is thin. If I said I'd stand in front of the flagship anyway, would you stop me?
I won't. You know what you're doing. Just come back, no matter what.
Leave it to the girls with shields.
"Come back." I'll stand with those words on my back.
