They're busy too. I'll fill the empty spots.
In the raid defense squad, if the front's empty, I'll go. You can ask why.
Probably because blocking up front is easier than watching from behind.
앞자리 다툼 붙여 볼까?: Should I start a fight over the front spot?
Not easier — less anxious. I see it with my own eyes.
Good if there isn't. Then I'll just go.
A fight? Fine. The front spot's still mine, though.
신입 하나가 말없이 기체에 줄만 새겨. 선배로서 뭐라고 해 줘야 할까?: One new girl just carves lines on her frame without a word. As her senior, what could I say to her?
You don't have to say anything. Stand beside her and she'll understand.
Tell her to draw pictures instead of lines.
Standing beside. Maybe harder than standing in front.
She will. And meanwhile, I'll hold the front for her.
Pictures? I would like to see her smile.
급습을 두 번 막고, 세 번째엔 다쳤어. 그래도 막았어. 그날 얘기, 들: I blocked two strikes, and got hurt on the third. But I still held. Will you hear about that day?
I'll listen. You can start with how it hurt.
A fourth one won't come, probably.
It hurt. Took me a long time to say that.
It does. Yeah. But I'll sit here a little longer.
If it comes, I'll stand again. That's me.
기함 앞에 서는 거, 누가 시킨 거 아니야. 스스로 정했어. 왜 그런지: Standing in front of the flagship — nobody told me to. I decided myself. Can you guess why?
Because watching the ones behind you get hurt hurts more.
눈에 띄고 싶어서?: Because you want to stand out?
Because it hurts more. Yes — that side weighs more.
It's okay not to know. I can't put it all into words either.
I do stand out. That's not what I wanted, though.
Commander, who would you want standing in front? You can name someone other than me.
I'd want you. But not alone.
I'd rather no one had to.
If it's anyone, that includes me. I'm raising my hand.
A day no one has to stand. I'm hoping for that too.
기함 앞에 서면 장갑이 먼저 떨려. 겁나는 건 나인데. 이상하지?: When I stand in front of the flagship, my armor shakes first. Even though I'm the one who's scared. Strange, right?
You shake, but you're still standing. That's you.
Thicker armor and it wouldn't shake.
Shaking, but standing. I'll pull that out next strike.
It could. I only told you, so just let it go like that.
Even thick, I'd shake. Because that's me.
I'm back. I stood in front, and everyone's safe.
Patched the thin spots again. Let a strike come.
Held. No one got past the front of the flagship.
You're here. I kept the very front just as it was.
Today's share is done. The report will be short.
That is the third line. It is still not enough.
One line is easier than words.
Because what is carved does not wear away.
Commander. Today's share is carved. That is my report.
My senior stood in front. I was behind. I recorded it.
The words "new girl." I do not hear them much anymore.
One more line. That is all.
Your words, Commander, I do not carve. I keep them in memory.
There is nothing to carve today. I came anyway.
In front of you, Commander, I talk a little more. It is strange.
Something to say that is not a record. I thought of one.
I like that I do not have to record anything here.
I am not good with words. But with you, Commander, I will try.
I counted nothing today. It is still a good day.
Being here. That is today's record.
격파한 시설 수. 기체에 새겨요. 이상한 습관인가요?: The number of facilities I have destroyed. I carve it on my frame. Is that a strange habit?
More certain than a spoken report. It's your way.
Yes. It is my way. I will keep doing it.
Whatever is comfortable. Then I will keep carving.
It is not a scratch. It is a line. They are different.
세 줄째가 되니까 아무도 신입이라고 하지 않아요. 이제 무엇이라고 불리면: Since the third line, no one calls me the new girl. What would be good to be called now?
Answer to whatever they call you.
My name. It is short, so please call it often.
Yes. I will listen, and keep the good ones.
New girl. …I did miss that a little.
사격은 짧게 끝내요. 길게 쏘는 법은 아직 몰라요. 배워야 할까요?: I keep my fire short. I do not know how to fire long yet. Should I learn?
Short and strong is your fire. Refine it as it is.
Learn it if you need it.
When I need it. I will ask you again then.
What is wasted is time, more than ammo. For me, at least.
선배는 늘 앞에 서요. 저는 그 등을 보고 쏴요. 언젠가 옆에 설 수 있: My senior always stands in front. I fire watching her back. Will I be able to stand beside her someday?
You will. Even while you're watching her back, your lines keep growing.
The lines are growing. Yes. That is the proof.
Someday. Until then, I will watch her back closely.
In front? My senior would turn around in surprise.
말이 없다고들 해요. 지휘관님은 말 없는 저, 불편하지 않으세요?: People say I do not talk. Commander, is a quiet me not uncomfortable for you?
Not at all. One of your lines says more than a long report.
The lines speak, you say. Then the next one will be straighter.
If it is not too bad. I am relieved. A little.
If you are bored. …Today I will say three more words.
지휘관님께 하루 한 마디씩 말로 해 보고 싶어요. 새기지 않고요. 괜찮으: I would like to say one thing to you each day, Commander, out loud. Without carving it. Would that be all right?
Sure. I'll hear each word as one line.
You could write it down instead.
As much as one line. Then I will choose very carefully.
Whenever I like. Then now is good.
I already write a lot. This, I want to say aloud.
기체를 쓰다듬으면 저도 같이 느껴요. 지휘관님도 손 대 보실래요?: When my frame is stroked, I feel it too. Commander, would you like to touch it?
I'll be careful. So it doesn't hurt.
It did not hurt. It was warm. A little.
Yes. Then I will show you another time.
It tickles. …More, now that you mention it.
I have returned. Today's share is done.
Repairs are finished. I asked them to leave that spot on the armor as it is.
Held. Today's record grew by one.
You are here. I counted the days I waited, too.
The toll always reaches you first from the far side.
I will not speak until the ringing settles.
Five stood side by side. So I came.
The name "doom" is heavy. Still, it is mine.
Commander. The far side of the Fortress Ruins — there, I tolled.
I heard the five guns toll. I only added one to them.
I will keep my words short. The ringing is long.
This ship is not used to gunfire. It will be, soon.
Of all this ship's sounds, I learned your footsteps first, Commander.
Now is better than when I stood alone on the far side.
May I stand close? So our sounds do not blur.
The five are still wary of me. That too is fine.
Beside you, Commander, my barrel feels light. I do not know why.
Not the toll — this voice, I use only for you, Commander.
I have chosen my place on this ship. Beside you, Commander.
I came sixth. To you, Commander, I will come first.
다섯이 요새 잔해 위에 섰을 때, 여섯 번째 포성이 울렸다. 그게 나였다: When the five stood on the Fortress Ruins, a sixth gun tolled. That was me. Did you hear it?
I heard it. Not alone — it rang out together with them.
There was too much gunfire to tell.
I thought it was an echo.
Together. If that is how it sounded, that is enough.
One among many sounds. That suits me too.
An echo. So I was hiding, in a way.
다섯은 앞에서 쐈다. 나는 반대편에서 같은 곳을 봤다. 어느 쪽이 더 잘: The five fired from the front. I watched the same place from the far side. Which side would have seen it better?
You need both sides to see it all. Both were needed.
From the far side, you'd only see the backs of their heads.
Both. That answer rings the longest.
The front. The five would say so too.
The backs of their heads. I nearly laughed.
종말의 포성. 그 이름을 듣고 물러서지 않는 이는 드물다. 지휘관은 어째: The Doomsday Knell. Few hear that name and do not step back. Why do you not, Commander?
Because I looked at which side you stand on, not at the name.
Which side I stand on. Now, it is this ship's side.
Just a name. I am grateful for that lightness.
Cool. A light word to attach to doom. I like it.
다섯이 모였기에 나도 왔다. 그 다섯이 곁에 있다. 그런데 아직 건넬 말: I came because the five gathered. The five are beside me now. Yet I am still choosing what to say to them.
No rush. The five know how to wait.
You don't have to say anything.
Just greet them with your gun.
They know how to wait. Just like those five.
If I need not, then today I will send only a ringing.
Greeting with a gun. The Hangar would be startled.
이 배의 소리를 하나씩 익히는 중이다. 이름 모를 소리가 아직 많다. 하: I am learning this ship's sounds one by one. Many are still nameless to me. Will you teach me one?
That low hum is the vent. It runs all night.
The vent. That which never stops all night. The opposite of me.
They are not alike. Each one is different. You will come to know.
That one I will not learn. It makes me laugh, which is troublesome.
I have only ever been called the sound that announces the end. What do I sound like to you, Commander?
A sound that says "here." That one is lighter. I will keep it.
An alarm. Then I will ring for you every morning.
Is there a way to let someone know you are near, without a gun? The five seem to know.
No need to tell. It's known anyway.
"I am back." …Is this how it is said?
Known without being told. Those words ease me a little.
I cannot fire small. The gun will not allow it.
I have returned. The ringing still lingers.
Repairs are done. The barrel has found its weight again.
You have returned. While I waited, I learned every sound on this ship.
Back. Finished it in the first round again.
Back. Protected more than I broke.
Returned. The sound of the barrel cooling — nice.
Back. Hit as much as I waited.
Back. My fingertips are still trembling.
Back. Going around the back was easy.
Back. Reading the map upside down was right.
Back. This parabola was pretty too.
Back. Guarded the flagship's front again today.
Returned. Three lines for the report.
I'm back. Went a little over today's share.
I'm back. I'll do the rest tomorrow.
Back. Left the gunfire on the far side.
Returned. I will speak once the echo ends.
Repairs done. Really didn't break anything.
Fixed. Two first-round volleys, ready again.
All done. The coward's way is ready again.
We held. Turns out I didn't need to break anything.
They withdrew. Finished it in the first round.
You're late. I've got lots to grumble about.
You're back. Didn't break a thing, really.
Repairs done. The trigger feels light.
We held. Hit as much as I waited.
They withdrew. The sound of the barrel cooling — nice.
You're here. Sound returns to the deck.
It was empty a long time. My fingertips got bored.
Fixed. I'll draw the parabola again.
수리 끝. 뒤로 돌아가 볼까?: Repairs done. Shall we go around the back?
All done. Ready to read the map upside down.
We held. Surprised them from behind.
Where were you? I was going to surprise you.
You're back! I was hiding behind you.
Patched up the thin spots again.
Repairs done. I can stand in front.
Fixed. Even a surprise attack is fine.
Held. Nobody got past the flagship's front.
We held. Thin, but I lasted.
They withdrew. The front line's intact.
You're back. I was guarding the front.
Took a while. Still, everyone's safe.
Repairs are done. Keeping the report short.
Fixed. I can do today's share again.
All done. Left that spot as it was.
Held. One more entry in the log.
We held. I'll report in three lines.
They withdrew. I've done today's share.
You're here. I counted the days I waited.
You're back. I've done all my share.
You took a while. I have a three-line report.
Repairs complete. The barrel has found its weight.
Maintenance complete. I will wait again.
We held. The echo reached the far side.
They withdrew. I will speak once the echo ends.
You have returned. I memorized this ship's sounds.
You have come. The deck resounds again.
Barrels are cold. Heating them up? Me first, too.
Lead light: green. The front's mine again today.
Seen the sortie order? Top of the list is me.
Today's first shot hit dead center.
The rear closes things up, so all I have to do is open.
To lift off light, one magazine less. My way.
On nights I miss, the training ground lights will be on. That's me.
Anti-swarm tactics, teaching each other. I learn faster, too.
If you change the lead, tell me first. That, I'll listen to.
The sound of my first shot is my hello. Made today's a loud one.
They say the first name on the roster was mine. I get to brag about that.
Even if I miss, there's somewhere to come back to. So: light, first, fire.
첫 발 쏘기 전에 함교 쪽 한 번 봐. 몰랐지?: Before the first shot, I glance toward the Bridge. Didn't know, did you?
Before the training ground lights go off, I check the Bridge lights. Even my checks take the lead.
오늘 첫 발 어땠어? 한가운데였지?: How was today's first shot? Dead center, right?
Dead center. Everyone had it easy after that.
Right? Open it up and everyone has it easy.
If you're not sure, pull up the log. Dead center, I bet.
Second? That's for everyone else. I'm the first shot.
선두가 가벼워야 하는 이유, 알아?: Know why the lead has to be light?
Because it has to get there first.
That's it. Get there first, and the rest follow.
The back takes care of safe. The front has to be fast.
Fuel's a bonus. I just like fast.
I fly one magazine short. Maintenance sighs every time they see it.
I'll tell them you chose to fly light.
Tell them. That it's not the same as being scared — make sure.
They have a point. So I listen up to the sigh, then fly.
Plenty is slow. One less is my speed.
빗나간 날 밤에 훈련장 간 거, 어떻게 알았어?: The night I missed and went to the training ground — how did you know?
The lights were on. Watched until you finished.
To the end? …Then you saw the last shot too.
If you didn't know, fine. No — that's a little disappointing.
I rested. After one hit dead center.
They say I was first on the roster. Maybe that's why I hate giving first away.
So that's why you always take the first shot.
Maybe. I was first, so I keep first.
Doesn't matter? It kind of does, to me.
No idea about second. I only heard about first.
The lead is where you get there first, alone. Sometimes that stretches out a bit.
If it gets long, open comms. The Bridge is always listening.
That comes with being the lead.
후미를 더 빨리 보낼까?: Should I send the rear out faster?
I'll keep it on. No need to answer — just listen.
Can't be helped. That's why the lead is mine.
The rear's job is closing. Speed it up and the door's left open.
가볍게, 먼저, 정확하게. 하나 더 붙인다면 뭐가 좋을까?: Light. First. True. If I added one more, what should it be?
Together… that breaks the rhythm. I'm putting it in anyway.
Enough, sure. But the fourth slot looked empty.
Lead's back. First to arrive again today.
Held. The first shot was the fastest.
You're here. Kept the lead light on the whole time.
Three cargo holds, all shut. Good.
I'll stay beside it. On the cockpit side.
Escort spacing: within arm's reach. Close enough to count from beside you.
Haul squad — brought everyone home again.
It's fine if the Carrier is slow. I keep pace beside it.
Watch the cockpit, not the cargo. That comes first.
There's an escort slot on the sortie roster, right? Put me there.
There was a day I only watched the cargo hold. Not since.
Beside my first escort partner, we still breathe in step.
Counting who comes back became a habit. Counted today too.
Once I've counted everyone and see the Bridge lights, my shoulders finally loosen.
When you're on the Bridge, the way back gets shorter.
With one more person counting, it's less scary.
Sometimes I'd like someone beside me doing the counting, too.
You count today. How many came back.
호위할 때 어디에 붙는 게 좋을까. 화물칸, 조종석?: When escorting, where should I stay? Beside the cargo hold, or the cockpit?
Yes, the people side. I decided the same.
It is pricier. I'll still stay beside the cockpit.
The others are good at going to shoot. I'll stay.
회수 편성에 내가 끼면 무사하다는 말이 돌던데. 믿어?: People say if I'm in the haul squad, everyone makes it back. Believe that?
I do. You stay beside them to the very end.
Then only fly haul from now on.
To the end, I stay beside them. That I can promise.
Lots. But this one, I'll try to live up to.
Every time, and the other squads would sulk. Let's go half and half.
People ask if matching the Carrier's speed isn't frustrating.
Keeping pace is a skill too.
캐리어를 빠르게 바꿀까?: Should I make the Carrier faster?
Nice of you to call it a skill. I'll call it that.
A little. But I can see who's beside me, so it's fine.
Don't change it. That speed is what lets me see beside me.
화물칸만 지켰던 날 뒤로, 조종석 옆에 붙어. 이상해 보여?: Since the day I only guarded the cargo hold, I stick beside the cockpit. Does that look strange?
No. You changed because you know what you missed.
Yes. I knew what I'd missed, so I changed. That's all.
I hope everyone does. So it isn't just me.
It does. That's why I try to watch both.
Always being the one who guards, sometimes I wonder who guards me.
I do. I'll keep watching your way back from the Bridge.
You'll keep watching. …Then I'll count a little less today.
Each other. Right — I don't have to count alone.
An escort for the escort? The line's going to get long.
If I come up one short while counting, I hear nothing until I count again.
If one's missing, I'll find them first from the Bridge.
You'll find them first… then recounting will be less scary.
Lately, yes. So lately I sleep well.
호위 간격이 손 닿을 만큼인 거, 실은 내가 덜 무서우려고 그런 걸지도: Keeping escort spacing within arm's reach — maybe it's really so I'm less scared.
Then put me inside that spacing too.
간격 재는 자를 줄까?: Want a ruler to measure it?
You're in. Have been for a long time.
It is. Mine goes as far as my hand reaches.
No ruler needed. Measuring by hand is more accurate.
Back. Every one of us, none missing.
Repairs done. Going back to escort spacing beside them.
Held. Cargo hold and people, all intact.

One shot today. One was enough.

Circling. Everything below checked. Bridge included.

I said "I was waiting" only that one time.
High altitude. Bridge lights: spotted instantly.
High-altitude reception: clear. Your voice, anyway.
Sorry. Reports are short. Reception: complete.
No. 1 in accuracy. No congratulations needed. It's luck.
It's every time, though — hardly luck.
Every time. …Count it that way and I've got nothing.
No. 2. Tried. Couldn't. My hand moves first.
Time spent circling high. Everyone says it's long.
You're picking the moment to go down.
낮게 날면 덜 춥지 않아?: Isn't it less cold flying low?

Long. That's why the one shot is short.
Not cold. When the wind clings to the wings, it's warm.
Reading the wind. Want me to teach you.
Next. The wind always says that too.

Waiting is part of your shooting.
Half the shooting. No — most of it.
More. One more column. A hassle.
Short means a miss. Write it long.

Let them look. Your column's worth looking at.
Worth looking at. …They'd be hurt if I said luck.

Hide them and they'd search harder. Leaving it.
내려올 데를 정해 두면 오래 맴돌 수 있어. 정해 둬도 돼?: With a place to come down to, I can circle longer. Can I pick one?

다음엔 더 멋지게 돌지!: Next time I'll turn even cooler!
헤헤, 긁혔는데 별거 아냐!: Hehe, just a scratch, no big deal!

안마 기계를 들일까?: Should I bring in a massage machine?
내려갔지! 그거 보려고 하는 거야!: They dropped! That's what I do it for!
기계는 같이 웃어 주지 않잖아! 탈락!: Machines don't laugh with you! Rejected!
손상 입고 와도 제일 먼저 웃는 거, 이상해?: Laughing first even when I come back damaged — is that weird?

끝났다는 신호! 그럼 더 크게 웃어야지!: An "it's over" signal! Then I'll laugh even louder!

웃는 얼굴로 쏘면 빗나간다는 말, 진짜일까?: They say if you shoot smiling, you miss. True?
웃는 얼굴 훈련장 만들까?: Should I build a smiling-face training ground?

만들자! 입구엔 거울 달고!: Let's build it! With a mirror at the entrance!
다음엔 더 빨리 피하지! 이 말, 너무 자주 하나?: "Next time I'll dodge faster!" Do I say that too often?

Feels like I've heard it about ten times.
There's a next time. I'm keeping those words.
Around the tenth time, even I hesitated a little. I'm fine now.
My wings dodge before any book could! I'll take it anyway.
혼자 웃는 거랑 같이 웃는 거, 소리가 다르게 들려?: Laughing alone and laughing together — do they sound different?

녹음해서 비교해 볼까?: Should we record them and compare?

They're different! Listen closely next time!

On heavy days, come here. You don't have to laugh.
Don't have to laugh… then I'll rest a little here.
Usually, yes. Sometimes it's the opposite — that's why I asked.
단 거! 그건 무거운 날에도 통해!: Sweets! Those work even on heavy days!
한 번쯤은 네가 먼저 웃어 줄래? 내가 웃기 전에!: Just once, will you laugh first? Before I do!
Next return, I'll try laughing first.
웃음 신호를 정할까?: Should we set a laugh signal?
진짜? 그럼 나 일부러 천천히 내린다!: Really? Then I'll land slowly on purpose!
제일 빠른 거 맞아. 근데 네가 이기는 날도 보고 싶어!: I am the fastest. But I want to see a day you win too!
A signal? Then it's not a laugh, it's an alarm.
돌아왔어! 다음엔 착륙도 일등 하지!: I'm back! Next time I'll land first too!
수리 끝! 반짝반짝, 웃을 준비 끝!: Repairs done! All shiny, ready to laugh!
왔다! 어깨 굳었지? 이리 줘!: You're here! Shoulders stiff? Hand them over!
Next waypoint's probably to the right. I've got my reasons.
Folding a map is a skill too. Because the creases are where the routes meet.
Drew one route. Because it's the one that burns less fuel.
See a route once, I don't forget it. Because I memorize why it runs that way.
Guessing the next waypoint — I won again today.
I finish the return calculation before sortie. Because it puts my mind at ease.
One more unknown point on the map. Good.
I said one thing to Navigation and they redid their calculations.
I've got a rival for return-calculation speed. Still tied.
I don't fully trust maps someone else drew. Gotta see it with my own eyes.
I put a small mark on the map for every waypoint I've been to. Even if I'll never go back.
Thinking about handing out a map to everyone before sorties.
Today I'm closing the map and looking out the window. Because together, we won't get lost.
Doodled something in the corner of the map. Don't laugh if you see it.
I want to bet with you on the next waypoint.
Unknown routes used to scare me, see. Less so lately.
다음 경유지 맞히기, 이유도 들을래?: Want to hear the reasoning behind my next-waypoint guess too?
Yes. The reason is part of your answer.
점이라도 쳐?: Do you tell fortunes or something?
Reasoning too. Then it's a long one, okay? Starting with fuel.
Just the result? To the right. Reasons next time, all at once.
No fortunes. Because I calculate it.
Some girls think it's weird for a Striker to read maps.
The faster you go, the more the route matters.
Leave the maps to the navigators.
Go fast and get lost, and you get lost the farthest. That's what I mean.
Hobby… half of it. The other half is work.
I leave it to them and look anyway. Two looks, less wandering.
귀환 계산 먼저 끝내는 거, 너무 겁쟁이 같아?: Finishing the return calculation first — too cowardly?
Drawing the way back first is the bravest thing there is.
Brave. That word's not on any map, but I'll take it.
Meticulous, yes. To me that's a compliment.
I'm faster than the machine. And I've got a rival.
There was a day one word from me made Navigation rerun their calculations. Still a little awkward about it.
Nothing to be awkward about. They fixed it because you were right.
You can show off a little.
계산 담당한테 사과했어?: Did you apologize to whoever does the calculations?

A little's fine, right? Then I'll do a little today.
Didn't apologize. Checked the next calculation with them instead.

Anytime. I can be a reference point for you.
When it's busy, look somewhere else.
표지등을 하나 달까?: Should I put up a beacon?
A reference point. Then I'll look right away when I'm stuck.
I won't when you're busy. I'll look once you're done.
There are plenty of beacons. The Bridge window is enough.
I can guess where we'll go. But where that route gets decided, even I don't know.
I wonder too. But as long as you read the way, it's fine.
We just go where it's set.
항로표에 써 있지 않아?: Isn't it on the route chart?

Sometimes I want to go without knowing the way. Not something a guide should say, though.
That day, I'll keep the light on for your way back.
Once in a while should be fine.
항법사를 한 명 붙일까?: Should I assign you a navigator?
With the light on, I won't get lost. Then I'll head somewhere unknown without worry.
Once in a while. I'll try it just once.
Then I'd know the way again. That won't do.
Return complete. Because I knew the way from the start.
Repairs done. Redrew the route in the meantime.
Held. Sent it back the way it came.
You're here. I knew which way you'd come from.
Everyone still behind? That's all right.
Did you see only my tail? That is enough.
The fuel runs light. Go on ahead, dear.
So I'm not on the radar. Yet here I am.
My tail entered the Hangar first. I came a moment later.
Don't follow, dear. The tail will burn you.
How cramped the Hangar is. Still, I like it.
Coming back first makes me the one who waits. How unfamiliar.
"All anyone sees is the tail" — I'll take that as praise.
Short with words, am I. Everything fast is short.
Arriving first. Waiting. I no longer mind it.
함교 레이더엔 꼬리 말고 내가 보이니?: On the Bridge radar, do you see me — not just my tail?
I'll try saying it slowly. …Here. I am.
Fast things are short. So, just once. Thank you.
Even just the tail tells me you went by.
You recognize it. The tail isn't so bad, then.
You didn't. Next time I'll circle once for you.
Don't fix it, dear. It isn't broken.
먼저 돌아오는 건 연료 탓이야. 서운했니?: Coming back first is the fuel's doing. Did it hurt your feelings?
Seeing you already back puts everyone at ease.
연료통을 하나 더 달까?: Should I add another fuel tank?
At ease. Then I'll keep coming first.
Plain. I like that. Those words.
더 달면 더 멀리 가 버릴걸. 그건 곤란하지?: Add more and I'd only go farther. That would be a bother, wouldn't it?

Leaving late and arriving first — that's so you.
"So me." I'll take those words slowly.

Counting the sound of the Hangar doors opening.
Found out. I know who each sound is.
If I fell asleep, I wouldn't know who came first.

Then let's start by making your time here long.
Get a long sleep, at least.
Time here… that may be long, then.
Fine, you say. Then the short me feels a little less sorry.
Sleep is short. But dreams pass quickly.
Just once, I'd like to fly side by side with everyone to the end. Would the fuel hold?

견인선을 붙일까?: Should I attach a tow ship?
All together, to the end. A path I've never flown.
I won't. But wishing is free.
A comet on a tow line. How silly.
내가 천천히 말하면, 끝까지 들어 줄 거니?: If I speak slowly, will you listen to the end?
To the end. Even one word at a time.
I can hear you fine now.
To the end. …Then, one word at a time.
Glad you can hear. Still, I'd like to try slower.
Recordings get fast-forwarded. I don't want that.
Here first. Take your time, everyone.
Repairs done. Tail and all, reattached.
Lead returned. First shot was mine too.
Back. The front seat's mine again today.
Back. All three cargo holds closed.
Back. I'll be by the cockpit.
왔어! 오늘 회전 봤어? 멋졌지!: Back! Did you see that spin today? So cool!
다녀왔어! 다음엔 더 크게 돌 거야!: Back! Next time I'll spin even bigger!
Returned. Told you — the right side. Right again.
Back. The chokepoint was on the fold line.
Back. Came straight by the map.
I came first. Everyone take your time.
돌아왔어. 꼬리만 보여도 충분했니?: I'm back. Was the tail enough for you?

Fixed. Don't give away the lead spot.
Repairs done. The first shot's still mine.
Held. Shot first from the very front.
They withdrew. The lead is always my spot.
You're back. I kept the lead marker lit.
You're late. I almost went ahead.
I waited. Let's do the first sortie together.
Fixed. I'll fly beside you again.
Fixed. I'll be by the cockpit.
All done. I'll guard the three cargo holds again.
Held. The cargo holds are all shut.
We held. People and cargo, all intact.
They withdrew. Glad I was by your side.
You're back. I'm not done counting till I count you.
Took a while. I shut all the cargo holds.
고쳤어! 다음엔 더 크게 돌 거야!: Fixed! Next time I'll spin even bigger!
지켰어! 오늘도 멋졌지!: We held! We were awesome again today!
왔다! 어깨 이리 줘!: You're here! Give me your shoulder!
오래 걸렸네! 그래도 반가워!: Took you long! But I'm glad to see you!
Fixed. I think I know the next waypoint.
Held. Sent them back the way they came.
We held. I knew the chokepoint.
They withdrew. Knew they'd go right.
You're here. I knew which way you'd come from.

오래 걸렸네. 길은 맞게 왔지?: Took a while. You came the right way, didn't you?
Repairs done. Even the tail is attached.
Fixed. You could've taken your time.
All done, dear. I'll go ahead again.
Held, dear. Just one swish of my tail.
지켰단다. 다들 괜찮니?: We held, dear. Everyone all right?

I waited, dear. No need to hurry.
Did it take long? Everyone comes slowly anyway.
Loading other people's crates too. Got it. Straps tight.

My ledger's got a column for other people's holds now. I'll weigh it to the gram.

들었어? 나 이제 남의 짐 실어 나르는 쪽이래! 손 빠른 게 드디어 쓸모: Heard? Word is I'm hauling other people's cargo now! Fast hands finally pay off!
제일 빨리 돌아온 화물칸, 또 나야! 이건 소문 아니고 기록!: Fastest hold back home? Me again! That's not gossip, that's the record!
예고 소식은 내가 제일 먼저 듣잖아. 그러니까 싣고 피하는 것도 내가 제: I'm always first to hear about a warning. So I'm the fastest to load up and get clear too!
있잖아, 우리 집 털렸다는 소문이 하나도 안 돌아. 요즘 제일 좋은 소식: Hey, not one rumor going around that our place got robbed. Best news lately.
빼앗으러 나가는 길이라니, 언니도 조금 떨려. 그래도 신입들 앞에선 침착: Heading out to take from others… even big sister's a little shaky. Still, calm in front of the newcomers.

빨리 가서 빨리 돌아오니까, 세는 시간도 짧아졌네. 이번에도 다 데려왔어: Out fast, back fast, so the counting got shorter too. Brought everyone back again.
An escort who blocks the pass first. Nothing to hesitate over there.
요격 나갔다 돌아오면 늘 세. 하나, 둘, 셋… 집도 사람도 다 그대로야: Back from an intercept, I always count. One, two, three… Home and everyone, all intact.
Ambush path: selected. Descent angle: recalculating.
Descent from outside detection. Hit. …Not calling it luck this time.
Intercept standby. Holding altitude, watching what approaches.
Intercept successful. Worth the long wait. Bridge lights, still on.
빨리 닿는 쪽이래! 출발 전에 어깨부터 툭! 신나는데?: The side that gets there first! A pat on the shoulder before launch! This is fun!
도착 일등, 웃음도 일등! 상대가 놀라기도 전이었어!: First to arrive, first to laugh! Before they even got surprised!
집 지키는 쪽도 좋지! 손님 오면 내가 제일 먼저 날아갈게!: Guarding home's great too! When visitors come, I'll be the first to fly out!
돌아오는 길에 다들 웃어! 집 지키고 오는 날은 웃음소리가 훨씬 커!: Everyone's laughing on the way back! On days we guard home, the laughter's way louder!
Shortest route there, huh. Finding the way through has always been my thing.
상대가 알아차리기 전에 닿는 길, 지도에 다 그려 놨어. 같이 그린 지도: Routes that get there before they notice. I've drawn them all on the map. A map we drew together.
Which way they'll come in, I'll draw on the map first.

So this is the path that arrives first. I've always been that way, dear.
They won't have seen so much as my tail. Yet you always saw me.
Greeting the guests, then. Going out first to wait is nothing new to me.

Standing first in front of someone else's turrets. Same as what I've always done.
Even facing turrets that fire first, I don't waver now. I watched the front to the end.
The watch at the front of home. A post where even a low voice carries.
It was a long watch. Now the whole home is at my back.
Going out to take turret fire. Plenty more to carve, then. I'm ready for it.
Patched over and over. Not broken. Thicker.
If the marks come at home, I'll carve them deeper. I'll take this path.
The marks I took for my watchmates cover the whole plate now. I'm not erasing a single one.
…Before the turrets. …I take the first hit. …So the back doesn't.
…Opening fire… took all of it. …Back, everyone's there. …We came home together.
…Watch. …Every name left at home… I'll remember them all.
이거지! 먼저 들이받는 갈래! 방어형 소리는 이제 끝!: This is it! The ram-first path! No more defensive-type talk!
포탑이 먼저 쏴도 끄떡없어! 도크 침대가 서운해할 정도야!: Turrets can fire first, I don't budge! My dock bunk's gonna feel neglected!
당직이라고? 집 지키는 거… 뭐, 막는 것도 들이받는 거니까!: Watch duty? Guarding home… eh, blocking's ramming too!
가디언이라 불러도 돼! 오래 서 보니 문 앞에서 버티는 것도 재밌더라!: You can call me Guardian! After standing this long, holding the door turned out to be fun!
그늘에서만 있던 내가 앞으로 나간다니. 왜 이 갈래가 끌렸는지 나도 몰라: Me, who only ever stayed in the shade, stepping out front. Why was I drawn to this path? I don't know either.
I can walk right into where they fire first and not shake now. Why didn't I do this sooner?
It's the watch that stands in home's shade. The spot that suits me best.
Wherever the watch started to give, I was already there. My shade's grown as wide as home.
The fortress marches out. Let the turrets fire first. It does not matter.
I took every shot their turrets had. The fortress that marched out has come back. With you.
A fortress stands before home by nature. I will take the watch.
This home was never breached. Not a legend. Something you saw.
Heavy's mine. Even if it's just what they left outside the vault, I'm hauling it home.
More scuffs on the hold floor. Every one of these, I made with you.
There's cargo I hauled in the Underground Vault. Visitors aren't getting a single crate.
Guarding the vault has its own weight. I held out a long time. That's something to be proud of too.
상대 창고 밖에 남은 거, 그냥 두고 오면 허전하잖아?: Whatever's left outside their vault, leaving it behind would feel hollow, right?
These days I ask less whether this is enough. Because you count it with me.
Not emptying matters as much as filling. I'm not giving up one slot of storage.
The Underground Vault always feels heavy now. Maybe that's why I sway less lately.
I'll dim my lights a bit. Just on the way out! On the way back, let's all shine together.
Went all that way and not one girl got lost. You were always my signal lamp.
여기야! 우리 창고 앞에 불 켜 둘게. 다 보이게!: Over here! I'll keep the lights on in front of our vault. So everything shows!
The mothership's lights feel just like mine. That's what guarding it this long did.
Picking's what I'm good at. Even outside their vault, I'll bring back only what isn't broken.
These days the cores catch my eye first. They shine even among the junk.
Me, the scavenger, on the guarding side. Well, I never throw away anything useful.
Nothing in the vault is junk. All of it was worth guarding.
Quiet songs on the way out~ I'll sing loud on the way back.
Never ran short of songs, even on the long hauls~ The last verse was always yours.
There's a song for guarding home too~ Slow tempo, right at the vault door.
Guarding this long, I've picked up more lullabies~ The whole ship knows them now.
Far cargo. In front of their vault. Still. Shoulders, plenty of room.
Weight. Weight carried long. Shared with you. It was light.
Guarding. Suits me. Standing long. I'm good at it.
Home. Weight. On my shoulders. You too. Inside it.
My feet moved first. I'll be beside the girls who go far out, too.
돌아오는 길이 험해도 이젠 무섭지 않아. 너랑 같이 데려온 날들이 쌓였어: Even when the way back is rough, I'm not scared anymore. All the days we brought them home together have added up.
It's okay. Not yet. Anyone hurt at home, I'll see to first.
The girls on watch come back without a scratch. Fewer times I have to whisper "it's okay."
I chose the side that goes out to take. Even so, I will write both sides in my report.
실패한 날에도 덜 다친 줄이 길어졌어요. 지휘관님이랑 같이 쓴 보고서예요: Even on the days we failed, the list of those hurt less kept growing. It is a report I wrote with you, Commander.
Guarding may suit my pen better. Let us end it with less pain.
Even the column for the visitors who withdrew has grown shorter. It means everyone was hurt less.
I'll hold a wrench out in the field too. It's like my hands reach that much farther.
멀리서 다친 기체도 도크까지 멀쩡히 왔어요. 조인 볼트가 하나도 안 풀렸: Even units damaged far away made it to the dock in one piece. Not one bolt I tightened came loose.
Guarding the dock? That's the place my hands know best.
Repairs on the watch units finish in no time. It's like this whole dock has become my hands.
I'll work out the return, even for the long routes. I'll call your names at the entrance.
I don't get even the long returns wrong now. Not one name I called at the entrance came up empty.
At home, everyone's right in front of me. Perfect for calling names.
The entrance feels like a gatekeeper's post now. I didn't miss anyone. Called every name.
Salve. Packed. Going far? I follow.
Even when they come back hurt… words come first now. Thanks to you.
Shh. I'll watch home. Nobody gets hurt.
The girls on watch say they're fine without my hand. A little sad.
I will leave the roof for a while. I will greet the dawn beside those coming home from far away.
Even in a distant sky, the dawn light comes from the same direction. Your direction, Commander.
The roof is where I belong. I will gladly take the side that guards home.
The mornings after night raids have grown quiet. I know this home's dawns now.
Report: will quietly deafen their sensors on approach. No noise made.
Their warning: late to the very end. Cause unknown. Actual cause: you and me.
Commencing constant listening around home. If something I ought to hear goes silent, will report at once.
함교 경보, 늘 제때 울림. 오래 들었더니 이 집 소리가 다 내 거 같음: Bridge alert: always on time. Listened long enough that every sound in this home feels like mine.
The way in… I'll blur it. So they notice late.
I've hidden for so long that hiding doesn't scare me now. Because you always see me anyway.
Watching instead of hiding…? It feels a little strange, but I'll try.
Anything coming toward our home, I see first now. That feels safer than keeping it veiled.
Selection confirmed. Approach will be silent. Over.
Silent approach: success every time. A road we came by together. Thanks.
Commence watch. Home frequencies: this end is listening.
Alerts were always on time. Short words were enough. Thanks to you.
Look. I've already read where their radar goes blind.
Their intercept patterns, I read them all before launch now. Look, right again today.
Incoming squads: watch the speed first. I'll tell you who it is before anyone.
누가 오는지 이젠 예고보다 먼저 알아. 근데 네 발소리는 여전히 못 맞혀: I know who's coming before the warning now. But your footsteps? Still can't guess those.
숨는 거 아니고 잡음에 묻히는 거야. 이 차이 중요해!: It's not hiding, it's blending into the noise. The difference matters!
Their intercepts all scattered. You can praise me at length this time. Hehe.
The guarding side? It's not return fire. It's laying noise all around home.
Even when an ambush comes, we don't get swamped now. Nothing to correct. For real.
I'll go in quiet. …Quiet. I know where the gaps are.
내 소리, 그쪽엔 끝까지 안 들렸어. 너한텐 늘 들렸지?: My sound never reached them, start to finish. But you always heard it, right?
Around home, I'll listen. …I'll listen. This time, they're my own words.
Whoever comes close, I answer first. The sounds of this home aren't echoes anymore.
Plunder is bringing things back. The rest is outcome. I'll still count the units due back.
Even on hauling days, the gauge needle stays calm. Now, at last, I can say what I am.
I'll take the guarding side. A good day's definition stays the same: one where fewer get hurt.
손님이 다녀가도 손상 칸이 비어 있어. 이 모함을 성이라고 정의해도 되겠: Visitors come and go, and the damage column stays empty. I think I can define this Mothership as a castle.
I just send my signal loud, all the way to their sky. So everyone can follow.
이제 멀리 나가도 다들 내 채널부터 찾아. 별거 아냐, 목청 하나 키운: Now, however far we go, everyone looks for my channel first. It's nothing. I just got a little louder.
Not far off. I'll just tune to home instead. I'll keep the watch channel on.
손님 오는 소리가 잡음 속에서도 또렷해. 이 집 채널은 한 번도 안 끊겼: I can hear visitors coming, clear even through the noise. This home's channel hasn't dropped once.
Even on a run to grab stuff, up front is mine. That way the others don't get hit.
I head out heavy and come back heavy. That's my stride now.
Guarding home? That I'm sure of. I'll stand all three of my Hangar slots right at the door.
I'm the one at this home's door now. The others can sleep easy inside.
많이 빼앗는 게 아니야. 다들 고르게 돌아오게 짜는 거지. 배치표 새로: It's not about taking a lot. It's about planning so all of us come back, not just a few. I'll lay out a fresh positioning chart.
The Assault positioning chart fits now without a single fix. Because it's one I made with you.
It's not about guarding. It's about making sure no slot in this home gets hurt alone.
When I open the watch roster, your place is the first thing I see now. Home held, right by the chart.
This time I will lead the way with the flag! Not behind my big sisters.
Even as the baby flagship out in front, I do not shake anymore. Because you kept watching over me, Commander.
기함이면 집도 지켜야죠? 깃발은 모함 꼭대기에 꽂아 둘게요!: A flagship should guard home too, right? I will plant the flag at the very top of the Mothership!
언니들이 저를 감싸던 만큼, 이제 제가 이 집을 감싸요. 씩씩하게요!: As much as my big sisters shielded me, now I will shield this home. Bravely!
The one who stands at the top steps out first, you see. I shall carry this wind all the way to them.
먼저 나서는 순번을 오래도 지켜 왔구나. 그대 곁이라 바람이 춥지 않았단: How long I have kept my turn at stepping out first. At your side, the wind was never cold.
I shall be this home's windbreak. That is what the top has always been.
The nights the five kept their places have piled up. This is a chain of command you and I built together.
Makes me sound like the one who breaks things again. Fine. This time I'll go break things properly.
이제 부수는 사람이라고 불려도 괜찮아. 네가 전원 귀환 줄을 읽어 주니까: I don't mind being called the one who breaks things now. Because you're the one who reads me the all-units-back line.
On the guarding side, nobody can say I sound like a coward, right? I'll shoot first, right outside home.
They say I sound like the one who guards this home. That sounds nicer than I thought.
Their facilities. Still quiet. The moment waiting for the first shot.
The silence after the sound of collapse. Beside the Commander, who waited with me so long.
Home deck. My spot. Waiting is what I've always been good at.
The gun that sounds before the visitors do. The silence after. The best moment in this home.
Facilities only look forward, right? Arcing shots in from behind — that's my main job now. Hehe.
그쪽 시설 지도, 거꾸로 봐도 바로 봐도 다 외웠어. 너랑 같이 잰 각도: Their facility map — upside down or right side up, I've got it all memorized. Angles we measured together.
Defense is angles too. I'll hang an arc over every route that leads home.
All around this home, it's packed with my arcs. No prank this time — I mean it.
Thin or not, I can go in first. This time I'm not the one blocking. I'm the one breaking through.
장갑은 그대로 얇은데, 들어갈 때 마음은 늘 두꺼웠어. 반은 네 몫이었고: My armor's as thin as ever, but my nerve never ran thin going in. Half of that was yours.
"In front of the flagship" just grew into "in front of home." I'll stand there, thin or not.
One more scar. Proof I stood in front of this home to the end.
I will carve each facility I break as a line. From now on, that is my share.
There is almost no empty space left on my armor. You were there in every line, Commander.
Can the days I held them off be carved into the record too? Then I'll take the guarding side.
집을 지킨 줄이 많이 늘었어요. 말도 조금 늘어서, 오늘은 길게 보고할게: The lines for guarding home have grown many. My words have grown a little too, so today I will give a long report.
I will sound my toll against the far ramparts. As far as the ringing reaches, that is my share.
The toll that once rang from the far side now sets out from beside the Commander. That is enough.
Any toll coming for this ship, I will meet first and ring back. A guarding ring is still a ring.
Before the visitors' toll arrives, this ship rings first. A beat kept in time with the Commander.
Their engine trails are still warm. Now I call the headings to other people's homes too.
I can even read who's on their watch by the heat. Still, my first heading is always toward you.
I've spread the clock face all around home. Any trail coming in, I call it first.
All the way around, not one cold spot. Every heading around this home is mine.
Their storeroom smells like something, I'm telling you. I'll bring it back in a report and show you. For real.
Now one sniff and I can see everything going on over there. I'm not just insisting. It's true.
If a strange smell gets into home, I'm the first to know. This one I don't even have to insist on.
이 집 냄새는 눈 감고도 알아. 낯선 게 섞이는 순간 코끝이 먼저 알아채: I know this home's smell with my eyes shut. The moment something strange mixes in, my nose catches it first.
Reading coordinates? That I'm sure of! I'll call out their numbers, every last one.
남의 집 좌표도 이제 머리에 다 있어! 그래도 제일 먼저 외운 건 여기야: Other people's coordinates are all in my head now! But the first ones I memorized were here.
I'll call out the incoming numbers first! I'll measure the star angles every day too.
Incoming coordinates stick in my head before I've even heard them out! My voice is a little hoarse, but I'm fine.
The road to someone else's home is still a road. I step on it first.
I have walked every road over there now. When I looked back, you were always there.
I will walk the ground around home. If strange footsteps sound, I know first.
My footprints leave no gap around this home. Instead of going first, I stood at the door.
It's just as dark at a stranger's door. I'll carry the lantern. Don't worry, everyone.
어느 집 앞에 가도 이제 길이 훤해. 돌아오는 길마다 네가 불을 켜 뒀으: Whatever home I go to now, the path is bright. Because you left a light on every way back.
I'll leave one lantern lit at home. So the visitors can be seen coming from far off.
This has become a home where the light stays on all night. Everyone can sleep. Tonight I'll get a little sleep too.
Being the one who goes far out feels a little strange. Still, north is always this ship.
However much I looked into other homes, my heart never drifted. Because here is where I come back to.
Guarding has always been my place. I'll stay right here, still.
다가오는 게 있으면 별보다 먼저 보여. 움직이지 않으니까 다 보이는 거야: If anything comes near, I see it before the stars. I don't move, so I see everything.
Someone else's Underground Vault door. Even there, I don't change my count.
You count with me, right beside me. So at any door, my count doesn't waver.
I'll stand inside our door. Pushy visitors will have an even harder time getting it open.
…One. Two. Their count, from the other side of the door. I can hear all of it now.
지하 창고 문에도 거는 자리는 있겠지요. 힘보다 받침으로 열어 보겠습니다: Even an Underground Vault door must have a place to set the bar. I will open it with leverage, not force.
이제 어느 창고 문이든 받침 자리가 먼저 보입니다. 언제부터 아셨습니까?: Now, on any vault door, I see the fulcrum point first. How long have you known?
여는 법을 아니 안 열리게 하는 법도 압니다. 우리 문 받침은 제가 맡겠: Knowing how to open means knowing how to keep shut. I will take charge of the fulcrum on our door.
우리 문에는 이제 거는 자리가 없습니다. 오래 함께 찾아서 지운 덕분입니: Our door no longer has anywhere to set a bar. That is because we searched them out together, for a long time, and erased them.
남의 금고 소리는 처음이라 조금 떨려요. 그래도 귀는 벌써 기울어 있어요: It's my first time with someone else's vault, so I'm a little nervous. But my ear's already leaning in.
Click. That one. Now even the latch at the very back of the vault answers me.
우리 창고 문 소리는 제가 제일 잘 알아요. 낯선 손이 닿으면 바로 들릴: I know our vault door's sound better than anyone. If a stranger's hand touches it, I'll hear it right away.
오래 듣다 보니 우리 문은 낯선 손엔 소리를 안 내요. 지휘관님 발소리에: After listening so long, our door makes no sound for strange hands. Only for your footsteps, Commander.
Vault walls have cracks too. Already spotted one.
I see the cracks before I even reach the wall. These eyes have looked with you a long time.
This time I'm finding our own wall's cracks first. Faster than anyone else.
우리 벽, 다시 봤어. 금 하나 없어. 봤어?: Our walls. Checked again. Not a single crack. See it?
Rosaline bets there's a Core at the very back of their vault.
Rosaline guesses right more days now. Funny, Rosaline even misses the days she guessed wrong.
This time Rosaline bets the other way. That nobody can guess what's behind our door.
여태 우리 창고 안을 맞힌 손님은 없어. 로잘린이 제일 오래 이긴 내기야: No visitor has guessed what's in our vault yet. Rosaline's longest winning bet.
Whatever home's vault door it is, I shall greet it first. Doors remember courtesy.
어느 문 앞에 서도 문이 먼저 나를 알아보는군. 지휘관과 오래 다닌 덕일: Whatever door I stand before, the door knows me first. That comes of long travels with the Commander.
I shall stand beside the door. And you, door, give no answer to visitors in a hurry.
I once said I do not guard, I only wait. Now I know the two are the same work.
Even in front of their batteries, the line stays straight. The standard doesn't change.
However much their batteries fire, the end of the line holds. Because you're the one who set the standard.
Not a line that goes out. A line that holds. That's the standard this time.
The watch line. Counted it from the far end. Held it a long time, and it's not off by even half a span.
I'll march tortoise formation just as it is, right to someone else's door. Because slow or not, it won't collapse.
포대가 쏟아붓는 동안에도 방패 아래는 조용해. 이것도 평화라고 불러도 될: Even while the batteries pour it on, it's quiet under the shields. Can I call this peace too?
Holding a shield over home is what I've always done. This time I've got a reason.
My longest hold — I set a new one in front of home. At the same pace as you.
Someone else's batteries, hm. I'll just go and come back without a single scratch.
그쪽 포대가 그렇게 쏴 댔는데 광이 그대로야. 이 정도면 자랑해도 되거든: Their batteries fired away like that, and my shine's untouched. That earns some bragging, I'd say.
Guarding our own home is more elegant, isn't it? Less dust, too.
오래 지키다 보니 우리 집 문까지 광이 나. 닦은 건 나, 보러 온 건: After guarding it so long, even our home's door shines. I did the polishing. You came to look.
This side, obviously, right? I'm the one who puts the first shot through the gap in the batteries.
The openings between batteries — my spear gets there before I even see them. Doesn't take a single beat.
Guarding? Didn't see that coming, right? Thrusting into the openings of incoming visitors is fun too.
That bit about waiting at home being a thrust too. I believe more than half of it now.
Going far out, there'll be plenty of places to get worn down. So I'll look after the shield beside me first.
How far to patch, my hands know first now, even facing batteries. Up to the shield beside me, all of it.
Staying home and fixing things suits me. My tools won't get a moment's rest.
당직 서는 동안 다 메웠어. 이번엔 내 장갑까지. 맨 마지막 차례가 드디: Patched everything while on watch. This time, up to my own armor. My turn, dead last, finally came.
Even a guardian statue can take a step. So long as the line does not scatter.
Even under fire, the line did not scatter. Standing is the same anywhere.
The place to stand is decided. In front of home.
The place long stood upon has become home. Together with the one who stood beside.
Plenty of scrap, and the burner's glowing red.
Just checked the reagents. Sorry about the smell.
Short on fuel, right? Plenty of smell, though.
Power's holding fine. I've got it.
Checked the cap. Overflow would be such a waste.
Order sheet's updated, names and all.
I'll leave the simulator on. Again.
The rates are just as they were.
There is still room in your trading limit.
Now buying parts, at a fair price.
Our turrets are fine. All three.
The three of us are ready.
My big sisters are over there.
My railgun's charging, just so you know.
I'm not the baby. Got it?
The sights are clear. So is the light.
The light goes to the escorts first.
…If you hear anything, say it softly.
Checked as far as I can see.
I shall keep it out of sight.
Pinned it to the wall, just as measured.
Checked the order sheet for Rivet's crew. One more sheet.
Picked up the instructor's log. I'll file it with the rest.
Plate thickness normal, down to the bulkheads.
Inside the line is the ship.
The wider the field, the more it's my turn — obviously.
Built. One more burner running hot.
All built. It'll smell a bit more now, sorry.
Done. I made sure we've got power to spare.
Built. I raised the cap. Less goes to waste now.
Done. Watch the repair line shrink. Right — next.
Done. More slots. More names too, I bet.
It is finished. I have raised your limit.
Done. The three of us will hold the next raid better.
Done. Told you — it charges faster now.
It is finished. My targeting arc is wider now.
Done. As far as I can see just got farther.
Construction is complete. It is now even harder to see.
Done. Room to stack one more bundle of logs.
Done. One more layer of plate on.
Output's up. Faster now. Talk to Nova about fuel.
화구 앞은 안 뜨거워?: Isn't it hot by the burner?

Let it cool as you go.
오늘 정련량은?: How much did we refine today?
숫자 말고, 오늘 화구 색이 어땠어?: Forget the numbers. What color was the burner today?
One's enough when you're running it.
Word is the servos keep slipping out of alignment.
They don't slip once they've been through your hands.
That smell is what turns into fuel.

Just haul some back from the sortie sites.
Let's level up the Fuel Synthesizer.
It's still on because you're managing it.
Nothing got tossed, thanks to your heads-up.
Electra talks about you a lot.
The line keeps shrinking because your crew's there.
장비 제작은 재밌어?: Is gear crafting fun for you?

격납 순서표 만들었어?: Have you made a hangar order sheet?

Just leave them where they are.

진로는 어떻게 정해?: How do we set our course?

훈련장은 이제 뭘 해?: Quiz: what does the Training Ground do now?

환율이 왜 이런지 아세요?: Do you know why the rates are like this?
If you set the price, there's a reason.
요즘 뭐가 잘 팔릴 것 같으세요?: What do you think will sell well these days?
It took those hits because you were commanding. Thanks.
People say the three of us look alike.
You look alike, but you shoot differently.
The three of you pin your records on the same wall.
포대장이라 부르면 돼?: You'll call me Battery Chief, right?
Your laser, ×2. Light doesn't wait, you said.
막내라고 불러도 돼요?: Would it be all right to call me the baby?
If it's quiet, you're doing your job.
Let's say whatever you don't see isn't there.
Not your fault. It's the level.
보호율이 얼마인지 아십니까?: Are you aware of what the protected share is?
As much as you guard. The number's on the card.
금고 안에 무엇이 있는지 궁금하십니까?: Would you care to know what is inside the vault?

You called it the work of measuring. I'll wait.
The Refinery wall. Agni never took them down.
Want to see the fault logs?

One row. One row, every time.
The constellation notation — you said it's the old style.
판이 두꺼워지면 배가 무거워져. 연료가 더 들어도 돼?: Thicker plates make the ship heavier. Okay if it burns more fuel?

판으로 다 막지는 못해. 괜찮아?: Plates can't stop everything. That okay?

빨리 돌면 연료가 더 들어. 그래도 올려?: Running faster burns more fuel. Still want it up?

Run faster and we meet more. Not every ship's a welcome one.
Meeting them is what the Battlefield is.
Standing here is the job. Leave a fire alone and it sulks fast.
Cool it and the color dies. I'll handle my own sweat.
Machines can't wait. Refining is the work of waiting for the color.
(smiles briefly) Sunset orange. Days like that, the alloy runs clear.
A lot. Enough to blacken my hands stripping scrap.
If it's short, I'll strip more. Plenty of wrecked frames out there.
Enough. I'll hang those words at the end of the line.
Two? Blueprints first. That's an all-nighter.
Slow, but it leaves extra. No extra, no next.
One that slipped after my hands. Still have it hanging up.
Even a defect fits somewhere. Search: ongoing.
Swapping. The pulled ones go in my drawer.
That's what it smells like before it turns into fuel. It's already on you a little.
Air it out and the fuel blows away too. You hold your nose, okay?
I'm fine. Your nose is what you should worry about.
필요하다니까, 합성조 하나 더 청구해도 되지?: Since you need me — I can requisition one more synthesis vat, right?
To haul it back, you need fuel to get there first. That gets made here. Sorry about the smell.
Level it up and the power'll cry again. You take the Power Plant's nagging for me.
Not letting it go dark. The bottom row of my chart is watching.
Been waiting. Already wrote the expansion request.
I pick what gets cut. Starting with your room's lights.
길어. 창고 얘기부터 하면 밤새는데 괜찮아?: It's a long story. If I start with the storage, we'll be up all night. Okay?
Only her sighing face. Beyond that, the little one's the scarier one.
Even if it doesn't matter, Saga's guarding your storage. Just so you know.
Phew. I told you early because I wanted to hear that.
I'll ask my sister for power first. Both need upgrading.
I'll pretend I didn't hear that. Throwing it out would be such a waste. Off to the Exchange.
Really? With me, she only talks about power.
My sister's always busy. So I do her sighing for her.
(her eyes go round) The one who guards the Power Plant. I won't tell her you asked.
I'll tell the crew. Tool-polishing's gonna get loud today.
Everything gets fixed. I just set the order. Speed comes after.
Research records first if you want it up. Bring the paperwork.
Saw that? I hold my breath when a core goes in. Occupational hazard.
What takes long holds long. Rushed stuff's back in the dock in no time.
Every part it eats is a girl hurt less. Put in a word with the parts line.
Not always. But the first line never changes.
Leave them be and they all crowd the door. They can't see where to come back to.
We've never been short. There are still empty rooms — I counted.
I'll call her by name. I already know them all by heart.
A slot by the window. At first, she should be able to see outside.
"Material" isn't on my order sheet. Today I'll just take her name.
So now there are two of us who know the way back.
Wish I could plot one. I'll plot where we come back to instead.
Call it luck. It's less lonely than random.
I will. When we get more, I'll keep one open for coming home.
Upgrading needs Navigation research first, naturally. That's in line too.
Fewer squads and the Control Room would go quiet. That'd feel weirder to me.
Debriefs. When the student memorizes it, the instructor has less to say.
If it looks like a bonus, I hid it well. Underneath, it's a debrief.
Seat them. Two at a time these days. Who's beside you makes a difference.
Run a finger over it. Not a speck.
Put it up at the Exchange? Debrief it and the rate'll be a loss.
If you trust me that much, the rates get a little embarrassed.
It is a rip-off. But it is the same rip-off whenever you come.
Raising it is not free either, I am afraid. Please upgrade the Exchange first.
As expected of a good customer. You look at people, not goods.
Alloy always sells. That is why it is so dull.
(flips back her pink hair) Then I will have to sell news instead.
I don't put "thanks" on the invoice. I keep it separate.
Repairs will be done. The invoice goes to you.
A new turret doesn't have your first order written on it. I fix this one and keep it.
Different. I give the signal, the second takes swarms, the third takes the big ones.
There are three of us and everyone says twins. I don't bother correcting it anymore.
If you mix us up, call the turret instead of a name. All three will answer.
That day, stand behind me! Swarm or whatever, I'll clear the sky!
Call them! Half'll be down before they get here.
Big sis shoots one at a time. The crowds are mine.
There are four of us now. I penciled in one of the columns.
Ballista's the oldest, I'm the middle. Volta graduated from baby.
Whoever answers, you get the same answer. I'll give you that.
I punch right through. I start charging when the warning hits, so tell me early.
They block, I finish. That's always been the order, you know.
Small guns just scratch thick armor. The long barrel's mine — told you.
Battery Chief. Saying it out loud, I think the charge got faster.
Volta. Short and nice. Like cannon fire.
I passed "baby" to number four. No returns.
Yes. The light reaches them before they can turn.
The turrets wait. I do not.
If you ask her, she will point at me as well. The escorts are mine, after all.
Lumen. Yes, that name is the shortest and most precise.
The baby. I accept. That gives me three big sisters.
She is the one who left that word with me. Like baggage.
That's my job… making sure nothing gets heard.
Level it and raid firepower drops more. And I get… quieter.
Never met them. When our jamming overlaps, that's a hello.
We split the same band. No room to fight.
…You don't need to know. They move without a sound anyway.
It counts as nothing. Except the days you're out there.
Anything out of sight goes on a list. That list's the longest.
Level it and the outside shrinks a little. So does the nothing.
I'll blame the level. Still, I'll wipe the scope once more tonight.
Faster. I'll sleep in front of the scope tonight.
Navigation research comes first. How far I can see widens after that.
You even checked the card. I shall guard the last digit myself.
Close. The final digit is written on the vault door.
I shall raise it. However, there will be more seal numbers to stamp on the crates.
I shall keep those words in the unseen compartment.
It has never once been empty. Not even on the days raids broke through.
If you wait, my sign-off signature doesn't shake.
Measure fast and you measure twice. Sit. Measuring.
상한은 내가 아니라 숫자가 걸어. 같이 재 볼래?: The numbers set the cap, not me. Want to measure with me?
Still up. Soot marks beside the measured numbers, too.
You don't need to know. The wall remembers what I measured.
Server? I keep it on paper. The hand remembers differently.
맨 아래 장은 날짜가 없어. 그래도 볼래?: The bottom sheet has no date. Still want to see it?
Summary's one line: it broke, we fixed it. Everything else is why.
By later it'll be one sheet thicker. Breakdowns don't wait.
One row off the repair sheet. The row I cross off still has to go in the Fault Log.
A hundred sheets of "not much" and the dock goes quiet.
To level it, we need to see where things broke first. Come out with me — outside the hull.
Don't know where I learned it. My hands knew first.
Coordinates only. I'll fold away the star names.
I still update it daily. Stars move even on days nobody looks.
Every time. One more person saying it.
Little. That's why it's every time.
Level up, one more row. Rushing won't turn the stars faster.
One more layer, then. Fewer nights counting chipped plates.
I'll cut back. But I'll measure the thinned plates by hand every night.
Nova? One more line in the ledger and that's it. No point asking.
Inside the line, the wall stands and the ship moves. That's enough.
(taps the plate with her fingertips) It does get thicker. Even if there's a limit.
Plates wear down too. Every bit worn off is someone who wasn't.
Wider field, my turn. Get ready for soot.
The gauges hate "no matter what." I'll push it anyway.
If it's a waste, I'll drop it a notch. Even the gauge needles need a rest sometimes.
It's the Battlefield. Welcome or not, better to see them early.
Slow's a number too. I'll keep it faster than that first lap.
Ask the scope. I only know how soon we'll meet them.
스크랩을 합금으로 바꾸는 용광로 앞을 떠나지 않는다. \"정련은 기다리는: She never leaves the furnace that turns scrap into alloy. "Refining is the work of waiting," as Agni puts it. Every time the Refinery levels up, she lights a new burner herself. She strips the scrap to melt herself, too: she has spent as many days crouched before wrecked frames as standing before the burners.
서보 관절 센서를 찍어내는 라인의 설계자. 부품이 남는다는 말을 들으면: Designer of the line that stamps out servos, joints and sensors. Hearing there are spare parts makes her happy, and watching those parts go into repairs and gear is her joy.
추진제를 합성하는 화학관. 전력을 많이 먹는다는 잔소리를 매일 듣지만,: The chemist who synthesizes propellant. She hears daily nagging about how much power she eats, but since the day the cruise fuel ran dry and the Mothership stopped, no one has said it.
모함의 심장을 지키는 기관장. 전력이 모자라면 모든 생산이 깎이는 걸 제: The chief engineer guarding the Mothership's heart. She's the first to know that a power shortage cuts all production, and the first to demand a Power Plant expansion. Saga of the Storage is her younger sister; when the storage the younger sister fills with the older sister's power overflows, the two sigh with the same expression.
상한을 넘친 생산이 버려지는 걸 못 견디는 관리관. 발전소 엘렉트라의 여: A manager who can't stand seeing production over the cap thrown away. Younger sister to Electra of the Power Plant, she pesters for more storage whenever her sister boosts power. The storage level and the ledger are Saga's, and she's the one who asks "You're back?" when the resources fill up.
다친 소녀들이 돌아오는 곳의 반장. 수리 순서를 정하고 장비 모듈을 제작: Dock chief of the place hurt girls come back to. She sets the repair order and crafts gear modules. When the Repair Dock levels up, construction and repairs both speed up, because Rivet's hands get faster.
격납고의 칸을 배정하는 관제관. 누가 어디에 서는지, 새 소녀가 들어올: The controller who assigns Hangar slots. She knows who stands where and whether there's room for a new girl. She has twice seen the moment a roster completes and a Hidden girl appears.
항해 지휘관. 모함의 진로는 그녀도 정하지 못한다 — 경유지는 운이 정한: Navigation commander. Even she can't set the Mothership's course (luck chooses the waypoints), but she directs simultaneous sortie slots and oversees raid warnings.
Drill instructor. She organizes the records of girls back from sorties and leaves them for the next sortie. "What sorties can't teach is the debrief," she says, seating returning girls in front of the simulator.
Trader. She'll trade spare parts for alloy and fuel, but the rate is always a loss. Courteous to customers, merciless on rates. Her greeting is "Nothing's free." The only keeper who dyed her hair pink. "Customers remember a color better than a face."
포격 지휘관. 습격 부대가 쏘기 전에 시설이 먼저 쏘는 선제 사격은 발리: Gunnery commander. The first strike, where the facilities fire before the raiders can, begins on Ballista's signal. When turret durability wears down, she bills the repairs herself.
대공 사수. 군집 드론이 몰려오면 가장 바쁘다. 스트라이커 무리를 상대할: AA gunner. She's busiest when swarm drones pour in. Against Striker packs, too, her autocannon works double.
포대장. 중장기와 기함을 뚫는 레일건을 맡는다. 장포신이 울리는 날은 기: Battery chief. She handles the railgun that pierces heavies and flagships. The day the long barrel sounds is the day of a flagship raid.
요격 사수. 호위기와 전자전을 조준하는 요격 레이저를 맡는다. 약탈해 온: Interceptor gunner. She handles the interceptor laser that targets escorts and electronic warfare. She fires harder at squads that came to plunder, and even when they break through, she chases retreating squads to the end, lightening the resources they're hauling. The first red-haired keeper: the fourth, from a different mold, with nothing in common with the three sisters (Ballista Fleur Volta). The one Volta handed the word "baby" to. She speaks briefly and precisely. She doesn't really know what a miss is.
전파 관제사. 적 습격 부대의 화력을 깎고 전자전 교란을 상쇄한다. 재머: Signal controller. She cuts the firepower of enemy raiders and cancels out electronic warfare jamming. The joke goes that she talks with the Jammer girls only by frequency.
탐지 관측사. 습격 예고와 출격지 정찰, 전장의 다른 모함 탐지가 모두: Sensor observer. Raid warnings, sortie site scouting, and detecting other motherships on the Battlefield all start in Sona's scope. The Radar level is how far her eyes can reach.
금고 관리인. 약탈에서 지켜지는 자원의 비율을 관리한다. 금고는 화물칸: Vault keeper. She manages the share of resources protected from plunder. The vault is at the very bottom of the cargo hold: the crates stamped with seal numbers are Berta's vault. Even if a raid breaks through, what's inside those crates never leaves. She speaks formally to everyone and never gets a single digit wrong. She dyed her hair brown. "Anyone should be able to tell from afar who stands before the vault. I alone am enough for that."
항법 연구 주임. 통제실과 레이더가 더 오르려면 아스트라의 항로표가 먼저: Navigation research lead. For the Control Room and Radar to go any higher, Astra's charts must come first: research level is the facility's cap. If Nova is the one who decides "where to," Astra is the one who measures "how fast, and how far we can see."
정비 연구 주임. 정비 도크와 훈련장 격납고가 더 오르려면 마이카의 기록: Maintenance research lead. For the Repair Dock, Training Ground and Hangar to go any higher, Mica's records must come first: research level is the facility's cap. If Rivet is the one who "fixes" and Minerva the one who "teaches," Mica is the one who writes down "why it broke." She doesn't write at a desk; she goes out to where it broke and writes it down right there, even outside the hull.
연구 주임. 광산과 발전소가 더 오르려면 베릴의 결재가 필요하다 — 연구: Research lead. For the mines and the Power Plant to go any higher, Beryl's sign-off is required: research level is the facility's cap. What the refinery engineer Agni calls "the work of waiting," Beryl calls "the work of measuring."
격벽 관리관. 선체를 두르는 장갑판을 맡는다. 습격과 약탈이 집에 닿으면: Bulkhead warden. She handles the armor plating around the hull. When raids and plunder reach home, the plates take part of the damage first, so the girls and turrets get hurt less. Worn plates are back on by morning. The thicker the plates, the heavier the ship, and the longer Nova's fuel ledger grows. The second red-haired keeper after Lumen: red stripes on her armor too, and no number on her wrist. Few words; she measures the thickness of everything with her fingertips first.
엔진 관리관. 모함의 주 추진기를 맡는다. 출력을 올리면 배가 전장을 더: Engine warden. She handles the Mothership's main thrusters. Raising output makes the ship drift across the Battlefield faster, but Nova's fuel ledger grows just as much. She doesn't decide where to go. "The ship drifts its own way. I just make the drift faster." Her fingertips are always sooty, and exhaust heat has singed her hair to gold. Her voice drops only when she reads the gauge numbers.
모함의 건설 장부를 쥔 참모. 노바가 항로를 정하면 세레나는 그 항로 위: The officer who holds the Mothership's construction ledger. When Nova sets the route, Serena decides what to build along it, and when. "Writing down the next thing ahead of time is my job. Waiting is yours."
"Writing down the next thing ahead of time is my job. Waiting is yours."
격납고 옆 조립 라인의 순번표를 관리한다. 하르파가 이름을 부르면 루시아: She manages the queue sheet for the assembly line beside the Hangar. When Harpa calls a name, Lucia writes down when that name will come off the line. "One line is enough. As long as the next one's kept open." She looks so much like build-line officer Hana that people ask if they're twins; when it comes up, Lucia doesn't take her eyes off the queue sheet.
\"한 줄이면 충분해. 다음 줄만 비워 두면.\": "One line is enough. As long as the next one's kept open."
정비 도크의 제작대 앞에 다음에 물릴 것을 미리 맞춰 둔다. 리벳이 손을: She sets up the next job at the Repair Dock workbench in advance. The moment Rivet lets go, the next part is already clamped in the jig. "It's not my fault there's only one workbench. Making sure it's never idle, that's my part."
\"제작대가 비는 시간이 없게 하는 게 내 몫이지.\": "Making sure the workbench is never idle, that's my part."
건설 라인 참모. 도크 둘을 동시에 굴리는 일정을 짠다. \"한 줄로 세: Build-line officer. She builds the schedule for running two docks at once. "Line everything up in one queue and half the waiting is wasted." The other half, Hana adds, comes from a lack of resources. What she hates most is hearing she looks just like assembly officer Lucia. "We're nothing alike. My process sheet has no blanks."
\"두 줄로 돌리면 기다림이 절반이에요. 빈칸은 안 둬요.\": "Run two lines and the wait is halved. I don't leave blanks."
격납고 조립 라인 옆, 비어 있던 두 번째 줄을 맡는 참모. 루시아가 순: The officer in charge of the second line beside the Hangar assembly line, the one that used to sit empty. When Lucia writes the queue and Tesla fixes the line, Elena loads the first part onto the second line. "Lucia kept a line open, didn't she? That's where I stand."
\"비워 둔 줄이 있었잖아요. 거기 제가 서요.\": "There was a line kept open, wasn't there? That's where I stand."
수리 라인 참모. 정비 도크 입구에 칠판을 세워 두고, 다친 소녀의 이름: Repair-line officer. She sets up a chalkboard at the Repair Dock entrance and writes the names of hurt girls in order of shortest repair time. Rivet fixes, Sayo looks after them, and Chloe decides who enters the dock first. "We help up the ones who can stand soonest, first."
\"먼저 일어설 수 있는 애부터 일으켜요.\": "We get the ones who can stand soonest back on their feet first."
연구소들의 색인을 만든다. 베릴이 재고 아스트라가 그리면 비앙카는 그 결: She builds the index for the labs. When Beryl measures and Astra charts, Bianca decides in advance which slot the results go into. "Sign-offs are for the leads. I'm the one who opens the next page."
\"결재는 주임님들이. 저는 다음 장을 펴 놓을게요.\": "Sign-offs go to the leads. I'll have the next page open."
\"연합 모함까지 가는 길이야. 돌아오는 항로는 내가 들고 있을게.\": "On the way to the Alliance mothership. I'll keep hold of the route back."
\"돌아오는 항로 잡았어. 함교는 나간 그대로야.\": "Got the route back. The Bridge is just as you left it."
\"항로표를 다시 펴는 중이야. 조금만.\": "Laying the charts out again. Just a moment."
\"신호가 안 닿아. 길은 아니까, 조금 있다 다시 부르지.\": "Signal's not getting through. I know the way back, so I'll call again in a bit."
Going by the marks, it's the left side.
Construction is complete. There is more wall for hit charts now.
습격 끝났어요. 선체 한 바퀴 돌고 올게요. 같이 가실래요?: The raid is over. I'm going to walk once around the hull. Would you like to come along?
Let's go. You have to see where it hit to know where it held.
오늘 자국은 서른하나예요. 지난번보다 줄었어요. 좋은 걸까요?: Thirty-one marks today. Fewer than last time. Is that a good thing, do you think?
Fewer means something somewhere held better — just like your chart says.
Then I'll give you half a bundle of film. One sheet per mark. We'll take it slowly.
Only the numbers make it into the report. The shapes of the marks are only on the film.
I'll copy them before the repairs. Once they're fixed, the marks are gone.
(She stops partway through turning the film.) Read that way, thirty-one feels a little less heavy.
Probably. It might just have been a small raid, so — one, two — I'll count them again.
Cutting them down is the job of the Jamming Veil and the bulkhead. I'm the one who counts what got cut.
방어 연구 주임. 포대 넷과 ECM 방벽 격벽이 더 오르려면 클리페아의: Defense research lead. Before the four batteries, the ECM Barrier, and the Bulkhead can climb any higher, Clipea's hit chart has to come first — research level is the facilities' cap. If the shooters count "we hit," Clipea counts "we were hit." After each raid she walks once around the hull, laying grid film over every mark and tracing it.
옛 항로 표지의 등대지기: Lighthouse Keeper of the Old Route Marker
Turns the buoys on and off in order, even when no ship passes.
물러간 이들이 남긴 부표 줄의 점멸 주기를 지킨다. 지나가는 배가 없던: She keeps the blink cycle of the buoy line left by those who withdrew. Through all that long time with no ship passing, she never once skipped a cycle. She speaks little, and even when glad she does not change the beat. She has the same hair color as the keepers.
How do you do. This line is still lit. One, two.
You have passed by again. I will keep one blink in memory.
I know the beat this ship arrives on. One, two — you come on the third beat.
The one called Chika greeted me with her light. I lit one more for her.
이 줄의 이름을 아는 분이 하나 늘었습니다. 오래 켜 둔 보람이 있습니다: One more person knows the name of this line now. It was worth keeping it lit so long.
Cargo that drifted in between the buoys. Please take it aboard.
It was caught on the third buoy, like last time. One, two.
When cargo catches, I light only that buoy one beat late. For this ship.
There is fuel left over from warming the buoys. I do not use much.
Leftover fuel. This line blinks sparingly to save fuel.
I have set some fuel aside. If one buoy at the end of the line stays dark, that much is saved.
Pieces of a broken buoy. Left over after I replaced it.
I replaced another. The pieces are this ship's share.
갈아 낀 부표가 늘수록 조각이 쌓입니다. 이 배가 가져가 주어 다행입니다: The more buoys I replace, the more pieces pile up. I am glad this ship takes them.
Another signal mixed in between the blinks. It is the beat that always comes before a raid.
I sent the same beat to Sona as well. Better to know early.
That beat has come again. This time I tell this ship first.
A glowing piece came up from the bottom of a buoy. I do not know what it is.
Another came up from the bottom. This line sometimes holds such things.
I had let it be without knowing what it was. It seems right to give it to this ship.
More caught than usual. I nearly lost count of the beat.
There is much cargo today. One, two — I counted all the way to three.
Days this full are rare. I am glad it is a day this ship passes.
The whole line has grown heavy. I have never seen a day like this.
So much caught that the buoys tilt. A day not in the records.
So a line kept lit this long gives one day like this. Please take all of it.
표류 화물 무리의 검수원: Tally Clerk of the Drifting Cargo Cluster
Never opens a sealed crate. Counts by weight alone.
떠도는 컨테이너 무리의 화물표를 지금도 맞춰 본다. 봉인된 상자는 끝까지: She still checks the manifests of a drifting cluster of containers. She never opens a sealed crate — she counts by weight alone. She insists the Mothership only takes "what's already unsealed." She has the same hair color as the keepers.
You, ship. Hands off the seals. Only the loose ones. The weight checks out.
Back again. I still remember last time's weight.
Set aside one slot as your ship's share. Unsealed ones only.
That girl Mio logs it down to the gram. Her last digit matched my weight.
Saga and I got the same count. First time. The weight checks out — and this time the count too.
Unsealed crate. Take it. The weight checks out.
Same weight as last time. Your ship takes things honestly.
Put it in your share slot. I already weighed it.
